body:
Nomad Kitchen is a new stall at Taman Jurong
Finding quality Middle Eastern fare in Singapore isn’t always easy. But a stall serving dishes from Iran, Turkey, Italy, Greece, Morocco, Saudi Arabia, and Afghanistan? That’s even harder to come by. So when we came across Nomad Kitchen , we knew we had to check it out.
Located in Taman Jurong Market and Food Centre , the new stall has already earned itself a solid reputation, reportedly selling out daily. Its founder, Fuad Salim, a self-professed F&B nomad, picked up the recipes throughout his 30-year career in hospitality, where he worked as an F&B and hotel manager.
Food at Nomad Kitchen
The menu consists of Afghan Chicken (from $6) from Afghanistan, Saffron Jujeh ($8) from Iran, Iskender ($12) from Turkey, Shakshuka ($7) from Morocco, Lasagna ($8.50) from Italy, Moussaka ($8) from Greece, and finally, rotisserie chicken and street wraps inspired by Saudi Arabia.
Chef Fuad prepares everything from scratch daily, including handmade Lavash flatbreads, grilled meats, kabuli rice, saffron rice, and lasagna.
We started with the $6 portion of Afghan Chicken. For an extra $2.50 , you can get another quarter of the rotisserie chicken, which we thought was extremely generous in this economy.
While I tend to find roast chicken too dry for my liking, this one was juicy, moist, and expertly cooked. The seasoning was flavourful too, with a blend of spices that added depth without being overly salty. However, we found the white meat slightly bland, as most of the seasoning was concentrated on the skin and hadn’t penetrated the meat.
According to the chef, raisins and carrots are integral to an Afghan kabuli rice dish. I could see why: they added a burst of sweetness to the aromatic rice, making for a complex and layered flavour profile.
The Saffron Jujeh was probably my favourite dish—it came with two chunky grilled chicken kebabs, saffron rice, roasted tomatoes and peppers, and a yoghurt sauce. Again, the generous portion size was a pleasant surprise.
The kebabs had a similarly intense spice blend to the rotisserie; however, they were thoroughly marinated, so every bite was full of flavour. The yoghurt-based sauce was tangy and refreshing, but more subtle, which worked well to highlight the kebab rather than overpower it.
The roasted vegetables were smoky and juicy, and good enough to stand alone as a side dish. Traditionally, though, Persians would mash the juicy tomatoes into saffron rice, turning them into a flavourful “sauce”.
Lastly, we tried the lasagna. Most faux-Italian places I know of put an ungodly amount of cheese on their lasagna (I’m not complaining). This one was more well-balanced, with all the elements complementing each other rather than overpowering the dish.
The pasta sheets were quite thick and satisfyingly chewy. They made for a great vessel for the layers of beef ragu, Neapolitan sauce, and bechamel. The dish was savoury and hearty, with hints of sweetness and acidity to balance it out.
Ambience at Nomad Kitchen
Nomad Kitchen is tucked away in the corner of Taman Jurong Market and Food Centre. We arrived around 12:30pm to a short queue and a steady stream of customers.
The market itself was huge and happening, with three stories worth of food and retail stalls. It was relatively well-ventilated, with multiple fans working overtime to combat the Singapore stuffiness.
The market is a 10-minute bus ride or 18-minute walk from Lakeside MRT Station.
Nomad Kitchen – Eatbook Review
I visited Nomad Kitchen with high expectations, knowing Chef Fuad Salim’s hospitality background, and was still pleasantly surprised. Every element of the food was well-cooked and flavourful. The dishes also seemed to stay true to their cultural roots, with ingredients and flavours recreated as authentically as possible.
As a Westie, I will definitely be revisiting to try the rest of the menu.
View this post on Instagram
Check out our Instagram Reel for the full scoop!
If you’re on a hunt for more unique hawkers, check out our pork rib prawn mee review , which features a 90-year-old hawker. And while you’re in the area, here are the best Jurong East food places to visit.

body:
1-day Bugis and CBD itinerary
Bugis and the CBD are only a short train ride apart, but they can feel like two different worlds. Bugis, the trendier one, is packed with aesthetic cafes and thrift shops, while the CBD is chock full of affordable hawker stalls catering to office workers.
The good news is that Singapore is small enough to walk between the two, weather permitting. I’ve also included a few things to do along the way so you can walk off the calories in between meals. If you’d like to carry on to Orchard afterwards, hop on the train from City Hall or Raffles Place MRT Station on the North-South Line and go straight there—our 12-hour Orchard food itinerary will help you make the most of your time.
Breakfast: Bao Er Cafe
Image credit: Sean Goh via Google Maps
I have a bad habit of skipping breakfast, but if anyone recommends Bao Er Cafe , you know I’ll be there bright and early. Located at Fortune Centre , an older mall full of affordable eats, Bao Er Cafe is an eight-minute walk from Bugis MRT Station .
The cafe is known for its Singaporean breakfast dishes, and this is its third outlet, after Balestier and Holland Village. If you’ve never had kaya toast , it’s a local breakfast staple of crisp toast with kaya—a coconut and egg jam—and butter, usually eaten with soft-boiled eggs and a cup of local coffee.
The Kaya Butter Toast Set is the one to get, and it comes with your choice of hot kopi or teh and two soft-boiled eggs. If you’ve had kaya toast at Ya Kun, Singapore’s best-known chain, you’ll know the formula: thin, crisp brown toast, cold butter and fragrant kaya. Bao Er follows the same recipe, with kaya made from fresh coconut milk. At $6.20 , it’s also slightly cheaper than Ya Kun’s $6.30 set.
For something more filling, get the Signature Fried Hokkien Mee ($8.80) , which has earned plenty of rave reviews for its rich seafood broth, chunky tiger prawns, and smoky aroma. The outlet-exclusive Jeremy’s Beef Hor Fun ($10.80) is another popular pick, comprising flat rice noodles stir-fried with beef.
Read our Bao Er Cafe Fortune Centre feature .
Address: 190 Middle Road, #02-06, Fortune Centre, Singapore 188979
Opening hours: Daily 8am to 8pm
Website
Bao Er Cafe is not halal-certified.
Bao Er Cafe Opens At Fortune Centre With New Western Menu And Famous Kaya Toast
Lunch: Smashed
For lunch, head to Smashed , a halal burger shop that went viral after IShowSpeed tried their food during his visit to Singapore. You’ll even spot an “IShowSpeed approved” poster in the shop.
I used to queue for their burgers when they were still a stall at the Kampong Gelam Ramadan Bazaar, where the lines could stretch for an hour. It has since turned into a proper store on Baghdad Street .
Smashed is inspired by the smash burgers that have been trending in London since 2023. The menu is small, with just three burgers, each with two thin patties smashed on the grill and topped with melted American cheese, caramelised onions, and pickles.
The House Smashed ($10) is a solid place to start. It comes drenched in a tangy, savoury house sauce that’s similar to mayonnaise. The patties are smashed but still have a meaty bite, with charred edges that add a nice crisp.
My go-to is the Spicy Smashed ($12) , which features a house-made sambal balado sauce that reminds me of a spicy Thousand Island dressing. I highly recommend getting a side of Dirty Fries ($6) too. These sinful fries come topped with hot melted cheese and bacon that’s fried to a crisp.
Read our Smashed review .
Address: 21 Baghdad Street, Singapore 199066
Opening hours: Sun-Thurs 12pm to 9:30pm, Sun-Mon 12pm to 10pm
Tel: 9181 1665
Website
Smashed is halal-certified.
Smashed Review: London-Inspired Halal Smash Burgers Near Haji Lane
Sightseeing: Kampong Gelam
Image credit: @catwongnailq
After lunch at Smashed, you’re only a short walk from Kampong Glam ‘s Haji Lane, one of the most popular hangouts for young Singaporeans. Named after the Arab pilgrim brokers who once arranged the haj for Muslims here, its shophouses were once used as pilgrim lodges. Today, they’re filled with indie boutiques, cafes, bars, and thrift stores.
Image credit: @takara.house
Self-photo studios are big here. Solace Studios changes its themes with the seasons, and the current one is picnic-themed, complete with props. Along the same stretch, One Click Studio is a good pick for bigger groups, since its rooms fit up to 10 people. For thrifting, the one to go for is Takara House , a vintage shop with a cafe tucked in the back. The owners source their finds from Japan and Vietnam, so you’ll come across out-of-production Japanese fashion, plushies, vintage teaware and nostalgic toys.
Before you leave Kampong Glam, take a short walk to Sultan Mosque , one of Singapore’s most important landmarks that’s been around since 1928. Visitors are welcome, but dress modestly and check the visiting hours first.
Image credit: The Smart Local

Thai Seng Fish Soup opens second outlet in Bugis
Image credit: CP via Google Maps
Fish soup fans are probably well familiar with Thai Seng Fish Soup , which has consistently drawn hour-long queues at Ubi. After more than 20 years, the brand finally expanded to a second location in Bugis in July 2026, so heartlanders in central Singapore can get in on the hype.
https://eatbook.sg/best-fish-soup-singapore/
We also heard that a third location is in the works, so keep your eyes peeled for more information!
Do note that this is not to be confused with Tai Seng Fish Soup , another well-known fish soup stall with a nearly identical name.
Image credit: foodpanda
Thai Seng’s fish soup is popular for its strong umami flavour, which sets it apart from the more traditional, lighter versions of fish soup. They’re also known for using freshly sliced batang fish for a superior taste.
Image credit: foodpanda
The menu is pretty standard, with options including Sliced Fish Soup (from $6), Seafood Soup (from $8), and Fried Fish Bee Hoon Soup (from $6).
Image credit: foodpanda
For a spicy option, the Tom Yum Seafood Soup (from $8.50) is a crowd favourite, thanks to its punchy flavour and balance of sweet, sour, and spicy notes. Other options include Fish Head Bee Hoon (from $6), Fish Belly Soup ($10), Fish Porridge (from $6), Double Fish Soup (from $6), and Sliced Fish Mee Sua (from $6).
Many regulars recommend getting the soup with ee mian and the “egg bomb”—deep-fried egg floss strip— which adds another layer of flavour and depth to the broth.

body:
Best food in Orchard
Meeting up with my friends in Orchard for a meal used to mean eating at Genki Sushi or Saizeriya, but now as the food writer among my group of friends, I’ve become the one they turn to for recommendations instead. Now, the pressure’s always on to suggest something that won’t disappoint or bore them.
Thankfully, after plenty of trips to Singapore’s bustling shopping district over the years, I’ve built up a solid list of go-to spots. If you need something more specific, we also have guides to the best cafes in Orchard , or affordable Orchard Road food spots to help you out.
Best Orchard Road food spots, in a nutshell:
• Affordable restaurant in Orchard: Nantsuttei at Orchard Central – Black garlic ramen from $13.40 ++
• Affordable cafe in Orchard: Fan’s Cafe at Far East Plaza – Fresh shio pan bakery near Orchard MRT Station
• Instagrammable cafe in Orchard : Nuldam Space at Scape – Plant-based Korean cafe
• For special occasions: sen-ryo at ION Orchard – Luxe but value-for-money Japanese fare
• For large groups: Seoul Restaurant at Conrad Singapore – Authentic Korean BBQ in Orchard
Affordable options
1. New Station Rice Bar – Hearty rice meals at Far East Plaza
Hidden eatery with famous salted egg pork rice
What is New Station Rice Bar? New Station Rice Bar does a smashing version of Salted Egg Pork Rice ($9) . Redolent of curry leaves, the creamy and savoury sauce adds depth to the juicy fried chicken. Don’t worry about the dish being jelak, as the hints of chilli padi cut through the rich gravy with a fiery kick.
If you aren’t a salted egg fan, they’ve also got a signature Marmite Chicken Rice ($8.50) and other popular zi char dishes, including Sweet and Sour Pork (from $15) and Chye Poh Omelette (from $10) .
Read our New Station Rice Bar coverage .
Expect to pay: $8.50-$9 for rice sets, $10-$22 for zi char dishes, $15-$30 for seafood
What to order: Salted Egg Pork Rice ($9), Hot Plate Black Pepper Beef (from $16), Assam Crispy Fish (from $12)
Address: 14 Scotts Road, #05-95, Far East Plaza, Singapore 228213
Opening hours: Daily 11:30am to 8:45pm
Tel: 8999 4064
Website
New Station Rice Bar is not halal-certified.
2. My Favourite Cafe – Affordable yong tau foo in Lucky Plaza
Homely yong tau foo with famous fried meatball
What is My Favourite Cafe? While I seldom visit Lucky Plaza , that is not the case now with the discovery of My Favourite Cafe . Have your own pick of ingredients for your bowl of yong tau foo, before you’re charged accordingly. One thoughtful gesture by the chefs is that they’ll put your deep-fried ingredients in a separate bowl to prevent them from turning soggy in the soup. Like most yong tau foo stalls, My Favourite Cafe offers both soup and dry versions. The fried meatballs and braised mushrooms are must-haves here! Prices start at $7 for six pieces of yong tau foo and noodles or rice.
Check out My Favourite Cafe review .
Expect to pay: $7 on average per bowl
What to order: Yong Tau Foo (6 ingredients) with noodles/rice ($7), Fried Meatball ($0.90 per piece)

My Favourite Cafe is not halal-certified.
3. Greenview Cafe – Well-loved mee hoon kueh in Far East Plaza
Low-key eatery with handmade noodles
What is Greenview Cafe? Another low-key eatery worth checking out in town is Greenview Cafe , a no-frills spot at Far East Plaza . Go straight for their best-selling Minced Pork Mee Hoon Kueh ($6.90) , a flavourful mix of handmade mee hoon kueh, minced pork, and mushrooms, also available fried. Alternatively, for a taste of something more unique, order their Fried Mee Tai Mak ($7.90) : stir-fried noodles with a prominent charred fragrance. If you want something soupy, we recommend their Minced Pork With Egg & Tomato Soup ($6.90).
BTW: Greenview Cafe is closing its Far East eatery soon, so head there before it’s too late.
Read our Greenview Cafe review .
Expect to pay: $6.90-$10.90 per mee hoon kueh bowl, $6.90-$8.50 for soups
What to order: Minced Pork Mee Hoon Kueh ($6.90), Mala Mee Hoon Kueh ($10.90)

Tel: 6734 2312
Greenview Cafe Website

4. Puncak Best Noodles – Muslim-friendly Chinese cuisine
Affordable halal zi char at Far East Plaza
Image credit: Nor Asyraf via Google Maps
What is Puncak Best Noodles? For my fellow Muslim friends who want to try Chinese cuisine, check out Puncak Best Noodles . This casual eatery has been open for several years, and many patrons claim that they have the cheapest and best halal noodles in Singapore, just as their name suggests. A must-try dish is the Honey Dew Chicken Noodle ($7) , an interesting combination we have never seen elsewhere. I’ve been going to Whisky Live Singapore for about four years, and if there’s one thing I’ve learnt, it’s to just fork out for the VIP pass. I know it’s a hundred bucks more, but hear me out.
Credit: La Maison Du Whisky
The regular Connoisseur section is pretty much the same every year. For first-timers, there’s plenty to explore with hundreds of whiskies to try. But after a few visits, deja vu starts kicking in and you’ll recognise a lot of the same bottles and brands .
Most of the interesting stuff is in the VIP area anyway, especially the limited editions that would be really expensive to taste. Last year, I tried a Signatory Vintage Caol Ila 2013 that was so good for the value, I ended up buying a bottle. La Maison du Whisky’s ARTIST range has also been consistently worth checking out, with unique releases each time I visit.
Credit: La Maison Du Whisky
This year, I’m particularly interested in the ARTIST Nikka Whisky collection, featuring eight single casks from Yoichi and Miyagikyo. There’s a 40-year-old Yoichi going for S$26,000, with only three bottles allocated to Singapore (but I highly doubt they’ll be opening that).
Credit: La Maison Du Whisky
I’m not Crazy Rich Asian enough to blow S$26,000 on a whisky I’ve never tasted, no matter how rare it is. The 10-year-olds start at S$580, which is a lot more realistic. Still expensive, but at least within my range of a possible drunk purchase.
How to get the most out of Whisky Live Singapore
Get there at 12pm if you have VIP . I’ve found that’s the best time to go before the crowds arrive at 2pm. Some of the more exclusive bottles run out early, so don’t leave those till later. Same with purchasing: buy them early then head back to tasting. I missed out on getting a Chichibu Umeshu Cask because it was all snapped up!
Credit: La Maison Du Whisky
My usual strategy is to head straight for the VIP area and taste the rare stuff first, then work my way through the main hall. After about 20 pours, my taste buds are pretty much useless anyway. No point paying extra for good whisky when I can barely tell the difference anymore. If you’re on the Connoisseur pass, brand highlights I’d personally prioritise first in the Whisky Hall are Amrut, Benromach, Nikka, Bruichladdich, Gordon & MacPhail or other brands you want to do a vertical tasting on. Some American Bourbons can surprise you, too.
Eat before you go. I’ve never been particularly impressed by the food at the event since shifting to EHL Campus. It’s expensive for what you get, and I’d rather spend that money on whisky.
Address: EHL Campus (Singapore), 3 Lady Hill Road, Singapore 258672
Dates: 21 – 22 November 2026
Getting there: Free shuttle from Newton MRT
Expected damage: S$120+ (Connoisseur) to S$220+ (VIP), before the bottle you swore you wouldn’t buy
12 wine bars in Singapore recommended by wine club members
summary: Four years of Whisky Live Singapore, one piece of advice: go VIP. The Connoisseur hall barely changes, but VIP is where the limited editions are. This year’s headliner is ARTIST Nikka, topped by a S$26,000 40-year-old Yoichi I’ll admire from afar. Arrive at 12pm before exclusives sell out, drink the rare stuff first, and eat beforehand. 21–22 November 2026 at EHL Campus.
title: Whisky Live Singapore 2026: Why I only go VIP now & the S$26,000 whisky I’m skipping

Shipping Taobao orders to your hotel in China
We all need a little Taobao haul once in a while. From trendy clothes to quirky home finds, the platform has plenty of items to tempt us into adding more to our carts. But while it’s easy to get carried away with all the shopping, have you ever stopped to think about how much you’re spending on shipping fees?
With Singaporeans’ love for travelling to China showing no signs of slowing down, your next holiday could be the perfect excuse to go all out on Taobao. Instead of shipping your haul to Singapore, consider having your orders delivered straight to your hotel there. It might sound unconventional, but shipping Taobao orders to your hotel in China is easier than you think.
The current exchange rate is RMB1 = ~S$0.20 as of 26th October 2026.
Why should you ship Taobao items to your hotel in China?
Shop exclusive items & enjoy lower prices
Image adapted from: @格子间里，丈量世界 & @灰灰哥哥&千禧妹妹 via RED
While we’re not suggesting you book a flight to China just to shop on Taobao, you might be surprised by how much cheaper your haul gets when you ship it domestically instead of all the way to Singapore.
When using the Taobao app , setting your location to Mainland China unlocks deals that may not be available to shoppers in Singapore, including lower prices and products sold exclusively within China . If you are not well-versed in Chinese, use a translation tool like Google Translate to navigate the app without changing its language settings.
We also hope you’ve got Alipay ( App Store | Google Play ) set up on your phone by now. After all, getting around China without it can be a hassle. While not compulsory, we’d also recommend getting a Chinese phone number, as it makes it easier to contact your courier directly and request delivery address changes if needed.
P.S. Check out our China travel guide , which includes apps you’ll need for a fuss-free trip.
Cheaper or free domestic shipping
Image adapted from: @桔子酒店 广州北京路步行街越秀 公园店 & @3月的白羊佳 via RED
Alas, the biggest deal breaker when shopping on Taobao is often the shipping fees. But one of the biggest perks of shipping your order to your hotel in China is that you’ll get to enjoy lower domestic shipping rates , ranging from RMB5 (~S$1) to RMB15 (~S$2.90) . Many listings even offer free domestic delivery , marked as bāo yóu (包邮).
On the other hand, shipping orders to Singapore typically involves 3 common methods: direct shipping , consolidated air shipping , and consolidated sea freight . Direct shipping sends your orders straight to Singapore, while consolidated air shipping combines multiple parcels at a warehouse in China before sending them over by air. If you’re buying bulkier or heavier items, consolidated sea freight is another option, though delivery may take longer.
Image credit: @养出光的ZOEY via RED
To give you a rough idea of what to expect, we’ve included some estimated shipping costs to Singapore for reference. Actual prices may vary depending on your parcel’s weight and dimensions, as well as your chosen shipping service.
Shipping method
Estimated cost
Estimated shipping time
Direct air shipping
RMB42 to RMB78/kg (~S$8 to S$15)
5-8 days
Consolidated air shipping
RMB42 to RMB78/kg (~S$8 to S$15)
5-8 days
Consolidated sea freight
RMB16 to RMB31/kg (~S$3 to S$5.90)
12-20 days
BTW, even though Taobao now offers free sea shipping to Singapore with no minimum spend on eligible items, not all items qualify . So if the item you’ve had your eye on doesn’t qualify for free shipping, bookmark it and place an order on your next trip to China, then have it shipped to your hotel instead.
Fast local delivery
Image credit: @佳. via RED
By removing the main bottlenecks of cross-border e-commerce, like international shipping and customs clearance, domestic delivery in China becomes much more straightforward.
Local courier services such as SF Express, ZTO Express, YTO Express, and Yunda Express use automated sorting facilities and scheduled dispatch windows to handle high-volume deliveries across the country. When you ship your Taobao order to your hotel in China, you can expect to receive it as soon as the next day for local deliveries, or within 2-4 days if it’s coming from another province.
How to ship Taobao items to your hotel in China
1. Add your hotel address in the right format
Screenshot from: Trip.com
Formatting your delivery address correctly is arguably the most important step in this guide. You don’t want your Taobao haul to end up at a hotel in another province, leaving you on a wild goose chase to track it down.
Screenshot from: Taobao
Finally, tap the address book icon in the top-right corner of your Taobao app and paste your hotel address into the relevant field. Make sure you’ve selected the correct hotel branch and filled in your personal details to avoid any delivery mix-ups.
2. Check your hotel’s delivery package policy
…

Haunted bus rides in Singapore
Just when you think we’ve exhausted the list of the scariest things to do in the country, we’re hitting you with another one: the scariest bus rides in Singapore .
From whizzing past cemeteries to possibly sitting beside “otherworldly” passengers, here are some bus services for chill (read: bone-chilling ) night rides that’ll have you thinking, “Maybe I should have just Grab-ed instead.”
1. Bus 975
Passes by forested roads with no street lights
Let’s start strong with what many claim to be the most haunted bus route in Singapore : bus service 975 . But why is it so scary?
Image credit: amaran via Google Maps
For starters, it operates in the West, which is horrifying. This bus will take you from Bukit Panjang Interchange to Lim Chu Kang Road, with the last bus operating at 11.35pm.
Image credit: MEGUMI NAKAZAWA via Google Maps
Other sights to look out for in the dark are army camps like Sungei Gedong Camp, the abandoned Neo Tiew Estate , and Choa Chu Kang Cemetery . Bus 975 also holds the distinction of being the only bus that serves what might be the most ulu bus stop in Singapore: the Police Coast Guard bus stop at the very end of Lim Chu Kang Road.
Creepy tales of bus 975 include stories of bus drivers stopping at seemingly empty bus stops to let “something” get off, and even sightings of a mysterious priest walking along the route’s pitch-black roads .
Bus service 975 route: Bukit Panjang Interchange ⭤ Lim Chu Kang Road
2. Bus 171
Route so ulu that it serves bus stops named after lamp posts
Image credit: NEA
In a similar vein, the route that bus 171 plies is equally as desolate during certain stretches of the journey. That’s because it drops passengers off directly in front of the Mandai Crematorium and Columbarium Complex, a macabre stop which can definitely stir up an eerie vibe, especially under the cloak of night.
The LP 162 bus stop.
Image adapted from: Google Maps
What’s more, the bus travels along stretches of forested sections on Mandai Road, flanked by kilometres of towering trees that cast looming shadows on the road when day turns to night. These sections are so remote that bus stops here are named after lamp posts, such as the LP 159 and LP 162 stops, because those are the only man-made points of interest in the area.
Bus service 171 route: Yishun Interchange ↺ Upper Bukit Timah Road
3. Bus 29
Drives by Old Changi Hospital
Fun fact: Bus service 29 will bring you the closest to Old Changi Hospital (OCH), traversing where no other bus dares to go. But it’s not just OCH that’s spooky – the general Changi area does have a reputation for being eerie, with haunted chalets and a beach that was the site of a WW2 massacre .
Get off at “Aft Turnhouse Rd” if you’d like to cop a peep at OCH.
Image adapted from: Google Maps
The bus operates daily from 5.20am till 11.45pm, so you have the option of spotting Changi’s hantus in the wee hours of the morning or night, hehe.
Bus service 29 route: Tampines Interchange ↺ Tampines Interchange (Loop at Changi Village Terminal)
4. Bus 172
Along Jalan Bahar’s ulu “cemetery route”
Image credit: Singapore Ghost Club
Joining Old Tampines Road as a certified freaky street 7 days a week is Jalan Bahar, infamous for being surrounded by several (definitely more than 4) cemeteries. If you’d like a humble tour, hop on bus 172 , which will take you to and fro Choa Chu Kang and Boon Lay interchanges through the entire graveyard stretch.
The Pusara Aman Mque bus stop along Jalan Bahar is also pretty infamous for being the “most haunted bus stop” in Singapore, with tales of phantom passengers waiting for the bus and odd smells at night.
Bus service 172 route: Choa Chu Kang Interchange ⭤ Boon Lay Interchange
5. Bus 200
Late-night rides along “99 Bends”
Image credit: NParks
Anyone into the supernatural in Singapore would have heard of the 99 Bends – what many paranormal aficionados call South Buona Vista Road. Besides being one of the scariest roads in Singapore, it is also one of the most dangerous , thanks to its sharp turns and blind spots.
If you’d like to experience this for yourself, board bus 200 , which will take you along the 99 Bends’ steep lanes. The last buses are at 11.35pm (from Buona Vista) and 11.59pm (from Kent Ridge), so make sure you enjoy a late-night ride for maximum creeps.
Bus service 200 route: Buona Vista Terminal ↺ Buona Vista Terminal (Loop at Kent Ridge Terminal)
6. Bus 856
Stops near an abandoned hospital
Image adapted from: Google Maps
For scaredy cats, this is probably the least spooky route on the list. While most of the journey on bus 856 is uneventful, it does pass by one significant landmark – View Road Hospital . Think of it as the sibling in Old Changi Hospital’s shadow; most people don’t know this abandoned hospital exists.
You won’t get to see the building from the bus itself, but get off at “Aft View Rd” bus stop if you’d like to walk around the area to really soak it all in.
…
summary: These bus rides will have you thinking: “Maybe I should have just Grab-ed instead.”
title: 8 Scariest Bus Routes In Singapore For “Relaxing” Night Rides Away From Humans

body:
Somewhere along the way, the Internet decided that October should be called “Spooktober” – because Halloween falls on the month’s last day. This has prompted many companies and establishments to host themed events and activities.
But what if you prefer spending time at home or online with friends? This is where video games shine. With Steam’s Scream V Fest and Epic Games’ Halloween Sale happening right now, you might be looking for a game or two to scratch that horror itch.
We looked through the catalogue and curated a list of recommendations that carry intense gameplay, spooky atmosphere, and thrilling moments. Single-player and multiplayer PC games are included, and some even go beyond the horror genre. Keep reading and see if you agree with our picks!
Single-player
If you’re brave enough to face horrors on your own (unlike me), these games will be right up your alley. Fair warning – they might keep you up all night!
Resident Evil 2
Credit: Capcom
One of the most popular horror themes has always been Zombies. So let’s kick off our list with a game that features these undead, virus-stricken, relentless creatures. And trust me, it’s a real spooky one.
Many of you might remember the Resident Evil series for its blend of action and horror, and you wouldn’t be wrong. But the 2019 remake of Resident Evil 2 (RE2) takes players back to the series’ origins, which are mostly rooted in horror.
You play as two protagonists, Leon S. Kennedy and Claire Redfield, in a survival horror experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat. Expect long dark corridors, creepy enclosed spaces, and intense encounters with a deadly virus outbreak. If you enjoyed the latest Resident Evil movie, it’s time to check out the source material.
RE2 is available at 80% off on Steam until 2am on 4 November 2026 for just S$9.98. There’s no better time to visit Raccoon City.
Resident Evil 2 – 80% Off
Steam | Website
Now till 4 November 2026 (Steam)
Metro Exodus
Credit: 4A Games
This one’s terrifying too. Metro Exodus is the third game in the Metro series and its latest, before the upcoming Metro 2039 . This immersive first-person shooter (FPS) will place you in a post-apocalyptic Russian landscape full of bad guys and mutated beasts. Beautiful – but definitely not on your vacation list.
The most intense moments are probably when you are deep in the Metro tunnels, low on ammo and resources, trying to sneak around “unfriendly” inhabitants. What is also interesting is that the game’s story takes place over a one-year period, which means you will experience all 4 seasons in this thrilling adventure.
Metro Exodus is currently at a 90% discount on Epic Games until 1am on 10 November 2026 , and is available for just S$3.90 .
Metro Exodus – 90% Off
Epic Games | GOG | Steam | Website
Now till 10 November 2026 (Epic Games)
Subnautica
Credit: Unknown Worlds Entertainment
Subnautica is not exactly labelled a horror game, but I reckon it has given and will continue to give many people nightmares. If you have thalassophobia – or a fear of deep bodies of water – think twice before diving into this one.
The premise is that you crash-landed on an alien ocean planet and need to survive by gathering resources underwater. You will fight to find food, water, and oxygen, while building equipment and habitats.
At the same time, you will explore the depths of this mysterious planet and seek a way out. But beware. Mysteries and resources are not the only things lurking in the deep. You might not like what you uncover.
Subnautica is currently at a 75% discount on both Steam and Epic Games for just S$10 . The sale ends on 3 November 2026 for both platforms, at 2am and 12am respectively. Subnautica’s sequel, Subnautica 2 , is also available in Early Access for S$40.
Subnautica – 75% Off
Epic Games | Steam | Website
Now till 3 November 2026
Alan Wake (series)
Credit: Remedy Entertainment
Of all the single-player games I’ve listed here, Alan Wake is the only one I’ve survived and actually beat. RE2 and Metro Exodus sit in my games library, waiting for the day I feel courageous enough again.
But the funny thing is, Alan Wake and its 2023 sequel Alan Wake 2 might be the “purest” horror games of the bunch. Specifically, they belong to the psychological horror genre, which basically means what you experience might mess with your head a little bit.
I can’t speak for the second game as I have yet to play it, but the first is kind of a classic. It puts you into the shoes of the titular best-selling writer, searching for his missing wife in a strange small town.
Your only obstacles are scary pages from a manuscript you wrote coming to life, and a Dark Presence constantly stalking you. Your only defence? A gun and a torchlight. The game’s story is presented like a TV series, with a compelling narrative that leaves you wanting to know more.
…
summary: Looking for some thrills this Halloween season? Here are 6–7 spooky PC games you can grab on sale this week.
title: 6 thrilling PC games on sale for Halloween 2026

Side Quest – Creative studio & art cafe in Joo Chiat
Joo Chiat is known for its colourful shophouses, heritage spots, and trendy haunts tucked along its streets, from the Museum of Food to a dedicated Samoyed dog cafe .
Joining the neighbourhood’s list of places to check out is Side Quest , a newly reopened art jamming studio that sits atop one of Joo Chiat’s many shophouses, offering a cosy space to let your creative juices flow and design a masterpiece at your own pace.
What is Side Quest?
View this post on Instagram
Founded in 2025, Side Quest was started by 23-year-old Jessica Tay to share her love for art with others and inspire them to explore creativity through craft activities . It began as a mobile business hosting DIY workshops for private birthdays and events all around Singapore, before she decided to open her own studio in Joo Chiat.
Instead of serving food, the art cafe’s menu features a variety of hands-on art projects made for all ages . The space is also designed for visitors to slow down and enjoy creating their own keepsakes without expecting it to be flawless. There are also no formal instructors , so you can work on your crafts without any pressure and let your creativity take the lead.
Image credit: Side Quest via Google Maps
Since reopening on 13th October 2026, Side Quest has introduced a refreshed menu with beginner-friendly workshops and activities , aiming to be a creative third space where you can unwind with friends while trying something new.
What to expect at Side Quest
Unleash your inner artist with painting sessions
Image credit: @sidequest.sg via Instagram
Side Quest offers 6 painting activities , all with materials fully provided, and zero prior art experience needed. Pick up a brush and paint whatever’s on your mind on a blank canvas with the Canvas Painting ($38 for 2 hours) workshop.
Image adapted from: @sidequest.sg via Instagram
For beginners, Figurine Painting ($28 for 1.5 hours) or the crowd-favourite Trinket Tray Painting ($20/hour) will give you an easy starting point. You’ll get to choose from a selection of hand-cast figurines and trinket trays, then personalise them with your own designs.
There’s also the Colour Stories Coaster Painting ($35 for 2 hours) workshop, which lets you paint a pair of coasters with pre-drawn designs inspired by the Peranakan tiles found all over Joo Chiat.
Image adapted from: @sidequest.sg via Instagram
For something more practical, try Tote Bag Painting ($35 for 2 hours) and decorate an art piece that can be carried around wherever you go. Plant parents will want to check out Plant Pot Painting ($32 for 2 hours) , where you’ll get to customise your own flower pot and bring it back to spruce up your home garden.
Find your creative spark with DIY loop charms & postcards
Image adapted from: Side Quest
Painting is not all that you’ll find at Side Quest; those looking to explore other crafts or personalise mini tokens for friends and family can do so at the postcard and charm-making stations.
You’ll be given up to 2 postcards per session for you to write a heartfelt message to your loved ones and decorate them at the Snail Mail Postcard Bar ($25/hour) ; Side Quest will even help you mail it out for free .
At the Ling Long Loop Charm Bar ($18 for 30 minutes) , participants will get unlimited access to the cafe’s collection of beads and charms to create their own accessory. Make one for yourself or put together a little keepsake for someone special.
Celebrate birthdays with arts & crafts
View this post on Instagram
Skip the usual birthday dinner and celebrate your special day with a hands-on craft party hosted entirely by Side Quest. Starting at $60/pax , the Basic Birthday Party Package includes a 2-hour private celebration and your choice of any of the painting activities offered at the studio.
For more crafty fun, upgrade to the Bespoke Birthday Party Package at $90/pax . You’ll get an extra 30 minutes of party time , access to the Ling Long Loop Charm Bar , and curated goodie bags for each guest to take home.
Image credit: Side Quest
Parents can also leave the cleanup to Side Quest, so you can spend more time celebrating the special occasion with the little ones. The party can be hosted at the studio in Joo Chiat, or have the team bring the celebrations to your preferred venue at no extra charge.
Are food & drinks allowed at Side Quest?
While Side Quest does not serve any food or drinks as of yet, feel free to bring along non-alcoholic beverages from the cafes in Joo Chiat to sip on while working on your artworks.
How to get to Side Quest
View this post on Instagram
The art studio is a 7-minute walk from Marine Parade MRT Station . You’ll find Side Quest on the 2nd level of the 7-Eleven directly opposite i12 Katong .
Visit Side Quest for fun workshops at wallet-friendly prices
…
summary: Drop by this new art studio the next time you visit Joo Chiat.

Singapore Coffee Week 2026 is back at Marina Bay Sands
Image credit: Singapore Coffee Week
As a country filled with workaholics, our coffee culture is booming, and something’s brewing that’ll get us all excited— Singapore Coffee Week 2026 is back from 5 November to 8 November 2026 . Better yet, entry to the highly anticipated event is free of charge.
Get excited for exhibits by various coffee brands, both local and international, games, activities, and even live competitions. Read on for a sneak peek of what’s at the event.
Expect around 50 exhibitors, including popular brands such as Suzuki Coffee , one of Singapore’s oldest artisanal roasters, and Baristart Coffee , known for its signature creamy lattes. Cowpresso Coffee Roasters is well known among home baristas for its high-end home espresso gear, on top of specialty coffee beans.
Image credit: Singapore Coffee Week
Beyond the mainstream brands, here are some unique roasters worth seeking out. Shinkirou Coffee from Tokyo will be featured at the Japan coffee pavilion. You’ll find their Ethiopia Sidama Dembi #2 , known for its vibrant fruity flavour, and Colombia Granja Paraíso 92—Ombligon , with more intense fruity and acidic notes. Prices are TBD.
Image credit: Yorz Coffee
Another highlight is Yorz Coffee, a Singapore-based organic grower with cultivation grounds in Yunnan, China. Its specialties include Ou Yang Natural , Wine Natural , and YORZ Espresso Blend. Meanwhile, KenntaRoast is a Singaporean boutique micro-roastery that makes experimental specialty coffees in small batches.
You can also look forward to events happening throughout the three days, including social media giveaways, interactive board games, passport trail adventures, and a bean discovery bar.
That’s not all: Fans can learn more about coffee roasting at the Singapore Coffee Roasting Team Championship 2026, where teams will compete for the chance to represent Singapore at the upcoming ASEAN Coffee Roasting Championship 2027.
While I have the coffee addicts’ attention, check out these best coffee cafes in Singapore . And here are some Marina Bay Sands restaurants with meals under $50 that you can visit after you attend the coffee festival.
Address: 10 Bayfront Ave, Singapore 018956, Sands Expo & Convention Centre, Hall C, Level 1
Event hours: 10am to 8pm
Website

Feature image adapted from Singapore Coffee Week and Borderless Coffee

Deli Hub Catering has been suspended after 53 people at two MOE kindergartens, 51 of them students, fell ill with gastroenteritis symptoms, under a joint release from the Singapore Food Agency , the Communicable Diseases Agency and MOE on Tuesday (27 October). The suspension of the caterer’s premises at 30B Quality Road took effect that day and runs until further notice, with transmission suspected to be ongoing.
Photo: Singapore Food Agency
Two kindergartens affected
The 51 students and two staff members developed symptoms between 21 and 23 October after eating food supplied by the caterer. They sought outpatient treatment, took their own medication or recovered without treatment. None were hospitalised.
The cases were at MOE Kindergarten @ Springdale at 71 Anchorvale Link in Sengkang and MOE Kindergarten @ Gongshang at 1 Tampines Street 42. MOE is working with the Communicable Diseases Agency, SFA and the kindergartens on the investigation. Deli Hub Catering had been engaged by the Kindergarten Care (KCare) operator at both sites, and the operator has arranged another food supplier.
What the caterer must do
Before it can resume, Deli Hub Catering must clean and sanitise its premises, equipment and utensils. All food workers must re-attend and pass the Food Safety Course Level 1 and test negative for foodborne pathogens.
The appointed food hygiene officer must re-attend and pass the Food Safety Course Level 3 before returning to duty. Both kindergartens have stepped up hygiene and precautionary measures, including thorough cleaning and disinfection of the affected areas.
Fined in 2023
The caterer was fined S$4,000 in September 2023 after 21 people fell ill from its food in 2022. SFA found lapses then that included a dirty freezer, unclean food preparation containers and empty paper towel dispensers.
Members of the public who come across poor food safety practices are advised not to patronise such outlets and to report them through SFA’s online feedback form. SFA warned that it will take firm action against breaches of the Environmental Public Health Act.
summary: Deli Hub Catering was suspended from 27 October after 51 students and two staff at two MOE kindergartens developed gastroenteritis symptoms, under a joint SFA, CDA and MOE release.
title: Deli Hub Catering suspended from 27 October after 53 fall ill at two MOE kindergartens

Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Riverview is serving a Christmas Brunch at The Best Brew with local oat milk brand OATSIDE, from 21 November 2026 to 3 January 2027. It runs every Saturday and Sunday from 11am to 3pm and costs S$32.80++ per adult and S$18.80++ per child aged 6 to 12.
Image: Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Riverview
What is in the brunch
The buffet has more than 24 favourites, plus one freshly prepared à la carte main per guest and a selection of OATSIDE creations. Traditional dishes include Baked Turkey with Cranberry Sauce and Honey Baked Ham with Apple Sauce, alongside Scrambled Eggs, Crispy Bacon, Garlic Chicken Sausage, Baked Beans, Ratatouille, Baked Cheese Cauliflower and Tater Tots. A DIY Yoghurt Bar and Fresh Fruit Platters round out the lighter side.
Image: Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Riverview
Desserts include Ondeh Ondeh Cake, Royal Chocolate Cake, New York Cheesecake, Apple Crumble Tart and Assorted Cookies. For the à la carte main, guests choose between Beef Pie with Mash and Salad or Vongole Pasta.
The OATSIDE collaboration
The hotel uses OATSIDE’s Barista Blend, Chocolate and Matcha Oat Latte flavours in selected dishes and drinks. On the savoury side, there are a Chicken Ragout with Baguette and a Carbonara made with oat milk. Bread Pudding and Assorted Panna Cotta on the buffet also use OATSIDE.
Image: Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Riverview
Three drinks complete the collaboration: an iced Apple Pie Oat Latte, an iced Strawberry Matcha Oat Latte and a Hot Chocolate made with OATSIDE Chocolate oat milk. Any of them can be added to the buffet for S$6++, or ordered à la carte at S$10.80++ each.
Image: Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Riverview
Ah Pui Teochew Porridge Buffet

Sweet items include Assorted Japanese Mochi, Traditional Log Cake, Durian Pengat and Soft Serve Ice Cream.

Thanying at Amara Singapore is hosting a two-night four-hands dinner, A Gust of Snow, on 27 and 28 November 2026. Chef Chia Wee Loon, known as Chef Snow, of private dining concept Snowcology cooks alongside Thanying Head Chef Tamawat Itthipornwithool, known as Chef Gust.
Image: Thanying
Two chefs, one menu
The name is a nod to the chefs’ names. Thanying has served royal Thai cuisine since 1988, and Chef Gust builds on that heritage with careful preparation, balanced flavours and attention to detail in court-style cooking. Chef Snow brings an imaginative, contemporary approach to cooking and plating.
Chef Gust and Chef Snow in the kitchen. Image: Thanying
The specially curated menu includes each chef’s signature dishes as well as new creations developed only for these two evenings. Diners can look out for Chef Gust’s Fried Stuffed Yam and Chef Snow’s Aged Irish Duck, plus dishes the two chefs created together.
Aged Irish Duck by Chef Snow. Image: Thanying
What the chefs say
Chef Gust said the collaboration lets two perspectives share a kitchen while staying true to the care and thought behind every plate. Chef Snow said he wanted to bring curiosity into the kitchen while drawing on Chef Gust’s experience in royal Thai cuisine, and that some dishes were developed together.
An appetiser from the four-hands menu. Image: Thanying
Key details
• Dates: 27 and 28 November 2026
• Seatings: 6.30pm and 7.30pm each evening
• Price: S$168++ per person
• Venue: Thanying, Amara Singapore
More hotel dining news
Thanying also appeared in our earlier post on the Thanying DBS deal for 20 per cent off the a la carte menu . For another hotel restaurant seasonal menu, see our report on Cherry Garden by Chef Fei’s hairy crab autumn menu .

Starbucks Singapore is kicking off its Christmas season on 28 October, with the Toffee Nut Crunch Latte and Peppermint Mocha returning alongside new Cold Foam Iced Americano drinks. The campaign, called Wrapped in Joy, also marks 30 Years of Shared Moments for Starbucks in Singapore, with special treats promised each week as the year closes.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Festive drinks from 28 October
Two favourites return. The Toffee Nut Crunch Latte has espresso with toffee nut and toasted nut notes, whipped cream and crunchy Toffee Nut topping. It is served hot, iced or as a Frappuccino, and there is a new Toffee Nut Crunch Cold Foam Iced Americano.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
The Peppermint Mocha combines chocolate and peppermint, finished with candy cane sprinkles. It comes hot, iced or as a Frappuccino, and the new Chocolate Cold Foam Iced Peppermint Americano joins the line-up.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
The Christmas beverages are available in-store and via Mobile Order & Pay, Starbucks Delivers and GrabFood from 28 October, and on foodpanda from 4 November. The two new Cold Foam Iced Americano drinks will not be available on delivery platforms.
Christmas food
The seasonal food range is available from 28 October in-store, through Mobile Order & Pay and on Starbucks Delivers, GrabFood and foodpanda. It includes:
• S’mores Cookie, with melted marshmallow and warm chocolate chunks
• Peppermint Chocolate Cake, with chocolate sponge and peppermint-infused cream swirls shaped like a Christmas tree
• Caramel Apple Cheesecake, with spiced apple chunks and golden caramel
Image: Starbucks Singapore
There are also a Snowman Bearista Cookie and a Starbucks Christmas House Cookie, which the brand pitches as gifts or treats to pair with a festive drink.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Merchandise and gifts
The Snowman’s Amazing Day Christmas Collection follows a snowman making friends with woodland animals, with scenes of snowball fights, tree decorating and cafe moments in reds and greens with soft blues and pink accents. It goes on sale on 28 October in-store, on the Starbucks Online Store at 10am and on LazMall at 12pm, while stocks last.
From 4 November, the Party Delight Collection (festive reds and whites, inspired by the dessert course of Christmas dinner) and the Golden Lights Collection (ornament-inspired collectibles with geometric patterns) arrive, along with the nine-piece Holiday Gifting Collection. That collection includes two Singapore-exclusive accessories: a Bearista plush tucked into a pouch and a furry Bearista wristlet pouch. These are sold in-store, on the Online Store at 10am and on LazMall at 12pm, while stocks last.
Five Christmas designs of Starbucks Cards are also available from 28 October, while stocks last.
Key dates
• 28 October 2026: Christmas drinks, food, Snowman’s Amazing Day collection and Christmas Starbucks Cards
• 4 November 2026: foodpanda delivery for Christmas drinks; Party Delight, Golden Lights and Holiday Gifting collections
More from Starbucks Singapore
Catch up on the Winnie the Pooh collection and Black Cat Frappuccino and Starbucks Singapore’s autumn drop .

Tablescape Restaurant & Bar at Grand Park City Hall has unveiled its Christmas 2026 collection, a mix of a four-course dinner in its neoclassical dining room, two reimagined log cakes and Festive Celebration Sets for gatherings at home. The festive dinner runs from 2 December to 1 January, from 6.30pm to 9pm.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
The Festive Four-Course Dinner
The dinner costs S$98++ per guest. Each diner picks two starters, one main course and one dessert from a contemporary European menu.
The starters are Burrata with heirloom tomatoes and shaved melon, a Foie Gras Duo of pan-seared foie gras and mousse with beetroot, cocoa and salted chocolate, and Boston Lobster with charred onion, garden leaves and Avruga caviar.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Mains include Sea Perch, cooked sous-vide and wrapped in savoy cabbage with charred leeks, mussels and a bonito-onion emulsion, and a Roasted Turkey Roulade with potato mousseline, smoked bacon and asparagus. There is also a Josper-grilled Wagyu Beef Tenderloin with shallot confit, pumpkin fondant and tenderstem broccoli, and a vegetarian Truffle Courgette Risotto.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Dessert is the Coffee & Coconut Cloud, a coffee-coconut mousse with crisp meringue and candy floss, finished tableside with a spray of gold dust.
Two log cakes and a cheese board
The takeaway range includes two log cakes, each 1kg and serving 8 to 10 people:
• Santa’s Secret Rum & Kunafa Log, S$98, takes its cue from Dubai chocolate with crisp chocolate kunafa layered against moist chocolate sponge and a rum note
• Frosty’s Osmanthus & Yam Log, S$88, pairs osmanthus pear confiture with vanilla sponge, white chocolate mousse and Japanese yam filling
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Completing The Sweet Bar is the Charcuterie Cheese Yuletide Board at S$68, with cured hams, mortadella and salami, bleu, Asiago and Brie cheeses, marmalade and candy canes.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Festive Celebration Sets for home
Two sets are available. The S$228 set serves 6 to 8 people and includes two starters, one main, two sides and one log cake. The S$280 set serves 8 to 10 people and has three starters, one main, three sides and one log cake.
Starters include the Charcuterie Cheese Yuletide Platter, Snowy Burrata & Prosciutto di Parma, Rudolph’s Savoury Beef Meatballs made with Wagyu beef, and Golden Crown King Prawns with mango-spiced salsa and chickpeas. Mains are Roasted Festive Turkey, Holly Jolly Salmon Wellington, Honey-Glazed Gammon Ham and Prime Angus Beef Roast in striploin or ribeye, at about 2.5kg.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Sides include Mac & Cheese, oven-roasted ratte potatoes, glazed chestnuts with pecans, grilled vegetables with almonds, edamame with bacon and buttery Brussels sprouts. Each set comes with a choice of either log cake. Takeaway orders can be placed on the restaurant’s online store.
Key details
• Festive dinner: 2 December 2026 to 1 January 2027, 6.30pm to 9pm, S$98++ per guest
• Venue: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar, Level 3, Grand Park City Hall, 10 Coleman Street, Singapore 179809

Comparing options? See our guide to Christmas log cakes 2026 at voco Orchard, Fullerton and Holiday Inn Atrium , and the list of hotel Christmas turkey takeaways with early-bird discounts . Tablescape also featured in our Tablescape mooncakes 2026 guide .

Yes, you read that right. My colleague, Rachel and I were hit by major food coma after visiting OVER , competitive eater Zermatt Neo’s first-ever restaurant venture over at 54 Tras Street . Officially opening to the public on 28 Oct 2026 , this shophouse space will allow diners to experience over-the-top massive portions that are meant to be shared. So, what kind of cuisine are we looking at here? Think Asian fusion, with familiar, hearty flavours.
Credit – comeove_r via Instagram
Partnering with lifestyle and entertainment group, The Wolfpack Investment Holdings, Zermatt wanted OVER to be a restaurant that serves generous portions and possess a playful spirit. OVER is the table he had always wanted, with big plates, loud convos, and a friendly fight over the paiseh piece of chicken wing or spring roll.
Right off the bat, the menu gives you a choice of your portion size — Lesser (1 pax) or Standard (3 pax). Do note that the following pictures that you see are just teasers aka tasting portions that doesn’t depict the actual portion size.
The Rolling Over Wakame (S$10/S$18) is a vegetarian spring roll appetiser that comes with wakame salad and sesame dressing, drizzled with a tangy house-made glaze. A Belly Good Time (S$15/S$28) consists of sliced pork belly that’s layered with aromatic shiso leaves and topped with crispy chilli. The sauce on the pork reminded me of lor bak and its robustness unfortunately masked the flavour of the shiso leaves. I also wished that the pork belly was a little softer. Thankfully, the fiery but crunchy chilli clusters saved the day.
One of my favourites was the Shoryu -Clams! (S$35/S$68) that had scrumptious white clams and earthy mushrooms, all bathed in a rich buttery shoyu sauce. It even comes with a slice of sourdough to mop up all that lovely gravy. Another top pick was the Wing Me Over (S$10 for 6 pieces , S$28 for 18 pieces) . Indulge in crispy and juicy wings that come with your choice of house sauce — buffalo dashi , nam pla , or wasabi soy ginger. We dunked the wings into the wasabi soy ginger and though there wasn’t a spicy kick, the soy ginger concoction was robust enough to completely change the wing’s flavour profile in a lovely way.
For mains, we savoured the Somen Like You (S$28/S$54) . I was surprised that the somen , tossed in nanban and savoury soy sauce, looked more like linguine . However, ignore what I just said because I LOVED its chewy texture and fiery kick. It’s accompanied by crispy chicken cutlet, egg mayo, and fresh scallions. The Curry Me Over (S$23/S$44) comes with a crispy red snapper fillet, Nyonya achar , and fragrant Hom Mali rice. To me, the curry felt a little grainy and I wished they would have strained or mixed it more thoroughly.
We also loved the exclusive Over Jett (S$28/S$54) burger that’s launched in collaboration with Jett Barbecue . Available at OVER till 30 Nov 2026 , this decadent burger is stuffed with beef cheek, deep-fried chicken, crispy onion rings, eggs, and a creamy mayo dressing.
Diners with appetites and stomach capacities as formidable as Zermatt Neo, are you up for a challenge? OVER introduces the Ultimate Food Challenge , where 3 dishes on the menu bearing the 8kg Challenge label must be eaten within a strict 1-hour time limit . Contenders can take up the challenge solo or in teams of up to 4 people . Successful participants will secure bragging rights and a permanent spot on OVER’s official Hall of Fame. These are the dishes:
• Wing Me Over (S$239)
• A Belly Good Time (S$269)
• Over Jett (S$469)
So, if you don’t mind being OVERfed or having food coma, come with an empty stomach to OVER at Tanjong Pagar with your family or friends.
10 best wallet-friendly Japanese hawker stalls in Singapore
summary: OVER, competitive eater Zermatt Neo’s first restaurant venture at 54 Tras Street, opens on 28 October 2026 with Asian fusion dishes in generous portions designed for sharing. Diners can choose between single-person and three-person servings, while those seeking a greater challenge can attempt three 8kg food challenges within an hour, solo or in teams of up to four. It suits groups seeking hearty meals and competitive eating experiences.
title: We left Zermatt Neo’s 1st restaurant venture with major food coma

The HomePage @ Causeway Point
If you’re someone who spends hours wandering through niche bookstores in Singapore or are always on the lookout for new places to chill without spending a fortune, here’s something to look forward to.
In 2028, you’ll have a new hangout spot in Woodlands where you can curl up with a good book, catch a film, or simply spend time with your friends.
Dubbed The HomePage @ Causeway Point , this upcoming social and reading space is a collaboration between Frasers Centrepoint Trust and the National Library & Archives Board (NLB) . Here’s everything we know so far.
What is The Homepage @ Causeway Point all about?
Artist’s impression of the revamped Causeway Point.
Image credit: Frasers Property
When it opens in 2028 , The Homepage @ Causeway Point will boast a 32,000sqft space featuring books, community spaces, and activities for everyone of any age. It will span Levels 6 and 7 of Causeway Point, with communal areas for book reading, rest, and recreation.
It’s part of the 2027-2029 revamp of Causeway Point, after which the mall is expected to have close to 250 stores, refreshed dining and retail offerings, upgraded facilities, and new amenities.
So, even if you’re not much of a reader, there’ll be more reasons to visit Causeway Point once the revamp is complete.
What can I expect at The HomePage @ Causeway Point?
Communal social areas featuring heritage- inspired designs
Image credit: Frasers Property
Unlike your typical library, where you might feel compelled to keep your voice down, The HomePage is designed to be a space where reading and socialising meet .
And the best part? Visitors will be able to enjoy food and drinks within the community reading space, making it a potential spot for an afternoon of reading over a cuppa coffee.
Image credit: Frasers Property
The design will also pay tribute to Singapore’s heritage, with architectural elements inspired by the colourful HDB blocks in Teck Whye, the former Stamford Road National Library, and Singapore’s Brutalist architecture from the 1970s.
Browse & take home pre-loved books for free
Image credit: Frasers Property
Here’s arguably the highlight for bookworms: you’ll be able to take home pre-loved books f or free , without going through the usual borrowing process. The HomePage will house one of Singapore’s largest publicly accessible collections of pre-loved books from NLB’s libraries, with titles available in English and Mother Tongue languages.
These books also won’t have to be returned by a due date. Instead, visitors are encouraged to pass on books they’ve finished reading so that others can enjoy them too. We think this is a pretty neat way of helping to give old books a new lease of life.
Dedicated space for Singapore literature
Image credit: Frasers Property
Sing Lit lovers won’t be left out either, as The HomePage will feature an extensive showcase of Singaporean literature and local authors .
Catch film screenings, author talks & storytelling sessions
Image credit: Frasers Property
There’s more to The HomePage than just books. An indoor theatre and screening space will also host activities such as film screenings , author talks , storytelling sessions , and cultural programmes .
Families with little ones can also look forward to children’s play zones and interactive experiences , making this a potential family-friendly pit stop during weekend mall outings.
Look forward to The HomePage @ Causeway Point opening in 2028
Most of us know the struggle of having to talk in whispers in libraries, or mischievously sneak food in to fuel up for long study or reading sessions. With The HomePage’s opening, we’ll be getting not only a library we’re encouraged to chat in, but also one we can happily eat in. Best of all, they’ll never fine us for the late return of books.
So while 2028 might seem a little far off, the idea of a library experience like no other will keep us counting down till the day it opens.
More things to look forward to:
• Everything we know about the upcoming Woodlands Gateway
• Super Nintendo World to open at USS
• The Greater Southern Waterfront transformation
Cover image adapted from: Frasers Property
summary: Unlike an actual library, you’re free to enjoy food and drinks while reading your book.
title: A New Social & Reading Space With Free Books Is Opening At Causeway Point – Here’s What We Know So Far

Punggol ActiveSG Gym at the Punggol Regional Sports Centre
Punggol residents, your next workout spot has just launched, and there’s a bonus for your wallet too. The new Punggol ActiveSG Gym is now open, with free entry till 31st October 2026 . While the long-awaited Punggol Regional Sports Centre is only expected to officially open by the end of 2026, you can get a head start on your fitness goals at the gym in the meantime.
Spacious gym with a variety of workout equipment
View this post on Instagram
The new gym offers a spacious workout area filled with a variety of gym equipment, such as treadmills , weights , stationary bikes , rowing machines , and stair climbers .
Screenshot from: Instagram
Comments on social media have also pointed out how big the space looks, with the layout seemingly well thought out to accommodate gym-goers. This means you’ll get to work through your sets without feeling too cramped, while still having space to wait for your turn at a machine.
Get your reps in while enjoying scenic views
View this post on Instagram
Located on Level 2 of the Punggol Regional Sports Centre, the gym also comes with a pretty nice view to keep you company while working out. Floor-to-ceiling windows line the area where the treadmills and stationary bikes are placed, so you can catch views of the surrounding greenery while getting your cardio in.
Image adapted from: @tommyczw & @yx._.mohae via Instagram
There’s even a view of the infinity pool on Level 1, giving you something scenic to look at when you’re starting to feel the burn; having a view like this might just make those extra minutes on the treadmill feel more bearable.
Free entry from now till 31st October 2026
Screenshot from: ActiveSG
According to the ActiveSG website, entry to the Punggol ActiveSG Gym is free till 31st October 2026 . The gym is open daily from 7am to 10pm , making it easy to squeeze in a session before work or after knocking off.
Don’t worry even if you miss the free-entry period, because the standard rates are wallet-friendly too. Adults who are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents pay just $2.50/entry , while students and senior citizens enjoy an even lower rate of $1.50/entry . Looks like your fitness goals don’t have to come with an expensive gym membership after all.
Squeeze in a workout while the rest of the sports centre gets ready to open
Image credit: Mokkie Mok via Google Maps

body:
133 Penang Authentic has cheap Penang food in Bukit Timah
Being half-Malaysian on my mom’s side, I’m usually sceptical about Malaysian food in Singapore, thinking it can never beat the real deal across the border. We’ll never settle the debate on Singaporean vs Malaysian food, but when I came across 133 Penang Authentic at Bukit Timah Interim Market & Food Centre, I had to put my theory to the test.
Before diving into the food, this humble hawker stall boasts quite a background. Founder and chef Gary Tan spent 10 years as an executive chef at top hotels such as Marriott and Dynasty. Trained in Western, French, and Peranakan cuisines, he’s won accolades at competitions across Asia. After two decades in fine dining, he shifted to hawker life, running 133 Penang Authentic with his wife for nearly 20 years.
All in all, he’s spent over 40 years in the food industry. When asked why he’s stayed so long, he simply attributed it to his passion for cooking. Intrigued by his decorated past, we had to see if the food lives up to the name.
Food At 133 Penang Authentic
My scepticism faded when I learned that Chef Gary and his wife, Constance, were both from Penang. Their signature dish is the Penang Char Kway Teow (from $5.50) , fried by Chef Gary himself in a massive wok.
Penang-style char kway teow features a lighter colour and milder flavour profile, unlike its Singaporean counterpart, which is darker in colour and doused in a sweet, dark soya sauce. Penang char kway teow is also known as the “white” version, and I enjoy it as it’s lighter on the palate.
As soon as it was fried up and served, I could smell the smoky aroma. True enough, it did have a strong wok hei that any good char kway teow should have. The noodles were springy, with each strand having a nice char from the wok.
There were generous amounts of liao found throughout the dish, with my favourite hum in abundance. The lup cheong was cut into small bite-sized pieces, making it easier to chew, while the tau gay was juicy and plump, adding a nice crunch alongside the crispy pork lard.
As someone with a high spice tolerance, I would have preferred it slightly spicier or served with some chilli, but it was a good plate nonetheless—I do think it’s as close to the original as it gets.
The other two dishes we ordered were cooked by Aunty Constance, and I was most excited to try the Assam Laksa ($6) as this dish is hard to come by in Singapore. Right off the bat, the broth had a brighter, more orange hue than the Penang version, which tends to be a darker red.
Our bowl came packed with ingredients, including mackerel, onions, and mint leaves. The mackerel had a salty taste, which helped cut through the sour broth. The mint leaves gave off a floral note, adding another layer of flavour in every slurp.
For the broth, it had a distinct sour and pungent aroma, though it tasted more savoury than sour. My guess is that they tweaked the recipe to suit a more local palate, but as a true Assam laksa fan, I thought the broth could be slightly spicier for that shiok kick.
It’s also served with the usual thick and slippery noodles, AKA lai fun, so I’d recommend eating it the traditional way: scooping up both the noodles and broth with a spoon to prevent unwanted mess and stains.
Moving on to the Penang Prawn Noodle (from $5) . We bought the soup version, as that’s the way it’s usually served in Penang. As a prawn mee fan, I’m happy to report that the broth was rich in umami and boasted a natural sweetness from the prawns.
Just like the other two dishes, it came loaded with ingredients, including succulent prawns and chunky pork slices.
You can’t go wrong with the classic bee hoon and yellow mee combo, which made for a massive noodle pull. Both were cooked to a QQ texture and topped with lard and a tasty sambal, which added a hint of spice when mixed with the broth. This tasted close to how I remember Penang prawn mee to be.
I particularly liked the crunchy fried onions and kang kong, which gave the dish more texture.
Ambience at 133 Penang Authentic
Image credit: Scribbling Geek via Google Maps
133 Penang Authentic is tucked in the corner of Bukit Timah Interim Market and Food Centre. We were greeted with a fairly quiet space as we arrived after peak hours, though there was still a steady stream of customers. As with any other hawker centre, it’s best to come early to avoid the lunch crowd.
Space-wise, the aisles between tables and the shops are quite narrow. Though it was breezy on the day we visited, the food centre is also equipped with fans for hotter days.
The food centre is a short three-minute walk from Beauty World MRT Station .
133 Penang Authentic – Eatbook Review
…
summary: 133 Penang Authentic in Bukit Timah has been run by award-winning chef Gary Tan and his wife for nearly 20 years.
title: This Award-Winning Chef Sells Penang CKT And Prawn Mee At Beauty World: Here’s Our Verdict

body:
Mollie Makes is a new Chinese dessert cafe in Johor Bahru
One of my favourite things to do in JB is to go dessert cafe hopping . I love travelling from matcha cafes to artisanal bakeries in search of sweet treats to satisfy my sweet tooth. Recently, I discovered Mollie Makes , a new cafe near customs serving Chinese desserts with a contemporary twist. If you’re looking for another spot to add to your JB itinerary, this one’s worth checking out.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.31 as of 27 October 2026.
15 Best Dessert Spots In JB For Matcha Cakes, Black Sesame Shaved Ice And More
The cafe boasts a rustic Chinese look with traditional motifs and wooden furniture that’ll send you back to Season One of The Rise of Phoenixes . There are plenty of photo spots, so be sure to get your camera ready.
As aesthetic as the spot may be, they didn’t skimp on the quality of the desserts either. You can expect a wide variety of Chinese desserts, ranging from traditional classics to modern variants.
As a pistachio fanatic , their Pistachio Beancurd Mochi (RM15.90) was basically calling my name. Imagine a bowl filled generously with pistachio-flavoured tau huay, topped with stretchy mochi and cheese foam, then garnished with chopped pistachios.
This bowl met my rather high standards for pistachio desserts: it had prominent earthy, umami pistachio flavours, without being too sweet. The mochi also added a nice textural contrast—soft and stretchy with an indulgent milky taste. The cheese foam tied the whole dessert together, adding a subtle saltiness that offset the sweetness.
My dining companion preferred the Oh Yeah! Mollie (RM14.90) , comprising a base of coconut jelly piled high with toppings, including coconut milk he fen AKA Chinese wide noodles, rose-infused chestnuts, and fresh mango cubes. It’s then finished with a heaping scoop of coconut ice cream and a sprinkle of toasted coconut.
This dessert can be described in one word: refreshing. The coconut jelly is QQ and jiggly, and reminded me of the Chinese dessert bing fen.
The coconut ice cream, on the other hand, was soft and creamy. The fragrant coconut flavour was further accentuated by the coconut he fen, which tasted very similar to actual coconut meat.
The fresh mangoes were also slightly sour, cutting through the richness of the dessert, while the rose-infused chestnuts provided a nice crunch.
To wash everything down, we ordered the Taro Milk Tea With Mochi (RM15.80) , comprising Assam milk tea zhnged up with taro paste and handmade mochi, finished with a layer of cheese foam.
If you’re an orh nee lover , this drink is basically tailor-made for you. The Assam milk tea base was quite light and fragrant, allowing the stronger-tasting yam paste to come through. The mochi also added a nice bite: it was soft and slightly chewy, making it feel more like a dessert than a drink.
Interestingly, the dessert cafe offers a lineup of fresh shio pan. We ordered their Mentaiko Shio Pan (RM8.90) , and surprisingly, it could rival my favourite salt breads. It had a crunchy, buttery base, with a soft and chewy middle, and was garnished with mentaiko mayo, seaweed, and a slab of creamy Kewpie mayonnaise.
That’s not all: the bread is split lengthwise and slathered with more creamy mentaiko mayo for added umami.
Mollie Makes is located a seven-minute drive away from CIQ Jalan Jim Quee .
For more places to tick off your JB cafe checklist, read our guide to the best cafes in Johor Bahru . Alternatively, if you have no idea on where to start, our JB food itinerary might lead you in the right direction.
Address: 30 Jalan Dhoby, Bandar Johor Bahru, 80000 Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 8pm
Website
Mollie Makes is not halal-certified.

Its offering covers hair design, colour, texture control, anti-frizz treatments, scalp care, head spa experiences and nail services.
The group has also received industry recognition including the Asia Honesty Enterprise Award , Asia Pacific Super Health Brand , and International Prestige Brand Award , reflecting its stated focus on quality, professionalism, service excellence and consumer trust. Bali in Singapore? Never heard of it. Welcome to Wheeler’s Tropikana ; your next summer paradise is closer than you think.
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana’s Facebook
Palms and lush greenery frame an open, al fresco dining area, with rattan seating, a sunny lawn, and a dipping pool at the centre. It feels more like a Bali retreat than a Singapore restaurant.
Brunch
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana’s Facebook
Wheeler’s Tropikana offer the kind of menu you’d expect poolside on holiday: relaxed, flavourful, and easy to graze through all afternoon. Not sure about you, but my kind of brunch calls for Omelette au Fromage (S$18) and the Pastrami Panini (S$24) . Prefer a heartier and messier kind of breakie ? The Salmon Benny (S$26) or Egg Florentine (S$24) might be your cup of tea, and it’s great for sharing.
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana
Wheeler’s Tropikana also serves Kombucha on Tap for S$8 per glass – Strawberry Mint, Pink Guava, and Raspberry Passionfruit. Apart from that, there’s also a Weekend Bottomless Brunch happening every Saturday and Sunday , from 11am to 4pm, priced at S$68++ for 2 hours of free-flow drinks – Red, White, Rosé, or Beer on tap.
Dinner
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana’s Facebook
Not a morning person? Come for slower afternoons with refreshing cocktails – Lychee or Apple Martini (S$15) and Long Island Iced Tea (S$19) , or knock yourself out with their Cocktail Jug for S$48 , with 2 kinds to choose from. Wheeler’s Tropikana is the kind of place where one drink turns into an evening. Catch the sunset with their fresh Summer Caprese (S$26) and indulge in pizza and pasta .
For a sociable evening with a bigger group, order a Rack of Lamb (S$48) with smoked tomato salsa and their special Jeju Pork Tomahawk (S$60) with charred leeks. Pair these proteins with sides of Broccolini (S$12) and Roasted Carrots (S$12) with tahini yoghurt on the side for dipping. For the crust, we can trust their Artichoke & Parma (S$26) and the Good Ole Marg (S$22) – a pizza that never goes wrong.
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana’s Facebook
Come for the food, stay for a good time, then linger for evening live music and DJs on certain nights. Make your retreat-worthy reservations here today!

Snoopy , Charlie Brown , and their friends are pop culture icons that have existed in my mind for as long as I can remember. Even though I’m not personally a fan of Peanuts , its characters have always popped up in my sight once in a while on TV, in a cafe somewhere, or on a shelf in a toy store.
Well, from 27 October 2026 to 19 September 2027 , this beloved gang is going to stay in our minds for a while with the Snoopy Pop-up Library at Plaza Singapura !
My colleague and I dropped by to check out the space and felt like we stepped into the world of Peanuts . If you’re a Snoopy fan or a parent who wants to spark your child’s interest in reading , you’ll love it even more!
Peanuts Brought to Life
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
The first thing you will notice at this pop-up is reading corners inspired by classic Peanuts comic strips and scenes . I had almost forgotten that these characters first existed in newspapers, but it’s nice to see this pop-up paying homage to their origins.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
You can visit a familiar bus stop , hop onto the Peanuts School Bus for a photo with Snoopy, hang out at the Snoopy Garden , or read some books with the friendly beagle in Charlie Brown’s Classroom .
If you’re a Peanuts fan, you will have fun spotting references and also find how they are incorporated into the library charming and fitting.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Some of you might be wondering whether this pop-up is only for kids and their parents. Good news for all the adult Snoopy fans – it’s not! A huge part of the library, made up of about 10,000 physical and digital books , is catered to children. However, there is also a collection suitable for all ages .
Visitors will discover popular Peanuts titles, as well as other books specially curated by the National Library & Archives Board (NLB) .
Lucy’s Book Recommendations
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
If you’re spoilt for choice and need some book recommendations, head over to Lucy’s Booth . Simply answer a few fun questions to find the perfect book for you. Fortunately, consulting Lucy is completely free of charge (not even 5 cents), and you can even print out your Reading Prescription in the form of a physical bookmark !
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
These bookmarks contain personalised recommendations based on your mood (answers) and will even direct you to parts of the library where you can find them. At the same time, they double as keepsakes that will remind you of your time at the Snoopy Library and inspire you to
summary: We stepped into the world of Peanuts at this Snoopy Pop-up Library that just opened at Plaza Singapura. Inner child activated.
