If trimming the guest list is one of the first things on your wedding agenda, you’re in luck. Some of the best small wedding venues in Singapore prove that fewer guests doesn’t have to mean fewer bells and whistles. In fact, swapping a cavernous ballroom for a private dining room, rooftop or garden can make it much easier to actually spend time with everyone you invited.
We’ve done the venue scouting for you, with options for proper micro weddings of 25 or 30 guests, celebrations around the 50-person mark and slightly larger receptions that still feel personal. So if you’re hunting for small wedding venues for 50 to 100 guests in Singapore, consider this your shortlist. Or, peep our list of larger wedding venues in Singapore for more full-on celebrations.
1. Four Seasons Hotel Singapore
Photography: Four Seasons Hotel Singapore
For a five-star hotel wedding minus the sprawling ballroom, head straight for the top floor of Four Seasons Hotel Singapore. Windows East and Windows West sit on level 20, two elegant and intimate wedding venues with floor-to-ceiling windows boasting sweeping city views. Both also come with a private outdoor patio – a nice little change of scene for pre-dinner drinks and photos.
Each 101-square metre (1,087-square foot) venue accommodates up to 100 guests, with banquet seating for 60, and receptions for 80. Curate an individually plated six-course lunch or seven-course dinner from Michelin-selected Jiang-Nan Chun, including its signature mesquite wood-roasted Peking duck. Floral arrangements, wedding favours, and a one-night stay are included in the package, too.
For those who prefer their celebrations more convivial, Nobu, Jiang Nan-Chun and One-Ninety Restaurant also offer buy-out options for small weddings and solemnisation ceremonies in Singapore.
Best for: An intimate five-star hotel wedding with city views
Capacity: Up to 100 pax at Windows East and Windows West (60 pax for banquet, 80 pax for receptions). Up to 130 pax at Nobu; up to 120 pax at Jiang Nan-Chun; up to 80 pax at One-Ninety Restaurant
Price: From $238++ per pax for Windows East and Windows West, from $7000 for restaurant buy-outs
Address: Four Seasons Hotel Singapore , 190 Orchard Boulevard, Singapore 248646
2. Flutes
Photography: Flutes
If your idea of a wedding reception looks more like an elegant dinner party than a traditional banquet, bookmark Flutes. The longstanding fine-dining restaurant has moved into Midtown House on Beach Road, where its current home pairs heritage architecture with polished dining rooms and private spaces. Weddings can take the form of a solemnisation, lunch or dinner, with this small wedding venue in Singapore accommodating up to 90 guests.
The beauty here is that you don’t necessarily have to take over the entire restaurant. Flutes specifically offers smaller private-room and designated-area configurations for more intimate receptions, making it suitable for couples who would rather spend the evening over good food and wine than build an elaborate wedding programme around a ballroom stage.
Best for: An elegant restaurant wedding centred around food and wine
Capacity: Up to 90 pax
Price: From $236.10 per pax
Address: Flutes , 120 Beach Road, #01-02 Midtown House, Singapore 189769
3. The Summerhouse
Photography: The Summerhouse
Ballroom carpets and chandeliers not up your street? Take the party outside. The Summerhouse in Seletar is built around a heritage house and leafy grounds, giving couples a mix of indoor and outdoor spaces. We’d consider this for a late-afternoon ceremony, especially if greenery features heavily on your Pinterest board.
For a verdant small wedding venue in Singapore, the garden solemnisation is set up for 50 guests, while the courtyard accommodates up to 80. You can then move indoors for the meal, and useful wedding-day basics such as a bridal room, sound system, projector and microphones are available too.
Best for: A romantic and lush garden wedding
Capacity: Up to 50 pax for a garden solemnisation; up to 80 pax in the courtyard
Price: Enquire for a quote
Address: The Summerhouse , 3 Park Lane, Singapore 798387
4. Vineyard at Hortpark
Photography: Vineyard at Hortpark
Garden wedding dreams, Singapore humidity concerns – we hear you. Vineyard at HortPark gives you several ways to stage the perfect small wedding in Singapore. The outdoor patio works for vows and pre-dinner drinks, while the verandah keeps the greenery within your photo ops but adds air-conditioning. The latter seats up to 60 guests, while the indoor dining hall accommodates 86.

Things to do at Jewel Changi Airport
Jewel Changi Airport needs no introduction. Locals and visitors flock over in droves for that million-dollar shot with the famous Rain Vortex in the background. And not to mention, the mall is chock-full of delish grub, tempting stores, lush greenery, and of course, attractions that can keep you entertained for hours.
Trust us when we say – there’s a lot to cover. So here’s a comprehensive guide to all you can do at Jewel Changi Airport .
– Indoor garden spaces –
We don’t flaunt our Garden City status for nothing, and it only makes sense that one of the first few places tourists set foot in upon reaching Singapore reflects that reputation. Like all terminals in the airport, Jewel Changi is full of green spaces for that extra calming aura.
1. Rain Vortex
Be mesmerised by the tallest indoor waterfall in the world
Your Skytrain might cruise through this area, depending on which terminal you’re headed to.
Perhaps the most prominent green feature of Jewel Changi is its Forest Valley , which is stacked with trellis upon trellis of different trees and shrubs. And right at the centre of it all is the massive Rain Vortex , the tallest indoor waterfall in the world. The falls rain down 40m from Level 5 all the way to B1, and despite being artificial, it’s a sight to behold nonetheless.
Image credit: @blackminusgreen via Instagram
Come night, and you’ll be treated to a magical light-and-sound show, with rainbow-coloured animations projected on the wall of water itself. The Rain Vortex light show happens at 8pm and 9pm from Monday to Thursday, and at 8pm, 9pm, and 10pm from Friday to Sunday and on public holidays.
Occasionally, there’ll also be special, themed light shows based on big events happening on the Little Red Dot. A Disney Cruise one recently played here earlier this year, and December will see a BTS-themed takeover of the man-made marvel.
Note: The floor surrounding the Rain Vortex is usually wet due to the mist, so be careful not to slip and fall.
2. Forest Valley
Indoor “forest” decorated with over 900 trees & 60,000 shrubs
For a better view of the gorgeous Rain Vortex, you can climb up the Forest Valley stairs to reach an ideal vantage point. As you ascend surrounded by shrubbery and smaller water features, you’ll feel as though you’re taking a hike outdoors – minus the humid weather. Yup, you don’t have to worry about breaking a sweat here as temperatures are a comfortable 23°C.
To best enjoy the walking trails, it is advisable to wear comfortable flat shoes instead of heels as there are numerous steps to climb.
The entire Forest Valley is full of lush, leafy backdrops. Look out for the mini bamboo grove on the lowest floor of the Valley, where you can snap pics to bluff your friends that you’re in Japan .
– Canopy Park –
The top floor of Jewel Changi is where you’ll find the Canopy Park , which is less of a park and more of a giant playground that both kids and adults will find thrilling. Think bouncy nets to play on, flower gardens to walk through, and even mazes to get lost in.
Do note that general admission into the Canopy Park is from $6/pax for Singapore Residents and $8 for everyone else, and covers only the Discovery Slides, Foggy Bowls, Petal Garden, and Topiary Walk. The rest of the attractions have a separate charge, which includes admission to Canopy Park as well.

body:
Bukit Panjang finally has its own Sushiro. The Japanese conveyor-belt chain’s newest outlet sits on the second floor of Bukit Panjang Plaza, and it comes with two weeks of 1-for-1 sushi and S$6++ drinks to pull in the neighbourhood. If you live in the north-west and have been taking the bus to Lot One in Choa Chu Kang or Causeway Point in Woodlands for your salmon plates, this one is for you.
The grand opening deals run from 30 October to 12 November. Image: Sushiro Singapore
What the grand opening deals cover
The opening promotion runs from 30 October to 12 November. Sushi goes 1-for-1, and the second portion arrives on the same plate rather than as a separate plate on the belt, so one plate carries double the sushi. Ask the staff which plates are in the deal on the day you go.
Three drinks drop to S$6++ each for the same two weeks:
• Lemon sour, usually S$8++
• Suntory The Premium Malt’s draught beer, usually S$10.50++
• Kaku highball, usually S$9++
The sure-win gachapon for diners spending S$50 or more was an opening-day special on 30 October only, so that one has come and gone.
The second part of Sushiro’s October limited menu runs until 3 November. Image: Sushiro Singapore
The limited menu running alongside
Bukit Panjang opens in the middle of the second part of Sushiro’s October limited menu, which runs at every outlet until 3 November while stocks last. The headline plates are the Miyako salmon trout taste and compare from Japan’s Sanriku Rias coast at S$2.90++ and a fatty swordfish at S$2.90++.
The rest of the line-up leans on soy sauce koji, a fermented seasoning of soy sauce and koji, across four fish:
• Soy sauce koji fresh salmon, S$2.90++
• Soy sauce koji engawa, S$2.30++
• Soy sauce koji yellowtail, S$3.90++
• Soy sauce koji red snapper, S$4.90++
Pufferfish fans get two fugu plates at S$4.90++ each, and the bancha braised octopus uses Hokkaido mizudako at S$3.90++. Prices differ at the Digiro outlet in Mandai Wildlife Reserve.
Tuna, ikura, unagi and salmon from Sushiro’s regular menu. Photo: Sushiro Singapore
Where Sushiro goes next
Bukit Panjang is the first of three new Sushiro outlets on the calendar. Great World follows at the end of November at #01-112/113/114, and Funan comes next in early December at #02-16. Taste Orchard, on the other hand, has closed for good, which leaves Wisma Atria, Isetan Scotts and Orchard Gateway as the Orchard Road options. Parkway Parade is temporarily closed.
App reservations for Bukit Panjang opened on 24 October, and booking ahead through the Sushiro app is the sensible move for a new outlet in its first weekends.
Sushiro Great World is due to open at the end of November. Image: Sushiro Singapore (artist’s impression)

body:
A barista at a plant milk booth during the 2025 edition of Singapore Coffee Week. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
Singapore Coffee Week returns for its third edition from 5 to 8 November, filling Hall C on Level 1 of Sands Expo and Convention Centre from 10am to 8pm daily. Entry is free and you can simply walk in. Before the doors open, public voting for the Singapore People’s Choice Café Award of the Year 2026 starts tomorrow, 1 November, at 10am.
The event is run by the Singapore Coffee Association, the trade body for the local coffee industry. Its members span coffee traders, roasters, café owners, equipment suppliers and baristas.
How the café vote works
Café entries closed on 20 October, and approved cafés sit on the Singapore Café Map and the official voting platform. Each person gets one ballot tied to a verified Singapore mobile number and can pick up to three different café brands, with each pick counting as one equal vote.
• Online voting runs from 1 November, 10am, to 8 November, 6pm.
• Onsite voting at Sands Expo runs from 10am to 8pm on 5 to 7 November, and from 10am to 6pm on 8 November.
• Cafés are not allowed to offer payments, gifts or discounts in exchange for votes.
The café with the highest verified total is named the Singapore People’s Choice Café Winner of the Year 2026 and gets a trophy, a certificate, a digital badge and a free individual booth at the 2027 edition. The rest of the top ten receive a trophy or certificate and a counter in a shared café pavilion next year.
The interactive coffee map traces coffee’s journey around the world and into Singapore. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
What you can do in Hall C
The Bean Discovery Bar gathers beans from different roasters in one spot, so it suits anyone hunting for a new bag to brew at home. An interactive coffee map traces how coffee spread around the world and how Singapore built its own coffee habits, with trivia along the way.
Sip and Stamp is a coffee discovery trail, and finishing selected activities earns a turn at Spin and Win for coffee goodies and merchandise. There is also a Golden Bean Hunt for 24K golden beans worth S$10,000 in total. Collect any eight stickers on the pre-event Café Hopping Adventure and you receive a location hint for the hunt.
An oat milk exhibitor booth at Singapore Coffee Week 2025. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
Exhibitors include A.muse Tea and Co, Addison Institute, Asia Supply Trading, Balance Coffee, Baristart Coffee and Bettr.
Competitions on the floor
Teams in the Singapore Coffee Roasting Team Championship 2026 compete through roasting, cup tasting and voting for a chance to represent Singapore at the ASEAN Coffee Roasting Championship 2027. The Singapore Home Roasting Championship also runs during the four days.
Roasting teams compete through roasting, cup tasting and voting for a place at the ASEAN Coffee Roasting Championship 2027. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
The Singapore Fashion Drinks Competition takes place on 5 and 6 November, and its top three go on to the 2027 World Fashion Drinks Competition at HOTELEX Shanghai. People’s Choice winners are named on the association’s and the event’s social media channels on 8 November, once the votes are verified.
summary: Singapore Coffee Week takes over Sands Expo Hall C from 5 to 8 November with free entry, and People's Choice café voting opens on 1 November at 10am.
title: Singapore Coffee Week returns to Sands Expo from 5 to 8 November, with café voting open from 1 November

McDonald’s and Pokémon fans, here’s something to look forward to: the Pokémon Happy Meal collaboration is heading to Singapore and Malaysia in December 2026 , following its US launch on 10 Nov .
Credit – @HuinGuillaume via X (formerly Twitter)
The collection is said to feature 15 collectible mini box toys and 15 Pokémon trading cards . Each mini box is designed around a different Pokémon , including familiar favourites such as Pikachu, Eevee, Charmander, Bulbasaur, Umbreon and Piplup, alongside other recognisable characters.
Credit – @ModernNotoriety & @HuinGuillaume via X (formerly Twitter)
The mini boxes are arguably one of the more interesting parts of the collection. They can reportedly be turned into little charms that you can clip onto your keys, bags or even your trousers.
I don’t know about you, but the idea of having a tiny Pokémon companion from a Happy Meal tagging along on everyday errands, rather than leaving the collectibles at home is actually quite genius!
Credit – @pokehuntdotfun via X (formerly Twitter)
As for the trading cards , leaked photos suggest that the collection could include 15 designs , 7 of which feature a holofoil finish . The alleged line-up includes Jirachi, Tyranitar, Absol, Decidueye, Hawlucha, Pikachu, Palafin, Lucario, Snorlax, Eevee, Metagross, Mimikyu, Chandelure and Wooloo.
However, some reports have listed only 14 stamped cards , so the final selection remains unclear .
Each Happy Meal is also reportedly expected to include 2 Pokémon trading cards , though this detail has yet to be confirmed for Singapore and Malaysia.
The meals may come in special Pokémon-themed packaging , too, with 3 reported box designs featuring Pikachu, Umbreon and Torchic. The exact selection of toys and cards, as well as how they will be distributed, could vary by market.
The McDonald’s x Pokémon collaboration is expected to reach Singapore and Malaysia in Dec 2026, though local prices, exact launch dates and the final selection of toys and cards have yet to be confirmed.
For now, I’m curious to see which Pokémon make it into the local collection, especially if the mini box charms turn out to be as adorable as they sound (and practical, of course)!
Batam’s new waterfront resort Opus Bay opens this December, just 45 minutes from Singapore
summary: McDonald’s Pokémon Happy Meal collaboration is expected to arrive in Singapore and Malaysia in December 2026, featuring 15 collectible mini box toys and a reported selection of 15 trading cards. Pokémon fans can look forward to clip-on box charms and possible holofoil cards, although local prices, launch dates, final designs and distribution details remain unconfirmed.
title: McDonald’s x Pokémon Happy Meal with mini box charms & trading cards coming to Singapore & Malaysia

It’s finally Nov, with just 2 more months left before the year comes to an end. As the festive season draws closer, there’s plenty to explore around Singapore . From fitness competitions to a relaxed evening with orchestral music, the possibilities are endless.
If you’re wondering how to have a fun time in Nov 2026, here are 11 of the best things to do in Singapore during this month.
How I chose these best things to do in Nov 2026
These are the 3 main criteria I used to decide which activities to recommend:
• Variety : The activities on this list cater to a range of interests, from sports to arts & culture.
• Wide price range : From paid events to free events, there’s something for every budget.
• Accessibility : I included events located in different parts of Singapore so you can pick the one most convenient for you.
I have also grouped them into 3 different categories, so you can find what suits you best.
• Activities & Wellness
• Food & Beverages
• Arts & Culture
This isn’t a ranked best-to-worst things-to-do list, but a collection of the most enjoyable activities overall, in no particular order. Get ready to head out to have fun before the year inevitably ends!

1. AIA HYROX Singapore 2026 (26 – 29 Nov 2026)
Credit – HYROX Singapore via Facebook
Ready to put your strength and stamina to the test before the year ends? AIA HYROX Singapore 2026 returns from 26 to 29 Nov 2026 , bringing 4 days of high-energy fitness competition to our red dot. You can expect an accessible and inclusive fitness movement that remains challenging at HYROX. If you’re 16 years or older and prepared, you can take on HYROX as a challenge. Fun fact: their oldest contestant to date is 73 years old — wow!
There are 2 divisions in HYROX: Pro (for seasoned athletes seeking maximum intensity) and Open (for those wanting something a little more accessible). Each participant takes on an 8km run , broken up by 8 workout stations that include exercises such as sled pulls, sled push, burpee broad jumps and more.
If the thought of tackling the course solo in HYROX Open/Pro sounds intimidating, sign up for HYROX Doubles/Doubles Pro with a friend. Alternatively, you can find 3 friends and take on HYROX Relay , with each member completing part of the course. Younger fitness enthusiasts aged 8 to 15 years old can also look out for HYROX Youngstars , happening on 28 and 29 Nov 2026 .

Ask anyone from the Hou- gang (please tell me you get it) for the best porridge place and they’ll probably exclaim Sin Heng Kee Porridge in a heartbeat. The corner stall along Hougang Street 61 is renowned for its thick and hearty porridge bowls, and warmed tummies and souls since childhood days.
I thought I’d find out for myself what the hype was all about and rocked up to the bustlin’ store at 7am, just as they opened. Of course, there was no issue getting a seat but I was pleasantly surprised at the snaking queue to place dine-in and takeaway orders. Mind you, this was minutes after they just opened for the day!
What I tried at Sin Heng Kee Porridge
My ultimate favourite combination that I order everywhere I go is Century Egg and Meatball Porridge (S$6) . Given it was my first meal of the day, I thought I’d add an Egg (additional S$0.50) and You Tiao (+S$1.20) for that extra protein and energy.
Plus, I love how the colours come together so beautifully. Had to snap one for the ‘gram before I dug in.
As talk of the town, I’ll admit that I had high expectations for Sin Heng Kee. As I dived into my first spoonful with a little bit of everything, it surprised me that the flavours didn’t quite take me on a gastronomical ride.
The sharpness of the century egg and ginger didn’t quite cut through as I’d hoped for it to. Sin Heng Kee’s handmade meatballs were small and pretty much hidden in the huge bowl but just like its appearance, it was so-so.
Ye Lai Xiang Teochew Porridge: Your taxi uncle’s fave Teochew Mui, open till 4am
Of course, fried dough sticks are an absolute must. A great complement that gave the dish another dimension with its crisp texture. However, the thick gruel lacked a savouriness that perhaps could be alleviated with more soy sauce.
I also gave the seafood series a go with the Cuttlefish & Peanut Porridge (S$6) . If there’s one thing to count on at Sin Heng Kee Porridge, it’s their wide variety of porridge. I’m talking over 15 combinations!
While the large slices of ginger was a promising sign to me, the cuttlefish slices paired together with the peanuts as stars of the show, fell short of delivering a powerful combination. Rather, it was a tad too fishy for my liking. Altogether, not the biggest fan of the series but this might just appeal to lovers of seafood porridge.
Final thoughts
Overall, decent bowls that looked better than they tasted. Perhaps I should’ve given the Signature Porridge (S$7.50) a try, given that it’s loaded with century egg, sliced pork, meatballs, liver, intestines, cuttlefish, sliced fish, and minced chicken. Personally, Chai Chee Pork Porridge sets the bar when it comes to hearty, savoury porridge and handmade meatballs.
If you’ve yet to visit Sin Heng Kee before, I’d highly recommend visiting once to play judge to Hougang’s pride and joy.

The thick, generous portions and affordability may appeal to Hougang residents and comfort-food seekers, though the flavours vary in depth, making some bowls more satisfying than others.

Today, I had lunch at Bouillon Gavroche with my wife. It is on level 1 of Mandarin Gallery along Orchard Road, and you cannot really miss it. Bright red facade, black art-deco doors and old French posters on the walls.
A bouillon (an old-school Paris canteen serving hearty French food at everyday prices) is not something we see much of in Singapore. This one comes from the same father-and-son team behind Brasserie Gavroche. Classic dishes, no fuss.
Inside, it is red banquettes, globe lights and French music playing in the background. It is not a quiet place. But it is good for a casual meal with friends, where you order a few plates to share and just talk.
Drinks are easy. It is $1 per pax for free-flow water, and they bring it to the table in their own branded bottle.
We started with the French baguette and butter ($4). It came warm and crisp, with a slab of butter on the side. Simple, but very satisfying. What can go wrong with this.
For the steak, we went for the Wagyu Petit Tender ($38), which comes with peppercorn sauce and fries. The beef was very tender and juicy, still nicely pink inside. If you only have to try one dish, I would suggest this.
We also ordered the Parmentier de Canard ($24). Think of it as a shepherd’s pie, but with shredded duck confit at the bottom, crushed potato on top and a crust of breadcrumbs baked till golden.
It was good. But it is heavy, so it is better to share. For one pax, it can get too much.
My personal verdict.
Food: 4/5 — the Wagyu steak and the baguette carry it. Lunch for the two of us came to about $70+. Menu prices are before service charge and GST, so do factor that in. Not hawker cheap, but decent value for French food in the middle of Orchard.
Ambience: 4/5 — lively and comfortable. Suitable for a casual meal with friends.
Service: 4.5/5
Will I return? Yes. I am happy to come back and try the other items on the menu.
Bouillon Gavroche
333A Orchard Road, #01-16/17 Mandarin Gallery, Singapore 238897
Open daily, 11.30am to 11pm.

Singapore is the furthest thing from being short of amazing places to eat, and Chinatown is the crown jewel of our vibrant food scene. Nestled in the heart of this culinary haven is Chinatown Complex Food Centre , which sees throngs of locals and tourists alike.
Home to over 200 stalls, this bustling hawker centre offers a little bit of everything — from crowd favourites to tried-and-true hawker staples.
With so much in store, narrowing down the must-tries can be a challenge. Well, we’ve done the legwork for you. Here’s our list of 12 best stalls in Chinatown Complex Food Centre for the ultimate hawker feast !

1. Chef Leung’s Authentic Hand-milled Rice Noodle Rolls (#02-096)
The lengthily-named Chef Leung’s Authentic Hand-milled Rice Noodle Rolls will be any savoury chee cheong fun fan’s go-to breakfast spot. The stall is helmed by native Hong Konger Chef Leung, an ex-Raffles Hotel chef of 19 years, his wife, also a former chef, at Hilton Shanghai, and their son Lucas.
Chef Leung serves up 5 types of cheung fun : Plain (S$3.20) , Egg (S$3.70) , Pork (S$4) , Char Siew (S$4.50) and Prawn (S$5) . The rice rolls are made fresh on the daily with rice that’s milled by hand, giving it a distinct, clean rice flavour.
Don’t underestimate the Plain variation; the silky cheung fun is doused in plenty of their umami -laden soy sauce and, interestingly, a peanut sesame sauce that enhances the dish with a creamy nuttiness. It’s then finished off wonderfully with some savoury chye poh , crispy shallots and spring onions.
If you’re down for some tasty, creamy porridge, you can also find 4 types of Hong Kong-style congee here, including the likes of the classic Pork Ribs and Century Eggs Congee (S$5) and Watercress and Fish Congee (S$6.50) .
Price : S$3.20 – S$11.50 per pax
Key highlights : Freshly milled rice rolls with peanut sesame sauce; congee also available
Wed to Sun: 6.30am – 12pm
Closed on Mon & Tue
Facebook | Instagram
2. Canton Steamed Rice (#02-132)
Manned single-handedly by 67-year-old retiree Mr Ng, I really am puzzled to why Canton Steamed Rice doesn’t have a queue when the food is really delicious and executed well, in my opinion. His menu features 9 steamed rice options with meats like beef, pork ribs, chicken and pork patties. He does all the preparation, including crafting his in-house chilli.
The Steamed Scallions & Ginger Chicken Rice (S$4.80) is hearty and comforting just like a home-cooked meal . The chicken is succulent, tender and perfumed with the light fragrance of the scallions as well as ginger. There’s at least 6 to 7 decent-sized pieces of meat along with green vegetables and rice for the Canton Style Steamed Beef Rice (S$6) . Even though the beef may appear considerably thick, each morsel was actually soft like a down feather pillow, perfectly seasoned. My favourite is the Steamed Pork Patty with Preserved Vegetable (S$4.80) where fine bits of chopped-up preserved vegetables are embedded within the pork patty, giving it a special but yummy flavour that grew on me.
Price : S$4.80 – S$6 per pax
Key highlights : Chicken, beef and pork patties served with rice and vegetables
Tue to Sun: 11.30am – 6pm
Closed on Mon
3. Zhong Guo La Mian Xiao Long Bao (#02-135)
Zhong Guo La Mian Xiao Long Bao finds itself on just about every Chinatown Complex Food Centre guide — and for good reason, without a doubt. Run by an Anhui-born chef and his wife, this Michelin-recognised stall draws long queues for its handmade dumplings and la mian .
Xiao long bao at nearly half the price of Din Tai Fung’s? Sign me up. 10 pieces here set you back S$8 — a little pricier than several other dumpling stalls but still works out to be less than a dollar per piece. These morsels explode with savoury broth when torn into, and are chock-full of delicious pork filling studded with fresh chives.
Now behold, the Szechuan Spicy Wanton (S$5.50 for 10 pieces) , also known as my personal favourite chilli oil dumplings in all of Singapore. The secret lies in the bits of chye poh that adorn the silky dumplings, which add an addictive umami that complements the tasty filling and tangy mix of vinegar and chilli oil.
…
summary: Chinatown Complex Food Centre in Singapore’s Chinatown houses over 200 stalls, serving everything from handmade chee cheong fun and dumplings to claypot rice, Japanese noodles and local desserts. This selection of 12 stalls highlights options across different budgets, with dishes priced from S$2.40, making it a useful guide for locals and visitors navigating the sprawling hawker centre, though popular stalls may involve long waits.
title: 12 best stalls in Chinatown Complex Food Centre for the ultimate hawker feast

Little Farms is putting on a one-night Italian dinner at Little Farms Table in Tanglin Mall on Friday, 6 November, with a five-course menu at S$88 per person, and the same weekend brings two free Italian farmers’ markets at its Serangoon Gardens and Tanglin Mall stores. Both sit inside A Taste of Italy , the grocer’s month-long Italian produce and wine programme with the Italian Trade Agency, which runs until 18 November.
Chilled angel hair pasta with buffalo burrata, one of the dinner’s pasta courses. Image: Little Farms
The dinner starts from 5pm. The Little Farms culinary team has built the menu around Italian ingredients that the grocer stocks, and you can take the full five courses or order your favourite dishes à la carte.
On the list are a beef carpaccio and an heirloom tomato salad to start, then a creamy wild mushroom risotto with truffle or chilled angel hair pasta with buffalo burrata. Mains cover a golden Pollo alla Milanese, pan-seared seabass with salsa verde, and grilled O’Connor beef striploin with rosemary jus. Nonna’s Tiramisu, made with espresso and mascarpone, closes the meal. Bookings are open now for what is a single evening, so a Friday table for a group is worth sorting early.
Grilled O’Connor beef striploin with rosemary jus. Image: Little Farms
Free markets on 7 and 8 November
The Italian Farmers Market comes to Little Farms Market at Serangoon Gardens on Saturday, 7 November, and moves to Little Farms Market at Tanglin Mall on Sunday, 8 November. Both days run from 10am to 3pm, and entry is free with online registration.
Expect regional specialities and pantry staples, from olive oil and cheese to pasta and wine, with samples to try and representatives from the participating Italian brands on hand to explain how the products are made. It is the easier way into the programme if you would rather graze and stock up than commit to a full dinner, and since both stores host the same market, pick whichever is closer to home.
The Italian Farmers Market runs 10am to 3pm on 7 November at Serangoon Gardens and 8 November at Tanglin Mall. Image: Little Farms
A wine and cheese class at the Botanic Gardens
The third event lands on the same Friday as the dinner. The Bloomhouse by Little Farms, in Ginger Garden at the Singapore Botanic Gardens, holds an Italian Wine and Cheese Masterclass from 6pm to 8pm on 6 November at S$65 per person.
The guided tasting moves through five Italian wines, from a crisp Vermentino to Chianti and Brunello di Montalcino, each paired with artisan cheeses, with notes on how the pairings work. It has sold out on Little Farms’ own Eventbrite listing, so the Tanglin Mall dinner is the Friday plan still open.
The masterclass at The Bloomhouse by Little Farms pairs five Italian wines with artisan cheeses. Image: Little Farms
Outside the three events, Little Farms stores carry a selection of Italian products through to 18 November.
summary: Little Farms serves a one-night five-course Italian dinner at Tanglin Mall on 6 November, then runs free Italian farmers' markets on 7 and 8 November.
title: Little Farms holds an S$88 Italian dinner and free farmers’ markets from 6 November

Sake Matsuri, which bills itself as Southeast Asia’s largest sake festival, moves to Marina Bay Sands for its 13th edition on Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November 2026, with regular tickets at S$60 for a three-hour tasting session . The festival takes over Hall C of the Sands Expo and Convention Centre, and tickets are on sale now.
The organiser puts the pour list at more than 500 sakes, shochu and artisanal spirits from over 100 breweries and distilleries. A craft beer festival, Japan HopFest SJ60 Edition, runs alongside on the same weekend.
The move follows a March 2026 edition at the F1 Pit Building and a November 2025 edition at Jewel Changi Airport, beside the Rain Vortex.
Guests at a past Sake Matsuri edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
How the sessions work
Each day has two sessions: 11am to 2pm and 4pm to 7pm. The halls close from 2pm to 4pm while the organiser turns them over, so tasting stops completely in that gap.
A regular ticket covers one session only. You cannot stay on into the next one. If you want a longer day, you buy a second session or go VIP. Late arrivals still get in, but the session ends on time, so a 6pm arrival for the 4pm slot gets an hour.
An exhibitor booth at a past edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
What a regular ticket gets you
The S$60 regular ticket includes a complimentary Sake Matsuri tasting glass, unlimited sampling across the 500-plus labels and entry to every festival zone, including a dedicated Spirits and Liquor Zone for Japanese gins, whiskies and shochu.
Masterclasses run by sake and shochu educators are included too. Seats are limited and you sign up in person at the Masterclass Lounge on the day. Bottles are on sale at the booths at festival prices.
There is also a food hall. Dishes there are priced separately from the ticket.
Tasting tables at a past edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
Bundles and VIP tickets
Groups get bundle pricing on regular tickets: five tickets for S$275, or eight for S$400.
VIP tickets cost S$128 for one person or S$248 for a couple. They cover the full day, both sessions, on your chosen date. On top of everything in the regular ticket, VIP holders get priority for masterclasses, a VIP Lounge for seating through the day and two-day access to Japan HopFest. The lounge stays open during the 2pm to 4pm break, but no food or drinks are served there.
All prices include GST.
A group at the Omu Nomu Craft Sake and Raw Bar booth at a past edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
Before you buy
Tickets are final and non-refundable. They can be transferred to someone else if you contact the organiser’s support team at least 48 hours before the event with the new guest’s details.
The organiser strongly recommends buying online in advance and warns that past editions sold out before the festival weekend. Limited tickets might be available at the door.
Alcohol is served only to guests aged 18 and over, and staff can ask for photo ID at registration. Under-18s enter free with an adult but get no wristband or tasting glass. Designated drivers can enter with the ticketed guests they are driving, again without a wristband or glass. Paid parking is available at Marina Bay Sands.
An exhibitor at a past Sake Matsuri edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
Details
• What: Sake Matsuri 13th Edition, with Japan HopFest SJ60 Edition alongside (ticketed separately)
• When: Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November 2026; sessions 11am to 2pm and 4pm to 7pm
• Where: Hall C, Sands Expo and Convention Centre, Marina Bay Sands; nearest MRT is Bayfront (Downtown and Circle lines)
• Price: Regular S$60 per session; five for S$275; eight for S$400; VIP full day S$128, or S$248 for two (GST inclusive)
• Age: Alcohol served to guests 18 and over only
summary: Sake Matsuri's 13th edition runs at Sands Expo on 28 and 29 November, with 500-plus sakes and spirits, S$60 three-hour sessions and S$128 full-day VIP tickets.
title: Sake Matsuri moves to Marina Bay Sands on 28 and 29 November, from S$60 a session

body:
Island Penang Kitchen at 721 Clementi West Street 2 was an accidental discovery when I visited the West Coast neighbourhood. The eatery seemed popular, judging from the long line that had formed, so I made a mental note to visit them in the near future.
I also texted my relatives who live in the neighbourhood, and found out that they found the food to be quite good. Since it has been a while since I last had Penang food , I decided to pay them a visit at 11.30am before the lunch crowd arrived. True enough, it was relatively empty— hooray!
What I tried at Island Penang Kitchen
I started with one of my favourite appetisers, the Penang Rojak (Fruits & You Tiao ) for S$7 . I was more inclined on this although they had another variation that had you tiao only at the same price.
My first impression— the generous sprinkling of peanuts— a plus for someone like me who loves nuts in all forms ( ahem … don’t let your imagination run wild).
As for the ingredients, there were pieces of Japanese cucumber, turnip, you tiao and pineapple. But wait, is pineapple the only fruit ? I was a little confused since the combination was similar to a typical local rendition, except for the missing tau pok . I was expecting fruits like jambu to appear.
Nonetheless, I decided to go for it. The pieces of you tiao were super crispy and, most importantly, not hard. The pineapple was sweet and the turnip and cucumber gave varying levels of texture and crunch.
The hei ko sauce was seasoned to perfection and coated the ingredients evenly. Overall, I was pretty satisfied. This was a good start!
Instead of getting the iconic Penang Fried Kway Teow (S$7.80) , I decided to switch things up and ordered the Penang Fried Mi Tai Mak (S$7.80) instead. When the dish arrived, we were immediately captivated by its smoky fragrance.
The ‘rat tails’ were stir fried with slices of Chinese sausage, 2 peeled prawns, bean sprouts, fish cake slices and chives.
The noodles tasted as delicious as they smelled, each strand possessing a robust punch of wok hei smokiness. Although the chilli packed some heat, it still allowed me to taste the other components of the dish without numbing my tongue.
18 best street foods in Penang to uncover [Jan 2025 update]
The prawns were decent and firm, while the strands of tau geh retained a satisfying crunch. We also found mini golden nuggets of pork lard, hiding like bats hibernating in a cave. My only gripe? They were inconsistent— some were crispy and delicious, while others were slightly chewy and soft.
My favourite component of the Penang Fried Mi Tai Mak was the red slices of lap cheong , which injected subtly sweet and savoury notes throughout the dish.
We then shifted our attention to the bowl of Penang Assam Laksa (S$6.80) . The noodles were topped with bits of fish, sliced lettuce, mint leaves and chunks of pineapple.
The noodles used weren’t thick bee hoon but lai fun , which were slightly thicker and had a translucent appearance. It’s the same kind of noodles used in Penang, too— 100 points for authenticity!
The broth was gently tangy but I could hardly taste the umami -ness of the hei ko . Thankfully, we were given a bottle of shrimp paste sauce to enhance the flavour. I added about a full tablespoon of it, and that really helped to redeem the dish.
Initially, we debated whether the fish bits were ikan kembung (mackerel) or sardines, but we leaned towards the former due to its taste and texture. It added a depth of richness to the bowl of laksa .
The slices of pineapple gave the dish a mild sweetness while the mint leaves made things more herby and aromatic.
Since we always reserve a small compartment in our bellies for dessert , we shared a bowl of Penang Homemade Chendol (S$3.50) . Instead of red beans, kidney beans were used alongside the quintessential pandan jelly strands.
After giving it a good mix, the gula melaka at the bottom gradually turned everything a light brown hue. The taste was decent and satisfying, but it was similar to any other chendo l we had tried before— nothing to shout about.
Final thoughts
Overall, we were quite satisfied with the Penang dishes served at Island Penang Kitchen. Although there were some hits and misses, the positives outweigh the negatives.
With a decent menu, reasonable prices, and tasty dishes, I finally understood the appeal and popularity of this eatery, even though it’s tucked away in the back of the heartland neighbourhood where many might overlook it.
I guess from now on, if I’m craving Penang food, this place will be one of my top choices and recommendations.

Which hawker stalls at Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre are recommended?
summary: Island Penang Kitchen at 721 Clementi West Street 2 serves Penang dishes including rojak, fried mi tai mak, assam laksa and chendol. The fried mi tai mak stood out for its wok hei, while the assam laksa needed extra hei ko for more flavour. With reasonable prices and more hits than misses, it is suited to heartland diners craving Penang food.

Qiannan Bites brings the flavours of Guizhou to CityLink Mall , serving up the region’s unique cuisine. You might even spot ladies dressed in traditional costumes, decked out in hefty silver jewellery that jingles with every step. They represent the Miao people , one of Guizhou’s ethnic groups.
Let’s put mala tang and sauerkraut fish — the usual mall staples we’ve seen a hundred times over — aside for a moment. Qiannan Bites takes a different route with a distinctive menu that showcases flavours you don’t often find in Singapore.
It’s a little like travelling somewhere new and discovering an unfamiliar food culture, without having to pack your luggage. What’s even better is that the head chef is specially handpicked and recruited from Guizhou, with the rest of the kitchen team undergoing training months before. This ensures an authentic taste of the region in every dish.
What to order at Qiannan Bites
To kick off our lunch, we started with the Guiyang Silk Doll Rolls (S$11.90) or Siwawa , a traditional speciality in Guizhou. It came with a mini basket of glutinous rice skins, a saucer of gravy, and a colourful, segmented array of 9 condiments.
Besides cucumber strips, pink pickled radish, signature pork bits and tau kwa , one of the more unique condiments was this bean sprout-like root called chameleon plant (fish mint). I tried it on its own and its unique flavour reminded me of a cross between mild ginger and rojak flower. However, it’s an acquired taste and customers can request it to not be included.
The paper-thin glutinous rice skins were stretchier than your usual peking duck wrappers. You can mix and match any combination of the 9 ingredients, but my recommendation? Add a bit of everything for the ultimate experience.
Once you’re loaded it up, fold both sides in, mimicking the act of wrapping an infant. Finally, drizzle the special zingy gravy, sprinkle some pork bits and shove the whole thing into your mouth for one glorious bite.
The ultimate best Korean food guide in Singapore [2024]
The skin was chewy, giving way to a complex blend of savoury, tangy, spicy, and crunchy flavours — what they call the essence of Guizhou. It took me at least 10 seconds to process what I had eaten.
It was a flavour I had never encountered before, and the medley of textures kept me intrigued enough to go back for more. If this is Guizhou’s take on spring rolls, man, I’d travel there just to have this every day!
Each Fresh Meat Pastry (S$3.80) is handcrafted from scratch, and we had the opportunity to watch the chefs work their magic. The dough is portioned, stretched by hand, and left to rest for 15 minutes.
A filling of premium meat and Guizhou Sichuan peppercorns is then tucked into the dough, which is flattened before being shallow fried in hot oil on both sides. This gives the pastry its golden-brown hue before it’s portioned and served.
To my surprise, the pastry wasn’t oily at all. The exterior was crispy, while the juicy, flavourful meat filling came with onion and scallion bits. There was also a gentle, lingering numbing kick from the Sichuan peppercorns, which added character without overpowering the meat.
We then moved on to the Guizhou-Style Deep-Fried Skewers , a crowd-favourite that’s sold on the streets of Guizhou. When orders come in, the various premium ingredients are coated in a light batter and fried till crispy, before the signature Guizhou chilli dipping sauce is brushed on.
Let me first warn you that the skewers aren’t for the faint-hearted. With each stick, the heat slowly crept up on me until my mouth was buzzing with spice. I worked up a little sweat along the way, but it was so shiok that I happily powered through every fiery bite.
For those who can’t handle spice, not to worry. You can request for the skewers to be less fiery or not spicy at all!
I loved how flavourful the Pork Ribs (S$3.80 for 2 sticks) were with a well-balanced meat-to-fat ratio. Just like a good lup cheong , the Mini Sweet Sausage (S$3.60 for 3 sticks) was yummy with a soft texture and had savoury-sweet notes. One of my favourites was the soft and fluffy Potato Slices (S$3.60 for 3 sticks) , which paired beautifully with the punchy heat.
I also enjoyed polishing off the soft, gelatinous flesh of the Tender Braised Chicken Feet (S$3.80 for 2 sticks) — all that was left were the bare tendons and bones.
For the final dish, we settled for something hot and comforting with the Guizhou Lamb Rice Noodles (S$13.90) . We learnt that Guizhou locals grow up eating this particular street food dish. Ingredients were simple — sliced lamb, pickled mustard vegetables, and rice noodles steeped in a hearty lamb broth.
The lamb was tender and the pickled mustard vegetables added a tangy kick that helped mellow down the richness of the meat. I enjoyed slurping the noodles with the broth, and though the dish is simple, I can understand why it’s loved by many.
…
summary: Qiannan Bites at CityLink Mall introduces Singapore diners to Guizhou cuisine, with traditional snacks, handmade meat pastries, chilli-coated fried skewers and lamb rice noodles prepared by a kitchen team trained in regional cooking. Conveniently located near City Hall MRT, it suits diners seeking alternatives to familiar Chinese mall fare, particularly those who enjoy bold, tangy flavours and adjustable spice levels.
title: Qiannan Bites: This authentic Guizhou eatery in town has flaky meat pastries, silk doll rolls & deep-fried skewers

Planning another trip across the Causeway? JB has welcomed a new batch of cafes, bakeries and food spots worth adding to your itinerary this Nov . Think pink Parisian-inspired interiors, creative apam balik flavours, a British classic car-themed cafe and even a beachfront hangout in Forest City.
Here are 10 new places in JB to check out in November 2026 .
1. M&L Paris Cafe
Credit – M&L Paris Cafe
Pink cafe lovers, you’ll want to add new M&L Paris Cafe to your November 2026 JB itinerary. This Muslim-owned cafe brings a slice of Paris to Johor Bahru, complete with pink interiors and a miniature Eiffel Tower at the entrance that practically begs for a photo op.
Credit – M&L Paris Cafe & miyra jhri via Google Reviews
The menu covers sweet treats such as cinnamon rolls, cakes and sweet drinks, alongside Western mains including fried chicken chop, garlic bread and pasta. Drop by for a coffee-and-cake session or settle in for a proper meal while getting your next pink-themed photo dump.
Address: 22, Jln Beringin, Taman Melodies, 80250 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim
2. AL Bakehouse
Credit – AL Bakehouse
AL Bakehouse is a new bakery in Taman Sentosa, JB that opened in late October which makes it optimal to visit in November 2026, serving freshly baked bread and homemade pastries.
Credit – Jowee Hoh & Quintus Ong via Google reviews
This neighbourhood bakery is worth keeping on your radar during your next JB food run. Its selection includes shio pan in various flavours, sourdough, egg tarts and red bean buns.
Address: 187, Jalan Sutera, Taman Sentosa, 80150 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim
3. Munchi Pancakes
Credit – Munchi Pancakes
Singapore’s popular Munchi Pancakes has made its Malaysian debut at AEON Mall Tebrau City , bringing more than 20 flavours of its creative take on min jiang kueh , also known as apam balik. The brand started as a hawker stall in Yishun before expanding to more than 42 outlets across Singapore.
Credit – Munchi Pancakes
Classic fillings include Peanut, Coconut, Red Bean, Kaya and Black Sesame, alongside Belgian Chocolate, Milo Dinosaur, Biscoff, Oreo Cheese, Matcha and Thai Milk Tea. Feeling adventurous? Try Pistachio Kunafa , Kopi Gao or Pineapple Cheese. Mini Munchi comes in boxes of 6 , making it easy to sample different flavours, while traditional min jiang kueh remains available for those who prefer the original.
Address: F-K4B, First Floor, AEON Mall Tebrau City Shopping Centre, Jalan Desa Tebrau, Taman Desa Tebrau, 81100 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim
4. Johara Roastery
Credit – grassy via Google Reviews
Johara Roastery , which opened in mid-October, brings a British classic car-themed cafe concept to JB, with a menu spanning local favourites, Asian dishes, Western mains and speciality coffee. Start with Kaya Toast (RM4.50) or French Toast (RM10) before moving on to Nasi Lemak Ayam (RM23) , Nasi Lemak Daging Rendang (RM24) or Nyonya Curry Laksa with Pan-Fried Salmon (RM30) .
Credit – grassy via Google Reviews
Western options include Fish and Chips (RM35) and Grill Chicken Chop (RM24) , while dessert choices range from Johara London Cake (RM18) to Classic Tiramisu (RM18) and Sea Salt Soft Cookies with Ice Cream (RM13) . Coffee fans can also explore specialty drinks such as Tiramisu Latte and Choco Misu , both priced at RM18 , alongside matcha and classic coffee options.
Address: 1, Jalan Yahya Awal, Bandar Johor Bahru, 80100 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim
5. Gula Cakery x El Ocho
Credit – Gula Cakery
Cake lovers have another reason to visit Toppen Shopping Centre , where Malaysian cake brand Gula Cakery has opened its first JB outlet with El Ocho . Naturally, the cakes are the main draw, especially the Matilda Cake , known for its rich chocolate flavour and dense texture.
Credit – Gula Cakery
Other options include Raspberry Pistachio Cake , Pandan Gula Melaka Cake and Speculoos Cheesecake . The El Ocho concept also brings Mexican-inspired hot food such as quesadillas and fajitas , so you can settle your savoury cravings before ending your meal with a slice of cake.
Address: L1.03 & L1.03A, Level 1, Toppen Shopping Centre, 33A, Jalan Desa Harmonium, Taman Desa Tebrau, 81100 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim
Niko Group: A personalised hair, scalp, head spa & nail experience for beauty care in JB
6. The Pine Patisserie & Confectionery
Credit – The Pine Patisserie
Previously spotted at events, The Pine Patisserie & Confectionery now has its own spanking new cafe in JB, giving fans a permanent place to enjoy its bakes in November 2026 without waiting for the next pop-up. Expect favourites such as shio pan , croissants and cromboloni , alongside coffee and pasta for those looking to stay for a meal.
Credit – grassy via Google Reviews
One highlight is its open-kitchen concept , which lets diners watch the pastry chefs prepare and bake their creations. Paired with a homey atmosphere, it makes a cosy stop for a catch-up over coffee and freshly baked pastries.
…
summary: Johor Bahru has welcomed new cafes, bakeries and food spots in November 2026, from Parisian-inspired interiors and creative apam balik flavours to speciality coffee, traditional pastries and beachfront dining. These spots span shopping malls, neighbourhoods and Forest City, with options for cross-Causeway food trips, casual meals and cafe-hopping.
title: 10 new places in JB to check out this Nov 2026 — cafes, food & more

Chipotle Mexican Grill will open in Singapore in 2027
Image credit: @chipotle
Chipotle fans, here’s an update on that Singapore opening we told you about last year: the timeline’s officially been pushed back. Chipotle Mexican Grill has confirmed that its first Singapore restaurant will now open in 2027 , a year later than the 2026 date we first reported.
Jewel Changi Food Guide: 40 Best Spots For Truffle Gyudon, Mochi Donuts and More
Here’s the latest update: The burrito chain will open at Jewel Changi Airport !
View this post on Instagram
The delay comes as Chipotle finally kicks off its actual Asia debut, and Singapore, it turns out, isn’t first in line after all.
Image credit: @chipotle
Chipotle opened its first-ever Asia outlet on 2 September 2026 , located along Gangnam-daero in Seoul’s Seocho-gu district. The restaurant runs through a joint venture named S&C Restaurants Holdings, formed with South Korean operator Sangmidang Holdings (formerly SPC Group), the same group behind Shake Shack, Paris Baguette, and Eggslut’s presence in Singapore.
For the uninitiated, Chipotle is a fast-casual Mexican chain known for its customisable burritos, tacos, and rice bowls. It began in 1993 as a lone restaurant in Denver, and has since expanded to include more than 4,200 outlets across the world.
Their menu is slated to be identical to those in the US and internationally. You can expect endless customisability with their build-your-own-meal concept, where they use fresh, responsibly sourced ingredients.
Image credit: @chipotle
You can get fully-stuffed Burritos as well as loaded Burrito Bowls , or if you like your meal light on carbs, you can choose to get their Salads, as well as their Tacos .
All their meats are responsibly raised, including Chicken , Pork Carnitas , Steak , and Barbacoa (braised beef) . They even have plant-based options, including the Sofritas , a plant-based protein, and Veggie , which comes with guacamole and beans.
Image credit: Chipotle
Chipotle will face stiff competition from existing fast-casual Mexican chains in Singapore, such as Australian-born Guzman Y Gomez, and homegrown brand Stuff’d. We’ll update this article once we get more information!
In the meantime, you can follow Chipotle Singapore for the latest updates.
Craving tacos and burritos now? Our round-up of the best Mexican restaurants in Singapore has some solid picks to tide you over.

CHAGEE launches new Geelato series at three outlets
CHAGEE fans: this one’s for you. The cult-favourite tea brand has just debuted its all-new Geelato series, featuring a whopping eight new gelato flavours, ranging from classic teas to refreshing sorbets. When we heard about the launch, my colleague and I made a beeline for CHAGEE’s Orchard Gateway outlet to see if the new series lived up to the hype.
The new Geelato series is available at three outlets: Orchard Gateway, One Raffles Place , and Pagoda House at Chinatown.
All Geelato will be priced at $6.90 per scoop , with premium flavours going for $7.90 .
Top picks from the line-up include the signature BO.YA Jasmine , which tasted just like the original drink, but in dessert form. Fans would love the familiar floral Jasmine notes that put CHAGEE on the map.
Matcha lovers would be pleased to know that the Signature Matcha flavour did not disappoint, boasting a strong earthy taste and smooth finish. Another highlight would be the Pistachio , which was my personal fave. It featured a nutty aroma that was both rich and creamy.
Two sorbets are also up for grabs: Bergamot Pink Guava and Yuzu Jasmine —both were refreshing with a frosty finish. The former was pleasantly sour, with white chocolate curls adding a nice crunch and subtle sweetness, while the latter had zesty notes that paired well with the prominent Jasmine flavour.
Pair your Geelato with a wide range of toppings for a top-up of $2 , including raisins , Biscoff crumble , and dried figs for some IG-worthy pics. If you’re spoilt for choice like we were, go for one of the Signature Pairings (from $8.90) —we got the Pu-er Berry Crumble , which features the Yunnan Pu-er Caramel Geelato topped with raisins and Biscoff crumbs.
PSA: Look forward to two special promotions in celebration of the CHAGEE Geelato launch. From now till 30 November 2026 , pick up a Voyage Passport at any participating Geelato store and collect all three stamps to receive an exclusive Geelato Voyage Charm. Additionally, snag a limited-edition Geelato magnet with any purchase of two Geelatos, from 2 November to 14 November 2026 , while stocks last.

Tucked away in a corner all the way to the back of Ci Yuan Hawker Centre , Man Man Chi 慢慢吃 is one of those accidental finds that I had the pleasure of discovering on one of my weekend food hunts.
The food stall was started in 2019 by 45-year-old Mr Cheah Kok Hean, who hails from Ipoh. The bulk of the dishes and handmade kueh sold at Man Man Chi are from recipes which have been passed down from his ancestors.
Credit – Man Man Chi
When Mr Cheah began his operations during the COVID-19 pandemic, it was challenging to get business and introduce Malaysian cuisine to Singaporeans. Thankfully, during the circuit breaker period, he managed to tide through with delivery orders with the help of social media coverage.
He even managed to be nominated at the 2022 Singapore Hawkers Awards under the heritage category— 3 cheers for Mr Cheah!
Mr Cheah’s mother-in-law occasionally helps out at the stall. I could feel the warmth as she recommended some dishes and the condiments to pair them with— I felt as if I was a guest dining at her home.
What I tried at Man Man Chi 慢慢吃
The crowd-favourite here is Curry Chee Cheong Fun (S$4.50) , but when I spotted Curry Chwee Kueh (S$4.50) on the menu, I just had to try it!
According to the aunty, the people of Ipoh usually add some fried items to their curry. And so I ordered a fried Prawn Cracker (+S$1.30) . The luxurious plate had 4 pieces of chwee kueh (cut in half), a sprinkling of sesame seeds, and vegetables doused in a rich curry gravy.
The pieces of chwee kueh were like silky pillows in my mouth. They were extremely soft and fine. I could have eaten 50 of them!
The curry was seasoned perfectly. Slightly smoky, spicy and possessing creamy coconutty notes all at the same time. Ladies and gentlemen, this was liquid gold!
The curry vegetables consisted of long beans, carrots and cabbage. They were braised till soft (just the way I like it). The Prawn Cracker was extremely crispy and tasty, which raised the bar higher on my satisfaction metre. Shiok !
I gave their homemade snacks a try as well. I ordered the Pan Fried Png Kueh (S$1.50) as well as the Steamed Yam Cake (S$1.50) . I’d usually go for the steamed version of png kueh , so this pan-fried rendition was something different.
The crust was slightly crispy and the glutinous rice within was nice and chewy. However, the peanuts, mushrooms and dried shrimps were so fine that I had the impression of eating a plain glutinous rice filling— I wished they were chunkier.
Jalan Kukoh Teochew Kueh: Traditional hand-made kuehs by siblings at hidden hawker centre
Dipping it into the black sweet sauce salvaged it a little bit, though.
The Steamed Yam Cake was topped with chai poh and served with spring onions and red chilli strips. The cake was velvety and smooth, and had tiny bits of textural yam within. The chai poh added a tangy and crunchy touch to the dish.
The chilli was well-balanced and had just the right amount of heat. It was the perfect accompaniment to the yam cake.
The last dish I tried was the Glutinous Rice (S$3.20) . The recipe was passed down by Mr Cheah’s aunty, who has been selling it on the streets of Ipoh even before he was born, and still does it until today— impressive!
It was a scrumptious mound of brownish glutinous rice filled with black mushrooms, dried shrimp, chai poh , and garnished with spring onions and red chilli.
Unlike our local version which has peanuts, the Ipoh version uses chai poh instead. It gave a unique texture to the rice, and provided subtle salty and acidic punches to it as well. I’ve always loved this old-school dish and it definitely hit the spot for me.
Final thoughts
Having a Malaysian-style breakfast definitely was a great start to my morning. I’m definitely recommending the super unique Curry Chwee Kueh to my family, friends and colleagues. I’m excited to return here to try their other offerings, like the Fried Pumpkin (S$1.70) and Mushroom Chicken Chee Cheong Fun (S$4.50) .

Which food stalls at 724 Amk Market & Food Centre are worth a try?
summary: Man Man Chi 慢慢吃 at Ci Yuan Hawker Centre serves Malaysian and Ipoh-style dishes based on family recipes, including handmade kueh and traditional breakfast fare. The Curry Chwee Kueh and Glutinous Rice stand out among the dishes tried. It is best suited for diners seeking affordable Malaysian flavours and old-school kueh.
title: Man Man Chi 慢慢吃: Ipoh-style curry chwee kueh, handmade snacks & glutinous rice with recipes from ancestors

Free things to do in Singapore
Between the rising cost of living, GST hikes, and the ever-tempting $10 chicken rice, spending money in Singapore feels practically unavoidable. But some of the best experiences this city has to offer won’t cost you a single cent. Whether you’re a broke student, a frugal parent planning a family day out, or just someone who refuses to let their wallet dictate their weekends, there are plenty of free things to do in Singapore that are genuinely worth your time.
From hiking trails and heritage museums to rooftop gardens and beachside movie screenings, we’ve rounded up 44 free activities in Singapore that prove you don’t need to splurge to have a good time. So leave your credit card at home – or at least in your pocket – because Singapore is way more generous than you think.
– Nature & parks to explore for free in Singapore –
1. Stroll through Punggol Waterway Park
Image credit: Expedia
When it comes to parks in Singapore , North-Easties have it good, because Punggol Waterway Park is one of the island’s most picturesque pockets of greenery. Tucked away in the far reaches of the purple line, it’s a tranquil, 12.25-hectare sanctuary that has no shortage of awesome vantage points to appreciate the various species of flora and fauna that call it home.
The Jewel Bridge at Punggol Waterway Park.
Image credit: @ramesh_kurup_photography via Instagram
For instance, visitors can take a stroll down the park’s 2 bridges, the Jewel and Sunrise bridges , to try to catch a glimpse of wildlife such as otters and migratory birds. The park also has a nifty playground with an expansive water and sand play area for little ones to tire themselves out with. Plus, the massive Waterway Point shopping mall’s just a stone’s throw away, should you need to duck into its air-conditioned premises to cool off.
Nearest MRT: Punggol (NE17/CP4)

Mr CHEESECAKE has a limited-time pop-up in Orchard
Image credit: Inside Retail Asia
ION Orchard has recently been a hotspot for Japanese brand debuts , such as I’m Donut and fried sando shop Age.3 . Now, Mr CHEESECAKE is joining the mix, making its Southeast Asian debut from 11 November 2026 to 30 December 2026 .
20 New Japanese F&B Openings In 2026—Viral Fried Sando, Hot Stone Gyukatsu And More
Image credit: Ufu
For the uninitiated, Mr CHEESECAKE is a Tokyo-born cheesecake brand founded by Chef Koji Tamura, who has worked in Michelin-starred restaurants, including three-Michelin-starred Mirazur in France and one-Michelin-starred Restaurant ES in Paris. Since its launch in 2018, Mr CHEESECAKE has expanded to five stores in Japan and one in Hong Kong, selling over 1 million cakes to date.
Their cheesecakes are meant to be savoured at three different temperatures: frozen for a mouthfeel that’s similar to ice cream cake, fully thawed for a smoothness similar to creme brulee, and half-thawed for a mix of both textures.
Image credit: Mr CHEESECAKE
Their best-seller is the BASQUE CHEESECAKE Original ($62) , which boasts a toasted, caramelly exterior, a result of baking the batter at a high temperature, and a smooth, creamy interior with real vanilla specks. The combination of browned butter, vanilla, and brown sugar is said to give the cake a butterscotch aroma that’s best enjoyed with a cup of hot coffee.
Image credit: Mr CHEESECAKE
Those looking to amp up the coffee flavour should order the Mr CHEESECAKE Cream Brew Coffee ($68) , comprising coffee beans steeped in the same cheesecake mixture, which lends the cheesecake a rich, earthy, and slightly fruity flavour.
Image credit: Mr CHEESECAKE
Of course, matcha lovers can also get their cheesecake fix with the Mr CHEESECAKE Matcha ($69) . It features stone-ground Yame matcha from Fukuoka, prized for its mellow sweetness and rich umami flavour, complemented with creamy mascarpone, vanilla, and fruity extra-virgin olive oil for a decadent yet refreshing treat.
Image credit: Mr CHEESECAKE
For a more tropical variant, the Mr CHEESECAKE Sakekasu Coconut ($69) combines rich coconut, refreshing lychee puree, and umami sakekasu, AKA sake lees, for a cake that’s not too sweet.
Image credit: Mr CHEESECAKE
Those who aren’t too keen on cheesecake can opt for their RICH TIRAMISU ($69) instead—their interpretation of the Italian classic. Expect a delicate, crisp almond dacquoise layered with a light, mousse-like cream flavoured with coffee, cacao, and hojicha, further enhanced by the nutty aroma of browned butter.
Do take note that the cakes are available while stocks last, so it’s worth getting there early.
If you’re feeling peckish after your cheesecake haul, our guide to the best ION Orchard food has you covered. Then, wash it all down with a drink from Chinese chain Yee3 , known for their unique coconut drinks.

New restaurants and cafes in Singapore for November 2026
November is when most of us are already mentally on leave, with year-end dinners filling the calendar. But Singapore’s food scene isn’t slowing down. This month brings a competitive eater’s first restaurant, a Japanese beef bowl chain taking on Sukiya and Yoshinoya, and an ex-fine-dining chef wok-frying pasta at a Bukit Merah hawker centre. Here are the best new restaurants and cafes to check out in November 2026 .
1. Matsuya
Image credit: Japan Journeys
Japan’s Matsuya is one of the country’s most popular gyudon chains, with about 1,200 outlets back home and over 1,500 worldwide. Its first Singapore outlet lands at Suntec City in November 2026 , setting up a three-way beef bowl showdown with Sukiya and Yoshinoya.
Image credit: Japan Journeys
Local prices are still TBD, but in Japan the classic Beef Bowl —thinly sliced beef stewed with onions in sweet soy sauce—goes for just ¥480, or about $3.90. Other bowls include the Beef Bowl with Tomato and Cheese and Beef Bowl with Grated Radish and Ponzu Citrus Soy Sauce , while the Beef Curry with Hamburg Steak ($TBD) is the heartier pick. Ordering and payment are done at a kiosk, so this is very much an in-and-out lunch.
Read our Matsuya feature .
Address: 3 Temasek Boulevard, #B1-125, Tower 2, Suntec City, Singapore 038983
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Matsuya is not halal-certified.
Popular Japanese Gyudon Chain To Open At Suntec In Nov 2026
2. OVER
Competitive eater Zermatt Neo has made his first F&B move with OVER , a Tras Street restaurant about a five-minute walk from Tanjong Pagar MRT Station and Maxwell MRT Station . As you’d expect, size is the whole point—most dishes come in Lesser, Standard, or Challenge portions.
The Curry Me Over (from $23++) was our favourite: a huge, juicy chicken cut in nanban sauce over fragrant Hainanese-style curry rice. The Shroyu-Clams! Easties will be happy to know that Lola’s Cafe has set up shop at Tampines Mall . We recommend their Lamb Shakshuka ($18++) , a hearty stew combining tender lamb chunks, tangy tomato sauce, and poached eggs, served with sourdough bread for dipping. body:
We start Nov 2026 with some sad news for foodies: Maxim Tam Chiak Kopitiam at Tampines Street 64 ceased operations on 1 Nov 2026 . This kopitam will be deeply missed by residents.
If the name Maxim Tam Chiak sounds familiar, it’s because this kopitiam was part of the Tam Chiak Kopitiam group . The owner is fellow foodie Maureen Ow, aka Miss Tam Chiak , alongside actor Chew Chor Meng and DJ Dennis Chew.
Set below the Tampines GreenCrest BTO in Oct 2025 , it featured 10 stalls of a variety of cuisines for easily bored palates. From classic Nasi Padang at Boolatzkitchenz to traditional fish head curry at Jalan Wong Ah Fook Curry Fish Head, you were definitely spoiled for choice.
The Tampines outlet was the 4th coffeeshop under their wing. Their Kovan branch closed in May 2026 . Fret not, they still have 2 more outlets: one at Punggol and another at Bidadari but the stalls there are different from those at the Tampines outlet.
When they first launched, they had a banger lineup of diverse choices and flavours. This included Delight Hainan Western , Vege Bear , Steams Variety , Mohamed Waseef Indian Muslim Food and Chaoyuan Noodle. As you can see, residents of all backgrounds had a lot to choose from. While there are probably other coffee shops nearby, there’s no denying that there’s someone out there who just lost one of their favourites.
The options don’t just end at the stalls themselves, mind you. Delight Hainan Western offered over 40 dishes, most of which were under S$10. So to summarise, Maxim Tam Chiak Kopitiam had multiple stalls with different cuisines, affordable prices, and the kopitiam itself was open 24 hours. Their closure is definitely going to hurt for a while.
While this closure is heart-wrenching, it is far from the end — they recently teased a new outlet at Tengah with claims that it will be their biggest outlet yet. Keep an eye on their Instagram for future announcements. I doubt this will be the last of Maxim Tam Chiak Kopitiam.
The $2.50 Shop: Family-run hawker stall with $2.50 nasi rawon, lontong & $0.80 handmade kueh, opens at 4.30am
summary: Maxim Tam Chiak Kopitiam on Tampines Street 64 ceased operations on 1 Nov 2026, just over a year after opening below Tampines GreenCrest BTO with 10 stalls and 24-hour service. The Tam Chiak Kopitiam group still runs outlets in Punggol and Bidadari, and has teased a new outlet at an unannounced location. Useful for Tampines residents tracking where the group goes next.
title: Goodbye, Tampines – Miss Tam Chiak kopitiam closes on 1 Nov

body:
McDonald’s x Pokémon Happy Meal
Pokémon fans, rejoice! This December is looking extra exciting, as you’ll soon have another reason to flock to McDonald’s . The fast food chain is bringing its limited-time Pokémon Happy Meals to Singapore, giving local fans a chance to get their hands on some Pokémon collectibles.
What’s in the Pokémon Happy Meal?
Image adapted from: Pokémon & @cop_o_clock via Instagram
Beyond the burger, side, and drink, the toy that comes with the Happy Meal is often the biggest draw. But this time, it could be an even bigger hit than usual. Pokémon has maintained a massive global following for decades, and recent years have shown that the franchise still has an incredible chokehold on fans.
So forget the usual red box with the golden arches. McDonald’s is giving its iconic Happy Meal packaging a Pokémon makeover, with 3 different box designs featuring fan favourites Pikachu, Umbreon, and Torchic.
Image credit: Pokémon
Inside each Happy Meal, you’ll find 1 of 15 collectible mini box charms , featuring adorable designs modelled after Pokémon such as Pikachu, Eevee, Bulbasaur, Popplio, Rowlet, and Sprigatito, among other familiar faces.
Here’s the full list of collectible mini box designs:
• Bulbasaur
• Charmander
• Squirtle
• Cubone
• Pikachu
• Eevee
• Umbreon
• Torchic
• Piplup
• Oshawott
• Minccino
• Espurr
• Rowlet
• Sobble
• Sprigatito
Image credit: Pokémon
But these mini boxes aren’t just meant to sit on your shelf. They can also be converted into adorable charms, so you can take your favourite Pokémon everywhere by clipping them onto your backpack or using them as keychains.
Image credit: @mcdonalds via Instagram
And if the mini box toys aren’t enough to get collectors excited, there’s more. Each Happy Meal also comes with 2 Pokémon Trading Card Game (TCG) cards , adding to the collecting frenzy that has swept the world in recent years. With 15 cards to collect in total, including 7 foil variants , there’s plenty to hunt down.
Here’s the full list of Pokémon TCG cards you can find:
• Zoroark

• Wooloo
• Decidueye
• Chandelure
• Palafin
• Pikachu
• Mimikyu
• Lucario
• Hawlucha
• Tyranitar
• Absol
When will the Pokémon Happy Meal be released in Singapore?
Image credit: Pokémon
According to an official announcement by McDonald’s , the Pokémon Happy Meal will be rolling out in different countries at different times, and the rest of us in Singapore can get our hands on it in December 2026 .
An exact launch date has yet to be confirmed, so we recommend you keep a close eye on McDonald’s Singapore’s Instagram page so you don’t miss out!
Start counting down to the launch of McDonald’s limited-time Pokémon Happy Meal
We can already imagine queues snaking around McDonald’s outlets as Pokémon fans and collectors descend on their nearest branches to snag these limited-edition goodies. Now, the only question is how many Happy Meals it’ll take before you finally catch ’em all!

A Christmas log cake in Singapore is the ultimate showstopper, and we’ve found the best of the best. Forget having to stress about where to find Christmas desserts in Singapore , ‘cos these indulgent, sweet picks will do the job perfectly. From rich, chocolatey creations to lighter renditions that balance out all the feasting, here are the best Christmas log cakes in town (halal options included). Want to get in the festive spirit, stat? Check out our nifty guide to Christmas in Singapore !
Why trust this guide
Every year, during Christmas, our team combs through the festive menus, gift sets, hampers, and turkey and log cake offerings. We compare notes, taste menus where we can, and research everything else, so you don’t have to spend time figuring out what’s worth spending your money on. We prioritise stand-outs over exhaustive lists, we fact-check prices and availability before publishing, and we update guides as new launches come in. When in doubt, we ask around – our community is generous with its seasonal picks.
Our top Christmas log cakes for 2026
1. Cat & the Fiddle
Photography: Cat & the Fiddle
One of our go-to spots for the best cheesecakes in Singapore has launched two new renditions of classic log cakes, and you bet we’re giving them a try. Crunchy, creamy and fruity, the chocolate raspberry log cheesecake ($60.90) features a timeless pairing of chocolate and raspberry. From the velvety dark chocolate cheese mousse to the luscious raspberry mousse studded with real fruit bits, every layer adds to the decadence.
Can’t do without your caffeine? You’ll adore the caramel latte cheesecake ($48.90). Rich and velvety coffee cheese mousse is layered with a fluffy caramel sponge centre, before being topped with soft chantilly cream and delicate caramel sponge crumbs. This glorious dessert is then finished with shimmering gold coffee beans for a fun festive touch.
Best for: Satisfying both your cheesecake and log cake cravings
Price: From $48.90 for an 800g cake
When to order: Pre-orders open now; available for delivery and self-collection
Where to purchase: Order online and at multiple locations including Westgate and City Square Mall
Order from Cat & the Fiddle
2. The Lobby Lounge at Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore
Photography: Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore
Impressing your guests will be a breeze with the artisanal log cakes from The Lobby Lounge at Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore. Executive pastry chef Jason Goh and his team have designed an exquisite line-up that’s a feast for both the eyes and the palate. Cast your gaze at the Tropical Buche de Noel, which takes the form of a charming chocolate sleigh. This decadent treat features Spinto 70% dark chocolate mousse, tropical fruit coulis, passion fruit velvet, and luscious layers of chocolate sponge and hazelnut feuilletine.
Another elegant contender is the Golden Maple and Quince Yule Log. Adorned with festive ornaments and a reindeer sled motif, this royal blue creation combines quince confit, salted Canadian maple mousse, walnut praline cream and vanilla genoise. Meanwhile, those longing for a cosy white Christmas can go for the Litchi-Framboise Buche de Noel. Painted in a snowy white hue, it is a delicious combination of lychee and raspberry compote, coconut lime mousse, coconut cremeux, vanilla joconde and almond caramel croustillant.
Best for: Artisanal log cakes that are picture-perfect
Price: From $60 for a 500g cake
When to order: Online pre-orders open from now till 29 Dec 2026; available for delivery and self-collection from 23 Nov 2026 to 1 Jan 2027
Where to purchase: Order online; collection at the Frasers House Boutique, The Lobby Lounge (daily, 11.30am to 8.30pm)
Order from The Lobby Lounge
3. Singapore Marriott Tang Plaza Hotel
Photography: Singapore Marriott Tang Plaza Hotel
A Christmas celebration isn’t complete without a stunning showstopper, so bring on the decadent collection of handcrafted yule log cakes from Singapore Marriott Tang Plaza Hotel! This year, the hotel presents two new renditions, alongside returning classics. An unmissable fresh face is the fruity and tea-forward raspberry lychee oolong log cake. Sink your teeth into oolong mousse with lychee compote, raspberry cremeux and vanilla sponge over a crumble feuilletine base, all encased in a glossy red glaze.
Or, try the vanilla peach yoghurt cake, featuring yoghurt mousse, peach compote, peach cremeux, vanilla sponge and a crumble feuilletine base. Dressed in soft hues of orange and pink, and crowned with a charming chocolate house, this creation is a delight for the eyes. Other decadent must-tries include the hazelnut coffee yule log for a crowd-pleasing combination of coffee and hazelnut; and a perennial favourite, the signature chocolate fudge log cake made with premium Felchlin Sao Palme chocolate.
