body:
The Line, the all-day buffet restaurant in Shangri-La Singapore’s Tower Wing, runs a Flavours of Türkiye menu from 2 to 17 November 2026. Lunch and dinner carry separate prices, and the run ends on 17 November.
What is on the Turkish table
The kitchen works through a spread that moves from mezze to dessert. Cold plates take in muhammara, humus, çoban salatası, barbunya pilaki, cacık and kısır. Mains cover red lentil soup, İzmir köfte, fried chicken liver, grilled bonito, lamb leg confit on rice with lamb liver and sultanas, and cabbage mücver. A live station turns out Adana kebab, ground lamb on a skewer with grilled tomatoes and onions, served on bulgur pilaf. Dessert brings baklava, oven-baked rice pudding, pumpkin confit with walnuts and kazandibi.
The Line’s buffet spread of roasts, seafood, satay and local dishes. Image: Shangri-La Singapore
The Turkish dishes sit inside the wider buffet
The Line keeps its standing counters going alongside the Turkish section. The dinner menu also carries a seafood bar with Boston lobster, snow crab, sea prawn, blue mussel, white clam and sea conch. The restaurant runs nine live stations in all, and the kitchen covers Middle Eastern, Indian, Western, Peranakan and Asian cooking.
Prime rib and hot dishes from The Line’s international buffet. Image: Shangri-La Singapore
Prices, sittings and the 17 November end date
Lunch runs 12pm to 2.30pm at S$68++ per adult and S$34++ per child aged 6 to 11. Dinner runs 6pm to 9.30pm at S$98++ per adult and S$49++ per child in the same age band. Both carry a 10 per cent service charge and prevailing government taxes on top. The last day is 17 November 2026, and the hotel lists the buffet as running Monday to Sunday across the whole window. Dishes are on rotation and can change without prior notice.
The weekday discount and the prize draw
Shangri-La Circle members take 40 per cent off the adult buffet price at lunch and dinner from Monday to Friday, and joining the programme costs nothing. The offer page adds that terms and conditions apply to the discounted rate. Every paying adult also enters a draw for two Turkish Airlines return tickets and a two-night stay at Shangri-La Istanbul.
What a child costs depends on the booking. The S$34 and S$49 rates for ages 6 to 11 are already half the adult price. Below six, up to two children eat free, but only where a Shangri-La Circle member is staying in the hotel and dining with them. Any further children under six pay half the adult price, and so does any child under 12 brought by a walk-in guest who is not staying in the hotel.
Chilled seafood and carved meats served at The Line. Image: Shangri-La Singapore
How to book
Bookings go by email to dining.sls@shangri-la.com or by phone on (65) 6213 4398, and advance reservation is required. A reservation screen for the menu takes a date and a party size, with lunch slots from 12pm and dinner slots from 6pm. No seat count sits behind either sitting, so whether a given date still has room is a question for the dining team rather than something a reader can settle online.
The Line sits in the Tower Wing lower lobby at 22 Orange Grove Road, a casual room where smoking is not permitted. À la carte service runs 12pm to 9.30pm daily, and buffet lunch and dinner keep to the sittings above through the run.
summary: The Line at Shangri-La Singapore serves a Turkish buffet from 2 to 17 November 2026, with Adana kebab, lamb confit and baklava alongside its usual counters.
title: Turkish buffet at The Line runs to 17 November 2026

body:
After its previous Singapore shows in 2015 and 2019, CATS is finally back after 7 years , running until 22 Nov 2026 at the Sands Theatre . The musical is based on T.S. Eliot’s Old Possum’s Books of Practical Cats (1939), with the score made by the iconic Andrew Lloyd Webber. The book is a collection of poems, with each focusing on the different Jellicle cats’ personalities.
The word “Jellicle” actually comes from T.S. Eliot’s unpublished poem “Pollicle Dogs and Jellicle Cats”. There are many explanations for how the word came about. The most popular explanation is that it’s a play on how people say “dear little cats”. If you say “poor little dogs” and “dear little cats” fast enough, it does actually sound like “Pollicle” and “Jellicle”.
CATS first premiered in 1981 in London, playing for 21 years — one of the longest-running musicals in the West End. It is one of musical theatre’s most iconic productions, boasting many accolades such as the Olivier and Evening Standard Awards for Best Musical. The production has been watched by over 77 million people and performed in more than 54 countries. The Broadway cast even won a Grammy Award for Best Musical Theatre Album, and the original London cast recording was Grammy-nominated as well.
The musical unfolds in a larger-than-life junkyard where the Jellicle Cats gather for their Jellicle Ball because they Jellicle-can. Just like us humans, each feline has their own personality, quirks and story to share. Throughout the musical, they’ll share their stories with their leader — Old Deuteronomy , played by King B — who will pick one lucky feline to ascend to the Heaviside Layer (basically kitty heaven) for a new life.
This year’s Singapore cast includes Cindy-Ann Abrahams as Grizabella , whose performance of the iconic song “Memory” is one of the production’s key moments. Meanwhile, Mukeni Nel returns following his appearance in the musical’s 2019 Singapore season as Quaxo , also known as Mr Mistoffelees.
Although the most well-known CATS poster features a clean design, with bright, glowing eyes centred upon a black background, the set design and production are anything but minimal. With oversized junk items such as tennis rackets, pipes and more random knick-knacks, the junkyard looks less like heaps of rubbish but more like a playground where the Jellicle Cats have fun. The gigantic Jellicle Moon hangs over the entire set, shrouding the junkyard in mystical blue hues. The set looks otherworldly and multichromatic, with purple, blue and green colours.
The opening overture is anything but simple as well. The theatre turns pitch black, and neon eyes slowly start to appear, blinking at the audience. I actually felt a weird sense of fear here, as I wasn’t sure what to expect. It felt as if a wild animal was hunting me down in the dark, like I was prey. After a sequence of neon eyes emerging from the dark, the Jellicle Cats themselves appear, running down the aisles. During this and other segments, the cats break the fourth wall often, interacting with audience members. Although they’re human-sized, the way the actors behaved really felt as though they were… well… cats. The actors were vocalising, looking around apprehensively, slow-blinking and moving swiftly — just like cats.
The best vinyl cafes & bars in Singapore
Act 1 begins with an explanation of what the Jellicle Cats are and their purpose for gathering. After this, it’s basically a really elaborate show-and-tell, where each feline shares their stories, unique traits and quirks through song and dance. Victoria , a pure white kitten, opens the Jellicle Ball with an enchanting ballet solo. The introductory solos have eclectic mixes of performing arts, from Jennyanydots and her tap-dance number with pests, to Rum Tum Tugger and his flamboyant rock-star energy coupled with electrifying guitar riffs. There’s even high-intensity acrobatic movements, all of which mimic the movement of actual cats. Act 1 ends with Grizabella , a shabby-looking cat, attempting to join the ball. I felt my heart squeeze with sadness seeing how her decrepit condition stops her from doing so. She is also shunned by the other Jellicles, being swatted and hissed at.
Act 2 continues on with the patriarch, Old Deuteronomy , encouraging the Jellicles to ponder about the meaning of happiness. Other candidates continue vying for a chance to ascend to the Heaviside Layer with their solos. A standout for me during Act 2 is Asparagus , better known as Gus. He’s an old cat suffering from ‘palsy’, as they call it, who relives his heyday as an artist with a fantastical play-within-a-play performance.
…
summary: CATS the Musical returns to Sands Theatre at Marina Bay Sands until 22 Nov 2026, with a vibrant production featuring elaborate junkyard sets, distinctive costumes, energetic choreography and audience interaction. The review covers the Jellicle Cats’ stories, standout performances and overall experience, making it useful for theatre-goers who prefer spectacle and unconventional musicals over plot-heavy shows. Tickets start at S$68, with Bayfront MRT providing nearby access.
title: CATS: Pawsitively purrfect musical returns to SG after 7 years

body:
Enabling Lives Festival 2026
If your weekend plans usually stop at brunch and a mall walk, the Enabling Lives Festival is a good excuse to go a little further. On 28th and 29th November 2026 , the annual festival by SG Enable spills out of Enabling Village and into the Redhill neighbourhood, with more than 70 activities spread across Redhill MRT, a nearby plaza, and Delta Sport Centre.
Here’s the lobang: admission is free . You can get your portrait sketched live by artists with disabilities, try blind football with a ball you track by sound, or lock into a training wheelchair for a fencing bout. The idea is simple. Instead of reading about inclusion, you play, shop, and chat alongside persons with disabilities in spaces you already pass through.
What’s happening at Enabling Lives Festival 2026?
The festival starts before you even reach Enabling Village. ARTRA’s Festive Plaza, right next to Redhill MRT, hosts the pop-ups this year, so you can tick off a few activities straight off the train.
Get a free portrait sketched live at Portrait Café
Image adapted from: Enabling Village
At Portrait Café, 4 artists with disabilities sketch you while you chat, café-style. The line-up includes a Deaf artist and artists with ADHD, autism and cerebral palsy, each with their own drawing style.
You pick a conversation prompt off a “café menu”, and the chat happens through gestures, visual cues or whatever way of communicating suits each artist. Best part: the portrait is yours to keep, for free . With only 2 sessions a day, it’s worth turning up early.
Venue: ARTRA’s Festive Plaza, next to Redhill MRT
Date: 28th-29th Nov
Time: 12pm-1.30pm & 2.30pm-4pm
Admission: Free
Guiding Steps – Walk Redhill with a white cane & meet guide dogs
Image credit: Enabling Village
Run with Guide Dogs Singapore, this 1-hour route shows you what a familiar neighbourhood feels like with visual impairment. After a briefing at Redhill MRT, you pair up with a volunteer or another participant, learn how a white cane works, and put on special eyewear that simulates different kinds of vision loss.
The walk ends at Enabling Village with a twist: you guide your facilitators with visual impairment to the Cabana using what you just learnt. Along the way, you also get to meet guide dogs and their handlers.
Slots are limited, so sign up in advance.
Venue: Starts at Redhill MRT
Date: 28th-29th Nov
Time: 1-hour sessions starting at 11am, 11.30am, 12pm, 1pm, 1.30pm & 2pm
Admission: Free, registration required
Chit Chat Sing Song – Musical improv by Ask Aunties
Image credit: Enabling Village
This improv show by Ask Aunties turns everyday moments on the MRT, in shops and at the playground into on-the-spot songs and scenes. Its inclusive cast builds each bit from personal stories and audience suggestions.
So yes, your daily commute complaint could become a musical number. Throw one in.
Venue: ARTRA’s Festive Plaza, next to Redhill MRT
Date: 28th-29th Nov
Time: 2pm-2.30pm & 4pm-4.30pm
Admission: Free
District of Care walking tour with The Urbanist Singapore
If you’d rather wander with a guide, The Urbanist Singapore leads a learning tour across several stops on the way to Enabling Village, pointing out local stories and the small design details that make a neighbourhood easier to get around. Check the festival website for timings.
Try wheelchair fencing, blind football & inclusive pickleball at Delta Sport Centre
Over at Delta Sport Centre, para-sport coaches and Special Olympics athletes take you through adaptive sports you don’t usually get to try on a random Saturday. No experience needed for any of them.
Inclusive pickleball for beginners
Image credit: Enabling Village
If you’ve been eyeing the pickleball craze but never found a kaki to play with, here’s your chance. This 1-hour session covers the basics before you team up with Play Buddies of different abilities in a friendly doubles mini-game, with adaptive gameplay thrown in.
It’s open to beginners with and without disabilities, including families and caregivers. Do note you’ll need to move around the court on your own, so the session isn’t suitable for those who use a wheelchair or walker.
Venue: Pickleball court, Delta Sport Centre
Date: 28th-29th Nov Time: 2pm-3pm, 3pm-4pm & 4pm-5pm
Admission: Free, registration required
Blind football try-out
Image credit: Enabling Village
In Listen, Dribble, Score, facilitators show you how blind football players rely on sound, communication and spatial awareness. You’ll practise ball control, dribbling and shooting at goal with a ball that makes noise as it rolls.
Blindfolds may come into play, but the drills can be adjusted to your comfort level. Zero football skills needed, which is good news for those of us who peaked at primary school PE.
Venue: Delta Sports Hall, Delta Sport Centre
Date & time: 28th Nov 10am-1pm | 29th Nov 1pm-5pm
Admission: Free
Wheelchair para-fencing taster sessions
Image credit: Enabling Village

High tea in Singapore is one of our favourite afternoon guilty pleasures. That’s why we’ve nibbled our way through towers of scones and pastries to bring you the best picks, including elegant hotel lounge buffets and chic cafes serving delicate treats. Whether it’s a catch-up with friends or a solo pick-me-up, these are the high teas worth your time. For more afternoon delights, check out our recommendations for brunch in Singapore .
Why trust this guide
Eating our way around the high tea spots in Singapore is part of the job. Our food writers dine out constantly, across every neighbourhood and price point, so our recommendations come from personal experiences, not press releases. We only include places we’d go back to (or already have), and we update our guides regularly to make sure nothing on the list has slipped and all information is accurate. Honeycombers has been covering Singapore’s food scene for over 15 years, so we know what a great meal looks like here – and what doesn’t make the cut.
Best high tea spots in Singapore: Treat yourself at luxurious hotel spots
1. The Grand Lobby at Raffles Singapore
Photography: Raffles Hotel Singapore
Bask in the glow of natural daylight streaming through a majestic skylight, with floor-to-ceiling Victorian pillars, and a refined colonial architecture that oozes sophistication while you sip on your tea. This is The Grand Lobby at Raffles Hotel Singapore, one of our favourite restaurants for a chic afternoon tea sesh in Singapore.
Savour a curated selection of exquisite finger sandwiches, pastries, seasonal delicacies, and sweet treats served on a three-tiered silver stand. Wash it all down with coffee or your choice of tea – the latter is brewed with JING loose tea leaves on a tea trolley tableside. Save room for two different types of scones, a fan favourite bake that’s complemented by rose strawberry jam and clotted cream. Cap off the indulgence with a glass of Billecart-Salmon or Louis Roederer champagne for the ideal afternoon treat.
Best for: A colonial-style sunkissed setting
Price: $108 per person; from $128 with a glass of champagne, featuring Billecart-Salmon and Louis Roederer
High tea timings: Daily, 12.30pm to 5.30pm
Address: Raffles Hotel Singapore, 1 Beach Road, Singapore 189673
Visit The Grand Lobby
2. The Lobby Lounge at Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore
Photography: Frasers House
There are few things better than indulging in an elegant afternoon tea session on a leisurely day, and The Lobby Lounge takes things up a stylish notch with its refined decor and sophisticated setting. Located within Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore, this luxe destination offers two thematic afternoon tea sets, crafted by executive pastry chef Jason Goh. With almost two decades of experience, his creations promise to be delectable and visually-appealing. The Heritage Royale afternoon tea is a menu mainstay. Nibble on contemporary creations with local-inspired flavours and toast to two complimentary flutes of champagne.
In the spirit of the upcoming holiday season, there’s also a limited-time Festive afternoon tea. Served on a Christmas-themed three-tier stand, the menu features seasonal savouries, delicate pastries and freshly baked scones. Indulge in winter black truffle and foie gras parfait, mini Christmas gammon pie and strawberry mint yogurt cake, while sipping a choice of coffee or tea. Or, top up from $16 to enjoy it with a glass of sparkling tea, champagne or festive cocktail.
The little ones are also welcome to join the festivities, with a specially curated kids’ menu. The whimsical line-up includes roasted turkey and cranberry cream cheese pinwheel, smoked salmon tartare cone, and mini gingerbread house.
Best for: Thematic high teas with delectable bites
Price: Heritage Royale afternoon tea at $228 for two pax; Festive afternoon tea from $72 per adult (minimum two to dine) and $70 for every two children (aged three to 11)
High tea timings: Daily, 1pm to 3pm, 3.30pm to 5.30pm
Address: The Lobby Lounge at Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore, 80 Middle Road, Singapore 188966
Visit The Lobby Lounge
3. 10|Scotts at Grand Hyatt Singapore
Photography: 10|Scotts
Nestled in the heart of Orchard, 10|Scotts at Grand Hyatt Singapore nails the art of afternoon tea. Settle into the elegant lounge, where homely interiors and calming waterfall views serve as a gorgeous backdrop. Sip on a glass of Saicho jasmine sparkling tea, before tucking into an exquisite afternoon tea experience. Its beloved ritual is made for both weekday and weekend indulgence. The elegant weekday afternoon tea set consists of warm savoury favourites, finger sandwiches and artisanal Asian-inspired desserts served to the table.

Third Floor Singapore has opened on the rooftop of Design Orchard at 250 Orchard Road. It is an all-day neighbourhood bar from the team behind award-winning No Sleep Club, with cocktails, wine, coffee, food and music in a relaxed, living-room-inspired setting.
Image: Third Floor
Third Floor Singapore: a casual take on No Sleep Club
Overlooking Orchard Road, Third Floor brings the creativity and technical precision of No Sleep Club, which ranked No. 8 on Asia’s 50 Best Bars 2021 and No. 26 on The World’s 50 Best Bars 2021, into a more everyday space. Think comfortable seating, an open kitchen and bar, and a pace that suits morning coffee, casual lunches, afternoon drinks and evenings with friends.
Image: Third Floor
Founder Juan Yi Jun, who was born and raised in Singapore, says the name comes from her teenage years hanging out around Orchard. “The location became the name, and more importantly, it became ours,” she says. Her career took her through Tippling Club and Operation Dagger before she co-founded No Sleep Club.
Image: Third Floor
Cocktails worth ordering
Drinks start with a memory, an observation or a familiar ritual rather than a spirit. Jun’s graphic design training shapes how ideas are developed, with distillation, fermentation and clarification used to serve the idea, not to show off. Three drinks to look out for:
• Jolly Shandy: a beer-and-lime shandy poured over frozen house-made lime sherbet made from leftover citrus shells and peels, which you stir with a spoon.
• 3 Lime Vodka Soda: calamansi, kaffir lime leaf and Thai sweet lime with a citrus-hop distillate.
• Blue Cheese & Olive: a dirty martini with Stilton-infused gin, fino sherry, vermouth and a house-made tomato concentrate, finished with Gordal olives stuffed with blue cheese cream.
Image: Third Floor / Juan Qian
A place to return to
Beyond cocktails, Third Floor serves coffee, food, wine and beer through the day. Music and creative collaborations are part of the plan too. Events such as Void Deck Jam, which we covered when it stepped into Design Orchard on 4 October , bring DJs, independent food vendors and local collaborators together without losing the informality of a neighbourhood bar.
Image: Third Floor / Juan Qian
As Jun puts it: “We take what we do seriously, but that doesn’t mean our guests have to.”
Third Floor Singapore: details
Image: Third Floor / Juan Qian
• Where: Rooftop, Design Orchard, 250 Orchard Road, Singapore
• Reservations: via BistroChat
• Follow: @thirdfloorsg on Instagram for opening hours, events and updates
Looking for more places to eat and drink around Orchard? See how Tan Ser Seng opened its first mall outlet at Great World .
Images: Third Floor, with photography credits to Juan Qian where shown.
summary: Third Floor is an all-day neighbourhood bar at Design Orchard from the team behind No Sleep Club.
title: Third Floor Singapore opens on the Design Orchard rooftop from the team behind No Sleep Club

The Pompompurin + Starbucks collection lands in Singapore on 10 November 2026, and it is aimed squarely at collectors. Starbucks Singapore is marking its 30th anniversary alongside Sanrio’s golden retriever Pompompurin, who also turns 30 this year, with eight Singapore-exclusive pieces plus a blind bag lanyard and a free straw clip for delivery orders.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Pompompurin + Starbucks collection: what is in it
The range reimagines Pompompurin, with his signature brown beret and laidback charm, in Starbucks-inspired touches such as green aprons and cafe drinks. The eight items span drinkware, plush collectables and everyday accessories:
• Plush
• Furry pouch
• Reusable bag with canvas pouch
• Plush keychain
• 12oz ceramic mug
• 20oz stainless steel tumbler
• 16oz glass cold cup
• Ceramic plate set
Image: Starbucks Singapore
The plush and plush keychain are the obvious fan magnets, while the furry pouch and the reusable bag with its matching canvas pouch are the easiest to work into daily use.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Drinkware and tableware
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Fans who like to sip in character get a 12oz ceramic mug, a 20oz stainless steel tumbler and a 16oz glass cold cup. A ceramic plate set rounds out the table.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Blind bag lanyard and free straw clip
Shop more, collect more. A Pompompurin + Starbucks Phone Lanyard with Charms Blind Bag is available at S$9.90 with any purchase. It comes in three collectible designs, each pairing a Pompompurin character with a Starbucks-inspired beverage charm. The charms detach, so you can mix and match, and you will need all three to complete the set.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
For fans who prefer to stay home, a free Pompompurin + Starbucks Straw Clip Set comes with a minimum net spend of S$25 on delivery orders from 12 November. This covers Starbucks Delivers, GrabFood and foodpanda, and net spend is counted after Stars redemption and vouchers. Redemption is limited to one per qualifying transaction.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
When and where to buy
Release date: 10 November 2026, while stocks last.
• In Starbucks stores from 10 November 2026
• Starbucks Online Store at 10am
• LazMall at 12pm
• Straw clip set: from 12 November, delivery orders only
Purchase is limited to six pieces per item per customer, and the blind bag phone sling strap is limited to six pieces per customer. Expect the plush and tumbler to go first.
If you have been following Starbucks collabs this season, see our earlier coverage of the Starbucks Winnie the Pooh Collection and Black Cat Frappuccino . For more, follow @starbuckssg on Instagram.
Press images: Starbucks Singapore.
summary: Starbucks Singapore and Sanrio celebrate their 30th anniversaries with eight exclusive Pompompurin pieces from 10 November 2026.
title: Pompompurin + Starbucks collection arrives 10 November with eight Singapore-exclusive pieces

Tanica, the modern Asian restaurant at The Singapore EDITION on Cuscaden Road, has put prices to its first Christmas since opening: a four-course Christmas Eve set dinner at S$165++ per person, and a Christmas Brunch of unlimited small plates from S$128++. Both are taking reservations now.
Plated courses served at Tanica, the image the restaurant uses for its Christmas Eve dinner. Image: Tanica
The restaurant opened in September inside the hotel’s conservatory, a room of palms and green velvet banquettes, with a kitchen that leans on modern Asian flavours. Its regular calendar already runs a three-course weekday set lunch at S$48++, served in 60 minutes with complimentary hotel parking, and a Sunday Table spread from S$98++ with salads, charcuterie, cheeses and pastries. The two Christmas menus are its first festive additions.
The Christmas Eve dinner
The dinner on Thursday, 24 December, opens with a welcome glass of Champagne to toast the season. The first course is a char-grilled rock lobster tart, followed by a confit of Hokkaido scallop. Tea-smoked duck breast is the main course, and the meal closes on a pandan and coconut dessert.
It is a fixed menu rather than a choice of dishes per course, so anyone in your group who avoids shellfish will want to ask the restaurant before booking, since two of the four courses are built on lobster and scallop.
Small plates on a Tanica table, the image the restaurant uses for its Christmas Brunch. Image: Tanica
The Christmas Brunch
The brunch, on Friday, 25 December, takes the restaurant’s weekly brunch ritual and serves brunch classics as small plates, brought to the table without limit. Joining those classics, the festive specials are beef striploin, porchetta, roasted fish and truffle mac and cheese.
There are three drinks tiers:
• S$128++ with juices, soft drinks, coffee and tea
• S$198++ with flowing wines, selected cocktails and spirits
• S$228++ with flowing Champagne
What Tanica has not yet published is the seating times for either meal or a price for children, and no parking arrangement has been given for the Christmas meals. Tanica has also not named the Champagne for either Christmas meal; the regular Sunday Table pours Louis Roederer Collection 246 NV, alongside red and white wines and selected cocktails.
The dining room at Tanica, inside The Singapore EDITION on Cuscaden Road. Image: Tanica
Tables are booked through the reserve link on Tanica’s site, by phone on +65 6329 5000, or by email at tanica.sgedition@editionhotels.com. The restaurant is at 38 Cuscaden Road, and its regular dinner service runs from 6pm to 10pm on Mondays to Thursdays and to 10.30pm from Friday to Sunday.
summary: Tanica at The Singapore EDITION serves a four-course Christmas Eve dinner at S$165++ and an unlimited small-plates Christmas Brunch from S$128++.
title: Tanica prices its Christmas Eve dinner at S$165++ and a Christmas brunch from S$128++

If you’re wondering what’s happening in Singapore this week, we’ve got you covered. Life moves so fast it’s impossible to stay updated, so we’re bringing you the latest and greatest in food and drinks, entertainment, and viral trends – all in easy-to-read, bite-sized doses! Bookmark this page for your weekly dose, and check out our guide on things to do this weekend in Singapore .
The buzz on what’s happening in Singapore this week
1. Revisit Singapore’s changing streets and memories at Ion Orchard
Ang Ah Tee’s Singapore River (1976, oil on canvas). Photography: Ion Art Gallery
Sometimes, it’s good to look at the past to see how far we’ve come. And from 30 October to 8 November, you can do that at Ang Ah Tee’s free exhibition within Ion Art Gallery . The local artist and Cultural Medallion recipient presents Reminiscence (II), bringing together a selection of his works from the 1990s to the present. All the pieces explore how, over the course of more than five decades, places and experiences have shaped the painter’s art.
The exhibition moves from Chinatown , Ann Siang Hill and Marina Bay to landscapes inspired by his travels across Asia and Europe. Fun fact: the exhibition’s first iteration was presented thirteen years ago at the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts and features more than 50 works.
2. An American comic strip icon pops up in Singapore
Photography: National Library & Archives Board
The National Library & Archives Board is really going all out to encourage more people to read – and we’re so here for it. But how are they doing that? By inviting everyone to the Snoopy pop-up library, which calls Plaza Singapura home from now until 19 September 2027. Swing by and browse through 10,000 physical and digital books, and make yourself comfortable at any corner within the themed space.
Need book recs? Head to the iconic booth, ask a few fun questions, and you’ll get a list in the form of a printed bookmark. How cool! Visitors can enter the library by scanning their library-compliant ID card or NLB eCard. Alternatively, they can request a QR code day pass using a locally registered mobile number or e-mail.
3. Annyeonghaseyo, from Singapore to South Korea!
Photography: Konrad Ziemlewski via Unsplash
Is South Korea your top travel destination? YouTrip sees you, and that’s why the multi-currency digital wallet is giving away 100 return flight tickets to Korea! Existing users, just tap “join now” on the in-app banner and spend $500 with your YouTrip card. Not a YouTrip user? Well, download the app and sign up using the promo code “FLY100KR”.
31 winners – each receiving three flight tickets to South Korea – will be announced on 31 December. The remaining tickets will be given away through two upcoming initiatives. Stay tuned to the brand’s social media accounts to find out what those will be!
4. This is your sign to discover SingLit titles
Photography: BuySingLit
Speaking of reading, here’s another exciting initiative worth checking out. Taking place from 2 to 8 November at VivoCity is the inaugural Singapore Book Street , jointly masterminded by the National Arts Council and the Singapore Book Publishers Association. Touted as the largest book fair for SingLit, here’s where you can discover and purchase homegrown titles – and yes, you can use your SG Culture Pass for this.
Plus, visitors can look forward to over 30 literacy and interactive programmes, including exclusive book launches and opportunities to meet local authors and illustrators.
5. Oriental Kopi brings its taro creations across the border
Taro egg tart, taro polo bun and ayam masak merah. Photography: Yuki Ling
Taro fans, you can now skip the hassle of travelling to Johor Bahru and enjoy Oriental Kopi ’s iconic creations in sunny Singapore. From now till 30 November, the taro egg tart and taro polo bun will be available at all three locations (Bugis Junction, Nex and Westgate).
The taro egg tart ($3) puts a spin on the crowd-favourite Oriental egg tart. Bite into the 128-layer flaky pastry to reveal tender egg custard and creamy Taiwanese Dajia taro paste. We also recommend trying the taro polo bun ($5.80). Think of a divine combination of smooth taro paste and thick slabs of chilled butter, all encased in a soft, warm bun. To wash it all down, order the two limited-time sour plum drinks in lychee and passion fruit variations.
Baked goodies aside, Oriental Kopi also welcomes a new permanent menu item: the ayam masak merah (from $11.60), served with a choice of nasi biryani, nasi lemak, mee siam or kampung mee hoon. The mee siam is our pick for a more flavourful carb pairing. But a fair warning: the ayam masak merah packs a real spice punch!
6. Singapore’s largest nature film festival returns for its third edition
Film still of The Last Place on Earth. Image from Earth in Focus

body:
The menu said “curated for 2”.
Looking at the dishes on our table at 11Westside, that seemed like a useful reminder. This was a sharing menu. Kevin was entitled to some of it too.
I joined Kevin for a media tasting at 11Westside in Asia Square Tower 1 on 22 October. Arranged through COCO PR, the visit introduced the restaurant’s new menu, with Mexican-inspired dishes ranging from tableside guacamole to chicken fajitas.
We were there at lunchtime, although the invitation described this as a preview of the new dinner menu.
The plan for lunch. Sharing is in the small print.
The man behind the menu
Before getting into the food, I spoke with Chef Yong Soo Do, Liberty Group’s Group Executive Chef. Born in Korea and raised in Canada, he grew up surrounded by good cooking. His mother’s family were chefs, but they discouraged him from following them. He started washing dishes at an Italian restaurant anyway. A chef gave him the chance to learn, and after 7 years, he was running the kitchen.
Hong Kong broadened his experience across different cuisines. There was also a return to his roots: when an opportunity to cook Korean food arose, he turned to his mother and aunts for their recipes. Eventually, his work expanded from creating dishes to developing restaurant concepts, including helping bring 11Westside to Singapore.
His comparison stayed with me: a chef is an artist, while running a restaurant means organising the whole show. Food, service, atmosphere and commercial realities all need attention. He now has a deeper respect for humble eateries that keep customers returning for decades. That is the kind of lasting business he wants to help build.
An overhead photograph is useful when lunch takes up this much table.
First, a little theatre at the table
Someone else does the preparation. I handle the chips.
The tableside guacamole gives you something to watch before you start eating. The tasting menu describes avocados mashed to order with lime, coriander, onion and jalapeño, served with house-fried tortilla chips.
The preparation takes place beside the table, with the bowl of guacamole becoming part of the spread.
Kevin has a front-row seat. The chips are standing by.
It is a fitting way to begin a meal built around sharing. The chips, guacamole and other dishes sit in the middle, ready for everyone to help themselves.
The chip has a fairly important job here.
Two bowls of chips. Someone has planned ahead.
Choriqueso and a reason to keep the chips nearby
Alongside the guacamole was choriqueso , a combination of melted cheeses, Mexican chorizo and caramelised onion.
Before the cheese pull, a closer look at what is in the pan.
It arrived in a dark pan, with the chorizo and garnish in the centre of the cheese. Lifting a chip gave us a chance to capture the cheese stretch.
My contribution to the cheese-pull photograph: try not to drop it.
This is where a sharing meal becomes quite practical. You already have the chips. Now there is another pan to put them to work.
The guacamole and choriqueso also make a useful visual contrast: a bowl of chunky green avocado beside a pan of melted cheese. Both belong in the centre of the table.
Corn that deserves its own plate
The Baja Corn Elote came as long sections of grilled corn, arranged around a portion of sauce.
According to the tasting menu, the dish brings together sweet corn, Baja spice, brown butter, lime, cotija cheese and chipotle mayonnaise.
A short break from chips. Still eating with my hands.
The presentation makes it easy to see the seasoning and char on the corn. It also gives the corn a place of its own in the meal, rather than leaving it as something squeezed beside a main course.
Three tacos, then the fajitas
Our tasting menu listed 3 tacos.
The Beef Cheek Taco pairs slow-cooked pulled wagyu beef cheek with Monterey Jack cheese and beef consommé. The consommé comes separately, giving this dish another element beyond the tortilla and filling.
The taco brought a little company.
The Baja Fish Taco uses beer-battered fish with cabbage slaw, pico de gallo and chipotle aioli.
The Pollo Asado Taco brings grilled marinated chicken together with salsa roja, coriander and red onion.
The chicken continued with Sizzling Chicken Fajitas , served with sautéed vegetables, warm tortillas, crema, pico de gallo and guacamole.
Some assembly required. Fortunately, this is lunch.
A tortilla goes on the plate, followed by the filling and toppings. There is a little more participation involved than simply picking up a finished taco.
It suits the way this menu is served. Several dishes, a shared table and a meal you put together as you go.
The next taco is in my hands. Literally.
There is room for one more spoonful. Probably.
A mural worth looking up for
Between the food photographs, I also took several pictures of the large mural beside the booth seating.
Remember to look up from lunch occasionally.
…
summary: My 11Westside media tasting with Kevin: tableside guacamole, tacos, chicken fajitas and Chef Yong Soo Do’s journey from dishwasher to restaurant development.
title: My 11Westside Visit: Tableside Guacamole, Tacos and the Man Behind the Menu

Bugis Junction is one of my favourite haunts. It’s plonked right in the heart of Singapore’s downtown area and enjoys direct connectivity to Bugis MRT.
Many people have fond memories of grooving on the DDR (Dance Dance Revolution) machine at the arcade, rocking their oversized shirts and baggy JNCO jeans like it was nobody’s business!
This sprawling mall has close to 200 shops spread across 3 floors and a basement, and no matter the time or day, it always seems to be packed with a mixture of families, tourists, young teenagers out on dates, and working adults fleeting from meeting to meeting.
How I chose these best food spots in Bugis Junction
These are the 3 main criteria I used to decide which eateries to recommend:
• Variety : I picked eateries which offer a range of cuisines so you can pick what’s best suited for you.
• Wide price range : From more affordable eats to premium eats, there’s something for everyone.
• Independent businesses : I included brands with a smaller presence rather than big chains widely available around Singapore.
If you’re shopping your heart out and feeling peckish, this guide is for you. Here are our 12 best food spots in Bugis Junction for a yummilicious meal .

Thachang is a Thai restaurant with a vibrant and nostalgic atmosphere. The restaurant exudes a retro Thai market aesthetic with its array of Thai flags, a tuk-tuk on display and old-school gachapon machines. Besides the standard fried rice and noodles, Thachang also serves hot pot and boat noodles alongside other beloved sides.
Credit – Thachang
One of my favourites on the menu is the Beef Boat Noodle (S$11.90++) . I like how this dish is entirely customisable: from soup or dry preparation, to spicy or non-spicy, to a choice of 4 different noodle types. body:
A new local fusion Western hawker has officially landed in Little India ! Opened and run by an ex-restaurant chef, Botak Western has set up shop at 638 Veerasamy Road . It boasts an extensive menu composed primarily of hearty Western fare with an innovative local twist, and has already caught the attention of neighbourhood foodies.
Credit – Chen Melvin via Google Reviews
Chef Gino, the talented ex-restaurant chef behind the grill, pairs his work experience in Italian fine dining with bold Asian influences to create original recipes. He shared that opening a hawker stall was a longtime dream and is driven by a straightforward philosophy. “Having worked in restaurants previously, I’ve always believed that good-quality food shouldn’t have to come with a high price tag.”
Chef Gino’s ultimate mission with Botak Western remains clear — “to bring restaurant-quality food to the heartlands at affordable prices, so that everyone can enjoy a good meal without spending too much.” With Chef Gino at the helm, you can expect nothing less than professional cooking techniques and high-quality ingredients. The menu punches way above its price tag, with generous portions and great taste.
Credit – Botak Western
The Pan Seared Barramundi (S$16.80) comes beautifully crispy with white, perfectly flaky flesh served over roasted potatoes and vegetables in a creamy white wine and butter cream sauce. The fillet portion looks generous and hearty, with the dish reminiscent of something you’d find in an upscale restaurant setting.
Credit – Botak Western
If you’re in the mood for a truly unique fusion dish, check out their signature Sarawak Chicken Curry Shepherd Pie (S$10.80) . Underneath the crispy baked mashed potato crust lies a bed of deeply savoury and aromatic Sarawak-style chicken curry. The curry is traditionally prepared with santan — coconut milk — to produce a velvety and smooth texture while imparting a light fragrance to the gravy. The dish is topped off with shavings of mozzarella and parmigiano cheese for added umami .
Credit – Botak Western
Sides lovers, skip the plain fries and grab the Har Cheong Pork Belly (S$8.50) , fried till crisp and golden brown and paired with a punchy cincalok dipping sauce to cut through the unctuousness.
Whether you’re popping in for a quick lunch or a casual weekend treat, this spot proves you don’t need air-con or a fancy setting to enjoy serious restaurant-quality Western eats.
Wok-hei pasta? Woksta opens for just 3 hours daily with fusion spaghetti from $7
summary: Botak Western at 638 Veerasamy Road in Little India delivers restaurant-grade Western mains with local ingredients, helmed by an ex-restaurant chef in a hawker setting. Featuring dishes like crispy Pan-Seared Barramundi at S$16.80, Sarawak Chicken Curry Shepherd's Pie at S$10.80, and Har Cheong Pork Belly at S$8.50, the menu pairs technical culinary execution with kopitiam affordability. It is best suited for diners seeking high-quality fusion fare without restaurant service charges.
title: Sarawak Curry Shepherd’s Pie? Ex-Restaurant Chef opens fusion Hawker Botak Western

Things to do at Golden Mile Tower
When Golden Mile Complex closed in May 2023, Singapore lost one of its best-known Thai enclaves, affectionately dubbed “Little Thailand”. But just next door is its often-overlooked neighbour, Golden Mile Tower , a strata mall that’s home to a mix of niche shops and old-school eateries.
Sure, the mall might hold an eyebrow-raising reputation for its massage parlours, but look beyond that, and you’ll find Thai amulet shops, antique dealers, and indie cinemas worth visiting. With so many unexpected finds under one roof, it’s about time Golden Mile Tower got its moment in the spotlight.
What shops can I find at Golden Mile Tower?
Image credit: Tani Masa via Google Maps
Golden Mile Tower may have just 3 floors of retail shops and another dedicated to a cinema, but there’s still plenty to discover. From niche specialty stores to quirky finds, we’ve rounded up the shops worth checking out and categorised them to make your visit easier.
Old-school F&B outlets
1. Thian Kee Steamboat
74-year-old steamboat restaurant
Image credit: Victor Ng via Google Maps
One of the most popular eateries at Golden Mile Tower is Golden Mile Thien Kee Steamboat , tucked away in the mall’s basement. Established in 1952, this old-school eatery is one of Singapore’s few surviving spots for authentic Hainanese steamboat.
Image credit: EatSleepChyll L via Google Maps
Their hearty steamboat sets start at $38 and include 16 side dishes and meats, all served in a comforting chicken-based broth.
Image credit: Ma Ranchy via Google Maps
They are also known for their Hainanese chicken rice , served with tender poached chicken from just $4 . Alongside a range of zi char classics, the eatery has been drawing diners from across the island for decades.

body:
Changing of Guards Ceremony at The Istana
When it comes to events that warrant road closures on the Little Red Dot, 2 major ones float to mind immediately – the recently concluded F1 Grand Prix and the annual National Day Parade. As grand as they are, they only come around once a year, but what if I told you there’s another spectacle that takes place smack dab in the middle of Orchard Road almost every month?
Complete with a marching contingent, live military bands, and impressive rifle drills, the Changing of Guards Ceremony at the Istana is a free parade that you might not even know existed. Here’s all you need to know before heading down to catch the next one yourself, from dates to what to expect.
When & where does the Changing of Guards Ceremony take place?
The Changing of Guards Ceremony typically takes place on the first Sunday evening of the month , at 6pm . Lasting 30 minutes , the ceremony follows a short marching route along Orchard Road, starting from Koek Road which is just beside OG Orchard Point, and ends at the Istana ’s Main Gate . Viewing of the ceremony is free .
You can find the schedule of the Changing of Guards Ceremony on the official Istana website , which lists upcoming ceremony dates. The next Changing of Guards Ceremony happening this year will take place on 6th December 2026 .
What is the Changing of Guards Ceremony?
The Changing of Guards Ceremony at the Istana is a military tradition that dates back to 1959 , when the late Yusof Bin Ishak took up appointment as the Yang Di-Pertuan Negara, the then official title of the head of state of Singapore.
Image credit: National Archives of Singapore
Back then, the Istana was under the watchful guard of combat troops from Singapore’s only infantry regiment at the time, the 1st Battalion of the Singapore Infantry Regiment. In case you’re wondering, the Little Red Dot’s army has grown considerably over the years, and is now defended by 6 active infantry battalions.
The use of combat troops to guard the Istana ceased in 1968. Today, a 20-man strong platoon from the Singapore Armed Forces Military Police Command takes their place, each specially selected and trained to carry out sentry duties on the grounds on a monthly rotational basis.
The parade is based on the UK’s Changing of the Guard ceremony held at Buckingham Palace.
Image credit: The Singapore Army via Facebook
As for the Changing of Guard Ceremony itself, a total of 36 guards and 2 guard commanders will march from Koek Road to meet the outgoing guards at the Istana’s main entrance . Accompanied by military bands , a symbolic parade of handing over duties is then carried out, followed by a rifle precision drill performed by the guards.
What to expect at the Changing of Guards Ceremony?
Although the Changing of Guards Ceremony is free to observe, you won’t find it to be terribly crowded, perhaps because not many locals even know of its existence.
We recommend heading down to Cuppage Road , right outside of The Centrepoint, at around 5.45pm to catch the marching contingent getting ready. You’ll get to walk alongside the military band and mobilised Military Police Traffic Outriders and snap pics with them as they make their way to Koek Road where the ceremony officially begins.
Image credit: @orh.snap via Instagram
Once it does, you’ll have to keep your distance, as the military band comes alive with a symphony of organised drumbeats and brass instruments. Led by the Military Police Command’s Silent Precision Drill Squad (SPDS) , they’ll begin their journey to the Istana; it’s a rare sight to behold, as the hectic traffic of Orchard Road gives way to rows of uniformed soldiers all marching in unison.
All of the SPDS’ routine is performed without verbal c ommands, hence their name, tapping into hours upon hours of training.
Image credit: @orh.snap via Instagram
Upon reaching the Istana’s Main Gate, the ceremonial handover will be conducted, and then it closes out with another highlight of the ceremony – the rifle precision drills. Here, the SPDS takes centre stage, as they pull off synchronised, elaborate rifle drills, including stunts such as twirling their firearms and tossing them into the air, before catching them deftly.
Attend the next Changing of Guards ceremony along Orchard Road
If you can’t quite wait till National Day to catch a glimpse of our dapper servicemen marching down the asphalt, swing by Orchard Road the next time the Changing of Guards Ceremony comes to town. Moreover, it’s free to attend, which means you don’t have to go through the hassle of balloting for tickets or braving the crowds at the Padang.
Find out more about the Ceremonial Guards
For more free things to do in Singapore:
• 44 free things to do in Singapore
• Snoopy Library pop-up at Plaza Singapura
• A Walk Through Time exhibition
Cover image adapted from: @orh.snap via Instagram
summary: If you didn't get tickets to the NDP, here's the next best thing.
title: There’s A Parade Along Orchard Road Happening Throughout The Year That Most Singaporeans Don’t Know Exist

Best places to pump petrol in Singapore
When it comes to owning a car in Singapore, bidding and paying for the dreaded COE is not the only thing that’ll take a hefty chunk out of your bank balance. There are maintenance costs, parking fees, and road taxes to factor into your monthly vehicular expenditure, but most importantly, petrol.
How else is your hunk of metal supposed to move from point A to B? But, with political unrest happening elsewhere across the globe, gas prices have been on the rise lately, so a full top-up now is no doubt costly. Here are some of the best places to pump petrol in Singapore , along with the best petrol station brand, credit card, and loyalty programme “combos” to get the most mileage out of your money.
Where to get the cheapest petrol in Singapore?
Image credit: Esso Singapore
If you’re a frequent driver on Singapore’s roads, you would already be familiar with the common petrol station brands. There are 5 main ones to choose from – Shell , Esso , Caltex , SPC , Sinopec – and each comes with its own perks when refuelling with them. There are also smaller names with just a handful of stations peppered around the island too, like Cnergy and Smart Energy .

You can download the Consumer’s Association of Singapore ’s Price Kaki app ( App Store | Google Play ) to stay up to date with listed pump prices across the major petrol station brands in Singapore.
Image adapted from: Price Kaki
Simply hit the “Fuel” tab on the home page, and you’ll be shown tables comparing the prices of the different grades of fuel across the various petrol station brands. Tap on “Search stations” at the top, and you can see which stations are near you, along with listed pump prices; super handy for planning your next refuelling trip.
However, the prices for newer petrol station brands like Cnergy and Smart Energy are a little trickier to find; they’re not listed on the Price Kaki app. You can visit the Smart Energy website for updated pump prices, but as for Cnergy, your best bet is to keep tabs on their Facebook and Instagram pages for the latest rates and promotions, or head down to one of their stations to see for yourself.

These come with a whole host of perks, ranging from exclusive deals and vouchers for F&B items at their stations’ convenience store, discounts on car servicing products , and a fuss-free method to pay for your gas . About to kickstart your BTO reno and decor project? Or you just want to breathe some new life into your home? If these are part of your year-end plans, mark your calendars for the Shopee 11.11 Big Sale: we’ve got word there’ll be lots of great deals on Shopee Home across all home and living categories.
Sofas, bed frames, computer chairs… You name it. So if there’s a cute coffee table you’ve been eyeing or sitting in your cart, take this as a sign to cart it out, stat. And if you’re just browsing, we’ve rounded up some of the fab deals we saw here.
Shopee 11.11 2026 sale: Best home and living deals
1. Lounge and chill: Cellini’s Hemma fabric convertible sofa bed
Photography: Cellini
You need a guest bed, but you’re not always expecting guests. Something like Cellini’s Hemma fabric convertible sofa bed could fit the bill. With the size of a super single when opened flat to bed mode, this minimalist sofa bed fits nicely in your living or guest room. When there’s no guest, just set it to recline or sofa mode – there, all ready for some Netflix and chill time.
2. Sleep well: Woosa’s pillow
Photography: Woosa
When it comes to bedding and everything you need for a good night’s sleep, you can’t go wrong with Woosa. Woosa pillows come in four shapes and sizes, designed to complement your preferred sleep positions. There’s even a long pillow that couples can share comfortably – how about that?
3. Statement piece with storage: Yeswood’s Vista oak wood coffee table with moru glass
Photography: Yeswood
Nail that cosy Scandinavian home look with the Vista coffee table from Yeswood . Yeswood is a leading solid wood furniture brand from China, known for crafting beautiful home pieces from North American FAS grade oak wood that won’t break the bank. Functionality, aesthetics, and affordability – we stan this.
4. Save on bedroom space: Megafurniture’s Devonne grey fabric storage bed
Photography: Megafurniture
Need ample bedroom space? This storage bed might just be your wish come true. Megafurniture’s Devonne fabric storage bed comes with really generous storage space within the divan platform. Another plus point? Thanks to the powerful hydraulic system, you barely need to flex your muscles to lift the mattress and access your hidden stash.
5. Walk on clouds: Cozylant’s Olivia rug
Photography: Cozylant
Rugs can give your space a warm, inviting feel. Plus, a really good rug feels comfy and absorbs noise (your neighbours will thank you). For easy maintenance, look no further than Cozylant’s water-resistant Olivia rug . It’s easy to clean and maintain, durable, and feels oh-so-soft underfoot. Bliss!
6. Solo lounging spot: Caler Home’s Axer fabric manual recliner armchair
Photography: Caler Home
Always wanted an armchair that’s yours and yours alone? Treat yourself to the Axer recliner armchair from Caler Home , a perfect spot to put your feet up (for real), sit back, and relax. Trust us, it’s worth the splurge.

Why trust this guide
Every year, during Christmas, our team combs through the festive menus, gift sets, hampers, and turkey and log cake offerings. We compare notes, taste menus where we can, and research everything else, so you don’t have to spend time figuring out what’s worth spending your money on. Hi Bowl is a new malatang concept by Haidilao
Image credit: Hi Bowl
Singaporeans can’t seem to get enough of malatang (for good reason), and luckily for us, a new spot is coming to town. Hi Bowl is a malatang concept by the legendary Haidilao, so you know it’s going to be the real deal.
Pork Blood Curd Returns To SG After 27 Years—Here’s A Sneak Preview
Opening on 3 November 2026 in Rochor, the new restaurant offers over 100 ingredients to choose from. Night owls will also be happy to hear that it stays open till 1am daily, making it a perfect spot for a midnight meal.
Im age credit: Ryan Wang via Google Maps
For those who love trying new foods, you can look forward to less-common ingredients and seasonal items such as purple radish, black tofu, ice plant, carrot noodles and more.
Image credit: Bim Bim via Google Maps
After taking your pick, you can further customise with five soup bases and two dry bases. Soup lovers can go for Mala Milk Soup Base , Golden Sichuan Pickles Soup Base , Sichuan Mala Soup Base , Tomato Soup Base , and Golden Collagen Soup Base .
Image credit: @capygoeswhere
Alternatively, dry options include the Dongbei Creamy Mala Mix and Signature Mala Mix . Prices are charged at $2.98 per 100g . And if things get a little too heated, you can even get free-flow soft drinks for an affordable $2++.
Unlike its competitors, Hi Bowl also serves fried skewers and sides. You’ll find a variety, with vegetable skewers at $1++ each, while pork , beef , chicken , and lamb skewers are $1.50++ each.
You’ll also find Fried Shrimp Prawn Paste Chicken Wings ($8.80++) and Fried Crispy Pork ($8.80++) . The most unique, however, is the Fried Milk ($4.80++) , a traditional Cantonese dessert featuring a sweet milky custard, battered, then deep-fried.
Image credit: Hi Bowl
Don’t miss out on the opening promotions: get 50% off a second bowl on 3 November 2026 , 40% off a second bowl on 4 November 2026 , and 30% off a second bowl on 5 November 2026 . These deals are valid for dine-in only.
If you’re looking for affordable eats in the city, check out these cheap food places in the CBD for mains under $20. And for more exciting new openings, here are the best new restaurants and cafes in November 2026 .

body:
Starbucks x Pompompurin collab launches on 10 November
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
Sanrio fans, clear some shelf space. Starbucks Singapore is teaming up with Pompompurin for an exclusive Singapore merch collection, dropping on 10 November 2026 . The timing isn’t random. Starbucks is marking 30 years in Singapore, and the golden retriever in the brown beret turns 30 this year too.
Starbucks x Winnie The Pooh Collection To Drop On 20 Oct: Tumblers, Bags And More
It’s been a busy year for character collabs at the coffee chain. Starbucks’ Mofusand collab returned earlier this year, and Winnie the Pooh got his own honeypot-themed lineup just last month. This time, Pompompurin gets the barista treatment: green aprons, mini drink cups, and plenty of coffee-themed details across eight pieces.
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
The star of the lineup is the Pompompurin + Starbucks Plush . He’s dressed in a green barista-style apron with his signature beret, which makes him a clear pick for collectors. If you want something smaller to carry around, the Plush Keychain shrinks him down to bag-charm size, with a little whipped cream drink in his paws.
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
The Furry Pouch is shaped like Pompompurin’s fluffy face and beret. Judging from the press photos, it looks roomy enough for everyday bits such as earbuds, keys, and cards.
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
Meanwhile, the Reusable Bag with Canvas Pouch is a foldable shopper printed all over with tiny Pompompurins and Starbucks drinks.
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
For your daily coffee, there’s a 12oz Ceramic Mug with Pompompurin hugging a cup, and a 20oz Stainless Steel Tumbler in cream with scattered drink motifs. The 16oz Glass Cold Cup is the most eye-catching of the lot: a matcha-green glass cup with a small Pompompurin figure perched on the lid. Rounding things off is a Ceramic Plate Set in deep green and pastel yellow.
Prices for the aforementioned items are yet to be released.
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
Collectors, here’s the catch. The Pompompurin + Starbucks Phone Lanyard with Charms Blind Bag ($9.90) can only be bought together with another purchase. There are three designs to collect, and each one pairs a Pompompurin charm with a Starbucks drink charm on cream, mint, or brown straps. The charms come off, so you can mix and match them or use them on their own. You can buy up to six blind bags per person, in stores and on the Starbucks Online Store.
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
The full collection goes on sale on 10 November 2026 in all Starbucks stores, on the Starbucks Online Store from 10am, and on LazMall from 12pm. Each customer can buy up to six pieces per item, while stocks last.

body:
Yeah Gelato opens a new outlet at Jurong Point
Here’s a piece of good news for Westies: Yeah Gelato just launched its 7th outlet in Jurong Point , alongside three unconventional flavour releases. The Black Vinegar Gelato ($9.80++) , Mala Peanut Gelato ($9.80++) , and Misty Green Gelato ($7.80++) have soft-launched at the new outlet and will be available islandwide from 4 November 2026 .
Yeah Gelato: Viral Chinese Chain Opens At Plaza Singapura With Pistachio And Durian Flavours
The Beijing-born gelato brand first opened its doors in Singapore in June 2025 and has since exploded in popularity due to its fresh, daily-made gelato and premium ingredients. Curious about the bold new flavours, we headed down to give them a try.
The three new flavours came with Yeah Gelato’s signature peaks. The Mala Peanut was garnished with fried pieces of chilli, an interesting touch for a dessert.
I was most curious about the Black Vinegar, though I had my doubts about the unusual flavour combination. Surprisingly, it ended up being my favourite.
The tangy vinegar flavour was noticeable, yet subtle. The addition of cream cheese mellowed out its sharpness, resulting in unexpected caramel-like notes.
The Mala Peanut was another interesting number. It ended up tasting like peanut butter-flavoured gelato, with a mala aroma in the background. It reminded me of a thick, nutty, peanut-sesame dipping sauce that I would enjoy alongside a spicy bowl of mala, but in gelato form.
Of course, I had to try it with the fried chilli—it turned out to be crunchy and sweet with barely a hint of spice. The crunch and slight savouriness added a nice contrast to the creamy, sweet gelato.
The Misty Green Gelato is the most familiar flavour, made with matcha and green tea, which sets it apart from other matcha products. Personally, I could pick up on both flavours, though subtly. The green tea added a roasted, nutty flavour profile that complemented the earthy matcha notes.
We also tried out some of Yeah Gelato’s existing signatures. If you’re new to the brand, its Pistachio Gelato ($9.80++) is a fan favourite. While I’m not a pistachio fan, I immediately understood the hype. The pistachio flavour was rich and pronounced, with just the right amount of sweetness to balance its nuttiness.
Another best-seller worth trying is the Premium Rice Gelato ($7.80++) .
We also tried the Vanilla Gelato ($7.80++) , which is a staple in every gelato store. This one was speckled with real vanilla beans, giving it a rich, fragrant flavour. And the Hawthorn Gelato ($7.80++) hit me with a wave of nostalgia, as it tasted just like the hawthorn flakes that I’d snack on as a child.
The cafe in Jurong Point had a nice, calming ambience, with wooden furniture and beige walls, designed to mirror the serenity of a Chinese rice field.
To celebrate the new launch, Yeah Gelato is offering a 1-for-1 promotion at the Jurong Point outlet from 6 November to 8 November 2026, and 50% off a second cup from 9 November to 12 November 2026 .
On the topic of gelato, check out CHAGEE’s new gelato series , with eight new tea-inspired flavours. While you’re in Jurong, here’s a guide to some Jurong East food gems worth trying.

body:
Casa Vostra is opening at Wisma Atria with famous pizza
Fans of Italian food would likely already be familiar with Casa Vostra . When they first opened at Raffles City back in 2024, the queues stretched out the door—some waiting over an hour just to get a table. Since then, they’ve expanded to JEM and Tampines Mall , giving more diners a chance to try their offerings.
Image credit: Casa Vostra
If you still haven’t made the trip, good news: Casa Vostra is opening their fourth outlet at Wisma Atria , so those who work in the area can get a taste of their new outlet-exclusive menu items. Look forward to their trademarked Roman SquareCrunch Pizza , as well as mascarpone gelato served in a crunchy pastry cone, in collaboration with Mediterranean-Levantine restaurant Petra.
We Visited Casa Vostra Again To See If The Italian Restaurant Fared Better
For those unfamiliar, Casa Vostra is a casual Italian dining concept by Mission Group and Chef Antonio Miscellaneo, the same chef behind La Bottega Enoteca, which is widely regarded as Singapore’s top pizzeria.
What makes the food here different is how it’s made. The pizza dough is cold-fermented and the pasta hand-rolled, with ingredients either sourced directly from Italy or made in-house. Their pizzas come in three styles: Newpolitan Red , which has a San Marzano tomato base, Newpolitan White , featuring a cheese base, and the Doublecrunch , essentially a pizza-sandwich hybrid.
When we visited their OG outlet in 2025, we tried the Peposo ($22++) —braised beef cheek served with rosemary roasted potatoes and finished with black pepper. We also enjoyed the Crab Tagliatelle ($26++) , generously loaded with sweet crab flesh and tossed in a savoury mix of olive oil, garlic, and butter.
On the pizza side, the Tartufo e Funghi ($28++) is a must for truffle fans, topped with fresh black truffle, mushrooms, and a drizzle of truffle oil over a base of Fior di Latte and Taleggio. And if you’re in the mood for something sweet and savoury, the Prosciutto e Figura ($27++) —Parma ham, fig puree, rocket and walnuts on freshly baked dough—holds its own as one of the best pies on the menu.
The new outlet boasts an 85-seater open-plan space, perfect for date nights or a meal out with the fam. Do note that the restaurant operates on a walk-in only basis, so it’s best to head down early to beat the queue.
For more good food in the area, read our Orchard food guide or Somerset food guide . If you’re looking for more Italian food, our guide to the best Italian restaurants in Singapore has got you covered .

Opening hours: TBD

If you love animals but don’t have a furry or feathery friend at home, pet cafes are the perfect option. Image credit: Thanathip Moolvong via Google Maps
What The Pug , Singapore’s first pug cafe, opened in 2022. You can play with 12 charming pugs, each with a unique personality. Entry costs $25 on weekdays and $28 on weekends for a 45-minute session, which includes a canned drink and a souvenir photo.
Image credit: Steven Masi via Google Maps
Guests are greeted by the enthusiastic pugs as they rush out from behind a small gate, creating an exciting atmosphere. The cafe caters to all visitors, offering both playful pups for active fun and older pugs for a relaxed cuddle experience.

Tel: 6293 3350
Website

Snow Pawttage is a new pet cafe in Joo Chiat that is dedicated to the lovable dog breed, the Samoyed. Unlike the rounder Chow Chow or smaller Pomeranian, these fluffy white pups are eager for belly rubs and treats. Visitors can cuddle and play with them for 45 minutes at $45 p er person . Do take note that you’ll need to purchase an admission ticket beforehand.
Image credit: NAhtAXi via Google Maps
Here, every Samoyed is a bonafide su-paw-star, with each one having their own quirks and personalities. Also, each doggo has their tail dyed a special colour so the owners can tell them apart! While dog treats are available for purchase at $10 , the cafe doesn’t serve food or drinks for the humans.

Image credit: Cafe Moshikomu via Google Maps
If you’re feeling peckish, fret not, as there’s a wide range of dishes you can choose from. Get the Mr Jamon Sunny Sandwich ($17++) , which comes loaded with a sunny-side-up egg and Jamon Iberico pork slices. Wash it all down with their Kuromitsu ($7++) , an iced latte with Japanese sugar syrup.

Their signature dish is the Stray Chicken Rice (price TBD) : a marinated grilled chicken chop, served alongside a heap of chicken rice, a dollop of sambal, and a sunny-side-up egg. body:
When it comes to Middle Eastern cuisine in Malaysia, I think most of us have a certain picture in mind: something heavily spiced, flavourful, colourful, and, most importantly, made for sharing. At Mezze Mazi , a cosy neighbourhood pork-free eatery in Ara Damansara , the concept of sharing plates is the main focus.
Specialising in Levantine cuisine, this little eatery is tucked among several other dining spots in the neighbourhood. Its interior makes it a nice place to settle down for a meal with friends and loved ones, without anything feeling too formal or stuffy.
What to order at Mezze Mazi
Despite having just a single sheet of menu printed on both sides, it still took us quite a while to decide what to order. We eventually settled on Hummus (RM25) with Flatbread (RM10) , Maroulosalata (RM18) , Spring Chicken (RM29 for half) , Falafel (RM15) , and a glass of Sparkling House Lemonade (RM15) .
Hummus is easily one of my favourite dips of all time. I’m talking top-tier, keep-thinking-about-it-after-the-meal kind of favourite. A really good bowl of hummus can occupy my thoughts for an embarrassingly long time, so I was particularly keen to try theirs.
Mezze Mazi’s version looked incredibly inviting, with thick, smooth chickpea hummus topped with tarator, whole boiled chickpeas, green and black olives, homemade pickles, red onions, za’atar, and olive oil. I liked how the flavours stayed true to the main ingredients, allowing the chickpeas and tarator to shine instead of relying too heavily on spices, smokiness, or other additions. The pickles were a particularly nice touch, adding a little tanginess to each bite.
My only complaint was the flatbread. Despite being freshly made, it was surprisingly tough. Having made more flatbreads than I can count, especially for large family gatherings, I’d say the dough measurements could use a little tweaking. It’s a shame because the hummus itself was lovely, and a softer flatbread would have made the pairing so much better.
The Maroulosalata is a simple salad made with crunchy lettuce, mint, Akkawi cheese, za’atar, and a dressing of lemon, olive oil, and honey. Nothing particularly complicated, but I found myself reaching for it more than expected. Akkawi is also a good choice here, especially if you enjoy feta but aren’t particularly fond of its stronger, richer taste.
I have to give Mezze Mazi’s Spring Chicken a special trophy of some sort. Served as sliced portions of a half chicken, including the leg, breast, and wing, it comes with charred skin, coriander hot sauce, and toum . Frankly, this chicken is stuff dreams are made of. If you’ve ever struggled to find properly juicy roasted chicken, you might want to give this a try.
The chicken is brined so well that even the breast meat is incredibly tender and juicy, almost tasting like your usual thigh meat. The coriander hot sauce has a pretty serious kick, so those with a lower spice tolerance might want to take it easy. The toum , meanwhile, is creamy without being too rich, although I would’ve liked a stronger garlic flavour.
10 new places in JB to check out this Nov 2026 — cafes, food & more
Falafel is another dish I tend to approach with caution when dining out in Malaysia. It’s frustratingly easy to get wrong, but Mezze Mazi does a good job of getting the basics right.
Cutting into one, I was genuinely pleased to find a vibrant green interior instead of the muddy brown centre I’ve encountered at other places. The chickpea and parsley mixture was flavourful, soft and crumbly inside, with a crunchy exterior that wasn’t tough or overly dry. Served with toum , these were seriously good.
The Sparkling House Lemonade was refreshing, with a pronounced lemon flavour and a subtle hint of herbs. A nice drink to have alongside the meal.
Who is Mezze Mazi best for?
The sharing-style menu makes it a good choice for dates, family meals, or catching up with friends. I’d recommend coming with a few people so you can order several dishes and have a taste of everything.
How to get to Mezze Mazi?
Getting here is easiest by car, as public transport isn’t particularly convenient. Parking can also be a bit of a nightmare, so do factor in some extra time to find a spot.
Do we recommend Mezze Mazi?
Yes! I’d happily return for the spring chicken and falafel , and that’s saying something when I usually have a hard time deciding what to order on a second visit. The flatbread could do with some improvement, but the hummus is enjoyable and the chicken is genuinely worth coming back for. If you’re in Ara Damansara and feel like something deliciously comforting, Mezze Mazi is worth adding to your list.
People also read:
What to eat at Ombak KLCC?
Where to get the best halal ramen in KL?
summary: Mezze Mazi is a pork-free Levantine eatery in Ara Damansara, Malaysia, serving sharing plates suited to meals with friends, family or a date. Prices range from RM10 for flatbread to RM29 for half a spring chicken, with highlights including juicy roasted chicken, crisp falafel and hummus. The neighbourhood spot is best reached by car, though limited parking may require extra time.
title: Mezze Mazi: This cosy Levantine eatery in PJ gets its hummus, falafel & spring chicken right

Castlery’s Sleep Easy pop-up at Jurong Point
Singapore was unfortunately crowned the world’s most fatigued country in 2021 , so when it’s finally time to get some proper shut-eye, every hour counts, and that starts with choosing the right mattress . But with so many factors to consider, finding one that suits your sleeping preferences will probably take some trial and error.
To make the search a little easier, homegrown furniture brand Castlery is hosting Sleep Easy by Castlery , a sleep pop-up at Jurong Point to help you find your perfect mattress from now till 15th November 2026 . Here’s what you need to know before heading down.
What is the Sleep Easy by Castlery pop-up all about?
Modern furniture brand Castlery recently launched its new Ayrie Mattress Collection , and to celebrate its expansion into the sleep economy, the brand is hosting its first-ever sleep pop-up , Sleep Easy by Castlery. At the heart of the pop-up are 3 mattresses from the Ayrie collection, each catering to different sleeping preferences.
Back sleepers who prefer firmer support may like the Ayrie Mattress (from $999) , while those who enjoy a softer, plusher feel can opt for the Ayrie Plush Mattress (from $2,199) . Somewhere in between is the Ayrie Comfort Mattress (from $1,790) , which offers a balance of comfort and support.
But if you’re not sure which mattress is right for your next sleep upgrade, the pop-up lets you try Castlery mattresses in-person and get a proper feel for which support level and firmness cater to your sleeping habits, before committing to the purchase.
What to expect at the Sleep Easy by Castlery pop-up
Step into a free 15-minute immersive sleep pod
The pop-up’s main highlight is its complimentary immersive sleep pod experience , which features the Ayrie Comfort Mattress. Styled like a cosy bedroom, the fully enclosed space offers a little more intimacy when mattress shopping, so you can unwind without feeling like you’re on display. Each session lasts 15 minutes and can accommodate up to 2 guests .
To start things off, grab a sleep mask from the bedside drawer and make yourself comfortable on the bed.
Then, dim the lights to your liking and relax to the soothing background music . The room is also scented with Castlery’s signature Morning Tea room spray , adding to the calming atmosphere. The Ayrie Comfort Mattress gives you a good reference point for figuring out whether you prefer something firmer or plusher.
As part of the session, you’ll also receive a complimentary 5ml bottle of Morning Tea to take home and freshen your room with.
If you’re interested in trying out the sleep pod for yourself, either walk in and check for available slots at the counter or book a time slot in advance to secure your preferred timing.
Make your own personalised keychain
Besides the sleep pod, head over to the Build Your Dream Charm Station to customise your own keychain and create a personalised keepsake to take home for free .
To get started, simply sign up for The Castlery Club for free and show your membership to the counter. The staff will then guide you through making the keychain.
Choose between a light blue or maroon carabiner , then pair it with a coloured rope that matches your style.
Next, pick 1 of 5 charms that resonates with you the most. Each charm has its own meaning, from prosperity and abundance to love and connection. If you’re not sure which to choose, there’s a handy guide for you to refer to as well.
Finally, top it off with a Castlery tag to complete your dream charm keychain.
Exclusive goodie bags on selected dates
There are extra freebies to grab on selected dates too. Besides the sleep pod experience and free DIY keychain, the first 100 guests to RSVP for 7th , 8th , 9th , 14th , or 15th November 2026 and arrive on each day will be given a Castlery tote bag containing goodies like Moom Health Mellow-Mag Sachets and a Castlery measuring tape .
Learn about Castlery mattresses through room sets & educational zones
There are also 3 curated bedroom sets to explore, each featuring 1 of the Ayrie mattresses. These offer a more straightforward way to try out the mattresses if you’re short on time and can’t spare 15 minutes for the sleep pod experience.
Feel free to sit, lie down, or get into your usual sleeping positions to get a feel for each mattress. You can also take your time to move around and test out features found across the collection, such as the breathable TENCEL Lyocell covers and motion isolation .
There’s also an interactive display that offers a closer look at the layers, materials, and design choices behind the Ayrie collection. You can even touch and press on the individual material samples to get a better sense of how they contribute to the mattress’s overall feel.
Enjoy discounted prices & exclusive gifts with any Ayrie mattress purchase
…
summary: The pop-up is running from now till 15th November 2026.
title: There’s A Castlery Pop-Up At Jurong Point, With A Free Sleep Pod Experience, DIY Charm Keychains & Goodie Bags
