Singapore Book Street 2026
Bookworms, here’s another event to add to your calendar. Singapore Book Street 2026 , happening from now till 8th November 2026 , has landed in VivoCity . The event brings together a massive collection of local literary works, interactive activities, and opportunities to meet the creative minds behind your favourite reads.
Fun fact: This is Singapore’s largest book fair dedicated to SingLit, with over 1,200 titles across 4 languages to browse. We headed down to check out the fair for ourselves, and here’s what you can look forward to.
What can I expect at the Singapore Book Street?
This inaugural fair marks the return of book fairs to the HarbourFront area after several decades. Back in the 1970s and 1980s, the Singapore Festival of Books and Book Fair were held at the former World Trade Centre, now known as HarbourFront Centre .
Browse over 1,200 SingLit titles across 4 languages
If your bookshelf could do with a refresh, you’ll be spoilt for choice at Singapore Book Street 2026. Organised by the National Arts Council (NAC) and Singapore Book Publishers Association (SBPA), the fair showcases over 1,200 SingLit titles in English , Malay , Chinese , and Tamil .
There’s a little something for every kind of reader, with genres spanning fiction, non-fiction, fantasy, poetry, and children’s literature. You’ll also find picture books, educational titles, and heritage books that offer a closer look at Singapore’s culture and history.
Meet the people behind the books
Besides browsing the shelves, visitors can look forward to meeting local authors, illustrators, and poets. There’ll also be book-signing sessions, so keep an eye out for the chance to get your purchases signed by the people who created them.
You will get the chance to meet authors like Janice Khoo , Ames Chan , Ling Yuan , Shirley Ong , Maria Mahat , and more authors from publishers like Epigram Books , Education Publishing House (EPH) , Lingzi Media Pte Ltd , and Shing Lee Publishers . Check out the full list of Singapore Book Street programmes .
Use your SG Culture Pass credits to purchase eligible books
Here’s some good news for those looking to stretch their book-shopping budget. Many titles at Singapore Book Street 2026 are eligible for purchase using SG Culture Pass credits , giving you another way to support Singapore’s literary scene.
To get started, head to the official SG Culture Pass website and log in using Singpass. Complete your profile details and a short survey, and your credits will be automatically disbursed through GovWallet.
Keep a lookout for books with the red SG Culture Pass label – these are the ones that can be purchased using the credits.
Take a reading break at the cosy seating area
After browsing the books, choose to settle down at the fair’s dedicated reading area to take a breather.
Complete with bean bags , tables , and chairs , this cosy corner offers a comfortable space for visitors to flip through their new reads. Families can also sit down together and enjoy some reading time with their little ones.
It’s a welcome spot to rest your feet after browsing the fair, especially if you’ve spent the afternoon adding more books to your growing collection.
What are the interactive activities at Singapore Book Street?
There’s more to Singapore Book Street 2026 than simply shopping for books; you can also enjoy several interactive activities that bring literature and art to life.
Live Drawing Station
Ever wondered what you’d look like through an artist’s eyes? At the Live Drawing Station , you can share a favourite book, a memorable line, or simply strike a pose for a personalised portrait.
A featured artist will create your portrait on the spot in under 10 minutes, making it a unique keepsake to bring home. Different artists will be featured each day, so you can look forward to a variety of creative styles.
You’ll need to spend a minimum of $50 at the fair to redeem a portrait. Do note that the activity is limited to the first 10 customers per timeslot .
Date: 3rd-8th November
Time: Tues to Fri 3pm-4pm | Sat & Sun 2.30pm-3.30pm & 4.30pm-5.30pm
Live Typewriter Poetry
Then head over to the Live Typewriter Poetry station, where you can get a poem written specially for you. Simply give the poet your name and 3 random words, and watch as they transform your prompts into a personalised piece of poetry using a vintage typewriter.
The best part? You’ll get to take home a one-of-a-kind poem created just for you. A minimum spend of $50 is required to redeem a free personalised poem, and this activity is also limited to the first 10 customers per timeslot .
Date: 3rd-8th November
Time: Tues to Fri 6pm-7pm | Sat & Sun 1pm-2pm & 6pm-7pm
SingLit Cloud Printer
If you love collecting little mementoes, don’t miss the free SingLit Cloud Printer . This interactive kiosk resembles the self-ordering machines at McDonald’s, except instead of ordering a meal, you’ll be getting a poem.
…
summary: Singapore's largest SingLit book fair is here, with over 1,200 titles to browse.
title: Browse Over 1,200 SingLit Titles At Singapore Book Street 2026 & Take Part In A Free Stamp Rally

Social travel groups in Singapore
Every friend group has that one chat. The Japan trip has been in planning since 2023, someone is still checking their leave, and the only thing anyone has booked is a reminder to talk about it again next month. Basically, the trip never made it out of the group chat. The fix is to stop waiting and join one of these social travel groups in Singapore .
They sort out the itinerary, the logistics and, most importantly, the company. You show up solo or as a duo and leave with a new hiking crew, ski buddies, or a group chat that actually goes somewhere. We rounded up 9 Singapore-based groups that run adventure trips across Asia and a little beyond, from $120 day hikes in Malaysia to Kilimanjaro summits.
What is a social travel group?
A social travel group is a trip you join on your own or with a friend, where the organiser handles the logistics and deliberately mixes the group so strangers bond. Most groups add a social layer , like pre-trip meetups, group chats, or trips sorted by age.
1. sotravel
Age-banded group trips, from volcano weekends to dog sledging in Mongolia
View this post on Instagram
Chances are your friends have already heard of sotravel . It started with a 7-day French Alps ski trip, and its Telegram group grew to nearly 200 members within days of launch. Today it runs dozens of trips for a crowd that is mostly adventurous Gen Z and millennials.
The main draw is that each trip comes with an age group, so you won’t be the only 24-year-old on a bus of retirees. Trips are usually built around a specific activity, like skiing, surfing, climbing, or diving, so everyone already has something to talk about by day 1.

Weekend sunrise hikes in Malaysia, with a Telegram bot that finds your next mountain

For the lesser-known Telegram crowd, Little Monsters Travel is a licensed agency that lives on chats rather than glossy ads. New hikes drop on its Telegram channel, and there’s even a Telegram bot, @LMTfindmyhike_bot , that helps you pick one. Trips are led by founder Gan, whom past hikers describe as the kind of leader who hangs back so nobody gets left behind.
Most trips are day hikes across the Causeway, picking up from Marsiling MRT. Recent listings feature Malaysia day hikes, covering 2-way transport, a trek leader, local guides, and park permits. Food and insurance are on you.

The Gunung Datuk sunrise hike is billed for hiking beginners and ends with a Malacca stop for chendol and kueh, which is honestly reason enough to wake up at 3am. Pompompurin + Starbucks collection
ICYMI, Starbucks recently sent Sanrio fans into a frenzy after teasing its upcoming Pompompurin collaboration on Instagram, and finally, the wait is almost over. Celebrating their 30th anniversaries this year, the coffee giant and everyone’s favourite golden retriever are coming together for a special collection featuring SG-exclusive merchandise and freebies.
The Pompompurin + Starbucks collection officially launches on 10th November 2026 , so mark your calendar, especially if you’re a Sanrio fan or know someone who is.
What’s in the collection?
Image credit: Starbucks
The Singapore-exclusive collection gives Pompompurin a Starbucks-inspired makeover, with the adorable character appearing across a range of merchandise and collectibles, and even donning the brand’s iconic green apron.
You can expect to shop a range of cute finds when the collection drops, from tumblers and mugs for your daily caffeine fix to plushies that Sanrio fans will want to kope .
Plush & Plush Keychain
Image credit: Starbucks
The star of the collection has got to be the Pompompurin + Starbucks Plush ($46.90) . Dressed in the green Starbucks apron and his classic brown beret, the huggable plush comes with a sling and 3 mini charms attached – a croissant, a Starbucks coffee cup, and a cookie.
We reckon it’ll be snapped up pretty quickly once the collection launches, so you’d better be ready to act fast if you want to bring one home.
If you’re planning to bring Pompompurin with you on your adventures, go for the smaller Pompompurin + Starbucks Plush Keychain ($29.90) , featuring the character holding a Starbucks cup.
Furry Pouch
Image credit: Starbucks
For something practical, there’s also the Pompompurin + Starbucks Furry Pouch ($29.90) . It has a soft, fluffy texture and comes in a handy size for keeping your little knick-knacks organised. Your AirPods, lipsticks, keys, and other small essentials will finally have a proper home, instead of getting lost in the depths of your bag.
Reusable Bag With Canvas Pouch & Large Reusable Bag
Image credit: Starbucks
If you always have barang-barang to lug around, consider getting the Pompompurin + Starbucks Reusable Bag With Canvas Pouch ($21.90) . The reusable bag can be folded neatly into a compact canvas pouch featuring a Pompompurin print, making it easy to stash in your handbag for your next shopping trip.
There’s also the Pompompurin + Starbucks Large Reusable Bag ($24.90) , with even more room for all your next haul.
Puffy Card Pouch
Image credit: Starbucks
Here’s another excuse to splurge: the Pompompurin + Starbucks Puffy Card Pouch ($20.90) is both cute and functional. You can use it to keep your cards in one place instead of digging through your bag for them. It even comes with a matcha latte charm for the finishing touch!
PVC Pouches (Blind Bag)
Image adapted from: Starbucks
Add a surprise to your shopping spree by getting the Pompompurin + Starbucks PVC Pouches (Blind Bag) ($10.90) . There are 2 designs to collect, but the catch is that you won’t know which one you’re getting until you open the packaging.
12oz Ceramic Mug
Image credit: Starbucks
Since we’re on the topic of Starbucks merch, you can expect a range of drinkware to add to your collection too. One of the cutest picks has to be the Pompompurin + Starbucks 12oz Ceramic Mug ($32.90) , just the right size for sipping your morning coffee or tea.
20oz Stainless Steel Tumbler
Image credit: Starbucks
But if you need caffeine to power you throughout your day, get the Pompompurin + Starbucks 20oz Stainless Steel Water Bottle ($52.90) instead. It keeps your drinks hot or cold, and you’ll get to take your time sipping on your coffee without worrying about it losing its temperature too quickly.
16oz Glass Cold Cup With Lid
Image credit: Starbucks
Can’t get enough of Pompompurin? The Pompompurin + Starbucks 16oz Glass Cold Cup With Lid ($42.90) comes with a Pompompurin straw topper, so you’ll have the golden retriever keeping you company with every sip.
24oz Water Bottle
Image credit: Starbucks
Or get the Pompompurin + Starbucks 24oz Water Bottle ($29.90) , a lighter option for getting your daily hydration in. This would make a great water bottle for little Pompompurin fans too; parents don’t have to worry about their kids lugging around a heavy tumbler or accidentally breaking a glass cup.
10oz Double-Wall Glass With Lid
Image credit: Starbucks
Rounding out the list of drinkware is the Pompompurin + Starbucks 10oz Double-Wall Glass With Lid ($34.90) – you can never have too many cups at home, especially when it’s a Sanrio-themed one.
Ceramic Plate Set
Image credit: Starbucks
The Pompompurin + Starbucks Ceramic Plates Set ($39.90) comes with 2 plates in different sizes, colours, and designs to spruce up your dining table. This is not something you see in Starbucks merch drops every day, but we’re glad they included it.

Little India is Singapore’s go-to neighbourhood for South Indian food : fish head curry eaten off banana leaves, masala dosai folded around spiced potato, and biryani by the plateful, mostly within a few minutes’ walk of Serangoon Road. Besides food, a few colourful blocks pack in spice and flower stalls, saree specialists , century-old Hindu temples and some of the best jewellery shops . Along with the gleaming Deepavali , there’s plenty to see and do in Singapore’s Little India. Here’s where to eat, what to buy and what to see.
Why trust this guide
Little India is one of Singapore’s most vibrant neighbourhoods, and knowing where to eat, shop and explore can make all the difference. Our guide brings together a curated selection of restaurants, cafes, shops, hotels and cultural attractions. We’ve drawn on our knowledge to highlight places worth adding to your itinerary, whether you’re a first-time visitor or a local looking to rediscover the neighbourhood.
Little India at a glance
• Best South Indian feast: The Banana Leaf Apolo
• Best vegetarian food spot: Ananda Bhavan
• Best splurge curry: Muthu’s Curry
• Best hawker fix: Tekka Centre
• Best things to see: Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple , Indian Heritage Centre , the house of Tan Teng Niah
Where are the best restaurants in Little India, Singapore?
The best-known restaurants are The Banana Leaf Apolo and Muthu’s Curry on Race Course Road for fish head curry, Komala Vilas on Serangoon Road for vegetarian dosai, and the biryani stalls inside Tekka Centre.
1. The Banana Leaf Apolo
Photography: The Banana Leaf Apolo via Facebook
A hotspot for Indian cuisine lovers, this long-standing institution has been doling out its food on banana leaves for over 40 years. It offers a mix of North and South Indian fare. Think tandoori chicken, fried fish and mutton masala. But we’re positive most patrons come for the signature fish head curry, which packs a punch. We certainly do!
Best for: Fish head curry and North and South Indian classics
Must-try items: Fish head curry; mutton briyani; naan platter; tandoori chicken
How much: Starters from $8.30; tandoori dishes from $17.90; vegetable dishes from $13; rice dishes from $5.40; chicken dishes from $7.80; seafood dishes from $8.30
Opening hours: Daily, 10.30am to 10.30pm
Address: 54 Race Course Road, Singapore 218564
Visit The Banana Leaf Apolo
2. Muthu’s Curry
Photography: Muthu’s Curry
Savour eye-watering, lip-tingling spicy fare at this longstanding restaurant in Little India. It’s known for doling out one of Singapore’s favourite delicacies : fish head curry. Need less spicy options that won’t leave you sweating? Muthu’s Curry also serves a range of tamer, flavour-packed Indian fare, from North to South Indian. Plus plenty of vegetarian dishes to go with it.
Best for: Spicy South Indian fare
Must-try items: Fish head curry; lamb rack ananas; palak paneer; chicken tikka; butter chicken; moru moru vendakkai
How much: Starters from $9; chicken dishes from $17; seafood dishes from $12; mutton dishes from $19; vegetable dishes from $13; rice dishes from $4.50; kebabs from $17; breads from $4; sides from $3; drinks from $5
Opening hours: Daily, 10.30am to 10.30pm
Address: #01-01, 138 Race Course Road, Singapore 218591
Visit Muthu’s Curry
3. Sakunthala’s
Photography: Sakunthala’s Restaurant via Facebook
If you’re craving scrumptious Indian fare, Sakunthala’s will charm you with every bite. The menu is packed with North and South Indian cuisine, plus Chinese dishes. Yes, plenty to appease fussy eaters. Try the biryani, tandoori platter, masala chicken, prawn masala and fish head curry. Then, cool down from all the spices with a refreshing glass of lime juice. Bring the whole family along because, trust us, you’ll have a lot to taste before you leave.
Best for: Family-friendly Indian dining
Must-try items: Biryani; tandoori platter; masala chicken; prawn masala
How much: Prices vary across each outlet
Opening hours: Daily, 11am to 10.30pm (Race Course Road and Dunlop) and 11am to 1am (Syed Alwi Road)
Address: Multiple locations including Race Course Road and Syed Alwi Road
Visit Sakunthala’s
4. MTR Mavalli Tiffin Rooms
Serving Karnataka cuisine for over nine decades, MTR Mavalli Tiffin Rooms is the numero uno South Indian restaurant for a quick snack or light meal. We recommend you tuck into a plate of steamed rice cakes (idli) or savoury onion pancakes (onion uthapam). Or opt for the hearty dosa set if you’re feeling peckish.
Best for: Traditional Karnataka-style vegetarian food and tiffin favourites
Must-try items: Set dosa; tomato rice; maddur vada; shavige bhath; white uppit; pulliogre
How much: Idlis from $3; dosas from $6; rice dishes from $6; snacks from $3.50; desserts from $4; drinks from $2
Opening hours: Tuesdays to Thursdays, 8.30am to 3.30pm & 5.30pm to 9.30pm and Fridays to Sundays, 8.30am to 3.30pm & 5.30pm to 10pm
Address: 438 Serangoon Road, Singapore 218134

The travellers amongst us may have heard of BAO, the popular London restaurant. The chain is opening a Taiwanese convenience store pop-up called BAO Fast Foods (BFF) at New Bahru on Kim Yam Road .
Inspired by Taiwanese convenience stores, the pop-up will be open from 11 Nov to 28 Dec 2026 . Some of you might also be familiar with the very popular Taiwanese Fried Chicken , popular at many convenience stores in Taiwan. If you’re the type to explore every new spot, add BFF to your list.
Credit – BAO Fast Foods Website
BAO Fast Foods becomes the newest addition to the notoriously difficult Singapore food scene. This pop-up will act as a test for whether they will open a permanent spot sometime in 2027.
Asian convenience stores are the place for a decent bite at a very good price, and this pop-up gives you a more niche example. Unlike most convenience stores, they also serve proper hot meals prepared fresh daily.
Credit – morly_19 via Instagram
Of course, expect some regional snacks made in Taiwan, as well as some local and homemade brands. You could also grab the quintessential convenience store sandwiches. I personally like to combine an egg mayo sandwich with a fried chicken cutlet, and I hope to find that at BAO Fast Foods.
BAO Fast Foods was started by 3 people: married couple Shing Tat Chung and Erchen Chang , along with Chung’s sister, Wai Ting . They began with a stall at London’s Netil Market . They now run up to 7 outlets in the city. With their great success in London, it will be exciting to see them try their luck in Singapore.
Credit – morly_19 via Instagram
The trio had a similar pop-up in Taipei in June 2026 . It reportedly drew people obsessed with convenience stores as well as people hungry for the taste of Taiwan.
Credit – morly_19 via Instagram
There are several ways to get to New Bahru once they open. The closest MRT is Fort Canning , a 13-minute walk away. The closest bus stop to New Bahru is called Before Kim Yam Road , and it’s just a 6-minute walk from there.
Chung has said that the aim is to spread Taiwanese culture because the world lacks Taiwanese representation. And I agree. Hopefully this BAO Fast Foods pop-up succeeds, which could lead to much more Taiwanese food across Singapore. But no pressure, one step at a time.
Jyu Gae Bistro: Taiwanese all-day breakfast, braised pork rice & other delights at Bras Basah
summary: Bao Fast Foods (BFF) is a Taiwanese convenience store pop-up from London restaurant Bao, open at New Bahru on Kim Yam Road from 11 Nov 2026 to 28 Dec 2026. It serves Taiwanese-style fried chicken, hot meals and regional snacks, and acts as a test before a possible permanent outlet in 2027. It suits travellers and anyone who likes trying new pop-ups while they last.
title: Bao Fast Foods – London’s viral Taiwanese minimart pop-up opens Nov

body:
Carrotsticks & Cravings doesn’t make you pick a side. Some days you want a full plate. On other days you want something you can carry out the door. Either way, the menu has room for it!
Sip your Superfoods
Credit: Carrotsticks & Cravings’ Facebook
For the after-training crowd , or anyone who wants a shake that does a bit more than a regular smoothie, the Protein Wake Up Call (S$14) features Chocolate Whey Protein Powder and Espresso to keep you caffeinated. If you want something fruity and easy to drink, the Berry Boost (S$12) is berry-licious with Acai and Vanilla Whey Protein Powder , hitting your protein intake with enjoyment.
Cravings, Served
Credit: Carrotsticks & Cravings’ Facebook
Good food isn’t just one ingredient; it’s the whole plate. Got a craving ? Pancakes The Right Way (S$23) is a blueberry banana oat pancake, gluten- and sugar-free , served with Greek yoghurt and fresh berries. Prefer savoury? The Signature Smash Avo (S$18) is there for you.
Credit: Carrotsticks & Cravings’ Facebook
And if you think sandwiches are boring, you haven’t tried any of the 8 on the menu. Feeling adventurous? The Chicken Goat Cheese (S$20) and the Eggplant (S$22) with Tahini and pickled lemon cream aren’t your classic kind of sandwich. Want something more familiar? There’s the Pastrami (S$24) , rich brisket on toasted sourdough, or the Pesto & Roasted Pepper (S$18) , a herby, fragrant Focaccia sandwich. Either way, you’re ordering what you feel like eating.
Juice Break
Credit: Carrotsticks & Cravings’ Facebook
Not in the mood to sit down for a meal? Fresh juices are a simple alternative. Celery Cleanse (S$8) is slightly citrusy, and Green Detox (S$10) is refreshing, with a hint of sweetness from the apple. Order one because sipping the green stuff sounds good.
Something for Every Order
We know superfoods are great, but balance is better . No food from Carrotsticks & Cravings is “good” or “bad.” Just food, and a menu that trusts you to know what you’re in the mood for.
Go if you want a protein shake after a gym or pilates session, a juice just because, or a proper meal to fuel your body with nutrients and energy. And if you’re dining with someone whose order looks nothing like yours, Carrotsticks & Cravings has you covered with an extensive menu.

Tiger Remix is here, and Singapore gets it first. Tiger Beer has launched the flavoured lager range globally in Singapore and Malaysia, starting with two Asian-inspired flavours: Peach Oolong and Yuzu Lime.
Image: Tiger Beer
What is Tiger Remix?
Tiger Remix keeps the crisp, balanced character of the brand’s premium lager and adds a fruit-and-tea twist. Peach Oolong pairs juicy peach with aromatic oolong tea for a smooth finish, while Yuzu Lime combines zesty yuzu and tangy lime for a brighter, citrus-led sip. Both are described as low in bitterness, which should make them an easy first step for drinkers who find regular lager too sharp.
Both variants contain 4.2% ABV and come in 320ml cans.
Image: Tiger Beer
Street-culture design, local roots
The packaging leans on Asian street culture, with signboard-inspired typography, shophouse forms and motifs that reflect the region. Tiger was born in Singapore in 1932, and Magdalene Tan, Head of Marketing of Asia Pacific Breweries, said the debut here carries special significance: Singapore is shaped by cultures from around the world yet remains distinctly Asian at heart.
Sam Fielding, Tiger Global Brand Director, framed the range as a new flavour platform for the brand, with Peach Oolong and Yuzu Lime as the first two releases.
Where to buy Tiger Remix in Singapore
Tiger Remix is available now in single-can and 3-pack formats at 7-Eleven stores islandwide and on RedMart. A progressive rollout to major supermarkets, including FairPrice, Sheng Siong, Cold Storage and Giant, follows this November.
If you are stocking up for the festive season, our guide to FairPrice’s current in-store voucher offer may help. For more drinks news, see how Third Floor is pouring creative cocktails at Design Orchard, and the Pompompurin + Starbucks collection arriving on 10 November.
summary: Tiger Remix launches in Singapore with Peach Oolong and Yuzu Lime lagers at 4.2% ABV, at 7-Eleven and RedMart now, with supermarkets to follow.

McDonald’s Singapore’s new McCrispy Fried Chicken goes on an in-store offer from Thursday, 5 November: the two-piece McCrispy Fried Chicken is S$7.95 until 25 November.
The chicken comes in Spicy and Signature. McDonald’s pitches the new recipe on more crunch outside and more juice inside, with a spicier kick on the Spicy version. Both are sold as two or three pieces, or in a six-piece box meant for sharing.
Before the launch, McDonald’s held Bite Club, a preview tasting on 30 and 31 October for MyM Rewards members who redeemed 2,500 points in the app for an invite admitting two people.
The S$7.95 offer
The S$7.95 price covers the two-piece McCrispy Fried Chicken, and it runs in stores only, from 5 to 25 November. McDonald’s pictures the offer with fries and a Sprite.
McDonald’s banner for the S$7.95 two-piece McCrispy Fried Chicken offer, in stores from 5 to 25 November. Image: McDonald’s Singapore
Fried chicken at McDonald’s is an after-breakfast item, so the earliest you can order it is when the breakfast menu ends. It is sold while stocks last.
Coleslaw and crinkle cut fries
Two sides arrive with the chicken. Coleslaw is the first McDonald’s Singapore has ever sold, crunchy and creamy and made to sit next to fried chicken. Crinkle Cut Fries are a ridged take on the regular fries, with a fuller, crispier bite.
Coleslaw, a first for McDonald’s Singapore. Image: McDonald’s Singapore
Spicy Chicken McNuggets are back as well, in six, nine and 20-piece portions. For dessert, the Hershey’s Cone tops vanilla soft serve with Hershey’s chocolate, and the Twist Cone swirls the two together. The Hershey’s Cone is sold all day at Dessert Kiosks and participating restaurants.
The six-piece McCrispy Fried Chicken box. Image: McDonald’s Singapore
Allergens
The McCrispy Fried Chicken contains egg, soybean and wheat, and carries gluten. The coleslaw contains egg and soybeans. The Crinkle Cut Fries contain soybeans. The Spicy Chicken McNuggets contain soybean and wheat, with MSG and gluten.
Where it is not sold
Six McDonald’s restaurants do not carry the McCrispy Fried Chicken: Shell Tampines, Shell Hougang, Shell Havelock, Clementi Avenue 3, Parklane and the Tampines Kiosk.
summary: McDonald's Singapore's new McCrispy Fried Chicken comes in Spicy and Signature, with a S$7.95 two-piece offer in stores from 5 to 25 November and its first coleslaw.
title: McDonald’s new McCrispy Fried Chicken is S$7.95 for two pieces in stores from 5 to 25 November

Your Hogwarts letter might be a little late, but your next chance to shop for wizarding merchandise is just around the corner. House of Spells , a UK-based multi-fandom store, is opening its first outlet in Asia at 118 Mall KL , on 1 Dec 2026 , bringing collectibles inspired by Harry Potter , The Lord of the Rings and more to local fans.
Credit – House of Spells
Founded in 2016, the retailer brings together officially licensed merchandise from popular film, television and fantasy franchises. Potterheads can look forward to items inspired by Harry Potter and Fantastic Beasts , while fans of Game of Thrones , The Hobbit , Stranger Things , Marvel, DC Comics and Studio Ghibli will have plenty to browse too.
Credit – House of Spells
The collection includes magic wands , character figurines , themed apparel , jewellery , stationery , mugs , posters and other collectibles . You might find something to add to your display shelf, a souvenir featuring your favourite character or a gift for that friend who can recite the entire film from memory.
Credit – House of Spells
Beyond the merchandise, House of Spells aims to make the shopping experience part of the attraction. Its stores feature fantasy-inspired interiors, atmospheric lighting and interactive displays designed to evoke the fictional worlds behind the products. Staff who share an enthusiasm for these franchises are also available to help visitors explore the collections.
Credit – House of Spells
The brand operates several stores across the UK, including in London, Liverpool and Stratford-upon-Avon, as well as an outlet in New York City. Its Kuala Lumpur opening marks its first move into Asia, giving Malaysian fans a new place to discover officially licensed merchandise without travelling overseas.
Do note that the exact look and layout of the KL store have yet to be revealed.
Situated at 118 Mall within the Merdeka 118 precinct in KL, the opening House of Spells could be a fun addition to your next shopping trip , even if you only intend to browse. After all, resisting a collectible featuring your favourite character is one thing; having an entire store of them in front of you is another.
10 new places in JB to check out this Nov 2026 — cafes, food & more
summary: House of Spells is opening its first Asian outlet at 118 Mall in Kuala Lumpur on 1 December 2026, bringing officially licensed merchandise from franchises including Harry Potter, Marvel, Studio Ghibli and Stranger Things. The UK retailer offers wands, figurines, apparel, jewellery and other collectibles in fantasy-inspired stores with interactive displays, making it a useful stop for Malaysian fans seeking character merchandise, souvenirs or gifts without travelling overseas.

body:
Cute fitness apps
We get it, keeping fit and staying in shape to sculpt a rockin’ bod is an arduous pursuit. Throw in external factors like a hectic work schedule and the recent haze situation, and your motivation to even head out for a jaunt swiftly plummets to its nadir. Thankfully, we live in an age where technology can give us a jolt of dopamine to get us off the couch and get active.
Should you need a little nudge to keep your fitness goals on track, take a peek at these cute fitness apps that’ll have you looking forward to lacing up those trainers. From Tamagotchi-like critters that feed off your steps to playing dress-up with virtual outfits purchased with sweat-earned currency, here are some to accompany you on your next workout.
1. Walking Charlie
Register up to 10k steps daily for in-game currency to buy virtual outfits
To say the Walking Charlie app took our office by storm is no understatement. The premise of registering steps daily in exchange for virtual outfits for our avatars won us over instantly, and in just a couple of days, a good chunk of our colleagues were obsessed with getting their steps in.
Screenshots from: Charlie
The app’s as simple as it gets; users will receive donuts by hitting 5,000 and 10,000 step milestones every day. You can then use your donuts to purchase adorable outfits, accessories, and backgrounds to doll up your avatar; there’s even a Merlion background to strive for, if you’re feeling extra patriotic.
Screenshots from: Charlie
You are also able to upload snaps of your daily walks to the app to subtly nudge your friends to log their steps, as well as create houses so your avatars can all live under one roof.
BTW , if you don’t hit a step count of at least 5,000 every day, your avatar will fatten up a little. Conversely, meeting your step goals will result in them getting fitter, so you’re encouraged to get off your bums if you’d like a killer 6 pack, both in-game and IRL .
Download Walking Charlie ( App Store | Google Play ) .
2. Wokamon
Raise cute monsters who feed off your steps
Image credit: Hazim Hamid
Pokémon fans, you’ll love this one. Wokamon is a creature collecting game where you’re tasked with nurturing Wokamons , which are quirky monsters that originate from the fictional planet Laya. Here’s the catch: instead of levelling up via combat, Wokamons get their sustenance from energy generated by human movement, AKA our steps.
By walking in the real world, you’ll expand your collection of Wokamons, discover new worlds for them to roam in, and unlock outfits to kit out your favourites with. You can also connect with friends via the app, which allows you to see who can rack up the most steps on a daily and weekly basis. Honestly, nothing’s a better motivator than some friendly competition.
Download Wokamon ( App Store | Google Play ) .
3. Habbie
Take care of Tamagotchi-inspired pets by completing daily goals
If you’ve spent hours on end fiddling with a Tamagotchi as a child, then Habbie ’s the app for you. This habit-tracking app is inspired by the popular Japanese gizmo of the late 90s, and you’ll see why immediately when you boot it up. Charmingly presented in pixel art, the app will have you caring for a Habbie Pet by completing daily goals which you can set yourself.
Image credit: Habbie: Habit Tracker & Pet
The app has custom timers, counters, and checklists that cater to all sorts of goals, from physical ones such as jogging to more sedentary activities like studying or reading for a certain amount of time. Hook it up to Apple HealthKit, and the app can even track metrics such as cycling distance, swimming distance, and wheelchair pushes.
You can also view your Habbie Pets on your Apple Watch or a widget on your phone’s home screen.
Image credit: Reddit
Completing your daily goal will reward you with a gift that contains food for your pet. On the flip side, take it easy for a day, and your pet will lovingly leave a pile of poop that’ll remain till you meet your goals.
Download Habbie ( App Store ) .
4. Stepets
Build your own island & round up cute companions
Image credit: Platonic Games
If you’d like your accumulated steps to go towards a bigger project, how does building an entire island sound? Enter Stepets , a fitness tracking app that doubles as a whole game that’s fueled by the steps you take throughout your day. For starters, you’ll be rewarded with lovable baby pets that grow and evolve as you record your walks, and there’s over 100 of them to call yours.
Image adapted from: Platonic Games
The app also features a whole island that’s entirely customisable to your liking, and it also serves as the home for your pets. When you find yourself dragging your feet, take a breather and have a go at some of the mini-games alongside your companions; the app is also fully functional offline, so you can accompany your babies virtually even during the most remote of hikes.
Download Stepets: Walking Pet Simulator ( App Store ) .

title: 7 Cute Fitness Apps That’ll Make You Look Forward To Clocking In Your Daily 10K Steps

body:
Ume San 100 has new konbini-inspired lunch sets
Behind the nostalgic facade of Fortune Centre lies plenty of hidden gems, from affordable Korean food to handmade Japanese onigiri and traditional Chinese tong sui . Now, there’s one more reason to visit the strata mall: Ume San 100 has recently released a new lunch set, alongside other exciting menu items.
Ume San 100: New Japanese Bar Hidden Behind Vending Machines Has SG’s Largest Umeshu Collection
ICYMI: Ume San 100 is a Japanese speakeasy bar, and its iconic vending machine storefront is hard to miss. You’ll spot it almost immediately upon reaching the second floor, as it’s brightly lit and colourfully eye-catching.
Image credit: Ume San 100
Frequent Japan-goers would know that convenience stores, AKA konbinis, are a must-visit in Japan. The bar has given its menu a konbini-inspired spin, introducing familiar treats as part of its all-new Konbini Set ($19.90++) .
Image credit: Ume San 100
One highlight is the Truffle Ramen , topped with prawns, a jammy hanjuku egg, and fish cakes for a classic yet hearty bowl of ramen.
Since no konbini haul is complete without a drink, each set comes with Ume Cola that’s made in-house with ume syrup and house-made cola for a fizzy staple. If you prefer something more hardcore, top up $5 to add whisky or vodka to your cola for a “grown-up” upgrade.
Image credit: Ume San 100
A must-order at any kobini would be the fried chicken or Umechiki , which is also part of the lineup. Guests get to opt for a spicy or non-spicy set, and the chosen spice level will apply to both the ramen and Umechiki.
The set also comprises Crispy Fries , with both sides being served in a striped paper sleeve, just like the ones in Japan.
To add on to the fun, every konbini set comes with a Japanese-style receipt, allowing diners to try their luck at the Gachapon machine for some enticing rewards. Prize value varies based on capsule colours: Gold entitles diners to 10% off their next visit ($30 min. spend), Silver offers a free highball or mocktail with any main, Green provides a free Fruit Tasting Set ($70 min. spend), and Black awards a $25 return voucher ($100 min. spend).
Image credit: Ume San 100
Besides the Konbini Set, the eatery is also expanding its dinner menu with three new fusion dishes. Mentaiko Pasta with Seared Scallops ($22++) for a Japanese take on the Italian staple, Spicy Beef Ramen ($18++) comprising bold Sichuan-inspired flavours, as well as Foie Gras Bara Chirashi Don ($24++) , which sees French foie gras and salmon, tuna, and tamago atop a bed of sushi rice.
Image credit: Ume San 100
You can also explore Ume San 100’s extensive selection of Japanese umeshu, AKA plum wine. Their collection is said to be one of Singapore’s largest, boasting over 100 varieties with rare and exclusive labels. If you’re new here, go for the Low-ABV Taster Set ($15++) that features three floral-infused umeshu flavours: Rose , Lavender , and Jasmine .
Fans of the tall, carbonated mixed alcohol highball would be pleased to know that they offer 13 different choices, including Ume Whisky ($14++) , Premium Toki Highball ($15++) and more.
Image credit: Ume San 100
Much like the izakayas in Japan, the seating capacity is cozy but rather limited, with 28 seats on the floor and six by the bar, so it’s best to book ahead or come down early to get a table.
While you’re in the area, check out our 12-hour Bugis and CBD guide for more good eats. In other news, read our Hi Bowl feature for more deets on Haidilao’s new malatang restaurant in Rochor.
Address: 190 Middle Road, #02-07, Fortune Centre, Singapore 188979
Operating hours: Mon-Thu 11:30am to 2:30pm, 5pm to 10pm, Fri-Sat 11:30am to 2:30pm, 5pm to 11pm, Sun 11am to 4pm, 5pm to 8:30pm
Tel: 8897 4575
Website
Ume San 100 is not halal-certified.
12 Hours In Bugis And The CBD: Famous Kaya Toast, Vintage Shopping And More
Feature image adapted from Ume San 100.
summary: Japanese speakeasy Ume San 100 debuts an all-new konbini-inspired lunch set from $19.90++, alongside other exciting menu items!
title: Ume San 100 Launches Konbini-Inspired Lunch Sets At Fortune Centre

body:
HANDO is a new izakaya with affordable Japanese fare
Image credit: HANDO
A Japanese izakaya has just opened in Bendeemer , offering affordable bar snacks and other small plates. Soft-launched on 30 October 2026, HANDO has a modern concept, with a dimly lit interior and laid-back atmosphere designed for friends to gather and hang out.
20 Bendemeer Food Places For KL Ban Mian, Orh Nee Puffs And More
The restaurant’s signature is its handrolls, made in front of you across the counter, so you can enjoy them fresh. Each handroll is customisable, with your choice of red or white vinegar, rice portion, and wasabi.
Image credit: HANDO
Prices start from $8++ with the Tai handroll . For a more indulgent option, the Uni Bomb ($28++) is loaded with fresh uni and uni cream. Other options include Seared Anago ($10++) , made with grilled eel, and Engawa ($10++) , an incredibly rich, buttery fish.
If you’re torn between choices, they offer sets such as The HAND-Some One ($45++) , which includes five rolls, and The Full HANDO ($78++) , which has seven rolls, including the Uni Bomb.
For a full lunch, the Quick HANDO ($28++) comes with three rolls, miso, pickles, and cold tea. You can top up with the More Fun ($18++) set, which offers two off-menu rolls on top of an existing set.
Image credit: HANDO
Beyond hand rolls, the izakaya also serves grilled food, bar bites and more. This includes Chicken Thigh skewer ($4.50++) , Shiitake skewer ($8++), and Mix Fish ($14++) , a selection of sashimi dressed in sesame sauce and seaweed tempura.
Image credit: HANDO
If you’re with friends, the HANDO Karaage ($12++) , Fish Skin (8++) , and Corn Tofu ($9++) are suited for sharing. For something heartier, the HANDO Uni Udon ($28++) has udon with uni cream, topped with more uni and ikura.
For more new Japanese eateries opening in Singapore, check out these Japanese F&B openings in 2026 for fried sando, hot stone gyukatsu and more. If you’re in Bendeemer looking for dessert, check out our Keong Saik Bakery review !
Address: 28 Cavan Road, Singapore 209855
Opening hours: Daily 12pm to 2:15pm, 6pm to 9pm
Website
HANDO is not halal-certified.

Feature image adapted from HANDO

body:
Amoy Street Food Centre guide
From wholesome fish soup to curry puffs and noodles awarded with the Michelin Bib Gourmand , here’s a list of the best stalls we recommend at Amoy Street Food Centre .
1. The Original Vadai
Image credit: Touristmouse via Google Maps
The Original Vadai is a household name in Singapore, famous for its deep-fried Indian fritters. It started its journey as a pop-up in the pasar malam before setting up hawker stalls across Singapore.
If you’ve never tried one of these, they could be described as a savoury donut: crisp on the outside, but pillowy and airy on the inside. The original Prawn Vadai ($1.30) features a whole unpeeled prawn that’s flash-fried with the fritter. Other flavours you can get at this stall include Chilli Vadai ($1.20) , Onion Vadai ($1.20) , and even a Cheese Vadai ($5) .
Unit: #02-84
Opening hours: Mon-Wed, Fri 8am to 3:45pm
Website
The Original Vadai is halal-certified.
2. Pepper Bowl
The amazing thing about Pepper Bowl is that no dish costs more than $7! We highly suggest you top up $1 for an onsen egg, to give your meal a little more variety! Get their Spring Onion Pork Rice ($6.50) , which comprises stir-fried pork tossed with spring onions. The pork is coated in a syrupy sweet sauce, while the meat is tender and juicy. If you’re a lover of all things spicy, you should definitely give their Black Pepper Beef Rice ($7) a try.
Read our Pepper Bowl review .
Unit: #02-102
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 10:30am to 2:30pm
Pepper Bowl is not halal-certified.
3. Lagoon In A Bowl
Image credit: @one_plain_breath
Lagoon In A Bowl is known for their healthy grain bowls. Their signature is the Mentaiko Salmon Bowl ($11) . Albeit a little pricey for hawker fare, you may find this unique salmon bowl rather value for money. All the bowls sold here contain butterfly pea rice meant to imitate a blue lagoon. Meanwhile, the slab of torched mentaiko salmon represents a fish in the ‘water’. This delectable analogy tastes as good as it looks, too.
Unit: #01-48
Opening hours: Mon-Thurs 11am to 3pm, 6pm to 8pm, Fri 11am to 3pm
Tel: 9119 2619
Website
Lagoon In A Bowl is not halal-certified.
4. Han Kee Fish Soup
Image credit: Woei Lin via Google Maps
If you’re prepared to brave the storm of office workers lining up outside Han Kee Fish Soup and wait for your turn, you’ll be rewarded with a hearty bowl of wholesome fish soup for lunch! Order their Sliced Fish Soup (from $6) , it’s one of the cheapest dishes on the menu, and worth every penny. The broth is simple and light, yet brimming with umami. The slices of fish soaking inside taste so clean and fresh, with a slight springiness as you chew.
Unit: #02-129
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11am to 3pm
Han Kee Fish Soup is not halal-certified.
5. A Noodle Story
Image credit: @jasyapxl
A Noodle Story is a Michelin Bib Gourmand award-winning noodle stall that sells ramen with a unique local twist. A bowl of their Singapore Style Ramen ($10.80) comes with tender chashu pork belly, a snazzy potato-wrapped prawn, juicy wontons and a lava egg with a gooey core. These ingredients are stylishly arranged atop springy noodles tossed in XO sauce. The noodles are also accompanied by a small, savoury bowl of soup.
Unit: #01-39
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 10am to 8pm
Website
A Noodle Story is not halal-certified.
6. Piao Ji Fish Porridge
Image credit: @unsophisticatedpalatesg
Piao Ji Fish Porridge is another fish soup stall in Amoy Street Food Centre with the ability to give Han Kee Fish Soup a run for their money. Freshly sliced fish simmer in a tasty, hearty broth. A classic bowl of Fish Soup costs $8 , but you can add in prawns at the price of $10 , for a stronger seafood taste.
Add a bowl of rice to complement your soup for an extra $0.50 . The queue at this stall is equally as intense as the one at Han Kee Fish Soup, so come to the food centre mentally prepped to wait in line. The owner has mentioned that he will close down Piao Ji if he is unable to find a successor, so dine here while you still can.
Unit: #02-100
Opening hours: Fri-Wed 10:30am to 3:30pm
Piao Ji Fish Porridge is not halal-certified.
7. Lian Hup Heng
If you’re looking for affordable bakes in the food centre, check out Lian Hup Heng , a humble hawker bakery selling sweet treats under $4. Besides the popular Orh Nee Tart ($3.80), they also sell Almond Financiers ($2.20) , and Lemon Meringue Tarts ($3.80) , a classic treat you typically wouldn’t find at such a competitive price in Singapore. During our visit last year, we also enjoyed the Yoghurt Cranberry ($3.80) cake, which was light and slightly tangy. Pay this hidden bakery a visit if you’re in the area!
Read our Lian Hup Heng feature .
Unit: #02-128
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 10:30am to 3pm
Website
Lian Hup Heng is not halal-certified.

8. Hong Kee Beef Noodles
Image credit: @jenteo27
…
summary: Located in the CBD, Amoy Street Food Centre has grain bowls to fill you up and artisanal toast when you're just looking for a small bite.

body:
Best Japanese buffets in Singapore
If someone told me I could pick only one cuisine to eat for the rest of my life, I’d choose Japanese cuisine in a heartbeat. I love how Japanese dishes can seem so simple, yet taste incredibly satisfying, which is why the idea of having unlimited servings of them feels even more irresistible. Few things compare to indulging in endless plates of sushi, sashimi, and grilled delights.
My love for Japanese fare has led me to compile a list of the 20 best Japanese buffets in Singapore, featuring spreads of sushi, sashimi, and other Japanese favourites across a wide range of price points. If you are looking for even more buffet suggestions, we also have guides to cheap buffets starting from $7 , as well as the best hotel buffets in Singapore .
Best Japanese buffet spots, in a nutshell:
• Cheap Japanese buffet in Singapore : Shabu Sai – Lunch buffet starting at just $18.99++
• Most Instagrammable buffet: Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant at Orchard Central – Popular buffet overlooking Orchard
• Most unique buffet: Maguro Samurai – Singapore’s first omakase buffet at Robertson Quay
• For special occasions : Gyu-Kaku – All-you-can-eat premium Japanese Wagyu cuts
<$40++ per person
1. Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant – Popular buffet in Orchard Central
Cheap Japanese buffet from $30.90++
Image credit: Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant
What is Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant? One of the more popular Japanese buffet restaurants in Singapore is Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant , located on the eighth floor of Orchard Central, which offers a wonderful view of the bustling Orchard Road. Lunch will set you back at $30.90++ while dinner is priced at $49.90++ per person . You can find a range of tempura, sushi, teppanyaki, and skewers here. For a broader selection with premium dishes, it’s highly recommended to go during dinner, which includes rotating items such as snow crab legs , oysters , robatayaki crayfish and more.
Expect to pay: $30.90++ per person (Lunch), $49.90++ per person (Dinner)
What to order: Aburi Salmon , Snow Crab Legs, Maguro Sashimi
Address: 181 Orchard Road, #08-01/02/03, Orchard Central, Singapore 238896
Opening hours: Daily 11:30am to 3pm, 6pm to 10pm
Tel: 9817 5259
Website
Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant is not halal-certified.
2. SUKI-YA – Iconic all-you-can-eat hotpot chain
Authentic Japanese broths at affordable prices
What is SUKI-YA? A popular choice among hotpot lovers, SUKI-YA is one of the few restaurant buffets in Singapore that specialise in Japanese-inspired sukiyaki and shabu-shabu. There’s no need to be afraid of burning a hole in your wallet here as their lunch buffets are going at just $23.90++ , every Monday to Thursday, and $28.90++ on Friday to Sunday. Choose from six different broths, including a hearty pork-based broth and fresh soya miso, a nutritious and milky broth. This meaty feast gives access to chicken, pork, and beef, and you get to pick from three different dips: ponzu , sesame , and fresh egg .
Expect to pay: $23.90-$28.90++
What to order: Mala Miso, Shabu-Shabu, Sukiyaki
Website | Full list of outlets
SUKI-YA is not halal-certified.
3. Tenkaichi – Award-winning BBQ restaurant at Marina Square
Japanese BBQ buffet overlooking the Marina Bay skyline
What is Tenkaichi? For the best meat and sashimi Japanese buffet in Singapore, Tenkaichi is a strong contender. Choose from three choices of buffet starting from $29.80++ on Mondays to Thursdays, and $35.80++ on Fridays to Sundays: Standard , Deluxe , and Premium . There are quite a few cuts of meat to choose from at their Deluxe Buffet , including thin-cut Wagyu shabu shabu and Angus ribeye steak. Make sure to leave room in your tummy for sashimi, of which you can choose from fish such as salmon, tuna, and sea bream.
Expect to pay: $29.80-$94.80++ (Mon-Thur), $35.80-$99.80++ (Fri-Sun)
What to order : Ton Toro, Miso Buta Kata Rosu
Address: 6 Raffles Boulevard, #03-129, Marina Square, Singapore 039594
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11:30am, to 2:30pm, 5:30pm to 10pm, Sat-Sun 11:30am to 10pm
Website
Tenkaichi is not halal-certified.
4. Kiwami Ramen & Gyoza Bar – Ramen buffet in Tanjong Pagar
Free-flow ramen with over 25 sides at Guoco Tower
What is Kiwami Ramen & Gyoza Bar? Available at their Guoco Tower and VivoCity outlets, Kiwami offers one of the more unique Japanese restaurant buffets in Singapore: an all-you-can-eat ramen galore. From just $28.80++ per person , you get to try eight kinds of ramen, sides and more, all at unlimited portions! You can find their signature ramen offerings here, such as the Premium Kiwami Tonkotsu Ramen , made with a 10-hour pork bone broth that’s rich and creamy. You can even try variations of this dish, such as with black garlic oil, mala, and yuzu. You can also get 10 different side dishes to fill your belly, and end your meal with various ice cream flavours.
Read our Kiwami ramen buffet feature .
Expect to pay: $28.80++ per person
…
summary: We've curated a list of the best Japanese buffets in Singapore for you to chow down as much food, sashimi, and sushi rolls as you want!
title: 20 Japanese Buffets In Singapore From $18.99++ For Unlimited Sashimi And Yakiniku

body:
Tiger has two new cans in the fridge, and Singapore gets them first. Tiger Remix is a new range of flavoured lagers in Peach Oolong and Yuzu Lime, and the brand is giving it a global debut here and in Malaysia before anywhere else.
Both flavours are built on the crisp Tiger lager most of us already know from hawker centre tables and kopitiam fridges. The twist is in the fruit and the tea: Tiger describes the range as its signature taste paired with distinctive Asian-inspired flavours, drawing on the energy and self-expression of Asia’s street culture.
Two flavours, two moods
Peach Oolong mixes Tiger beer with juicy peach and aromatic oolong tea. Tiger pitches it as effortlessly easy to drink, and it is the softer, rounder of the two on paper, with the tea there to stop the peach going too sweet.
Yuzu Lime is the sharper one. It pairs the crisp lager with zesty yuzu and tangy lime, a citrus combination built for group nights out rather than a quiet can at home.
Both come in 320ml cans at 4.2 per cent ABV.
Yuzu Lime is the sharper of the two; Peach Oolong leans softer. Image: Tiger Beer
Where to buy Tiger Remix
Tiger Remix is on shelves now at 7-Eleven stores islandwide and on RedMart, in single cans and 3-packs. Supermarkets follow through November, with a progressive rollout at FairPrice, Sheng Siong, Cold Storage and Giant.
FairPrice already has both flavours on its online store. A 3-pack of 320ml cans carries a usual price of S$9.95, and an offer price of S$9.50 runs until 30 November. The BCRS container deposit is charged on top and refunded when the empty cans go back to a return point.
Good to know
Tiger Remix is an alcoholic drink, and FairPrice’s online store tells shoppers under 18 to remove alcohol from their cart before checkout.
For a first can, Peach Oolong suits drinkers who like things on the gentler side, while Yuzu Lime is the pick for anyone who wants more citrus bite with their supper.
summary: Tiger Remix, a new range of flavoured lagers in Peach Oolong and Yuzu Lime, makes its global debut in Singapore, starting at 7-Eleven and RedMart.
title: Tiger Remix launches Peach Oolong and Yuzu Lime flavoured lagers in Singapore

Pokémon fans in Singapore, good news — PokéXciting! has arrived at Changi Airport and Jewel , until 3 Jan 2027 . This special Asia tour celebrates the 30th anniversary of the beloved pocket monsters with exciting events such as parades, meet-and-greets, and more.
The wider festivities last until 3 Jan 2027 , but there are highlights you won’t want to miss on 7 and 8 Nov 2026 , including a thrilling parade with many, many Pokémons. Keep an eye out for the exclusive PokéXciting! Pikachu , sporting a fluffy blue hairstyle. This rare Pikachu can be caught around Changi Airport and Jewel using the Pokémon GO app.
Credit – The Pokémon Company
Over at Jewel , there will be a Pokémon Parade featuring all 27 starter Pokémon from 9 generations of the video game series, alongside not 1 but 2 Pikachus. This adorable spectacle will take place at Jewel’s Level 1 Forest Valley on 7 and 8 Nov 2026 , 3pm and 6pm daily .
As the Pokémon march in sync with the music during the parade, it’s bound to be a heartwarming sight. Admission is free with registration required on-site prior to entry. Do note that each session operates on a first-come, first-served basis.
Don’t miss out on redeeming free Pikachu sun visors and Pokémon 30th Anniversary stickers . Grab ’em at Level 1 (opposite Porsche) on 7 and 8 Nov 2026 , 12pm – 9pm daily , on a first-come, first-served, while stocks last basis.
Credit – Changi Airport Group
Be sure to catch the PokéXciting! Special Night Sho w at Terminal 3 Departure Hall (Level 2, in front of Departure Immigration) on 7 and 8 Nov 2026, with shows daily at 4.30pm and 7.30pm . During the show, Pikachu dances to thrilling EDM beats under dazzling lights. Do note that you’ll also have to register prior to entry, with the queue opening an hour before each session.
Credit – Changi Airport Group
Besides watching the Pokémon, you can get up close with them during the various meet-and-greet sessions. On 7 and 8 Nov 2026 , meet Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Charmander, and Squirtle at 12pm , 2pm , 8pm and 9pm .
There will be other sessions on 14, 15, 21, and 22 Nov 2026 as well as on 5, 6, 12, 13, 19, and 20 Dec 2026 at 2pm , 3pm and 6.30pm for each date. You can expect to see Pikachu alongside other characters like Eevee, Snorlax, Gengar, Piplup and Mimikyu. The 2pm and 3pm sessions are at T3 Departure Hall , while 6.30pm sessions are at T3B2 ST3PS .
Credit – Changi Airport Group
Be sure to snap Pokégenic photos across 4 themed zones at Jewel’s Forest Valley, which has more than 30 installations . There’s even an enormous Pikachu! The wider festivities last until 3 Jan 2027, so don’t worry if you can’t make it on certain days — there are many more activities for you to explore.
More information, including operating hours for individual events, is available HERE ; go catch ‘em all!
McDonald’s x Pokémon Happy Meal with mini box charms & trading cards coming to Singapore & Malaysia
summary: Pokémon fans can enjoy 30th anniversary celebrations at Changi Airport and Jewel until 3 Jan 2027, with parades, meet-and-greets, photo installations and Pokémon GO activities. The festivities include special performances and free merchandise on selected dates, particularly 7 and 8 Nov 2026. With free admission to the parades and activities requiring on-site registration, it is useful for families and Pokémon fans planning a visit.
title: Free Pokémon parades, meet & greets, performances & more at PokéXciting!

Bookworms rejoice, especially if you reside in the north! Frasers Centrepoint Trust has partnered up with the National Library & Archives Board (NLB) to open The HomePage @ Causeway Point . Labelled as “Singapore’s first-of-its-kind” in a media release by Frasers Property, the hub is slated to open in 2028 as a brand-new reading and social destination. Spanning over 32,000 sq ft across parts of the mall’s sixth and seventh floors , the space will bring together books, community activities and family-friendly experiences.
Credit – Frasers Property
The name and design of The HomePage @ Causeway Point are inspired by the concept of home. Just as a home offers comfort, the hub will welcome visitors into a warm and inviting space. The design draws inspiration from familiar parts of Singapore’s architectural history, including the iconic Teck Whye HDB estates, the former NLB library at Stamford Road and the geometric forms of Brutalist architecture in the 1970s.
Credit – Frasers Property
One of Singapore’s largest publicly accessible assemblages of pre-loved books from NLB will also be available here for browsing. The collection of books includes both English and Mother Tongue languages. Look through the pre-loved books and bring them home without having to borrow them! There’s no return-by date; instead, we are encouraged to pass on the books to others to share the joy of reading.
Credit – Frasers Property
#Supportlocal; there will also be a dedicated showcase of Singapore Literature (Sing Lit) and local authors. NLB will curate the space alongside the National Arts Council . Through their wide variety of Sing Lit titles, thematic exhibitions and programmes, you can look forward to celebrating Singapore’s literary heritage.
Credit – Frasers Property
Beyond the books, it will also serve as a social hub for all ages. You’ll be able to enjoy food and beverages while relaxing with a book. The space also includes family-friendly amenities such as children’s play zones, an indoor theatre and a screening space. One key feature of The HomePage is The Social Steps , a multi-purpose terraced public living room where visitors can gather, unwind or participate in community activities.
10 best secondhand bookstores for thrifty bookworms
summary: The HomePage @ Causeway Point is a 32,000 sq ft reading and social hub opening in 2028 across the mall’s sixth and seventh floors. Developed with NLB, it will feature free pre-loved books, Singapore Literature, community programmes, food and beverage options, and family-friendly facilities. It is a useful future destination for book lovers, families and north-side residents seeking a shared space for reading and community activities.
title: The HomePage @ Causeway Point: Free books at 32,000 sq ft hub, opens 2028

Yup, you heard me right. Inspired by the success of his first Singaporean venture just months prior, Michelin-recognised Chef Shusaku Toba behind Sio Pasta in Raffles City has opened an upscale alternative among the colourful shophouses of Tanjong Pagar . While Sio Pasta focuses on fast and casual meals, the newly unveiled o/sio — which officially opens 4 Nov 2026 — pivots towards a complete dining experience while keeping prices reasonable.
With the original o/sio branch hailing from the affluent Marunouchi district in Tokyo, you can expect nothing short of impeccable standards from this new expansion. Additionally, a second branch of Sio Pasta is in the works and is slated to open in late 2026 to mid 2027.
Here’s what we tried ahead of o/sio’s official opening:
My personal favourite, the Snow Crab Genovese (S$26.80) struck a perfect balance between fresh, herbaceous flavours and rich umami from the G rana Padano . The rustic pesto sauce was a little coarse and had a nice mouthfeel. It leaned more towards being bright and less salty than a typical pesto, which was a great move considering the mountain of fresh snow crab meat crowning the pasta. The crab was slightly sweet and naturally briny, which added the subtle saltiness that the dish needed to shine.
The noodles had a unique texture, where they were slightly chewy and QQ , almost like udon noodles — rather than purely al dente . To me, this dish was exemplary of the fusion between Japanese ingredients and Italian techniques that o/sio specialises in.
Moving onto another classic Italian dish, we tried their Maple Quattro Formaggi (S$16.80) . It features an ooey-gooey mascarpone cream base, with melted Fior di Latte on top. The pizza is speckled throughout with crumbled G orgonzola and freshly grated G rana Padano , giving it a sharp, intense flavour every few bites.
The pizza dough at o/sio goes through an arduous fermentation process, which yields a light, flavourful crust in the final product. All the pizzas are then baked in a wood-fired oven for under 2 minutes, demonstrating complete mastery of heat control.
To really elevate the pizza to a whole new level, be sure to add a drizzle of the provided maple syrup. It’s a creative alternative to the more traditional honey pairing and adds even more to the dish with its subtle woody undertones which complement the funk of the gorgonzola better than I could have imagined.
Considering the quality and attention to detail of the dishes, the quality-to-price ratio here is more than decent.
If you’re looking for your next budget-friendly date night spot, be sure to check out o/sio, which officially opens its doors on 4 Nov 2026.
29 best Italian restaurants to relish in Singapore
summary: o/sio is a Japanese-Italian restaurant located among the shophouses of Tanjong Pagar, established by Michelin-recognised Chef Shusaku Toba as an upscale alternative to his Raffles City venture. The establishment offers reasonably priced menu items such as snow crab genovese and wood-fired pizzas, making it suitable for diners seeking budget-friendly date night options ahead of its opening on 4 Nov 2026.
title: Michelin Guide Tokyo chef’s new restaurant has pasta under $30

Smokin’ Hot
Credit: South & East

Credit: South & East

Festive Period

Credit: South & East

Smoke First, Dessert After

Do you wear clothes in an onsen?
Most onsens require you to be fully unclothed, but some onsens in Singapore allow you to wear approved swimwear or bathing suits, so check with the staff before entering.

PokéXciting! at Changi Airport & Jewel
The Pokémon hype isn’t dying down anytime soon, especially with the beloved franchise celebrating its 30th anniversary this year. And to mark the occasion, Changi Airport and Jewel Changi Airport have teamed up with Pokémon for PokéXciting! , a special Asia tour running from now till 3rd January 2027 .
We got a sneak peek of the festivities, and there’s a lot to get excited about, from fun photo spots to interactive activations. But if you’re short on time, we’ve rounded up the must-see and must-do highlights that Pokémon fans won’t want to miss.
What is PokéXciting! all about?
We’re not kidding when we say it’s a Pokémon fan’s dream come true. PokéXciting! Has transformed Changi Airport and Jewel into an immersive Pokémon-themed world, with activities to keep fans of all ages entertained.
You can take part in a Pokémon quiz rally to redeem a token, catch Pokémon parades , and meet Pikachu in person. There’s also the chance to browse exclusive Pokémon merchandise and snap IG-worthy photos at the various themed photo spots . We’ll get into the details below.
What are the highlights at the PokéXciting! event?
Catch all 27 first partner Pokémon in a heartwarming parade
Making its Asia debut, this highly anticipated PokéXciting First Partner Pokémon Parade brings together all 27 first partner Pokémon from the 9 generations of the video game series, alongside 2 Pikachu.
That’s 29 adorable characters in total, including fan-favourites like Charmander and Squirtle, all coming together for a lively parade at Jewel’s Forest Valley on 7th and 8th November 2026 , with 2 sessions daily at 3pm and 6pm .
We could barely contain our excitement seeing all the characters in person! Their costumes look just like the real deal, and watching them dance, sway, wave, and interact with the crowd was enough to make any Pokémon fan squeal.
As if that wasn’t cute enough, the characters also lined up together at the end of the parade, giving everyone a chance to snap a group photo of all of them.
Admission to the parade is free , but take note that you’ll need to register onsite before entering. Wristbands will be issued 2 hours before each showtime, and entry is on a first-come, first-served basis. If you’re hoping to catch these adorable creatures in action, we’d recommend heading down early.
Check out more than 30 PokéXciting! installations at Jewel’s Forest Valley
Don’t fret even if you didn’t manage to snag a slot to the parade. To fill up your camera roll, you can still make a beeline for Jewel’s Forest Valley , where over 30 Pokémon-themed installations are scattered across the space. These are split into 4 themed zones: the Eevee Evolutions Zone , Snorlax Zone , Mewtwo Zone , and Pikachu Zone .
We spotted a Snorlax lounging about, looking every bit as unbothered as the sleepy Pokémon usually does. But one of the highlights here is the larger-than-life Pikachu installation, which makes for an adorable photo op.
Hunt down photo spots across Changi’s terminals & Jewel
Make sure to also keep your eyes peeled as you explore Changi Airport’s terminals and Jewel, where you’ll find Pokémon-themed decorations and photo spots tucked away at various corners.
For starters, head to Level 2 of Jewel , near Wilson and PS.Cafe, where we spotted 2 photo opportunities. One features Charizard’s wings and fiery breath as a backdrop, complete with a mini Charmander by its side for you to pose with. The other showcases Ho-Oh’s majestic wings .
Over at Terminal 3 (T3) Departure Hall , remember to look up, where you’ll spot a banner featuring 3 Pikachus striking cute poses.
Meanwhile, along the check-in counters, look out for Pokémon popping up in groups of 3 . Each section features a different trio of characters, so see how many familiar faces you can spot.
Image credit: Changi Airport Group
There are also Pokémon-themed horticultural displays scattered across all 4 Changi Airport terminals . So if you have some time to spare before your flight, make it a Pokémon hunt and try to track them all down.
Take part in a quiz rally to redeem a Pokémon 30th anniversary postcard
Think you know all things Pokémon? Put your knowledge to the test with the Pokémon TCG Quiz Rally , happening across Jewel from now till 3rd January 2027 . Make your way from Basement 1 to Level 5 , where you’ll find TCG displays accompanied by a question board.
Complete the quiz, and you’ll get to redeem a Pokémon 30th Anniversary postcard as a keepsake to bring home.
To participate, collect your Quiz Rally card and redeem your prize at the Redemption Counter at B1 Atrium , between Birkenstock and ZARA. The counter is open daily from 11am to 10pm , with the last redemption at 9.30pm .
Visit the lounge with free Pokémon Trading Card Game (TCG) & video games
Or head to the Pokémon Experience Lounge , where you can try out free-to-play video games and Pokémon TCG till 3rd January 2027 .

It’s time for Thanksgiving in Singapore! Come 26 November 2026, we’ll throw on our loosest pants for a spectacular feast. Think of it as a Christmas prelude! So what if it’s been a chaotic year? There’s always something to be grateful for. Round up your family and friends – it’s time to gobble up Thanksgiving treats. P.S. We’ve also got guides on turkey delivery in Singapore and Christmas dinner in Singapore .
Why trust this guide
No one should have to spend Thanksgiving stressing over what’s for dinner. We’ve rounded up Singapore’s festive feasts, from traditional turkey spreads to indulgent buffets, so all you need to do is bring your appetite. Each listing contains details on menus, prices, locations and booking information to help you plan your celebration.
Best Thanksgiving dinners in Singapore for 2026
1. Andaz Singapore
Photography: Andaz Singapore
Thanksgiving is a full-blown celebration at all-day dining restaurant Alley on 25 at Andaz Singapore, with an all-you-can-eat dinner feast. For one evening only, the hotel beckons with a festive spread, featuring all-time buffet favourites, succulent meat carvings, seasonal specialties and decadent desserts. Ease into the indulgence with a round of fresh seafood on ice (think seasonal oysters, vannamei prawns and green-lipped mussels), charcuterie and cheese, as well as sustainably-sourced greens from the hotel’s partner farms. Next, the feasting continues with comforting hot dishes, including whole roasted barramundi, margherita D.O.P pizza and muscat pumpkin risotto.
To get into the festive mood, stop by the carving station for slow-roasted whole tom turkey (with all the trimmings, of course), pot-roasted wagyu brisket and slow-roasted porchetta. Enjoy these juicy meats with an array of seasonal sides, such as balsamic-roasted Brussels’ sprouts and maple-roasted carrots. The dessert selection is equally enticing. Sink your teeth into pumpkin spice trifle, pecan tartlets, or freshly-made apple pie crepes drizzled with vanilla sauce. The house-churned sorbet and gelato bar, and candy bar will be hard to resist, too. Want to dial up the merriment? Top up $58, and toast to a free-flowing selection of wines, beers and seasonal cocktails.
Best for: Indulgent festive buffet spreads with free-flowing booze
Price: From $88 per adult and $44 per child; top up $58 each for the bottomless boozy package
When: 26 November 2026
Timings: 6pm to 10pm
Address: Andaz Singapore , 5 Fraser Street, Singapore 189354
2. LUCE at Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore
Photography: Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore
‘Tis the season to visit, so take a seat at LUCE at Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel’s indulgent Thanksgiving buffet. From premium seafood on ice and Italian specialties to festive carving stations and international favourites, the abundant spread has something for everyone. We’ve got our eyes on classic holiday highlights, including roasted pumpkin and chestnut soup, traditional roasted U.S. tom turkey, and the Thankful turkey pinsa. The handmade pasta selection and signature seafood creations are not to be missed, too.
For a sweet finale, you’ve got a decadent array of seasonal desserts and sweet treats to choose from. Satisfy your sweet tooth with pecan tartlets featuring buttery crusts, and a Thanksgiving classic, The Great Pumpkin Pie. Prefer celebrating in the comfort of your home? Good news: Frasers House lets you bring home the festive warmth with takeaway gourmet roasts. Pick a star for your feast – among the likes of Nyonya spice-marinated turkey, oven-baked rosemary-marinated bone-in lamb leg, and spiced manuka honey and citrus-glazed gammon ham – pair it with seasonal accompaniments, and you’ve got yourself a sumptuous spread.
Best for: An all-you-can-eat holiday feast with Italian flair
Price: $98 per adult and $59 per child
When: 26 November 2026 (dine-in menu); online pre-orders open from now till 29 December 2026; available for delivery and self-collection from 23 November 2026 to 1 Jan 2027 (takeaway menu)
Timings: 6pm to 10pm
Address: LUCE , 80 Middle Road, Singapore 188966
3. Meadesmoore
Photography: Meadesmoore
Upgrade your Thanksgiving celebration at home with generous goodies from this modern steakhouse. Meaty mains get the spotlight: choose from the smoked honey mustard glazed turkey two ways or the Sanchoku F1 wagyu tomahawk MS 4/5 with flaky sea salt and black Kampot pepper. The sets, good for four to six people, also include a roasted butternut squash and couscous salad.
Don’t forget the sides! The signature mac and cheese is a creamy must-order, while the roasted squash and beetroot, along with shaved Brussels sprouts, apple and cranberry salad add a little veggie action to your spread. And for a sweet finish, enjoy the wild berry pie served with marbled chantilly cream.
Best for: Meaty feasts for your dinner table at home
Price: Thanksgiving sets from $328+

body:
I’ll admit, I’m hardly an expert when it comes to F&B drama, though my nosy streak usually keeps me in the loop. But it wasn’t insider gossip that first drew me to Boys Don’t Fry . Instead, it was the endless stream of golden, crispy fish and chips on my For You Page that finally convinced me to pay Wisma Cosway a visit.
The story goes like this. Once upon a time, there was a partnership called Lad & Fry , born from the collaboration of a British chap and a Singaporean partner. Somewhere along the way, they parted ways, resulting in two separate shops: Boys Don’t Fry and Lad & Dad . Both happen to be free of alcohol , pork , and lard . That’s the backstory I only discovered after choosing Boys Don’t Fry as my lunch spot, purely by chance and not out of preference, I promise.
What I tried at Boys Don’t Fry
Boys Don’t Fry keeps its menu refreshingly simple, which in itself feels like a quiet statement of confidence. Diners can either commit to the full set of fish and chips or build their own plate with à la carte options . They also serve breakfast butties , as well as bottled sodas from Melaka !
My meal began with the classic Fish & Chips Set (RM38) . It arrived with a generous slab of perch cloaked in golden batter, thick-cut fries, mushy peas, tartar sauce, and a choice between pickles or baked beans. I went with pickles. The set also came with bottomless lemonade, though its tang leaned more towards orange cordial than the sharp citrusy lift of real lemonade.
The fish looked promising at first glance. The batter was delicately crisp, the kind that shatters with a gentle tap of the fork. It wasn’t greasy, nor did it cling to the fish. Instead, it formed a light shell that sealed in the perch, which was astonishingly tender and juicy. I never quite realised fish could taste this good. Seasoning was straightforward, relying on savoury depth rather than spice.
The sides, however, had mixed results. The fries were a letdown — pale, soft, and lacking the satisfying crunch I prefer. The tartar sauce was serviceable yet strangely addictive, while the mushy peas were simply seasoned but comforting in their own way.
The pickled cabbage, served with half a boiled egg , tasted unexpectedly mild. Its gentle tang made it feel like it was only tossed in vinegar mixture for a while, even though its texture revealed it had been fermenting for some time.
For variety, I also sampled the Fish Nuggies (RM18) , smaller battered slices of perch paired with tartar sauce and lemon. These won me over instantly. The smaller cuts meant the fish stayed moist and tender while encased in that light, crunchy batter.
Final thoughts
Boys Don’t Fry knows how to make a fish shine. Their batter is crisp without being heavy, the perch inside is juicy and delicate, and the whole plate feels like a carefully constructed ode to the classic British staple. Still, the portion proved a little overwhelming, and I found myself slowing down before I could finish. That said, for anyone chasing a solid plate of fish and chips in Kuala Lumpur , Boys Don’t Fry is a worthy contender.
