What else to try at Wisma Cosway?
Which fish & chips spot reign supreme in KL?
summary: Boys Don’t Fry at Wisma Cosway, Kuala Lumpur, serves British-style fish and chips alongside à la carte options, breakfast butties and bottled sodas. Its RM38 fish and chips set features tender perch in crisp, light batter, while the RM18 Fish Nuggies offer a smaller alternative. With alcohol-, pork- and lard-free offerings, it is a useful option for diners seeking classic fish and chips, though the soft fries and generous portions may not suit everyone.
title: Boys Don’t Fry: Famous halal-friendly fish & chips in KL with crispy & juicy perch, plus breakfast butties & Melaka sodas

body:
Singapore-Malaysia customs rules
We’ve all been guilty of getting a little carried away with shopping in JB, especially when everything seems cheaper across the Causeway. But before you happily haul everything back across the Causeway, there’s one last hurdle to clear: Singapore Customs and bureaucracy. And we’re not just talking about the infamous 3/4-tank rule.
Turns out, there are quite a few customs rules that even frequent JB-goers might not know about, from how much you can spend before GST kicks in to which groceries you’re actually allowed to bring home. Here’s a handy guide to the SG-JB customs rules worth knowing, so your shopping haul doesn’t come with an unexpected bill or a lengthy stop at the checkpoint.
1. You only get S$100 in GST relief for a day trip to JB
It’s easy to just swipe your card at the shopping malls in JB , especially when clothes, sneakers, and electronics seem like such good deals compared to Singapore. But here’s something to keep in mind before going on a shopping spree: you only get S$100 in GST relief if you’ve been overseas for less than 48 hours.
That means if you spend S$250 on a new pair of sneakers during a day trip, you’ll have to pay GST on the remaining S$150. The good news is that if you’re away for 48 hours or more , your GST relief increases to S$500 , provided you’re eligible.
This applies to everyday purchases like clothes, shoes, and gadgets too. So if you’re planning a major shopping haul, remember to factor in the prevailing 9% GST on purchases exceeding your relief limit, along with any applicable duties.
2. No duty-free alcohol allowance when returning from Malaysia
Spotted a good deal on your favourite wine or whisky during a JB supermarket run? If you’re stocking up for your next house party, here’s something to know: there’s no duty-free alcohol allowance when entering Singapore from Malaysia, even if you’ve been away for more than 48 hours.
That means you’ll have to declare and pay duty and GST on any beer, wine, or spirits you bring back, even if it’s just a single bottle for personal consumption. And nope, the S$100 or S$500 GST relief we mentioned earlier doesn’t apply to alcohol either.
It’s not just the usual booze that’s affected. Alcoholic cooking ingredients like rice wine and cooking wine, as well as medicinal liquors like Yomeishu and D.O.M., are also included. If you’re planning to bring back more than 10 litres of liquor, you’ll need a Customs permit too.
You can declare your purchases and pay the applicable taxes through the Customs@SG web application up to 3 days before returning to Singapore. We’d recommend doing the maths to see if it’s still worth the savings after taxes.
3. Not even 1 packet of cigarettes is duty-free
Besides alcohol, Singapore also has no duty-free allowance for cigarettes . Even if you’re bringing back just 1 packet for personal use, you’ll still need to declare it and pay the applicable duty and GST.
There’s also a limit to how much you can bring back. Rather than counting by packets or cartons, the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) sets a maximum of 400g of tobacco products for personal consumption.
And don’t forget the packaging. Under Singapore’s standardised packaging requirements, cigarette packets must be drab brown, display graphic health warnings, and have no tobacco-related logos or branding.
4. Carrying more than S$20,000 in cash? You need to declare it
If you’re bringing a large sum of cash across the Causeway, whether it’s for a big purchase or a wedding in Malaysia, you might be surprised to know that Singapore doesn’t impose a limit on how much you can carry. However, any amount exceeding S$20,000 (or its equivalent in foreign currency) must be declared to the authorities.
And it’s not just cold, hard cash that counts. The rule also applies to bearer negotiable instruments, such as traveller’s cheques and certain other cheques. You’ll need to submit an electronic declaration within 72 hours before entering or leaving Singapore , which you can do through the MyICA app or ICA’s website .
So if you’re heading to JB with a particularly thick ang bao stash, make sure you’ve sorted out the paperwork before crossing the border.
5. There’s a 5kg & S$100 limit for JB supermarket snacks
A JB grocery run isn’t complete without stocking up on snacks and pantry essentials. The good news is that you can bring back plenty of supermarket finds, including biscuits, kimchi, nuts, jams, and even dairy products like milk and ice cream.
We love hitting up our favourite supermarkets in JB or the new ST Rosyam Mart just as much as the next person. But take note of the 5kg or 5-litre limit for processed food , with a total value of no more than S$100 per traveller under Singapore Food Agency (SFA) regulations. Another thing to note is that it’s the combined allowance for all your processed food purchases, not 5kg for each type of snack.
…
summary: Rules to know before your next Causeway trip.
title: 8 SG-JB Customs Rules You Should Know Besides The 3/4-Tank Rule

Fun things to do in Singapore this weekend are abundant, from checking out cool cafes, bars and restaurants to exciting things to do in Singapore in November . Bookmark this page if you’re always on the lookout for limited-time menus, parties, and news on all the new events happening during the weekend. Remember to keep up to date with what’s happening in Singapore ! Let’s hop on to the list of fun things to do in Singapore this weekend.
Things to do this weekend in Singapore
1. [Free!] Craft Festival 2026
Photography: Junhwa Studios (left) & Rosymaide (right)
Art markets in Singapore are the place to be when you need to get your Christmas gift shopping out of the way. That’s why you should free up your schedule and pay the Craft Festival a visit. In a room full of creatives, artisans, and designers, you’re sure to find gifts for everyone in your friend group.
When: 7 to 8 November 2026
How much: Free admission
Where: Craft Festival 2026 , Hall 401 – 402, Suntec City, 3 Temasek Boulevard, Singapore 038983
2. [Free!] Bonfire Market
Photography: Aa Furniture
It’s never too early to get your festive shopping out of the way. That’s why Aa Furniture is hosting its festive market a little earlier than usual! This year’s market shines a spotlight on ceramics, a material and craft connecting many of the cultures where Aa Furniture’s products originate. Plant enthusiast Dry Spell Garden offers an opportunity to explore a less familiar side of xeric plants, while Chu and Co will keep you fed with its glorious bakes. And if you need help staying awake, grab a cuppa from Flip Coffee Roasters.
When: 7 to 8 November 2026
How much: Free admission
Where: Bonfire Market , #07-01, Ho Seng Lee Flatted Warehouse, 10C Jalan Ampas, Singapore 329513
3. Singapore Cat Festival 2026
Photography: Singapore Cat Festival via Facebook
The biggest gathering of cats is happening this weekend! The Singapore Cat Festival returns for its sixth edition, creating the event of the season for cat lovers, owners, and enthusiasts. Expect all kinds of kitty things like products, art, treats, and activities by local vendors who celebrate our feline companions who call Singapore home. And there are cat adoption opportunities if you’re looking to adopt one of your own (assuming the cat distribution system hasn’t reached you yet).
When: 7 to 8 November 2026
How much: Tickets start from $7
Where: Singapore Cat Festival 2026 , Hall 6, Singapore Expo, 1 Expo Drive, Singapore 486150
4. Friends of Claudine: 5th Anniversary Edition
Photography: Claudine
Five years of Claudine’s beautiful French fine dining must be celebrated with something special – a guest chef collaboration! For one weekend, chef-owner Thomas Lefebvre of Auberge du Bac is coming to Claudine, bringing a bit of the French countryside to the restaurant. A dear friend of chef Julien Royer’s for over 20 years, the two share a love of honest home-cooking and generous hospitality. A special menu has been curated by the pair, featuring timeless French classics and personal recipes honed over the years at Auberge du Bac.
When: 6 to 8 November 2026
How much: Prices of a la carte dishes vary
Where: Friends of Claudine: 5th Anniversary Edition , 39C Harding Road, Singapore 249541
5. Singapore Clay Festival
Photography: Singapore Clay Festival
We’ll never say no to more ceramics in our collection, and this is our favourite art market in Singapore to find new creations. Connect with clay makers at the Singapore Clay Festival and browse wares of all shapes and sizes. Beyond shopping, you can admire the Shaping Clay exhibition, listen to talks by expert ceramic artists, and even participate in clay workshops.
When: 6 to 8 November 2026
How much: Tickets start from $10
Where: Singapore Clay Festival , Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre, 1 Straits Boulevard, Singapore 018906
6. [Free!] Retro Flea Market
Photography: The Retro Factory
Katong’s worst-kept secret is the Retro Vintage Flea Market that happens during specific weekends, and we’re here to spread the word. This is one of our favourite flea markets in Singapore with its wide array of vintage knick-knacks and old-school finds. We’re also partial to the vendors who sell a pretty selection of watches here. And for any filmmakers looking for realistic props, you know where to be.
When: 6 to 8 November 2026
How much: Free admission
Where: Retro Flea Market , 88 East Coast Road, Singapore 423371
7. Streetwearehouse 3
Photography: Weare via Instagram
If your wardrobe constantly needs refreshing, pay Singapore’s biggest streetwear market a visit this weekend. Streetweare is known to deliver some of the coolest threads that’ll jazz up any wardrobe. This time, the team is bringing in some Vietnamese labels along with its usual collection of vintage and thrifted finds. While you’re there, snap some pictures at the photobooth, or grab some jagua tattoos!
When: 7 to 8 November 2026, 12pm to 8pm
How much: Free admission

body: The Place Taking over the space of the now defunct PST Pizza Studio Tamaki – Singapore is o/sio from Tokyo, the original restaurant by Michelin-recognised Chef Shusaku Toba. This is the sister restaurant of sio pasta at Raffles City, where Chef Toba brings his restaurant from Tokyo’s Marunouchi district for its first international outpost. Think of sio pasta as a faster paced and more causal concept as compared to o/sio which offers a broader expression of Chef Toba’s culinary philosophy. The interior has not changed much from PST Pizza, where the ambience of the shophouse space is relaxed and cosy. The Food Expect fresh handmade pasta, charcoal-grilled meats, seasonal produce, sharing plates, desserts and wine in a relaxed and convivial setting designed for casual lunches and after-work drinks. In terms of menu for the Singapore outpost, there is slight variation to Tokyo. The appetisers selection is very wide and I had their Crispy Sweet Shrimp (S$12.80) which is fried to a crisp texture. Pasta selections are also very varied with all under S$30, where the Snow Crab Genovese (S$26.80) with basil pesto is done to an al dente texture and the heaps of snow crab is quite the highlight for

Gyu-Kaku closes its restaurant at CHIJMES on Sunday 15 November 2026, ending its run at the restored convent in the Civic District. Reins International (Singapore), which runs the brand here, made the closure public in a notice on 3 November .
Rewards cards stay valid to the last day. The card earns one chop for every S$20 spent on a single receipt. Ten chops bring a free serving of pork belly, 15 a serving of Gyu-Kaku Karubi on the next visit, and 20 chops take 20 per cent off the next bill. Redemptions need a minimum spend of S$50, are for dine-in only and do not apply to the buffets.
Four buffets before the last day
Every buffet runs for 90 minutes, with last orders 20 minutes before the end. Prices are per adult and carry service charge and GST.
• Family Buffet, S$38.80++: more than 30 dishes, Monday to Thursday only, not on public holidays or their eves.
• Signature Buffet, S$54.80++: more than 60 dishes, adding Dragon Karubi, Diamond Cut Misuji, Negishio beef tongue, scallops and prawns.
• Premium Buffet, S$79.80++: more than 80 dishes, with Australian Wagyu, King Harami and beef thick tongue.
• Wagyu Buffet, S$98.80++: the Premium spread plus Japanese Wagyu Nakaochi, Karubi and Sukiyaki.
The Wagyu Buffet is S$98.80++ and the Premium Buffet S$79.80++ per adult. Image: Gyu-Kaku Singapore
Children aged 12 and below pay half price, capped at two children for each paying adult. Green tea comes with every buffet; soft drinks, juices, ice lemon tea and oolong tea are S$4.80 more. Leftovers are charged at S$10 per 100g.
Monday 9 November is the Deepavali public holiday, so the Family Buffet’s last three days are Tuesday 10 to Thursday 12 November.
Weekday lunch is the cheaper last meal
Lunch sets run Monday to Friday, except public holidays, which makes Friday 13 November the final weekday lunch. The value lunch starts at S$9.80++ for a chicken teriyaki don, with a wagyu don at S$11.80++, spicy ramen or wagyu udon at S$12.80++, and tonkatsu or yakiniku teishoku at S$15.80++.
The grill-your-own BBQ lunch sets come with salad, kimchi, wakame soup and steamed rice. Pork belly and chicken (180g) is S$12.80++, Karubi and Harami (150g) and the Australian Wagyu set are S$28.80++ each, and the Japanese Wagyu beef set is S$38.80++. A 320ml Asahi is S$5.20++ at lunch only.
BBQ lunch sets run Monday to Friday, except public holidays. Image: Gyu-Kaku Singapore
A chain built on A4 wagyu
Gyu-Kaku, “horn of the bull” in Japanese, has more than 700 restaurants in Japan and outlets in the United States, Hong Kong, Taipei and Indonesia. In Singapore it serves A4 rather than A5 wagyu, and only chuck, rib and loin cuts, on the view that the grade measures marbling and yield rather than flavour.
The menu carries pork throughout, so Gyu-Kaku is not a halal option.
Details
• Gyu-Kaku CHIJMES, 30 Victoria Street, #01-01/02, Singapore 187996, a short walk from City Hall and Bras Basah MRT stations.
• Monday to Friday: lunch 12pm to 3pm (last order 2.30pm), dinner 5.30pm to 10pm (last order 9.30pm).
• Saturday, Sunday and public holidays: 12pm to 10pm (last order 9.30pm).
• Reservations: 6333 4001. Last day of service: Sunday 15 November 2026.
summary: Gyu-Kaku's CHIJMES restaurant serves its final meals on 15 November 2026. Buffets run from S$38.80++ and rewards stay redeemable to the last day.
title: Gyu-Kaku closes its CHIJMES restaurant on 15 November

body:
Can you have too much hawker food? No! Which is why, my dear friends, I bring you Hawkers’ Street. They have opened their 10th outlet at Anchorpoint . With this new spot, you can expect up to 8 different brands under 1 roof. 5 of them are even Michelin-recognised. Opened on 4 Nov 2026 , Hawkers’ Street is worth a visit to see what they have in store.
You can find this food hall at #B1-20/21 in Anchorpoint , and it can seat up to 200 people. That is a lot of hungry hawker fans in 1 place. I suppose this shows their confidence in the stalls they plan to showcase.
This is 1 of those rare cases where something has both quality and quantity. 8 stalls are nothing to scoff at. On top of that, 5 of those stalls are Michelin-recognised. Stalls like Song Fish Soup , Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice and Tai Wah Pork Noodle hold Bib Gourmand status. This place intends to elevate your day-to-day lunch.
Here’s some lore for you: Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice dates back to 1988 , and owner Cheong Weng Wah earned its Bib Gourmand in 2016. Their other outlets have all been highly rated across the board. I expect the outlet at Anchorpoint will be the same. Another notable entrant is Tai Wah Pork Noodle, which started in 1939 at Tai Wah Coffeeshop on Hill Street. You may recognise them for their bak chor mee .
Now, 545 Whampoa Prawn Noodles and Hokkien Man Hokkien Mee are the 2 stalls that are Michelin Selected. Both serve their own unique versions of prawn broth in some of their dishes. If you’re feeling curious, why not try dishes from both stalls and see if you can taste the difference? Or better yet, find the stall you prefer.
Mind you, the remaining 3 stalls are nothing to scoff at either. Hwa Heng Beef Noodles, Hill Street Hainanese Curry Rice and Hill Street Coffee Shop . Hwa Heng, formerly Odeon Beef Noodles Singapore , has been serving beef noodles since 1948 . And after their revival in 2022 at Jalan Besar, they are going to go even further. As you can see from the pic, the people are already loving it.
On top of the many yummy options, you can also stand a chance to win merch! Items include a thermal lunch bag, cutlery set, a sticker sheet or even a power bank. All you have to do is dine in and spend at least S$10 in a single receipt to get a scratch card. Each card reveals a piece of limited edition merchandise. The promotion runs from 11am to 9pm , from 4 to 10 Nov 2026 , while stocks last. Fans can aim to collect a full set of the 4 items.
Should you feel that Anchorpoint is far from where you live, don’t worry! They have 9 other outlets spread across Singapore. Check out their website to see which outlet is closest to you. Do note that each outlet likely has a different variety of food. Level up your lunch at Hawkers’ Street today.
Hock Gooi Hainanese Curry Rice: Loaded curry rice from $4 with crispy pork chop, braised pork & pork trotters
summary: Hawkers’ Street has opened its 10th outlet at Anchorpoint, bringing 8 hawker brands into one food hall at #B1-20/21, including 5 Michelin-recognised stalls such as Song Fish Soup and Tai Wah Pork Noodle. The 200-seat venue suits nearby residents and office workers looking for everyday meals. Diners who spend at least S$10 in one receipt from 4 to 10 Nov 2026 receive a scratch card for limited edition merchandise.
title: Hawkers’ Street – 5 Michelin guide stalls at Anchorpoint that will level-up lunch

In case you missed it, Pokémon is celebrating its 30th anniversary this year. To commemorate this milestone, the popular franchise is bringing a PokéXciting celebration to Singapore at Changi Airport and Jewel .
As someone who spent countless hours on Pokémon Ruby as a kid, and who still revisits the popular animation and songs from time to time, I was definitely PokéXcited to see what The Pokémon Company has cooked up.
And let’s just say that when my colleague and I dropped by for the first day of the PokéXciting event, we were overwhelmed in the best way possible. There was a surprising amount of Pokémon activities and appearances throughout Changi Airport, so here are our personal highlights we think you should catch… ‘em all .
Pokémon Parade
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
The Pokémon Parade at Jewel was definitely one of the best parts of our day. For those of you who would love to get up close with 29 adorable Pokémon from all 9 current generations, you cannot miss this.
This gigantic parade will take place on 7 & 8 November 2026 only , at 3pm and 6pm at Jewel’s Forest Valley . If you’d like to catch your favourite Pokémon, arrive early, as registration is required onsite on a first-come , first-served basis. Admission is free with limited capacity .
Pokégenic Photo Spots
Credit: Changi Airport Group
As you go on your own PokéXciting adventure around the airport, look out for Pokégenic photo spots , such as this cute Pikachu mural at Terminal 3 (T3) . Pokémon will make special appearances on walls and in installations across all four terminals, so spot them and snap many photos!
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Can’t get enough photos with Pikachu? Take one with this larger-than-life statue at the entrance to Jewel’s Forest Valley!
Exclusive Merchandise & Premiums
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
At T3’s Basement 2 , near ST3PS, you will find a Pokémon Pop-up Store and a Pokémon Personalisation Station . Here, you can get your hands on special-edition anniversary merchandise , including T-shirts, vinyl stickers , and more .
With a minimum spend , you can also unlock access to personalised exclusives !
Credit: Changi Airport Group
Spend at least S$60 on a single receipt at participating outlets across Changi Airport terminals, Jewel or on iShopChangi, and you can purchase a Pokémon Cap or Pokémon Poké Ball Bag for S$12.90 . These items come with a free charm featuring 1 of 3 starter Pokémon: Charmander, Bulbasaur, and Squirtle.
Credit: Changi Airport Group
For further customisation, you can top up S$9.90 for an additional Pikachu charm , as well as custom name embroidery .
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
If you’d like even more charms on your bag and cap, you can find and purchase them at the pop-up store. Look out for your favourite Pokémon and make your accessories truly unique!
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
With the same minimum spend of S$60 , you will also be eligible to purchase exclusive Pokémon 30th Anniversary premiums . This includes Pikachu and Eevee plushies (S$18.90) , a travel blanket (S$9.90) , luggage (S$52.90–S$74.90) , and more.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
These premiums can be found at a Redemption counter on T3’s Basement 2 level, not far from the Pop-up Store and Personalisation Counter. If you spend a minimum of S$100 on a single receipt , you can also head to this counter for a Memory Game Challenge .
Get a high score and stand to win Pokémon Medallions , Funko Pop figurines , Pokémon Trading Cards , and more.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Changi Rewards members who spend S$600 cumulatively get to redeem a special Pokémon 30th Anniversary premium and Fun Pack , which includes 3 collectable playing cards .
If you’re a Mastercard holder , use your card for your purchases, and you can buy an additional umbrella at the Redemption counter, and another Pokémon Cap or Pokémon Poké Ball Bag at the Personalisation Station.
Pokémon Experience Lounge
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
It wouldn’t be Pokémon without fun and games . Head over to T3’s Departure Hall , where you will find a Pokémon Experience Lounge , open daily from 12pm to 9pm , until 3 January 2027 . Here, you can battle other trainers in Pokémon Champions and the Pokémon Trading Card Game (TCG) , or discover Pokémon Pokopia .
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Join a free TCG tutorial to take home a Fun Pack , or compete in a Pokémon TCG Battle and Pokémon Champions Tournament on select Saturdays to win attractive prizes . Entry to this lounge is free , but booking a slot beforehand on the Changi App is highly encouraged as space is limited .
PokéXciting Stage and Meet & Greet
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)

body:
Crazy Rich Asians HBO series casting call
Over the last 8 years, many of us have probably repeatedly watched Crazy Rich Asians and imagined ourselves living the high life, complete with extravagant parties, designer outfits, and a bank account that seemingly has no limits. If you can relate, here’s something that might pique your interest.
An upcoming Crazy Rich Asians series by American cable TV company HBO is holding a casting call , and this could be your chance to make your on-screen debut. We’ve gathered everything you need to know if you’ve always fancied yourself as the next Rachel Chu or Nick Young.
What’s happening with the Crazy Rich Asians sequel?
Image credit: Inside Weddings
For those who haven’t heard, Crazy Rich Asians is making a comeback 8 years after the original movie hit cinemas in 2018. This time, we’re getting an 8-episode HBO series that picks up where the movie left off, with familiar faces including Constance Wu, Henry Golding, Ronny Chieng, and Michelle Yeoh returning to reprise their roles.
Production is expected to begin in 2027, although an official release date has yet to be announced.
What are the casting requirements?
Image credit: Amazon
Forget rewatching Crazy Rich Asians for the umpteenth time and fantasising about being an actual crazy rich asian. You might just have a shot at being part of the upcoming HBO series.
HBO and Firefly Casting have announced a global casting call for 2 roles , namely Posy and William. The former is a glamorous and ambitious East Asian woman in her 30s whose marriage to a wealthy tycoon has fallen apart, while the latter is a charming Chinese man in his 20s who’s the son of a Shanghai real estate billionaire.
Image credit: Getty Images
Applicants for both roles must be fluent in English , with those auditioning for Posy needing some familiarity with Mandarin , and those eyeing William’s role should be able to converse in Mandarin .
The best part is that no prior acting experience is required , and auditions are free of charge . Interested applicants just need to submit a self-taped audition following the instructions on the official casting website by 30th November 2026 .
What are netizens saying about the casting call?
Image adapted from: Instagram
Of course, an announcement involving Crazy Rich Asians was bound to get the internet talking. And judging by the comments section, netizens aren’t holding back on jokes and nominating their friends for the roles.
One commenter said, “I can be the plump, judgy auntie in the background. Learning Mandarin via binge-watching C-dramas,” while another joked, “I will be a good fit for a crazy poor asian. Sign me up.” So, it’s safe to say that the casting call has caught people’s attention, whether they’re here for jokes or actually serious about auditioning.
You could be the next Crazy Rich Asian
Image credit: CharacTour
If you’ve always dreamt of appearing on a screen, this might be your opportunity to give acting a shot. You’ve got to start somewhere, even if your bank account isn’t quite at Nick Young’s level yet.
Interested applicants can check out the original Instagram casting announcement for more information on how to apply.
For more reads related to Crazy Rich Asians:
• The Crazy Rich Asians mansion is now open to the public for free
• Spooky abandoned mansion in Singapore that inspired Crazy Rich Asians
• Every character from Crazy Rich Asians ranked
Cover image adapted from: Amazon, CharacTour
summary: Auditions are open till 30th November 2026.
title: HBO Is Holding A Casting Call For Its Upcoming Series – Here’s Your Chance To Be A Crazy Rich Asian

body:
Things to do this weekend in Singapore
Kid-friendly activities, live performances, and fun workshops – there’s plenty of fun to be had in the coming weeks. So, open your calendars and bookmark these things to do this weekend in Singapore.
1. Zoolympix: Stars of Mandai Festive Challenge
7th Nov 2026-3rd Jan 2027
Image credit: Mandai Wildlife Group
This school holidays, the Mandai Wildlife Reserve is hosting an epic event called Zoolympix: Stars of Mandai Festive Challenge . Head to the Zoolympix Village at the Mandai Wildlife EAST Lawn to take on 10 challenges inspired by the special abilities of 2 star animals from each of the 5 wildlife parks.
Each station tests a different skill – from strength and agility, to balance and problem-solving. Through this interactive play, kids not only learn more about these animals, but also find out how they can do their part towards wildlife conservation.
Image credit: Mandai Wildlife Group
Collect a stamp for every challenge you clear and get an exclusive Zoolympian medal which you can strike a victory pose with at the Zoolympix Podium. Present those stamps of completion at selected Mandai shops to take home a commemorative Zoolympix plushie for $9 (U.P. $12) .
The challenges don’t end at the Village either. Seek out Zoolympix Outposts across Singapore Zoo, Bird Paradise, River Wonders, Rainforest Wild Adventure, and Night Safari for bonus challenges inspired by the Stars of Mandai. Along the way, you’ll uncover fascinating animal facts, discover unique abilities, and be encouraged to visit the star animals in their exhibits.
Between the festive light-ups around the reserve and a Partners Zone packed with games and giveaways, there’s enough to fill a full day out. Plus, locals enjoy access to Zoolympix village plus a $10 retail and F&B voucher when they buy a ticket to selected Mandai attractions.
While you’re there, make sure to sign the kiddos up for a workshop or 2. There are a whole bunch to choose from, from pizza making and upcycled room scents to a sewing workshop where kids can design and create their very own chou chou plushie from scratch.
Learn more about Zoolympix at Mandai Wildlife Reserve .
Admission: From $15/pax | Local Residents enjoy access to Zoolympix Village
Venue: 80 Mandai Lake Road, Mandai Wildlife EAST Lawn, Singapore 729826
Date: 7th November 2026-3rd January 2027
Time: 10am-7pm, Daily (Last admission at 6.30pm)
2. Warrior 24/7
Now till 15th Nov
Image credit: Warrior 24/7
Those looking for a meaningful outing this weekend can visit the Warrior 24/7 installation at City Square Mall . Conceived by Parkinson’s disease (PD) advocate and multi-time American Ninja Warrior competitor Jimmy Choi , it’s a showcase of the indomitable fighting spirit that those afflicted with disease display on the daily.
Image credit: Warrior 24/7
It features various stations which invite visitors to step into the shoes of people living with PD. Challenges include fastening buttons with simulated rigidity, picking up fruits with tremor gloves, and testing your balance with wobbling bowls sliding across a food tray.
Complete all 7 stations, and you’ll be rewarded with a specially designed keychain that serves as a token of camaraderie and respect for the PD community. Also, you can get vouchers for a free bottle of Beutea cold brew tea upon completion of all the stations, redeemable only at the Beutea outlet located within the mall.
Admission: Free
Venue: 180 Kitchener Road, City Square Mall, Basement 1, Green Square, Singapore 208539
Date: 7th-15th November 2026
Time: 10am-6pm, Daily
3. Singapore Book Street 2026
Now till 8th Nov
If you’re on the prowl for your next read, there’s really no better place to look than the ongoing Singapore Book Street 2026 . Set up at VivoCity , it’s the largest book fair on the island that’s purposely dedicated to SingLit , with over 1,200 titles across 4 languages to leaf through.
It’s also worth noting that a huge chunk of Singapore Book Street 2026’s offerings are eligible for purchase using SG Culture Pass credits , so if you’ve got any left, now’s a great time to use them.
There’s pretty much every genre you can think of here; when we swung by, we spotted books of all kinds, including fiction, non-fiction, fantasy, poetry, and children’s literature just to name a few. The festival also has other activities such as book signing sessions , interactive storytelling for kids, and even a live typewriter poetry station to get personalised poems.
Learn more about Singapore Book Street 2026 .
Admission: Free
Venue: 180 Kitchener Road, City Square Mall, Basement 1, Green Square, Singapore 208539

Time: 10am-6pm, Daily

body:
Mcdonald’s Thailand and ChaTraMue launch Thai tea menu
Image credit: McDonald’s
Thai Tea lovers, something interesting is cooking at McDonald’s Thailand . For the first time ever, they are teaming up with ChaTraMue , one of Thailand’s most well-known milk tea brands, for a limited-time menu.
Launched on 4 November 2026, this collaboration will run until 5 January 2027 , combining iconic McDonald’s treats with the fragrant drink. Singaporeans taking a year-end trip to Thailand, make sure you give it a go.
The current exchange rate is 1THB = ~S$0.038 as of 5 November 2026.
Image credit: @Chatramue
The limited-time menu features three items. First up, the Thai Tea Custard Pie (THB 35) features the signature McDonald’s crispy fried pie crust, filled with Thai tea and custard filling. If you want something rich and aromatic, this is definitely worth a try.
Image credit: @Chatramue
They’ve also introduced a Thai Tea McFlurry (THB 49) , which puts a twist on the classic Oreo McFlurry by combining crunchy Oreo bits and creamy vanilla soft serve with the fragrant, floral notes of Thai tea.
Image credit: @Chatramue
The last item is the Patongko with Thai Tea Dip Set (THB 55) , fried dough sticks served alongside a Thai tea dip. For anyone wondering, the Patongko are very similar to a Chinese youtiao—crispy, airy, and slightly savoury.
Image credit: @Chatramue
Traditionally, they are enjoyed with condensed milk or pandan custard. However, you can now try them with the floral notes of a concentrated Thai tea dipping sauce thanks to this limited-time collab.

Cheap dim sum in Singapore
My dad is never more enthusiastic about eating in a crowded and bustling environment than when we’re having dim sum. He loves the old Hong Kong feel of enjoying these small bites surrounded by loud chatter from the tables around us, echoes of clinking porcelain tea cups, and harried women pushing dim sum carts stacked high with bamboo baskets around the dining hall. These cheap dim sum in Singapore may not have vibes of that sort, but any disappointment can be resolved by a couple more pieces of tasty siew mai.
1. Bei-Ing Dimsum Club
At Bei-Ing Dimsum Club , you get a creative twist on traditional dim sum. Fun fact: it’s opened by the son of the couple running the famous Bei-Ing Wanton Noodles at Roxy Square 1! Try the Black Truffle Xiao Long Bao ($ 10 .80 for six ) and the Golden Ebiko Cheese S iu Mai ($7.90 for three) , the latter featuring nacho cheese with juicy meat filling and a chewy dumpling skin. Their Aburi-Mentai Fried Chicken Bao ($7.20 for three) features fried bao filled with succulent chicken meat and mentaiko sauce, topped with delicate bonito flakes .
Check out our Bei-Ing Dimsum Club review .

Image credit: @mark.ptkw
Alongside Swee Choon, 126 Dim Sum Wen Dao Shi is undoubtedly one of the most popular dim sum stores in Singapore. Serving up relatively affordable dim sum fare, it’s no wonder this 24-hour dim sum store attracts a huge crowd, even in the wee hours.
Their Shrimp Dumplings ($4. 8 0 + for three) are a favourite of mine because they’re filled with plump pieces of prawns. If you prefer more intense flavours, their Chilli Crab Siew Mai ($6.80 + for three) and Seafood Tom Yum Siew Mai ($4.80 + for three) are worth a try! body:
Three Bowls serves kolo mee at Whampoa Makan Place
Image credit: T greensake via Google Maps
If you want a Din Tai Fung-quality meal without its price tag, this hawker stall is worth checking out. Helmed by former Din Tai Fung chef Robin Lee, Three Bowls serves up East Malaysian fare at Whampoa Makan Place .
Paying homage to his roots, Chef Robin offers Sabah-style kolo mee, less com mon in Singapore than the Sarawak-style. The key difference lies in the darker, savoury soy sauce base, which gives Sabah-style noodles a richer, more robust flavour compared to the lighter, shallot oil-based Sarawak version.
Image credit: Wilfred Loy Yong Kang via Google Maps
Signature dishes are the Pork Chop Kolo Mee ($6.90) and Pork Chop Mee Soup ($6.90) , both featuring a Din Tai Fung-style fried pork chop.
Image credit: Patricia Lim via Google Maps
Alternatively, you can keep it simple with the Home Taste Kolo Mee ($4.50) and Home Taste Mee Soup ($4.50) , served with slices of char siew.
Other kolo mee options include Chicken Chop Kolo Mee ($6.50) , Fish Roll Fish Ball Mee ($4) , and Wanton Kolo Mee ($4) , available soup or dry.
If you opt for dry noodles, you can also customise your sauce. Choose from three options: White, a savoury shallot oil sauce; Black, a dark soy sauce with a hint of sweetness; or Red, a sweet char siew oil sauce.
Image credit: Zoey W via Google Maps
Another specialty of Three Bowls is the Homemade Knife-Cut Noodles ($6.90) , featuring chef Robin’s hand-pulled noodles—said to have a chewy texture and topped with fish balls and meat balls.
While the store is relatively new, it’s already built a solid fanbase with long queues every day. If you love the iconic Ding Tai Fung pork chop, then you need to give this a go.
If you found this story interesting, check out our Nomad Kitchen review , featuring a hawker stall opened by an ex-hotel and F&B manager. For more Malaysian food recommendations, check out our guide to the best Malaysian food places in Singapore.
Address: 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-14 Whampoa Makan Place, Singapore 320090
Opening hours: Mon, Wed-Sun 1pm to 4:30pm, 5pm to 9pm
Three Bowls is not halal-certified.

body:
365 Bakery is a viral bakery in Austin Crest
If you’re a die-hard JB cafe and bakery hopper , chances are you’re well-acquainted with 365 Bakery , which has blown up on social media. Since opening in November 2024, they have amassed over 19K Instagram followers at the time of writing.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.32 as of 2 November 2026.
The highlight of 365 Bakery is the sheer range of bakes—there are over 100 options here—from classic French pastries to trendy shio pans, so there’s definitely something to satisfy your cravings.
Their best-seller, and what put them on the map, is their Swiss rolls, which have a cult following of their own. In fact, they even claim to have the “best Swiss rolls in Malaysia”, with six unique flavours to choose from.
While you can order the different individual flavours, we decided to order the Mystery Box (RM37.90) to surprise ourselves.
It’s akin to a blind box—it comes with four slices of random flavours, with a 1-in-100 chance of getting a rare mystery flavour and a 1-in-50 chance of getting their special Pistachio Kaw Kaw , which is individually priced at RM68.90 .
Unfortunately, luck wasn’t on our side and we got four of their regular flavours instead.
The taste was anything but ordinary, though: all were equally light and airy, yet packed with flavour. My personal favourite was the 70% Nama Chocolate (RM43.90) , featuring a rich cacao chiffon cake made with 70% Belgian chocolate, stuffed with dark chocolate-flavoured French Chantilly cream and a decadent slab of chocolate fudge. The dessert felt very rich and indulgent, without being too sweet.
On the other hand, my colleague preferred the Japanese Yuzu Creamcheese (RM32.90) , which had a more subtle tangy flavour. The cake was reminiscent of Japanese-style cheesecake: soft and spongy, while the cream cheese frosting was equally light and delicately flavoured with 100% Japanese yuzu.
The Silky Black Sesame Kinako (RM40.90) was a close second runner-up for both of us. It comprises roasted black sesame and kinako Chantilly cream, and house-made mochi, encased in black sesame chiffon cake, for a treat that’s well-balanced and not too sweet.
Last but not least, the Tropical Breeze (RM35.90) is their zhnged-up interpretation of a pandan cake, paired with coconut Chantilly cream and mango for a refreshing bite.
Of course, don’t miss out on their other bakes: their Purple Yam & Sweet Potato Bun (RM3.80) is highly popular among regulars. It’s made with Japanese flour and purple potato powder for a chewy, mochi-like mouthfeel, and stuffed with earthy sweet potato filling.
If sweet potato isn’t your thing, the Apple Cinnamon Bagel (RM7.90) is also equally popular.
Expect a crusty, chewy bagel cutely moulded into the shape of an apple, and generously loaded with a cinnamon-apple filling similar to McDonald’s apple pie, though I wish the cinnamon flavour could be more pronounced.
Shio pan enthusiasts can also get their fix with their Korean Garlic Cream Cheese Shio Pan (RM6.50) : salt bread with a soft, fluffy interior, slathered in savoury, garlicky butter and stuffed with a slightly sweetened cream cheese. The result is a sweet-salty combo that reminds me of Paris Baguette’s cream cheese garlic buns.
Those itching for a savoury bite can order the Chargrilled Vege Italian Focaccia (RM6.90) . Imagine soft bread generously topped with charred broccoli, tomatoes, and mushrooms, then finished with a salty cheese crust. The vegetables add a smoky aroma that’s mellowed by the natural sweetness of the tomatoes.
Their Pain Au Chocolate (RM7.90) was the biggest one I’ve ever seen. It was light and airy with many soft, fluffy layers.
Finally, wash it all down with their signature 365 Specialty Coffee (RM12.90) : an iced Americano flavoured with osmanthus syrup. The coffee is light and slightly fruity, perfumed by the floral notes of osmanthus.
365 Bakery is located in Austin Crest, a 15-minute drive from Mount Austin.
PSA to all coffee addicts: 365 Bakery is also coming to Singapore’s Coffee Week 2026 , so you can enjoy their iconic Swiss rolls with your coffee. You can also check out our guide to the best coffee cafes in Singapore to help you find the perfect pairing.
Address: 38, Jalan Jaya Putra 7/2, Bandar Jaya Putra, 81100 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim, Malaysia
Opening hours: Daily 10am to 9pm
Website
365 Bakery is not halal-certified.

body:
City Hall food guide
City Hall MRT Station is right smack in the middle of the East-West Line and North-South Line, making it one of the more convenient places to meet up with friends. Peppered with malls, there is no shortage of City Hall food places to choose from. Look below for our round-up of food gems to check out when in the area.
1. Ureshii
Korean-Japanese restaurant Ureshii is nestled away at The Arts House , a convenient eight-minute walk from City Hall MRT Station . Naturally, the menu is heavily influenced by a blend of Korean and Japanese flavours, such as the Kurobuta Udon Kimchi Soup ($28++) : a spicy-tangy kimchi soup with udon and pork meat. Alternatively, the Truffle Oil Tsuyu Pasta ($28++) is a great choice for those who enjoy oil-based pasta. This dish features fragrant truffle oil, aged tsuyu, and black tobiko.
Read our Ureshii review .
Address: 1 Old Parliament Lane, #01-02, The Arts House, Singapore 179429
Opening hours: Mon-Sat 11:50am to 2:50pm, 6pm to 11pm, Sun 11:50am to 2:50pm, 6pm to 10pm

This Korean-Japanese Restaurant Has Jeju Abalone Porridge And Cheese Tonkatsu In City Hall
2. Alice Boulangerie
Popular cafe Alice Boulangerie has a second branch at Raffles City , and what sets this outlet apart from the OG is the addition of Fine Crumbs Bakery . There are more than 15 buns available every day, and some of our favourites are the Black Sesame Peanut Mochi Bun ($4.80++) , which nods to muah chee, Matcha Nama Bun ($6.50++) , and Pistachio Cream Bun ($6.80++) .
If you’re dining with friends or colleagues, we recommend the incredibly flavourful Chargrilled Chicken ($38++ for half) , featuring seasonal vegetables on the side. There’s also Smoked Black Cod($39++) , served with a tomato and olive stew.
Read our Alice Boulangerie review .

Alice Boulangerie Opens At Raffles City, Get Fresh Buns With Matcha Nama And Pistachio Cream
3. Broth & Beyond
Many think that CHIJMES only houses fancy restaurants, but that’s not true. Broth & Beyond is a value-for-money hotpot spot offering fresh, locally sourced ingredients from Yunnan. Their Flavour Discovery Set is priced at $39.90++ per person , which includes one broth flavour, a portion of meat, a veggie basket, a portion of rice or la mian, and access to the Market Table, which is essentially a huge condiment and dessert station. If you can’t decide which broth to get, consider the Black Truffle Assorted Mushroom Broth that’s simmered for eight hours using chicken fat and Yunnan mushrooms to achieve a rich, robust flavour.
Read our Broth & Beyond review .

Ume San 100 has new konbini-inspired sets
Behind the nostalgic facade of Fortune Centre lies plenty of hidden gems, from affordable Korean food to handmade Japanese onigiri and traditional Chinese tong sui . Now, there’s one more reason to visit the strata mall: Ume San 100 has recently released a konbini-inspired menu, alongside other exciting dishes.
Ume San 100: New Japanese Bar Hidden Behind Vending Machines Has SG’s Largest Umeshu Collection
ICYMI: Ume San 100 is a Japanese speakeasy bar, and its iconic vending machine storefront is hard to miss. You’ll spot it almost immediately upon reaching the second floor, as it’s brightly lit and colourfully eye-catching.
Image credit: Ume San 100
Frequent Japan-goers would know that convenience stores, AKA konbinis, are a must-visit in Japan. The bar has given its menu a konbini-inspired spin, introducing familiar treats as part of its all-new Konbini Set ($19.90++) .
Image credit: Ume San 100
One highlight is the Truffle Ramen , topped with prawns, a jammy hanjuku egg, and fish cakes for a classic yet hearty bowl of ramen.
Since no konbini haul is complete without a drink, each set comes with Ume Cola that’s made with ume syrup and house-made cola for a fizzy staple. If you prefer something more hardcore, top up $5 to add whisky or vodka to your cola for a “grown-up” upgrade.
Image credit: Ume San 100
A must-order at any kobini would be the fried chicken or Umechiki , which is also part of the lineup. Guests get to opt for a spicy or non-spicy set, and the chosen spice level will apply to both the ramen and Umechiki.
The set also comprises Crispy Fries , with both sides being served in a striped paper sleeve, just like the ones in Japan.
To add on to the fun, every Konbini Set comes with a Japanese-style receipt, allowing diners to try their luck at the Gachapon machine for some enticing rewards. Prize value varies based on capsule colours: Gold entitles diners to 10% off their next visit ($30 min. spend), Silver offers a free highball or mocktail with any main, Green provides a free Fruit Tasting Set ($70 min. spend), and Black awards a $25 return voucher ($100 min. spend).
Image credit: Ume San 100
Besides the Konbini Set, the eatery is also expanding its dinner menu with three new fusion dishes. Mentaiko Pasta with Seared Scallops ($22++) for a Japanese take on the Italian staple, Spicy Beef Ramen ($18++) comprising bold Sichuan-inspired flavours, as well as Foie Gras Bara Chirashi Don ($24++) , which sees French foie gras and salmon, tuna, and tamago atop a bed of sushi rice.
Image credit: Ume San 100
You can also explore Ume San 100’s extensive selection of Japanese umeshu, AKA plum wine. Their collection is said to be one of Singapore’s largest, boasting over 100 varieties with rare and exclusive labels. If you’re new here, go for the Low-ABV Taster Set ($15++) that features three floral-infused umeshu flavours: Rose , Lavender , and Jasmine .
Fans of the tall, carbonated mixed alcohol highball would be pleased to know that they offer 13 different choices, including Ume Whisky ($14++) , Premium Toki Highball ($15++) and more.
Image credit: Ume San 100
Much like the izakayas in Japan, the seating capacity is cozy but rather limited, with 28 seats on the floor and six by the bar, so it’s best to book ahead or come down early to get a table.
While you’re in the area, check out our 12-hour Bugis and CBD guide for more good eats. In other news, read our Hi Bowl feature for more deets on Haidilao’s new malatang restaurant in Rochor.
Address: 190 Middle Road, #02-07, Fortune Centre, Singapore 188979
Operating hours: Mon-Thu 11:30am to 2:30pm, 5pm to 10pm, Fri-Sat 11:30am to 2:30pm, 5pm to 11pm, Sun 11am to 4pm, 5pm to 8:30pm
Tel: 8897 4575
Website

I’ve heard of food and music festivals all my life, but never have I come across a festival dedicated entirely to celebrating and honouring Jejudony Pork . That was until I travelled to Jeju Island to attend the 2-day 2026 Jeju Dosaegi Festival that took place at Saebyeol Oreum area , Aewol-eup from 17 to 18 Oct 2026 .
If you’re wondering what an oreum is, it’s that volcanic cone rising in the background.
Every year, Koreans from all over the country travel to Jeju just to attend this prestigious festival. In Korea, pigs are highly-regarded and considered the ultimate sacrificial offering when praying to the gods and ancestors. They are also slaughtered at weddings and funerals purely for culinary purposes.
White, circus-like tents fill up the vast festival grounds with retail shops peddling products like honey, soju , sausages, mechanical keyboard accessories, and much more.
Farmers receive VIP treatment here, complete with a dedicated seating area set aside in their honour. There are tons of activities happening all day long, including games, a roaming karaoke-on-wheels contest, and performances by the Marine Corps Military Band and Sori Punggyeong Children’s Choir . On Day 2, the legendary South Korean hip-hop duo, Dynamic Duo , made a guest appearance to fire up the crowd — see how big of a deal this is?
Stroll through the festival grounds to try your hand at darts, or browse the flea market to pick up a unique souvenir. Got little ones in tow? Let them bounce their energy away at the kids’ play area or craft adorable critters out of pipe cleaners!I even spotted a dedicated zone where kids can unleash their artistic talent by doodling on the ground with chalk.
A long, snaking queue had formed in front of the Jejudony Pork Booth with throngs of people relishing on cooked pork samples, immediately catching my attention. When I spotted the 25% discount on 500g packets of Pork Neck and Pork Belly, each priced at just ₩10,000 ( ≈ S$9.65) — that’s equivalent to below S$10 per meat — I finally understood what the appeal was.
Need a quick fuel-up amidst all the festivities? No sweat. Check out the outdoor food truck cafeteria where you’ll find plenty of street food options to choose from like skewers, corn dogs, and tornado potatoes. Need your daily caffeine fix? You’ll find fresh coffee available alongside a selection of refreshing fruit juices. October is considered one of the best times to visit Jeju, so rest assured the weather will be nice and cool.
Wait, I know some of you may be thinking, “I need proper food. This won’t even fill me up!” Fret not, there are makeshift restaurants and we visited one that was run by the Jeju Pig Farming Cooperative Women’s Club . You’ll be taken care of by a bunch of warm and friendly ahjummas . The place served hearty meals and soju (if you fancy a tipple).
You can enjoy a scrumptious Seafood and Green Onion Pancake (₩10,000 , S$9.57) or slurp on a hot bowl of Meat Noodles ( ₩5,000 , S$4.79) . The Meat Noodles come with freshly-steamed Jeju pork — you’ll soon realise that the meat has such a clean taste and possesses a perfect meat-to-fat ratio. For an extra touch of decadence, share a plate of Boiled Pork ( ₩15,000 , S$14.36 ). Just dip it in soy sauce, pair it with kimchi , and you’re good to go!
We had a clearer glimpse of Jejudony Pork’s versatility over at Kang Chef’s Kitchen. Chef Kang took us on a culinary journey through Jeju pork, highlighting the many creative ways this prized meat can be prepared right here in Singapore.
We started off with the Pork Jowl Sushi , where Chef Kang replaced the usual fish with tender pieces of grilled pork jowl, served with a vibrant chives salad. Next up was the Boiled 5-Layer Pork Belly Noodles — it was impressive how beautifully this dish came together with simple accompaniments like seaweed, cucumber, and lettuce.
One of my favourites was the lip-smacking Traditional Jeju-Style Seasoned Pork Skewers , which Chef Kang served with asparagus, oyster mushrooms, and peppers. Since it was a Singaporean-themed night, he intentionally replaced the usual onion, big leek, and carrots with bok choy for his Spear Squid w/ Stir-Fried Black Pork Shoulder dish. Both the pork and squid were cooked to tender perfection.
One of the specialities of Kang Chef’s restaurant is his tangsuyuk (Korean sweet and sour pork) and it was the perfect opportunity to showcase it for the Loin Tangsuyuk , Pig Trotter w/ Chilli . Korean restaurants in Singapore typically use lean cuts for the tangsuyuk . Chef Kang’s loin rendition had more fats that made it extra creamy and juicy — hands down, one of the best I’ve had in my life!
I also had the chance to visit the Jejudony Pork Meat Processing Plant , gaining firsthand insight into the advanced quarantine and bio-security protocols that supply their partner farms with premium breeding pigs.
…
summary: The 2026 Jeju Dosaegi Festival celebrated Jejudony Pork over two days at Saebyeol Oreum, Aewol-eup, from 17 to 18 October 2026. Visitors could sample Jeju pork dishes, enjoy cultural performances and family activities, and learn about pork production through a processing plant visit. The experience is useful for travellers interested in Jeju’s food culture and the origins of Korean pork supplied to Singapore.
title: What makes Jeju Island’s Jejudony Pork special? I visited its festival & processing plant

If you’ve been following The Sidemen on YouTube, SIDES , the fast-food brand founded by the group, has announced plans to expand into Malaysia . Kuala Lumpur is named among 4 upcoming international destinations .
Credit – SIDES
The announcement was shared on SIDES’ official social media channels, alongside New Cairo in Egypt, Kuwait City in Kuwait, and Mumbai in India. However, the brand has yet to reveal when its first Malaysian outlet will open or where it will be located.
For the uninitiated, The Sidemen are a British YouTube collective formed in 2013. The group originally comprised 7 creators: KSI, Miniminter, Zerkaa, TBJZL, Behzinga, Vikkstar123, and W2S — known for their challenge videos, gaming content, comedy and collaborations. However, KSI announced his departure from the group in May 2026.
Credit – SIDES
One of the group’s ventures beyond YouTube is SIDES, a fast-food brand with a menu centred on fried chicken. Expect chicken burgers , tenders and wings , alongside familiar sides such as waffle fries and milkshakes .
Credit – SIDES
There are several chicken flavours to choose from, including Nashville , London Jerk and Mango Peri Peri . Those who enjoy their food on the spicier side might look forward to Nashville Insane , which features Carolina Reaper peppers. According to my Singapore colleagues, who have it very frequently, it’s a dish that’s meant to bring the heat.
SIDES already has outlets in the UK and Singapore , and its latest expansion plans will bring the brand to more international markets. For Malaysian fans who’ve been curious about trying its food, the announcement is certainly welcome news.
Whether the local outlet will carry the existing menu or introduce flavours catering to Malaysian tastes remains to be seen. For now, we’ll have to wait for SIDES by The Sidemen to share more details about its opening date and first outlet location in Malaysia.
10 new places in JB to check out this Nov 2026 — cafes, food & more
summary: SIDES, the fried chicken fast-food brand founded by British YouTube group The Sidemen, has announced plans to open its first Malaysian outlet in Kuala Lumpur, alongside three other international markets. The menu centres on chicken burgers, tenders and wings, with flavours including Nashville and Mango Peri Peri. Useful for Malaysian fans keen to try the brand, though its opening date and outlet location remain unconfirmed.
title: The Sidemen’s SIDES is coming to Malaysia – here’s a look at its existing menu

IKEA Singapore is bringing back their highly anticipated Christmas Buffet for its 2026 run, starting this Dec.
Priced at just S $29.90 for adults , S $15.90 for kids under 12 , and FREE for toddlers below 4 , it’s a fantastic option for anyone looking for a decadent Christmas feast that won’t break the bank.
Credit – IKEA Singapore
This year’s all-you-can-eat Swedish feast takes place on just 3 Fridays in Dec 2026, across Singapore’s 3 IKEA outlets. The dates, locations and seating times are as follows:
IKEA Jurong: 4 Dec (Tickets on sale 5 Nov)
• Seating: 7.30pm to 9pm
• Last order: 9pm
IKEA Alexandra: 11 Dec (Tickets on sale 12 Nov)
• First seating: 5pm to 6.30pm (last order at 6pm)
• Second seating: 7.30pm to 9pm (last order at 9pm)
IKEA Tampines: 18 Dec (Tickets on sale 17 Nov)
• First seating: 5pm to 6.30pm (last order at 6pm)
• Second seating: 7.30pm to 9pm (last order at 9pm)
Tickets will be sold in-person only at Swedish Restaurant cashier counters of each respective store on a first-come, first-served basis while stocks last. Make sure your IKEA Family membership is active before queuing up at the counters to snag your tickets!
Credit – IKEA Japan
Diners can look forward to an array of Scandinavian classics like the one and only Swedish meatballs with cream sauce and ASC-certified salmon with hollandaise sauce . Other hearty hot dishes include Beef goulash with carrots and potatoes and Organic penne pasta with tomato sauce .
Credit – IKEA Singapore
The cold selection also comprises many Swedish staples, including ASC-certified smoked & marinated salmon , Swedish salmon salad and Swedish shrimp salad and MSC-certified assorted marinated herring .
Credit – IKEA Singapore
You’ll also find some exclusive festive additions, such as Sliced honey baked ham , and desserts with a Swedish twist like Lingonberry vanilla log cake and Swedish festive biscuits so you can close out your feast on a sweet note.
With tickets set to sell out fast, you’ll want to move quick if you plan to get your fill of unlimited meatballs and smoked salmon this holiday season!
summary: IKEA Singapore's Swedish Christmas Buffet returns on select Fridays in Dec 2026 across its Jurong, Alexandra, and Tampines outlets, serving unlimited Scandinavian cold starters, hot savouries, and festive desserts. Priced from S$29.90 for adults and S$15.90 for children under 12, the all-you-can-eat feast is available exclusively to IKEA Family members with tickets sold strictly in-person at restaurant cashier counters on designated release dates in Nov. It offers an affordable dining option best suited for families and budget-conscious diners seeking a festive meal.
title: IKEA’s Christmas Buffet is back from $29.90 — Here’s when & how to snag tickets

UGG pop-up at Jewel Changi Airport
If you’ve got a winter trip to Seoul or Sapporo coming up this December, there’s one less thing to panic-buy online the night before your flight. UGG has opened its first-ever pop-up in Southeast Asia at Jewel Changi Airport , and it’s staying for about 5 months from 1st November 2026 .
You’ll find the cult Classic boots, the Tasman slippers that are all over your feed, and new Fall/Winter 2026 styles, all on Level 1. Yes, we know it’s 32°C outside. But the pop-up is a short walk from the terminals, so it’s an easy stop for a pre-flight haul.
What to expect at the UGG pop-up
Image credit: UGG
The pop-up is small, at about 39.5sqm, and done up in UGG’s usual earthy style: curved wooden displays, soft textures, and lots of plants. It’s an open layout, so you can walk in, try on a pair or 2 and be out before your flight.
UGG says more seasonal styles will drop over time. If the pair you want isn’t there yet, it’s worth popping back later.
The classics: Tasman, Tazz & Classic Minis
Image credit: UGG
If you’re buying your first pair, start with the heritage styles:
• Tasman II ($189.90): The low-profile slip-on, now with UGGbraid trim on the collar. Comes in Chestnut and Moonlight for women, and Chestnut and Black for men.
• Disquette ($189.90): A slip-on with a 1″ retro platform. Comfy but loud.
• Tazz II ($199.90): A lightweight platform with a curved sole that makes walking easier.
• Classic Micro ($199.90): The shortest Classic boot. It slips on like a slipper but works for going out.
• Classic Mini II & Classic Ultra Mini ($229.90 each): The OG boots. The sheepskin draws moisture away, so they’re not as sweaty as you’d expect.
Most styles have soles made from sugarcane EVA, a foam that uses less petroleum.
New for Fall/Winter 2026: Boot charms, bows & platforms
Image credit: UGG
The new season gives the classics some cute add-ons:
• Classic Mini Heritage ($289.90): A Classic Mini with a removable mini sheepskin boot charm. It’s basically a bag charm for your shoes, in Chestnut or Sandcastle.
• Disquette Heritage ($229.90): The platform slip-on with an UGG logo charm and decorative lacing.
• Heritage Lace-Up Slipper ($249.90): A lace-up version of the classic slipper, with a suede upper and sheepskin lining.
• Ultra Mini Bailey Bow II ($249.90): The Ultra Mini with a satin bow at the back. Also comes in taller versions: the Mini Bailey Bow II ($279.90) and Bailey Bow II ($329.90).
• Classic Mini Enwrap ($289.90): A sleeker Classic Mini that wraps around the ankle and sits on a low platform. It works from day to night.
• Tazelle ($229.90): A very plush slipper on a 1.75″ platform with a sheepskin cuff. Get it in Mustard Seed if you want something besides brown.
Something for the guys & your snowy itinerary
Image adapted from: UGG
The men’s range covers more than slippers:
• Tasman Flex ($259.90): An all-season shoe in suede and nubuck, with a flexible sole that grips slippery floors.
• Tasman Outpost ($289.90): Inspired by rock climbing, with waterproof suede, a toggle lace and a grippy White Spider Rubber® sole.
• Classic Mini Outpost ($299.90): A waterproof Classic Mini lined with UGGplush , made from upcycled wool.
Pro tip: If you’re headed somewhere with real snow or slush, the waterproof Outpost styles are the ones to get. Regular suede won’t take kindly to it.
Festive gifting picks
Image adapted from: UGG
UGG’s year-end Gift the Feeling campaign features the Classic Mini II ($229.90) and Classic Mini Outpost ($299.90) . Matching pairs make a good jio-your-partner Christmas gift.
Image adapted from: UGG
The campaign also includes the Après City Tall Boot , which has suede laces, and the Classic Ultra Tall Boot , which is 4″ taller than usual.
Visit the UGG pop-up at Jewel Changi Airport
It’s not every day a global brand picks Singapore for its first pop-up in the region. If you want to try on a pair before buying, now’s the time.
Location: CL-L1-E, Level 1, Jewel Changi Airport, 78 Airport Boulevard, Singapore 819666
Dates: From 1st November 2026
Contact: UGG website | UGG Instagram
Other things to do at Changi Airport:
• We visited Stanley’s first pop-up in SG
• Changi Airport x Pokemon 30th Anniversary
• Kid-friendly things to do at Changi Airport & Jewel Changi
Cover image adapted from: UGG

Bedok South, Sungei Bedok & Xilin MRT stations opening
It sure took a while, but the wait is almost over. Easties, in a few weeks’ time, we’ll finally have a direct route up North to Woodlands with the opening of the Bedok South , Sungei Bedok , and Xilin MRT stations this December .
The completion of the Thomson-East Coast Line (TEL) and bolstering of the Downtown Line (DTL) changes the game for folks travelling to and from the East. Here’s what you need to know at a glance, so you can make changes to your daily commute to make the best of these new additions on our train network.
When are the Bedok South, Sungei Bedok & Xilin MRT stations opening?
Image credit: Khoo Yong Hao
On 4th November 2026, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) announced that the Bedok South and Sungei Bedok MRT stations on the TEL and the DTL’s Xilin MRT station will open simultaneously on 26th December 2026 . These openings are part of TEL Stage 5 and the DTL Stage 3 Extension , and fill the gap between Bayshore and Expo through Sungei Bedok.
What to expect from the new TEL & DTL MRT station openings?
Image adapted from: SMRT
With the opening of the 3 new stations, commuters working or residing in the area can expect to shave valuable minutes off their travel time. According to the LTA, the journey from Havelock to Changi will take 45 minutes , down from 75 minutes, minus a bus transfer.
For those bound for Expo travelling out of Marine Terrace, you can save up to 15 minutes by switching onto the DTL, a transfer now made possible with the new MRT stations. Easties who’re sick of doing their shopping at Tampines Mall, Parkway Parade won’t be too far away; the direct train ride from Tampines to Marine Parade is estimated to be a little over half an hour .
Sungei Bedok MRT station.
Image credit: LTA
The completed extensions mean more than 240,000 households are within a 10-minute walk of a TEL station, while 220,000 households will be within a 10-minute walk ofto one on the DTL. With this newfound convenience, a whole slew of amenities will also be just a stone’s throw away once you step off the platform of these freshly-opened stations.
Image adapted from: CK C via Google Maps, @mycatoot via Instagram
For instance, the popular Bedok Food Centre will be right at the doorstep of Sungei Bedok MRT station; those in green booking in and out from Bedok Camp can also take the trains there. Right next to Bedok South MRT station is Siglap CC , which plays host to a bowling alley , badminton courts, a food court, and a McDonald’s outlet.
Image credit: Changi City Point
As for Xilin MRT station, you’ll find that Changi Business Park will be made much more accessible, and by extension Changi City Point and its whole host of factory outlets.
Board your trains at the upcoming MRT stations on the TEL & DTL
The opening of the new TEL and DTL MRT stations is yet another notch in the belt for those staying in the East – perhaps this will quell any debate when it comes to deciding which end of sunny Singapore’s the superior one. We’ve still got some waiting to do, so in the meantime, start planning your next JB trip, because getting to the checkpoint is going to get so much easier.
For more new things to do in Singapore:
• PokéXciting! at Changi Airport & Jewel
• Castlery pop up at Jurong Point
• Singapore Book Street 2026 at VivoCity
Cover image adapted from: Khoo Yong Hao, LTA
summary: The wait is finally over.
title: 3 New MRT Stations Are Opening In December 2026, Completing The TEL & Improving DTL Connectivity

D23 Asia: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event in Singapore
Just when we thought the arrival of the Disney Adventure cruise was enough to send fans into a frenzy, there’s more magic headed our way. For the first time ever, the D23 Asia: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event is coming to Singapore , giving local Disney lovers a chance to immerse themselves in all things Mickey and co.
Here’s what we know so far.
What is D23 Asia: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event?
Image credit: The Walt Disney Company
Launched in 2009, the event has grown into one of the world’s biggest celebrations of all things Disney – think of it as Disney’s equivalent of Comic-Con, but with more pixie dust, of course.
It’s where hardcore fans get the inside scoop on upcoming projects , catch major announcements before everyone else, and take part in immersive experiences inspired by their favourite Disney, Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars universes.
The flagship event in Anaheim, California, in August delivered truckloads of reveals and updates, psyching Disney fans everywhere up for the year ahead. While previous Asia editions were held in Japan back in 2013, 2015, and 2018, Singapore is finally next on the list.
When & where will D23 Asia take place in Singapore?
Image credit: D23
D23 Asia: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event will officially land in Singapore from 25th to 27th June 2027 , at Sands Expo & Convention Centre , Marina Bay Sands .
What can I expect at the event?
Image credit: D23
This massive multi-day affair will be packed with live stage presentations , interactive experiences , exclusive previews of Disney+’s APAC Originals, and curated merch that any Disney fan wouldn’t want to miss.
Disney just announced on 5th November what you can expect during the 3-day event:
• 25th June Friday: Studio Showcase – A preview of what’s next from Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, and other franchises. You can also expect exclusive announcements, never-before-seen footage, and surprise celebrity appearances.
• 26th June Saturday: Disney+ Showcase – Attendees will get to see new Korean and Japanese series and new and returning global streaming titles. There will also be exclusive first looks and appearances by Asian celebrities and creators.
• 27th June Sunday: Disney Hits LIVE! – Be entertained with a finale concert with a setlist including Disney and Pixar’s most iconic songs performed by Broadway stars accompanied by a live band, rock concert lighting, and larger-than-life animation.
D23 Asia in Singapore will also have 15 immersive experiences like the Storytellers Stage , where fans can join panels with the creators and talent behind some of Disney’s biggest films, series, and experiences; Talent Central , where fans can meet their favourite Disney characters; and the Spotlight Stage with live entertainment, interactive activities, and fan-focused programming.
Of course, it’s not really a convention if there’s no merch to bring home. Attendees can head to the D23 Marketplace , the event’s central shopping hub, to score collectables, apparel, accessories and more. There is also the Walt Disney Company Store , which is stocked with D23 Asia-themed merch, things inspired by The Walt Disney Company, and a curation of items that are typically exclusive to Disney’s employee stores and will be available to the public in Asia Pacific for the first time.
D23 California 2026
To give you a rough idea of what could be in store for the Singapore edition, this year’s California event included the following announcements:
• Ridge Run Rally : A rally attraction at Piston Peak National Park, the upcoming Cars -themed expansion coming to Walt Disney World’s Magic Kingdom.
• Villains Land : An upcoming Villains-themed expansion at Walt Disney World’s Magic Kingdom, with a new roller coaster featuring Maleficent from Sleeping Beauty , and another ride themed around the Evil Queen’s Magic Mirror from Snow White . Other villains to look forward to include Cruella de Vil and Dr Facilier, of The Princess & The Frog infamy.
• Monstropolis : Monsters, Inc. -themed land at Walt Disney World Hollywood Studios will open in 2027, but Monsters, Inc. Door Vault , its new roller coaster, will not be ready.
• Antonio’s Fiesta de Encanto : New Encanto ride at Walt Disney World.
• “The Lion King” attraction at Disneyland Paris will debut its villan, Scar, in his final confrontation with Simba.
• Space Mountain: Earthrise : The Tokyo Disneyland’s Space Mountain ride will reopen.
• Sugar Rush: Sweet Rescue : World’s first Wreck-It Ralph ride will open at Tokyo Disneyland in Spring 2027.
• Ice Age: Boiling Point : Expected 5th February 2027 , starring Queen Latifah and Dennis Leary.
• Frozen 3 : New villain, a wedding, a new love interest, and new music, expected 24th November 2027 .
• Zootopia 3 : Ginnifer Goodwin and Ke Huy Quan are back for more adventures.
• Live-action Tangled : Coming to theatres 31st March 2027 .

body:
As the haze slowly dies down, people are starting to go out again. It was nice to see people chatting and connecting at Summer Folks Cafe & Steakhouse on Beach Road . When I got there, I was greeted by several breeds of adorable doggos – I’m assuming they were there for doggy training.
It was a blistering hot day, so I immediately took refuge in the cafe. Despite its balmy lighting, the AC provided much relief for my friends and me. As I sat down, my eyes couldn’t help but peruse the interior.
As I mentioned, the lighting was warm, but the AC made it nice and cool. The place was surrounded by glass windows that stretched from the ceiling to the floor, giving us a nice view of the doggos.
Also, I’d be remiss not to mention their gifts section, which included Pokémon cards for sale, as well as some free (I’m assuming) discard Pokémon cards by the cashier. One of my buddies hovered over that shelf for a long time. Like a moth to a flame.
What to order at Summer Folks Cafe & Steakhouse
I find that going anywhere with 3 dudes will eventually mean that you’ll be arguing over the menu for ages. Luckily, Summer Folks offers a Snack Platter (S$24.80), which made our lives so much easier.
The platter features 4 items: crunchy and fatty roast potatoes, Taiwanese-style calamari, tater tots, and creamed spinach. At the centre was a small portion of tartar sauce.
The tater tots were nicely salted, not too oily and overall a decent bite. The roast potatoes were slightly better, with a hint of rosemary perfuming the glassy crust.
However, the highlights of the snack platter (S$24.80) had to be the creamed spinach and the calamari. The delicate creamed spinach was rich and cheesy from the snowy parmesan. Despite being so creamy and rich, it didn’t feel overbearing.
And then comes the calamari. I was fully expecting a basic calamari ring. Boy, was I wrong. They were cut into strips and seasoned with a Taiwanese seasoning powder made from paprika, chilli powder and S&P. It added a smoky, spicy kick, making it oh so moreish. It was the first to disappear.
Curry Cafe: Secluded HDB void deck eatery with over 60 dishes like curry chicken & $1.20 prata
For the mains, we got 2 items: Cold Crab Angel Hair (S$16.80) & SF Meat Platter (S$118.80). Yes. We went overboard. Totally worth it once you’ve tried it.
Firstly, the Cold Crab Angel Hair (S$16.80). This dish was almost necessary for the hot weather that day. I’m kind of on the fence when it comes to cold, savoury dishes. But this dish in particular really convinced me there’s a place for it. The crab meat was fresh and sweet. There were also healthy chunks of prawn that had a more meaty texture compared to the delicate crab meat. The dish was also topped generously with tobiko and kombu.
This dish grew on me. The first flavour you get is salt. Like the best-tasting salt you have ever tasted. It’s only then that you realise the tobiko and kombu were seasoning the dish. The pasta was nicely cooked, with a slight bounce despite how thin it was. Now, I will warn you, if you have any seafood issues, this dish might not be for you. After cleaning the plate, we found that the fishy aftertaste overstayed its welcome. Luckily, we had a giant platter of barbecued meat to clear our palates.
The SF Meat Platter is a firm reminder that Summer Folk is also a steakhouse. After tasting each component, I wonder why they don’t just become a steakhouse completely! At the platter, you will be greeted by smoke. They lit a stalk of rosemary and placed it on the platter, perfuming the entire affair. The sight was mouth-watering, too. There was a roasted half spring chicken, 3 beef skewers, 3 turkey cranberry sausages and last but not least, a huge bone-in beef short rib. It also came with 2 sauces: brown sauce and Beurre Blanc sauce.
Let’s get straight to it. The chicken was alright; the meat was juicy, but the skin was painted with a sauce that was way too sweet for me. The turkey sausage was lovely. It had a nice snap and had a herby filling with a slight tang from the cranberry.
Now, for the highlights. The skewers were a great surprise. The marinade was slightly spicy, smoky and unctuous. I would compare it to some of the best kebab spots in Singapore. Even the roasted peppers added a much-needed change in texture. But the best part of the platter had to be the short rib. It was tender, fatty and oh so rich. The crust was caramelised, giving it a lovely crunch and a bitter note to the bite. It’s pricey, sure, but this is something you treat yourself with.
Now, normally, I don’t really care for the drinks. Most of the time it’s just a type of coffee that, to me, is nothing special. But the Sea Salt Yuan Yang (S$6.80) is something else completely.
…
summary: Summerfolks Cafe is a cafe and steakhouse at Guoco Midtown on Beach Road, serving a Snack Platter at S$24.80, Cold Crab Angel Hair at S$16.80 and an SF Meat Platter at S$118.80. The meat platter’s short rib and skewers stood out, while the pasta left a fishy aftertaste. Best suited to groups of friends and families, with Bugis MRT station about 5 minutes away.
title: Summer Folk Cafe & Steakhouse: Halal spot with Da Ji Pai-style calamari & platters galore

The F1 Grand Prix Season Singapore 2026 might have ended a month ago, but car enthusiasts still have something to look forward to. The Model Car Show (TMCS) 2026 is coming to 3 floors at *SCAPE on 22 & 22 November 2026 !
Credit: Eventbrite
So, what exactly is TMCS? Organised by Toy Space, this event is one of Singapore’s largest celebrations of diecast cars , model kits , collectables , and hobby culture . Let’s put it this way: if Hot Wheels, Tamiya cars, and Beyblades were your jam growing up (or even now), this show is for you.
Credit: The Model Car Show Singapore Facebook
The first thing you need to know about TMCS 2026 is that entry is completely free . Simply register on Eventbrite to get your free General Ticket . At the time of writing, previously available Fast Lane Tickets with exclusive merchandise have sold out.
But fret not! There are other ways to score merchandise. If you have a real car you think is worth exhibiting at the Outdoor Car Show Display , register your ride for a chance to win. Participants receive an exclusive T-shirt , a dedicated page featuring their car , and a TMCS lanyard pass .
Owners of the top 3 favourite rides at TMCS 2026 will also stand to win trophies , a hoodie , and more . Interested? Text +65 8851 9039 for more information. Don’t have a car to show off? You can still look forward to checking out others’ builds!
Credit: The Model Car Show Singapore Facebook
Now, let’s talk about the main highlight of TMCS 2026 – the toys! Spanning 3 levels at *SCAPE , the event presents more than 100 exhibitors and vendors across model cars , figures , trading cards , and more.
With event-exclusive launches and limited-edition collectables , you will discover rare finds you would want to add to your personal collection.
But beyond shopping for your next collector piece, there are also quite a few interactive activities with prizes involved. For instance, join the Tamiya Racing Competition for S$50 and stand a chance to win cash prizes up to S$888 !
Never lost your skills in Beyblade ? Enter the Beyblade Competition for S$20 and stand a chance to win exclusive gifts . Purchase your tickets to the Tamiya and Beyblade events here .
Prefer to drive to survive ? Take on the racing simulators at TMCS 2026 and compete for the fastest lap times. The top 3 fastest participants will walk away with their own racing simulator worth up to S$899 .
If any of these piques your interest, mark your calendars and race down to *SCAPE on 21 & 22 November for TMCS 2026.
The Model Car Show Singapore 2026
Facebook | Instagram | TikTok | Website
2 Orchard Link, *SCAPE, Level 1–3, Singapore 237978
10am–9pm
21 & 22 November 2026
For more lifestyle updates like this, subscribe to our Telegram channel at @confirmgood .
summary: The Model Car Show (TMCS) returns on 21 & 22 November 2026. Here are the highlights that will span 3 levels of *SCAPE.
