Free websites & tools for content in the AI era
Your For You page in 2026 is a bit of a mixed bag. In between your friend’s Japan trip photo dump and a hawker uncle going viral, there’s a cat playing the violin, a romance drama that wraps up in 90-second episodes, and a song you’ve had on repeat for a week before finding out no human sang it.
AI-made content is officially part of the scroll, and Singaporeans have feelings about it. This year, an AI-generated National Day banner in Kampong Chai Chee was taken down after residents spotted mistakes in it, and plenty of local artists have spoken up about what AI means for their livelihoods.
We’re not here to tell you to love AI or hate it. This list of free websites to bookmark is a beginner-friendly toolkit to help you save the content you love, spot what’s AI, make your own stuff for fun, and support the humans behind the art. Zero tech jargon, we promise.
Bookmark these free websites & tools for AI content

What it helps you do

1. Toolsmadefree
Save & edit TikToks and Reels without downloading an app
Screenshot from: Toolsmadefree
Toolsmadefree is a free toolbox for anyone who scrolls, or posts, on TikTok and Instagram. Paste a link into its downloader and the video saves straight to your phone or laptop. It’s handy for backing up your own videos.
Downloading is just the start. The site has 7 tools in total, including a video converter that reframes clips to vertical and trims awkward silences, a background remover, a compressor that also turns clips into GIFs, an audio cleaner that cuts out background noise, a thumbnail maker, and an auto caption generator that can transcribe and translate. Everything runs in your browser, so there’s nothing to install and no account to create.
One friendly reminder: a video belongs to the person who made it. Saving a clip to rewatch offline is one thing, but reposting someone else’s video as your own is a no-go. Ask the creator before sharing their work, and always tag them.
Website: Toolsmadefree
2. Hive AI Detector
Check if a photo, video or song was made with AI
That viral photo that looks almost too good to be true deserves a second look. Hive AI Detector is a free Chrome extension that tells you how likely it is that an image, video, piece of text, or audio clip was made by AI.
Using it is easy. Add it to Chrome, right-click anything suspicious on a webpage, and select Hive AI Detector. You’ll get a percentage showing how likely the content is AI-generated, and for images and videos it’ll even guess which AI tool was used. You can also upload or paste files saved on your device. No login needed.
Treat the score as a strong hint, not a final verdict. AI detectors can get it wrong both ways, so a high score isn’t a free pass to accuse a real artist in the comments. When in doubt, check the creator’s other work or ask nicely.
Website: Hive AI Detector on the Chrome Web Store
3. Aipopdb
An IMDb for AI-made movies, songs & creators
Screenshot from: Aipopdb
Think of Aipopdb as IMDb, but only for entertainment made with AI. It lists AI-made feature films, short films, series, and songs, along with profiles of the creators and studios behind them. At the time of writing, the database tracks 5,212 works.
Each title comes with a score, runtime, view count and the AI tools used to make it. For the uninitiated, tools like Kling and Seedance are AI video generators, which are apps that turn a written description into a video clip.
The site makes a point of ranking AI entertainment on its own charts instead of pitting it against human-made films and music. There’s also a news section that tracks what’s happening in AI entertainment, including legal developments, plus a weekly newsletter.
Website: Aipopdb
4. Photopea
A free Photoshop-style photo editor that runs in your browser
Screenshot from: Photopea
Not every creative tool needs AI. Photopea looks and works a lot like Photoshop, except it runs entirely in your browser for free. There’s nothing to download and no account to create, so you can start editing almost instantly.
You can open Photoshop files, work with layers, retouch photos, and design posters or social media graphics. It was created by Czech developer Ivan Kuckir and has been around since 2013, which in internet years makes it a seasoned veteran.
The free version shows ads on the side of the screen, while a paid Premium plan removes them. It’s a solid pick for students, home business owners, and anyone who wants to pick up real design skills.
Website: Photopea
5. Gentube
…
summary: No downloads or complex tech jargon required.

body:
Equoriel – DIY press-on nails workshop
If you’ve ever watched nail artists work their magic with ease and reckoned you could do it too, here’s your chance to put your skills to the test. At Equoriel in Queensway Shopping Centre , you can try your hand at creating your very own press-on nails , without having to splurge a fortune on an entire collection of nail polishes, tools, and decorations.
Freshly opened in October 2026, this new-to-Singapore concept is still a lesser-known gem. Anyone of any artistic ability is welcome, even people who know next to nothing about nail art.
How much does the press-on nails workshop cost?
Gel polish and pat gel selection at Equoriel.
Each 2-hour session is priced at $19.90 for a limited time for first-time customers , which is quite a steal compared to the usual price of $39.90 . That’s a pretty affordable way to try your hand at nail art without investing in your own supplies.
Not to mention, $19.90 is a far cry from the prices we’re used to paying for a full set of manicures at nail salons in Singapore. You’ll walk away with a set of nails and a fun new experience under your belt, so we’d say that’s money well spent.
What can I expect at the press-on nails workshop?
Aesthetic, intentional environment
Stepping into Equoriel, we were welcomed by its cosy, coquette- inspired interiors , put together by owner Jane.
The cohesive pink-and-silver theme was pleasing to the eyes, and a little photo corner complete with a pretty setup and mini Christmas tree caught our attention. This is a cute spot to snap some photos of your press-on nails after the workshop.
There are 7 craft stations lined along the walls, and each of them comes with an adorable gingham-patterned stool as well as their own set of tools and materials, so you won’t have to share anything with other participants.
Every item you see in the shop has been thoughtfully chosen to make the nail art process as fuss-free as possible. From nail polish bottles with long, easy-to-grip handles to handy cotton wipe dispensers on the table, even the smallest details have been considered with beginners in mind.
Jane also shared with us that her goal is to make the experience easy for everyone, making this a fun craft activity you can enjoy with family or a group of friends.
Arrive early for nail sizing & fitting
Before you get started, you’ll need to arrive 10 minutes early for a fitting, where you can choose your preferred nail shape and length . And once Jane has got your nail sizes down, she makes the effort to save them, so you won’t have to get sized again on your next visit.
Shop tour & basic demonstrations
The session starts off with a 15-minute tour of all the tools you’ll be using and a demonstration of basic nail art skills by Jane, who was eager and meticulous in her explanations and work.
During this time, she also showed us how to use cat-eye gel polishes in different manoeuvres and did a rundown of the different polishes and pat gels available.
We were also shown their charm and sticker bar , with a bountiful of different bits and bobs to pick and choose from. All charms, including the premium ones in display cases, come with no additional cost , so you can have fun piling on as many as you like.
Choose your nail polishes
After the shop tour, we headed over to the shelves stocked with nail polishes and pat gel polishes to pick out the colours we’ll be using. Colour swatches are framed on the shelf for easy reference, and you’re advised to pick up a maximum of 3 gel polishes at any point in time, which you can switch out as you wish.
Design & paint to your heart’s content
Following this, the fun of painting and designing begins. We recommend preparing some inspo pics or just winging it and letting your creative juices flow; you’ll have access to every tool you need, including gem pickers, tweezers, and lint-free wipes.
Jane will be around to guide you throughout the session. The polishes provided are also self-levelling, and the brushes are easy to grip, leaving no room for worry about shaky, unstable hands.
Pick from a wide range of charms & stickers
If you have your own charms you’re dying to wear on your nails, Equoriel welcomes you to bring them down and use them too. But don’t worry if you don’t, as there are plenty of options in their repertoire for you to be spoilt for choice with. They even have a basket containing seasonal charms and stickers .
For the upcoming Christmas season, we saw gingerbread man charms, gold stars, and Christmas tree stickers among the mix. If you don’t fancy seasonal nails, you’ll also be able to pick from the dozens of charms on the table, including glitters of different colours and Sanrio character charms.
Finishing touches by the owner herself
After we were done with the fun, the final layer of top coat on the press-ons was applied and cured by Jane herself, who also filed down the little imperfections on the nails to ensure a perfect, long-lasting fit.
…
summary: Comes with unlimited charms and stickers.
title: Try Your Hand At Being A Nail Tech For A Day At This DIY Press-On Nails Workshop In Singapore

Christmas is fast approaching in Singapore, but if you’re not in the mood for a festive dinner this year, how about going for brunch instead? You won’t have to battle the crowds for a table (it’s gonna be expensive anyway), and you can spend the evening admiring Christmas lights and shopping for last-minute gifts at Christmas markets across the island. Convinced? Here are the restaurants in Singapore offering Christmas brunches – some stretch over a couple of days, too!
Why trust this guide
Our team rounds up the best dining experiences, from festive restaurant menus to seasonal food events worth adding to your cal. For this guide, we’ve looked at Christmas brunch offerings in Singapore, taking into account menu highlights, prices, dining dates and locations to help you find a celebration that suits your plans and budget. We’ve also included key booking details so you can plan your festive get-together with ease.
Best restaurants for Christmas brunch in Singapore
1. Alley on 25 at Andaz Singapore
Photography: Andaz Singapore
Your brunch dates just got a major festive upgrade at Alley on 25 at Andaz Singapore. From 14 November to 27 December 2026, the Festive Brunch Social beckons with a generous spread of beloved Christmas classics and local favourites. Ease into the feast with freshly shucked oysters, sustainably sourced salmon, and a premium charcuterie selection including 20-month-aged parma ham and wagyu bresaola. Next, fill up on roaming cage-free egg specialties (think Sarawak black pepper crab eggs Benedict, Firecracker X.O. egg and Turkish breakfast eggs), alongside local dishes like Hokkien mee and satay. Desserts are a must, so indulge in Mont Blanc yule log and eggnog cheesecake, or stop by the festive waffle bar.
On Christmas Day, come by for an elevated Santa’s Brunch Social. As the restaurant’s most extensive festive spread yet, expect an elevated selection of premium seafood, artisanal Italian cheeses, gourmet salads and festive roasts. Come hungry for fresh tiger prawns and oysters, traditional roast turkey, maple-glazed bone-in ham and 12-hour braised Margaret River wagyu brisket. The feast continues with indulgent sweet treats, featuring Valrhona chocolate and hazelnut crunch cake, festive trifles, house-churned gelato, and a nostalgic Santa’s Candy Bar. Want to make it a boozy affair? Top up $58 to sip free-flowing sparkling wines, housepour wines, beers and DIY cocktails, or $88 to enjoy bottomless champagne, too.
Best for: Elevated festive brunch buffets with holiday classics and local favourites
When: Festive Brunch Social from 14 November to 27 December (excludes Christmas Day); Santa’s Brunch Social on 25 December 2026
How much: Festive Brunch Social from $69 per adult and $34.50 per child; Santa’s Brunch Social from $148 per adult and $74 per child; top up from $58 for the free-flow alcoholic beverage packages
Timings: 12pm to 2.30pm
Address: Level 25, Andaz Singapore, 5 Fraser Street, Singapore 189354
Visit Alley on 25
2. Pullman Singapore Hill Street
Photography: Pullman Singapore Hill Street
All aboard The Pullman Express for a brunch celebration unlike any other! Inspired by the nostalgic holiday movie, The Polar Express, Pullman Singapore Hill Street brings back its signature Mega Brunch for a Christmas edition. The massive brunch buffet spans across two dining concepts on level 1 of the hotel – Madison’s and MOGĀ – offering two distinct experiences in one seating.
It’s all about the classics at Madison’s. Start off with an icy fresh seafood display of Boston lobsters, Japanese oysters and tiger prawns, before indulging in carved-to-order roasted turkey, black angus tomahawk and honey-glazed gammon ham. Other mouth-watering dishes include the signature beef reuben sandwiches, artisanal cheeses, as well as festive log cakes and dessert canapes.
Meanwhile, modern Japanese flavours await at MOGĀ. Help yourself to copious amounts of sashimi and rolls, featuring salmon, hamachi and California rolls, alongside piping hot dishes like crispy prawn tempura and grilled unagi. Don’t forget to stop by the live udon station for comfort food with a festive twist: chewy udon noodles served in a rich dashi broth with tender turkey and a silky onsen egg. To amp up the celebratory mood, top up $68++ per guest for two hours of free-flowing Taittinger champagne, prosecco, red and white wine and beer.
Perk alert:
• The first 20 guests to make a reservation can enjoy early bird prices at $108++ per adult.
• Exclusive for All Accor+ Explorer members, the first 20 members to make a reservation can also enjoy the early bird price of $108++ per adult.
• Plus, receive a complimentary HYSSES Scented Indulgence set (worth $74.90) with every reservation.
Best for: A massive Christmas brunch spanning two unique dining destinations
When: 25 December 2026

body:
Good news for anyone who has been eyeing those Korean burgers from afar. Lotteria is now halal certified in Singapore, with both outlets at Jewel Changi Airport and Jurong Point listed on the MUIS HalalSG directory. The brand announced it on its official Instagram on 3 November 2026, a day after rolling out a new Teriyaki burger series.
When the South Korean chain opened at Jewel in February 2026, it was pork-free and lard-free but carried no halal cert. That kept a lot of Muslim diners at the window instead of the counter. Nine months on, that gap is closed.
Lotteria halal certified: what the MUIS listing shows
We checked the MUIS HalalSG establishment search on 6 November 2026. Two Lotteria outlets appear under the Eating Establishment scheme, restaurant category:
• 63 Jurong West Central 3, #01-47/48/87/88/89/90/91, Jurong Point (certificate EERT26100000119)
• 78 Airport Boulevard, #B1-248, Jewel Changi Airport (certificate EERT26100000120)
In plain terms: this is a MUIS halal-certified restaurant, not just a “no pork, no lard” kitchen. Halal certification in Singapore is issued per outlet, so if Lotteria opens a third branch, check the HalalSG listing for that address before you go. The Lotteria Singapore website now carries the Singapore halal logo too.
Source: Lotteria Singapore
What to order at Lotteria, with prices
Lotteria does not publish its a la carte prices online, and counter prices can shift, so the figures below are the deals the brand has posted on its official Instagram. Burgers are the main event here, and the Ria’s range is the one Koreans grew up with.
• Student Deal: any 2 burgers for S$10 (Double Bulgogi Beef Burger excluded), weekdays only, valid till 30 November 2026. Show a valid photo student pass and order at the counter.
• Add 2 regular soft drinks and 1 large fries to the Student Deal for S$3.50 more.
• Breakfast Burger Combo at Jewel: S$5 for a Beef Burger, K-Omelette Chicken Sausage or K-Omelette Turkey Bacon with a Milo, daily 10am to 12pm.
• Breakfast for two at Jurong Point: 2 K-Omelette Chicken Sausage plus Tater Tots for S$10.50, weekdays 9am to 11am.
• Coffee at Jurong Point: any 2 cups for S$5.80, daily till 12pm.
Without a deal, these are the ones to go for:
• Ria’s Beef Bulgogi Burger, the sweet soy-glazed patty that made the brand’s name in Korea (there is a double version if you are hungry)
• Ria’s Shrimp Burger, a thick prawn patty and a cult favourite
• the new Teriyaki series: Teri Egg Beef, Double Teri Egg Beef and Teri Egg Crispy Chicken, all with a fried egg, for a limited time
• Gangjung Chicken, coated in a sweet-spicy Korean glaze, sold by the piece or as a burger
• Shake Shake Fries for the seasoning-bag drama, and the Mango Peach Bingsu if you still have space
Source: Lotteria Singapore
Lotteria Jewel Changi Airport: address, hours and MRT
• Address: 78 Airport Boulevard, #B1-248, Jewel Changi Airport, Singapore 819666
• Opening hours: daily, 10am to 10pm (last order 9.30pm)
• Nearest MRT: Changi Airport (EW29/CG2), then walk through Terminal 2 or 3 to Jewel’s basement level
Jewel is the more touristy of the two, so expect a queue around lunch on weekends. It works well as a pre-flight meal, or as the bribe that gets the kids to the Rain Vortex without complaint.
Lotteria Jurong Point: address, hours and MRT
• Address: 63 Jurong West Central 3, #01-47/48/87/88/89/90/91, Jurong Point, Singapore 648331
• Opening hours: Monday 9am to 10.30pm (last order 10pm); Tuesday to Sunday and eve of public holidays 9am to 12.30am (last order 12am)
• Nearest MRT: Boon Lay (EW27), linked to Jurong Point via the bus interchange
Jurong Point opened in August 2026 and keeps much later hours, which makes it the better bet for supper. Westies, this one is yours. If you need a refresher on the outlet itself, our earlier Lotteria Jurong Point guide covers the layout and launch details.
Is it worth the trip?
For Muslim families who have been asking Korean friends to bring Lotteria back from Seoul, yes, finally. The burgers are fast-food burgers, not atas smash patties, but the bulgogi sauce and the shrimp patty taste different from anything at the big American chains. Go on a weekday afternoon with a student in tow and two burgers come to S$10, which is quite the lobang.
We first flagged Lotteria back in June with its S$5 Jewel breakfast combo . For a sit-down halal option with more variety, J65’s halal buffet at Hotel Jen Tanglin is another one we have covered. Deals and limited-time items change often, so check @lotteriasg before heading down.
summary: Korean burger chain Lotteria is now MUIS halal-certified at both its Singapore outlets. Here is where to find them, when they open and what to order.
title: Lotteria halal certified at Jewel and Jurong Point, with 2 burgers for S$10 till 30 November

body:
Nordic-inspired Christmas at Cedele
Pumpkin spiced latte season is out, and logcake season is in. This year, local favourite Cedele is celebrating the Christmas season, Nordic style, featuring wholesome ingredients and comforting flavours freshly made in Singapore, with a spread of new and returning hits that are sure to set the mood for sleigh bells jingling, ring-ting-tingling too .
First up, the savouries: Santa’s Surf & Turf Croissant Platter ($68) , a set of 12 buttery mini croissants sandwiching luxe crab mayo, as well as tender pulled beef.
You may recognise the platter from past editions, but here’s something new to 2026’s line-up━ Cheese & Spinach Brioche Wreath with Festive Dips ($48) . It’s the perfect grazing dish to kick off your Christmas feast, with your choice of Garlic Spring Onion or Pork Bacon Cream Cheese Dip .
Trust us when we say you’re missing out if you skip this. Think: warm, fluffy little cheese-speckled bread balls, dipped into creamy, umami-laden bacon cream cheese. You’re not drooling, we are.
Returning this year is the Truffle Mushroom Crown ($48) , another Christmas favourite at Cedele. You couldn’t ask for a better combi than this, with flaky, buttery pastry plus earthy diced forest mushrooms, elevated with truffle oil.
Rest assured, it’s not all about the finger foods, because Cedele’s bestselling Wagyu Beef Shepherd’s Pie ($79) is back on the menu this year!
Cedele fans will know the absolute treat this is, with a rich, tomato-based Wagyu braise below, and ultra smooth, fluffy mash on top, finished to golden perfection in the oven.
Balance this out with an order of Jolly Mesclun Salad ($48) , tossed in a bright, zesty yuzu vinaigrette that’ll have your palate refreshed before the sweets.
This year, the dessert spread is shaking things up with a Winterberry Banana Cake ($80) . As with all of Cedele’s bakes, it’s baked fresh daily right here in Singapore, with unrefined sugars or no trans fat .
If banana cake is your go-to sweet treat, this festive edition is layered with darling baby pink strawberry cream cheese, adding a bright, berry note to the rustic cake.
Then, there’s the all-new Winter Hearth Cheesecake ($60) , inspired by the warm hug of Nordic spices.
This cake starts with cardamon-infused cheese, poured over with toasty caramel apples, and given texture by a buttery walnut streusel. Don’t let the idea of cardamon sway you━this combi had us thinking of fireside cuddles on a snowy winter’s day.
Of course, Christmas ain’t Christmas without log cakes, and Cedele presents two of ‘em this year. There’s the classic Flourless Chocolate Log Cake ($78) that’s been a festive staple for every one the brand’s 29 years, crafted with the finest European butter, and gluten-free to boot.
On the same hug-in-a-dessert note, there’s the Spiced Apple Noel Log Cake ($82) , which we loved for its cinnamon-spiced apple filling, and brown butter chocolate ganache.
Another new item to add to your Christmas cart at Cedele is their Noel Tiramisu Tart , available in a set of four minis ($31.20) , or a 7-inch cake ($90) .
Their take on the Italian dessert sees a buttery tart shell filled with an utterly decadent, brandy-infused chocolate custard. For legit tiramisu vibes, this is piped over with mascarpone cream, before the tart is dusted in cocoa powder and cinnamon.
Whether you’re ordering the annual panettone for your fam or gifting, you’ll be happy to know that this year’s new creation is a Spiced Carrot Walnut Panettone ($48) , which reimagines Cedele’s signature Carrot Walnut Cake as the Italian sweet bread.
Yes, there is actual carrot baked into this panettone, as well as walnuts and chocolate chips, jazzed up with cinnamon, and dusted with a cinnamon streusel that had us coming back for seconds and thirds.
Otherwise, the classic Orange Jaffa Panettone is also available, both as a set of six minis ($25) , or a large 900g ($48) version.
For little treats to go along with those post-feasting cups of steaming hot tea, stock up your pantry with some cookies such as the new Assorted Christmas Cookies ($40) ━a tin of Almond Oat Long Black Cookies, alongside the brand new Cinnamon Nut Crunch, and Earl Grey Chocolate Chip flavours.
Alternatively, another new set is the Assorted Tea Cookies ($41) , with nine pieces each of Earl Grey Chocolate Chip, Classic Hojicha, and all-new Matcha Almond Shortbread.
Otherwise, the Assorted Espresso Cookies ($40) are their coffee-accented counterparts, with Almond Oat Long Black, Taro Latte Marble Shortbread, and Salted Walnut Espresso variants.
Here’s the best part: you can get two tins of these, or any of Cedele’s other Christmas cookies, at $75 , or four tins for $148 , which works out to be $37 a tin !
…

body:
Cafes in Singapore that accept CDC Vouchers sorted by area
Frankly, cafe-hopping in Singapore is an expensive hobby to have. Order one main and a drink, and there goes $30. But it’s a different story when you’re making use of your CDC Vouchers, which, by the way, aren’t just for grocery shopping or hawker meals. Check out our list of the best cafes in Singapore that accept CDC Vouchers for your next coffee run or WFH day.
66 Best Cafes In Singapore You Must Try
CBD cafes
1. The Better Half
Run by a young couple, The Better Half is a cosy nook at Everton Park selling drinks and fresh bakes. Almost everything is on display here, so take your time to pick what you’d like.
If you don’t know what to get, we recommend starting with their crowd-favourite Pistachio Raspberry ($8.50) : a pistachio cake with raspberry jam and the same tangy-zesty filling and buttercream. There’s also the lesser-seen Honey Kinako ($8.80) , featuring a wildflower honey cake with kinako buttercream and matcha glaze, finished with kinako crumble.
Read The Better Half review .
Address: 1 Everton Park, #01-43, Singapore 081001
Opening hours: Tue-Sun 10:30am to 4pm
Website
The Better Half is not halal-certified.
2. Bag Me Up Bagel House
Bag Me Up is another Everton Park gem that’s a stone’s throw away from The Better Half. This under-HDB cafe specialises in bagels and focaccia, all under $20!
If you prefer bagels, consider their Can Trust Chick ($14.50) , a simple combination of tender chicken patty and melted cheese. Something new on the menu is the Smash Bagel ($16.50) , which uses smashed beef patty as the key ingredient, alongside melted cheddar, caramelised onions, and a sunny-side-up.
Read our Bag Me Up Bagel House review .
Address: 2 Everton Park, #01-59B, Singapore 081002
Opening hours: Tue & Sat-Sun 9am to 3pm, Wed-Fri 9:30am to 3pm
Website
Bag Me Up is not halal-certified.
Bag Me Up Review: Unagi And Wagyu Beef Bagels At This Under HDB Bagel Shop Near Outram Park
3. Elijah Pies
If we had to introduce a cafe in Singapore known for pies, Elijah Pies would instantly come to mind.
Out of their nine flavours, the stunning Wild Berry Lavender Pie ($9++) is a bestseller. It features a crispy crust topped with fresh yoghurt infused with real berries and a hint of lavender, creating the perfect balance of tangy and creamy. Speaking of fruity flavours, the Yuzu Meringue Pie ($9++) and Lime Thyme Pie ($8.50++) are great alternatives. Otherwise, go straight for the Speculoos Hojicha Pie ($8.50++) or Pistachio Praline Pie ($9.50++) ; the former sees caramelised cookie butter and aromatic notes of roasted green tea.
Read our Elijah Pies review .

Elijah Pies Review: IG-Famous Bakery Opens Chio Cafe With Mac N’ Cheese Pie, Matcha Latte Pie And More
4. Hello Arigato
Hello Arigato has six outlets at the time of writing, and their Everton Park, Joo Chiat, and Seng Poh Road branches accept CDC Vouchers. We recommend the former for a serene atmosphere, while the latter is great if you want to dine within a Scandinavian-esque space.
The cafe is known for sando, such as the crowd-favourite Porkatsu Sando ($26++) and the popular Gyu Sando ($28++) . The Gyu Sando is especially worth a try, comprising a thick beef tenderloin katsu paired with caramelised sweet onion jam. There are pastas too, including the creamy Hokkaido Milk Udon Carbonara ($22++) and flavour-packed Mentaiko Pasta ($22++) . FYI, the menu varies depending on the outlet you’re visiting.

5. Pretty Good Muffins
ICYMI: Pretty Good Muffins went viral for their affordable muffins and matcha latte in early to mid-2025. After trying their goods, we can tell you that the Chinatown cafe’s hype isn’t dying down anytime soon because their muffins are, quite literally, pretty good .

body:
Pugners Dining is a private home diner in Hougang
You can have a special-occasion dinner without booking a hotel restaurant or heading into the CBD. In an HDB block in Hougang , Pugners Dining serves a restaurant-level tasting menu from a couple’s home, and Eatbook got first dibs on its new Menu 3.0.
The private diner opened in August 2025, founded by husband-and-wife duo Jon Marcus Tay and Krystle Tan.
Krystle manages the front of house, while Jon helms the kitchen, drawing on experience at Rhubarb, Buona Terra, Gunther’s, and Garibaldi, several of which have held Michelin stars.
This $88 Supper Club Sells Out In Minutes—Here’s What We Tried
Food at Pugner’s Dining
We started with the Bao , stuffed with a deep-fried prawn head, green mango slaw, and nam jim jaew, a tangy and slightly spicy Northern Thai sauce. The prawn bodies come back later, but more on that soon.
Next was the PB & J , a yeast-risen duck fat waffle topped with silky chicken liver mousse and the jam of the day. Our table got two flavours: sour cherry and fig.
The mousse was smooth and almost whipped, with the fig balancing its richness while the sour cherry added a brighter tang. The crispy waffle made the perfect base for both.
The Kajimoto Bay Oyster came with yuzu, dashi, little potatoes, and a cream sauce. The oyster was plump and very fresh, pairing especially well with the potato cubes and creamy white sauce.
My favourite course was the Kami No Ebi , an asam pedas orecchiette dish made with the same prawns from the bao. There were plenty of springy, perfectly cooked prawns, while the pasta was al dente.
The sauce had just the right amount of spice and tang, balanced by mint and ginger flower. Topping it all were deep-fried capers, which had been soaked overnight to mellow their saltiness before frying, giving the dish a lovely salty crunch.
The Swordfish is torched and served with a cincalok sauce made by blending fermented shrimp with onions and other aromatics. Alongside it is a “sambal caponata”, a riff on the Italian eggplant and tomato dish.
The tomatoes are cooked in ikan bakar sambal, while the eggplant is lightly salted first. The fish was perfectly cooked, and the sauce had a good balance of heat and sweet tang.
The Duck course paired duck confit with panang curry, pomelo salad, roasted coconut, and aromatics.
My main gripes were that the pomelo wasn’t as sweet as I’d have liked, while the duck confit was a little too chunky for my liking.
The menu also includes Sereni(Tea) , a rose, sakura, and yuzu palate cleanser served before dessert.
By this point, we were pretty much stuffed. But alas, dessert is a separate stomach! The star of the show was the Roasted Banana , inspired by banoffee pie. Banana flesh is mixed with mascarpone and sugar, while the banana skin is infused into milk and turned into a foam. It’s then served with yoghurt dulce de leche, toasted almonds, cocoa crumble, and a frozen vanilla bean and miso parfait. The result is warm on top and cold at the bottom.
This was my second favourite course, with contrasting textures and flavours in every spoonful.
The meal ends with three petit fours, each made using leftovers from earlier courses.
First up, the Potato & Chocolate : a macaron with buttercream made from potato skins from the oyster course, which are roasted and ground into a fine powder. It’s finished with potato chips. It was a little sweet, while the chips had gone slightly soggy. We heard they’re working to fine-tune the macaron!
The Strawberry & Ginger Flower was the winner, featuring a chewy butter mochi topped with strawberry jam and ginger flower saved from the asam pedas. It was tasty, if a touch sweet.
Lastly, the Hae Bee Hiam : madeleines made with prawn shell-infused butter and house-made hae bee hiam. They were light and fluffy, with a gentle prawn flavour reminiscent of the hae bee hiam rolls everyone eats during CNY.
The verdict
Menu 3.0 costs $150 per person , with a minimum of two guests per booking. Dinner took about two hours, and everything we tried was delicious and plated to a restaurant standard. Portions were generous too, and we were comfortably full by dessert. I was also pleasantly surprised by how protein-heavy the meal was.
You’ll need to book online, and note that the dishes we tried may change.
For a birthday, anniversary, or any occasion worth celebrating, Pugner’s Dining is worth the splurge.
While you’re here, check out our guide to the best new restaurants in Singapore for November 2026 ! You can also
summary: Pugners Dining is a popular private diner in a Hougang HDB home, run by an ex-fine dining chef and his wife!

body:
Planning a beach day at Sentosa just got tastier. Palawan Hawkers has officially launched at The Palawan @ Sentosa , and brings a vibrant cluster of 8 food trucks dishing out everything from decades-old heritage recipes to modern fusion bites.
Brought to you by the team behind Cosford Container Park, famous for being Singapore’s largest F&B container park, this pet-friendly open-air space serves up wallet-friendly bites starting at just S$5.90 .
Amongst the myriad offerings, look out for nostalgic heritage brands like Qing Heritage Hainanese Chicken Rice . They are known for their Hainanese Kampung Chicken Rice (price TBD) with tender steamed kampung chicken and their signature ginger paste, made from a secret recipe passed down since the 1940s. With its original outlet stationed all the way in Dover, Palawan Hawkers lets you can enjoy a taste of tradition by the beach.
Nearby, Boon Tat Street BBQ Seafood brings nearly 38 years of history to the shore, firing up smoky grilled BBQ Sambal Stingray (price TBD) , BBQ Prawns (price TBD) and Sotong (price TBD) . The seafood is then dressed in signature sambal chilli sauce — which was refined by its founder through years of trial and error — before being served on banana leaves to impart extra fragrance into the dish.
If you’re in the mood for something on the more experimental side, look out for Palawan Beer House , evolved f rom the popular Cluny Toast at the Singapore Botanic Gardens. They offer modern, elevated twists on local classics such as Sourdough Peanut Butter Toast (price TBD) and other innovative dishes created from collaborations with various Singapore dining brands. Some such dishes include Bacon & Egg Pizza by YOUNGS Restaurant & Bar (price TBD) and Authentic Signature Laksa (price TBD) by Nyonyas & Gentlemen at Village Katong Hotel.
To round things off, Urban Truck hits the spot with spicy, cheese-stuffed Indian fusion creations like Stuffed Parathas (price TBD) and Cheesy Kola Meatballs (price TBD) , while Creamy Duck Milkshake Bar cures sweet tooth cravings with a trendy Kunafa Pistachio Waffle (price TBD) and a thick, creamy Triple Chocolate Milkshake (price TBD) .
Operating daily from 11am to 9pm , it is an ideal pitstop to fuel up without breaking the bank after splashing around Sentosa .
10 best beach clubs in Singapore for your next sun-kissed escapade
summary: Palawan Hawkers at The Palawan @ Sentosa features 8 food-truck concepts offering traditional local dishes and contemporary fusion options from S$5.90. Operating daily from 11am to 9pm, the pet-friendly open-air space provides an accessible dining option for beachgoers and visitors looking for casual meals after exploring the island attractions.
title: Palawan Hawkers opens on Sentosa with 8 food trucks & heritage bites from $5.90

body:
Resorts World Genting helicopter service
While the holiday season is right over the horizon, not many of us have the luxury of jetting off to the far-flung reaches of the world, and we’re not talking about the lack of travel funds here. If you already had your fun and have burned through your ALs earlier this year, perhaps a shorter trip can still soothe your ache to travel.
Well, Genting still remains one of the most popular family destinations for weekend trips, and getting there isn’t too difficult. However, for those with a bit more moolah to burn but not as much time, Resorts World Genting has just the thing for you: a new private helicopter charter service that drops you into the middle of the fun in under half an hour.
Here’s what you need to know before booking your airborne rides – fair warning, they don’t come cheap.
What is Resorts World Genting’s new helicopter service?
Traditionally, getting to Genting from Singapore was pretty straightforward; you’d either take the 6-hour drive up North yourself or hop on one of the many Genting coaches bound for the misty highlands. Flying in’s also possible, as you’d catch a 1-hour flight from the Little Red Dot to Subang Airport , and then get a private hire vehicle to take you there in about 2 hours .
Image credit: Aviation International News
Should 2 hours sound like a ridiculous amount of time to sit in the back of a car, now you can opt for Resorts World Genting’s new private helicopter charter service to lavishly transport you there. The package is available for booking from now till 31st December 2026 , and you’ll get an entire twin-engine helicopter to yourself that seats up to 8 passengers .
Image credit: Klook
Since you’ll be taking to the skies to skip the jams down on the ground, you’re looking at flight times of just 25 minutes . After sitting through a 10-minute safety briefing, the VIP experience will take off from Subang Airport in Selangor, and you can choose to land at either Resorts World Genting or Resorts World Awana .
Image credit: Expedia
Of course, the views will be stellar during the ride. No longer will you have to keep your eyes trained on the road; instead, you’ll be flying above them, as the highlands unfurl before you with their lush greenery and rolling clouds. Once you’ve touched down, a complimentary limo transfer awaits you, which will bring you straight to any venue or hotel at either resort.
How much do helicopter rides to Genting cost & how to book them?
Now for the million-dollar – thankfully, not literally – question: how much do these helicopter rides to Genting cost? They don’t list prices publicly, but we’ve done the dirty work for you to call in to enquire. A 1-way helicopter ride from Subang Airport to Genting costs RM68,000 , or approximately S$21,339.16 .
Do the math, and even at maximum capacity, that’s still over S$2,660 per pax – a steep price to pay to arrive for your short trip like a movie star. If you’re not put off by that number, you can call Resorts World Genting’s booking hotline at +603-2718 1118 to make your reservations, and please do so 3 days in advance .
All you need to know about Resorts World Genting’s new helicopter rides
While not many of us will be jumping at the opportunity to fly over to Genting via helicopter, it’s interesting that the resort’s giving the ultra-affluent an extra way to get to their doorstep. Even for us regular folks, don’t discount this unique mode of transport just yet, as it could make for a romantic opportunity to pop the big question.
Just hope they don’t say no; being lovelorn after blowing a S$20,000 hole in your bank account is a fate I wouldn’t wish on my worst enemies.

Guide to buying a Christmas tree in Singapore
Every year, places like Orchard Road would be dressed up for Christmas with those big Christmas trees that light up the entire street. If you’re looking for a quick way to bring festive cheer to your home, take your parties up a notch this holiday season with this guide to getting a Christmas tree in Singapore .
Is there space in HDB flats for a Christmas tree?
Image adapted from: @bobobolster via Instagram
Yes, some Christmas trees are only 3ft (~0.91m) high, so they’ll fit right in in an average HDB flat. But you should still measure the space you plan to put the tree in beforehand, as it’ll make the buying process much easier.
When measuring, leave an allowance of about 30cm-60cm between the top of the tree and the ceiling to have room for a tree topper. The width of Christmas trees is also usually about half the height of the tree, so keep that in mind as well.
Should I get a live Christmas tree or an artificial one?
Image credit: Jelaine Massingham via Google Maps
Many prefer live trees because of their naturally crisp and fresh scent . It gives off strong winter vibes that we can never find in Singapore. Artificial trees, on the other hand, require much less maintenance. They’re hassle-free and are great for aesthetics as they have a more consistent look.
Some other important factors to consider are the different types of live trees , space , temperature , and safety .
Types of live trees
Image adapted from: Far East Flora Garden
The most common live tree you can find in Singapore is the Noble Fir , which has the classic Christmas scent and sturdier branches. If you’re looking for something that requires less maintenance and is more child-friendly, there’s also the Nordmann Fir tree which has soft needles and minimal shedding.
Space
Image credit: @how.jenny via Instagram
For HDB flats, you not only have to consider where you will place your tree, but also how to get it through the door and whether it fits into your lift. Remember to measure the width of your door, the entryway, and where you want to place the tree to be completely certain the space can physically accommodate the tree.
There are also some trees that are much slimmer which makes it easier to transport and takes up less space in a room. You can opt for these to minimise the hassle.
Temperature
Image credit: 81airconservice Singapore via Flickr
Live Christmas trees dry out very easily, so they need to be stored in a humid and cool room , roughly between 18°C and 22°C . Setting it up in an air-conditioned space can extend the longevity of your tree.
For the kiasu ones who have bought your trees too early and need them to last throughout the holidays, you can consider setting up a humidifier in the room. However, there is a risk of over-humidifying, causing it to decay faster, so remember to set the humidifier at a lower setting.
Safety
View this post on Instagram
Norman Fir trees – the most common type of pine tree sold in Singapore – dry easily which makes them highly flammable . Many Christmas tree stores, like The Green Corner, will finish their trees with a fire-retardant coating to make them less flammable, but it’s best to stay vigilant.
Ensure that there are no overcrowded power sockets near the tree. During the holidays, do your best to keep small children away from the tree as there is a risk of the tree falling over . You can also add sandbags on top of the tree stand to add more stability.
Tips on maintaining live Christmas trees
When getting a live Christmas tree, you must consider the extra effort it’ll take to maintain, especially during the hustle and bustle of the holiday season. It also depends on how long you want to keep the tree for .
If you’ll be very busy, artificial trees might be the best option. It also saves clean-up time, maintenance, and it’s reusable for many years. But if you want to get a live tree, here are some tips on how to keep it alive as long as possible.
Cut an extra inch at the bottom of the tree
Image credit: WheeliePete via YouTube
When a pine tree is cut, its sap seals the part that’s cut to ensure that the tree retains water. This sap stops the tree from taking in more water. Cutting an inch off the bottom of the trunk gives you time to submerge it in water before the sap can do its thing. It might be hard to do this in an HDB, so you could request the nursery to help you do so before delivery.
Water the tree ASAP & monitor the water level regularly
Image credit: Amazon Singapore
Fresh pine trees need 4 to 8 litres of water every day during the first 1 to 2 weeks. So, as soon as your tree arrives, add some cold water to the tree stand’s water reservoir and immediately keep the tree in the stand.
During these earlier days, keep an eye on the water level. The reservoir of water inside the tree stand is slightly below the bottom of the tree trunk, so make sure the water level doesn’t drop below the bottom of the tree trunk.

summary: Some of these tips will make sure your Christmas tree stays bright and fresh throughout the holidays.

Bao Fast Foods from London pops up at New Bahru
Image credit: BFF
Convenience stores are a huge part of the F&B culture in many Asian countries. While we have our 7-Elevens, BAO Fast Foods (BFF) is bringing a Taiwanese minimart-inspired concept to Singapore and serving up its iconic street food: Taiwanese fried chicken.
Image credit: BFF
BFF’s parent company, BAO, was first established in London and has since become a cult favourite there with seven locations across the city. It’s known for its contemporary take on Taiwanese street food, with signatures including pillowy pork baos and more.
Now, Singaporeans can see what the hype is about, as BFF will be popping up at New Bahru from 11 November to 28 December 2026 .
16 Best New Bahru Eateries, Including New Openings—Laifaba, Dumpling Darlings And More
BFF’s signature is the Chicken Chopper ($6.50) , a unique take on the Taiwanese fried chicken—here, the meat is cut in a manner where the bone acts as a handle for easy eating.
Image credit: BFF
The Chicken Chopper is served three ways. The Original Crispy is seasoned with Taiwanese white pepper; the Flame Glazed is brushed with either a honey-soy or mala hot honey glaze and charred; and the Master Scalded is dipped in a boiling soy, star anise, and cinnamon sauce.
Image credit: BFF
These can be enjoyed with a ricebox ($7.95) or as a combo (from $9.50) . For a heartier meal, you can also pair them with Dan Dan Noodles ($6.50) or the Beef Cup Noodles ($12.50) , topped with freshly carved beef from a slow-roasting spit.
Wash down your food with Taiwanese craft tea, including the Fluffy Natural Alishan Wintermelon ($5.95) , a black tea infused with nitro for a foamy texture, or the Orange Guava Beauty Tea ($6.50) , a carbonated fruit tea. Alternatively, The Original Peanut Oatside Milk ($6) is a richer option, served with oat boba and tea jelly.
If you’re in a hurry, consider their grab-and-go items, including the Egg Sando , Marinated Eggs , “Fried Rice” Quinoa , Soy Puddings and more.
For more new eateries to look forward to this month, check out these new restaurants and cafes in November 2026 , featuring the Japanese chain store Matsuya, adorable tiger-themed cafes and more. And with the holiday season around the corner, make sure you check out Cedele’s Christmas menu .

body:
Right along Robinson Road inside Oxley Tower , Nice Noodle , a low-key noodle bar, has been quietly drawing long lunch queues. Unsurprisingly, the very aptly named Nice Noodle serves just that — nice noodles with a sophisticated twist.
Nice Noodle is the second venture of Chef Mandel Ban, who previously trained at the former 1-Michelin-starred restaurant Vianney Massot before striking out on his own to launch Nice Rice, a hawker stall serving affordable French-Japanese fusion rice bowls. Similarly, the menu at Nice Noodle blends Chef’s expertise in French culinary techniques with Asian noodle dishes.
Credit – Nice Noodle via Google Reviews
I arrived promptly just past 11.30am (which is their opening time), feeling smug that I had beaten the CBD lunch crowd. To my absolute horror, a long, snaking line had already formed, winding halfway down the corridor. It took a patient 35-minute wait before I finally snagged a seat, eagerly awaiting my meal.
What to order at Nice Noodle
Nice Noodle lets diners build their meal by pairing 1 of 3 protein choices with 1 of 6 noodle varieties. The main options include pork belly chashu, butter-poached chicken breast, and marinated beef short plate (which incurs a S$2 surcharge). For the noodle base, the menu is split evenly between 3 warm broth preparations and 3 dry, sauce-tossed styles.
I made up my mind before coming here that I absolutely had to try their 5-year aged tare stock. In Japanese cuisine, tare refers to a highly concentrated seasoning sauce placed at the bottom of a ramen bowl before it is filled with unseasoned soup stock and noodles. Thus, it’s mainly responsible for the saltiness, umami , and overall flavour profile of the dish it is used in. In this case, the aged tare had more complex, layered flavours that have been built on for 5 years.
Needless to say, I quickly ordered the Cool Broth with Beef (S$14, including S$2 add-on for beef) which came adorned with cubed white onions, tobiko and house-made mushroom jam.
Initially, I worried the cubed onions would be too astringent and overpower the delicate broth, but they ended up offering a mild sweetness and a sharp, satisfying crunch. The tobiko acted similarly; rather than taking over, it imparted a subtle brininess that elevated the clean tare stock. The mushroom jam added an intensely earthy, umami richness. Every topping complemented the next, coming together in a perfectly balanced, cohesive bowl.
As mentioned earlier, I was particularly excited to try the broth — I mean, it’s not everyday you see a 5-year-aged tare on the menu, especially for just S$12. It had a rather delicate and refreshing profile, especially since it was served cold. It tasted really clean and complex, with the tare bringing a subtle, mellow depth rather than a heavy kick.
Another thoroughly well-executed and arguably second most important component was the noodles. If you’re anything like me and hate soggy, soft noodles, this is the dish for you. Beyond being just al dente , these noodles had an extremely springy texture and retain a satisfying snap when bitten into.
As for the protein, I’d say the beef shortplate is well worth the extra S$2 price tag. It’s fall-apart-tender and possesses a deeply beef-forward flavour profile. The cut is naturally high in fat, which becomes buttery and soft when cooked. Prior to serving, Chef blowtorches the beef slices to give them a good sear which creates a savoury, brown crust.
Nice Rice, French Rd: Hidden hawker gem has a S$10.80 steak bowl — and it’s worth every cent
Next, I moved on to trying Garlic Fantasy with Pork (S$10) . It comes dressed in a rich French butter sauce, roasted garlic, crispy garlic, and an aromatic herb trinity. Similarly to the previous dish, it also includes a small pile of cubed onions and a modest scoop of mushroom jam.
The noodles in this dish were noticeably softer and a different type from the noodles used in the first dish we tried, and clumped up slightly before mixing.
Contrary to the name, I didn’t find this dish to be particularly garlicky — though that might just be the garlic lover in me speaking. However, I found the French butter sauce to be absolutely delicious. It was rich, silky and paired well with the herb trinity, which I assume features fresh parsley. Butter and parsley remain one of my favourite combinations ever, because of the creamy yet bright, aromatic flavours it brings.
Similarly, the thick pork belly slices are blowtorched right before they reach your table, which results in a crisp, caramelised finish. While the leaner bits can be slightly dry, the fatty sections stay soft, with the marinade leaving a subtle, sweet finish on the palate. The fat itself was melt-in-the-mouth soft, while the thin layer of skin added a gelatinous, springy bite.
Who is Nice Noodle best for?

My first thought when I saw the news of Gosame opening its first outlet in KL was: what makes this place so special? Having never heard of the restaurant before, I was genuinely curious about all the excitement surrounding its arrival. Apparently, I might have been one of the last people in Malaysia to find out about this halal spot from Seoul , known for its charcoal-grilled mackerel, among other things.
Located at The Stories of Taman Tunku in KL (quite the bougie neighbourhood, if you ask me), Muslim-owned Gosame is tucked beside a narrow walkway that leads to the restaurant’s entrance. Like most establishments in the area, it has both indoor and outdoor seating, although neither is particularly spacious. It was raining when we visited, so the outdoor area felt a little stuffy, but thankfully not too warm.
There’s still quite a bit of hype surrounding the restaurant, so expect a queue. You’ll need to scan a QR code to get your name on the waiting list, though we only had to wait around 20 minutes, which wasn’t too bad. Of course, that’s assuming you’re not rushing back to the office after lunch.
What to order at Gosame
Imagine going to the “famous charcoal-grilled mackerel spot from Seoul” then not getting the said mackerel. Talk about not being like other girls. Not me, though!
We went straight for the Grilled Mackerel (RM37) , alongside Spicy Squid (RM35) , Sundubu Jjigae (RM25) and, naturally, a bowl of Rice (RM5) , which came with banchan .
The grilled mackerel was served as a whole fish split into two halves, with the skin grilled until beautifully charred while the flesh underneath remained moist and glistening with oil.
Now, I’m not exactly the biggest fan of fish, especially those with a stronger fishy taste like tuna and mackerel. So I wasn’t expecting to enjoy this as much as I did. It had a hint of the ocean, but nothing too overpowering. The flesh was buttery, juicy and wonderfully flaky, almost melting apart with each bite. A dip in the accompanying tangy sauce made it even better.
10 new places in JB to check out this Nov 2026 — cafes, food & more
But if you ask me which dish I’d order again, the Spicy Squid would probably be my answer. The squid was tender without being rubbery, while retaining a satisfying bite. What really stood out was the sauce, which tasted quite different from your usual gochujang -based Korean stir-fry.
It was smoky, deeply savoury and reminded me a little of sambal , though not quite Malaysianised. There was also a gentle kick of spice that made it dangerously addictive, especially with rice.
The Sundubu Jjigae was another no-brainer. You can’t really go wrong with a comforting bowl of kimchi stew, especially one that comes with generous portions of soft tofu and eggs. It had a nice touch of heat and paired well with the grilled dishes.
To wash everything down, we had the Yuja Blue Tea (RM12) and Yuja Soda Ade (RM12) . Both were refreshing choices for a meal like this, although I found them a little too sweet, particularly towards the bottom of the glass where the yuzu syrup and fruit strips had settled.
Who is Gosame best for?
Families, friends and casual catch-ups, definitely. It could work for a casual date, too, although I wouldn’t put it on my list for a formal dinner date.
How to get there?
Driving is your best bet, as the restaurant isn’t directly connected to public transport. There are paid parking spaces available in the area, though can fill up rather quickly.
Do we recommend Gosame?
How do I put this? The food was genuinely delicious, and I’d say Gosame is worth trying at least once, particularly if you’re curious about its charcoal-grilled mackerel. The Spicy Squid was also a pleasant surprise and easily my favourite of the meal.
Would I go out of my way to have it again? Probably not. At least, not yet. But if you’re already in the neighbourhood or have been curious about what all the fuss is about, I’d say give it a go. At the very least, you can finally see what the hype is about without having to wonder about it anymore.
People also read:
What to eat at Ombak KLCC?
Where to go for yummy Mediterranean food in PJ?
summary: Gosame is a Muslim-owned Korean restaurant from Seoul that has opened its first KL outlet at The Stories of Taman Tunku. Known for its charcoal-grilled mackerel, the menu also features spicy squid, sundubu jjigae and yuzu drinks, with mains priced from RM25 to RM37. Suited to casual meals with family and friends, it is worth considering for those curious about its grilled seafood, although queues, limited seating and a lack of direct public transport access are worth noting.
title: Gosame KL: We tried Seoul’s famous grilled mackerel & spicy squid everyone’s talking about

DBS TravelLah! Debit Card
The end-of-year holidays are upcoming, and if you’ve got travel plans all lined up, here’s a debit card to add to your wallet. New to the DBS lineup is the TravelLah! Debit Card , available to anyone from the age of 16. As its name suggests, it’s been designed all around any travels you may have on the horizon, with 0 FX fees , and 0 overseas ATM withdrawal fees .
0 FX fees on overseas spending
Now on to the real bonuses: first, 0 FX fees on overseas spending . Compared to other cards, where you may incur a fee on top of the exchange rate when you pay in a foreign currency, you’re looking at 0 additional charges when using the DBS TravelLah! Debit Card.
Whatever purchase you make is converted at Visa’s competitive exchange rates, which are almost as good as what you’d find on a quick Google search, with no markup fees from DBS. Should you want to check, all you need to do is open your DBS PayLah! app ( iOS | Android ) to view the indicative exchange rates.
Plus, everything is charged in Singapore Dollars (SGD), so you are spared the hassle of pre-converting money or juggling balances in a digital travel wallet.
This new card works in over 150 currencies . In other words, it’ll see you through your Euro summers, Bali sojourns, and skiing in Japan, no sweat.
No cap on overseas ATM withdrawals
Image credit: Japan Airlines
With this new debit card, you won’t have to beat the lunch crowd at The Arcade’s money changers, or find yourself paying above market rates at airport foreign currency exchange counters. That’s because DBS charges $0 in ATM fees on overseas cash withdrawals.
And the best part? There’s no cap on the number of ATM withdrawals , so you can access your money without worrying about interest charges imposed by the bank. You can also withdraw any amount, up to the daily TravelLah! spend limit of $5,000.
This is exceptionally handy if you’re the sort who walks around with no wallet or cash in hand – unlike in Singapore, many other countries still run on cash. So, instead of carrying a wad of cash around with you, the DBS TravelLah! Debit Card allows you to take out smaller amounts as you go.
Do note, however, that while DBS waives their fees, some overseas ATMs might still impose local withdrawal fees, which will usually be displayed on the summary screen.

Chalkak Collective – Photobooth museum in Singapore
We’ve all been guilty of squeezing into a photobooth with our besties, scrambling to strike a pose before the timer runs out, and walking away with a photo strip for keeps. But if the usual 4-cut photos aren’t enough to satisfy your inner model, there’s a new spot in Singapore that’ll have you striking poses for hours.
Chalkak Collective recently opened on 29th October 2026 , and it’s Asia’s 1st photobooth museum. Located just 8 minutes from Marymount MRT , this self-portrait playground features 4 themed studios, unlimited photo-taking opportunities, and personalised souvenirs, all for $59/pax .
How much does it cost for a session at Chalkak Collective?
Image credit: Jocelyn Yeo via Google Maps
Admission costs $59/pax for a 90-minute session , which includes access to all 4 stations and unlimited photo-taking . Children under 10 years old can join for $20 each , with a maximum of 3 children per booking and at least 1 accompanying adult .
4 themed photobooth stations with unlimited photos
Image credit: Chalkak Collective
Unlike your typical mall photobooth, where you’re limited to a handful of shots, Chalkak Collective gives visitors 90 minutes to explore its 4 stations and take as many photos as they fancy.
Each station comes with its own photography style, lighting setup, and print formats, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to switch up your poses and bring home different keepsakes.
Vintage Press Studio
Image credit: Chalkak Collective
If you’ve ever wondered what you’d look like on the front page of a vintage newspaper, the Vintage Press Studio has you covered.
This retro-inspired station transforms your photos into old-fashioned prints featuring your visitor number.
Image credit: @chalkak.collective via Instagram
There are 5 print formats to experiment with, including The Newspaper , Vintage Strip , Vintage Print , Vintage 2 Strip , and Museum Receipt .
Instead of relying on digital filters to achieve that nostalgic look, the studio uses monochrome lighting and print treatments to give your photos an authentic archival feel.
You’ll also find framed photographs , vintage posters , and record shelves decorating the space, making the studio itself a photo-worthy backdrop.
Set aside around 20-25 minutes to try the different formats, with physical prints available after each round.
Cutesy DIY Bar
Image credit: EveC via Google Maps
For those who love collecting adorable trinkets, the Cutesy DIY Bar takes the photobooth experience one step further by letting you turn your pictures into personalised souvenirs.
After snapping your photos, head over to the crafting station, where you’ll find stickers , frames , cutting tools , and other materials to decorate your creations.
There are 5 DIY formats to choose from: Purikura , Trading Cards , Explorer ID , Meme Sheets , and Keychains .
Image credit: Jiwoo Seo via Google Maps
You can channel your inner K-pop idol by designing your own trading cards, turn your funniest expressions into meme stickers, or create matching keychains with your besties.
The best part? All the crafting materials are included in your $59 admission, so you won’t have to fork out extra cash to get creative with your souvenirs.
The station recommends around 35-45 minutes for the full photo-taking and crafting experience, although you’ll need to keep an eye on your overall 90-minute session time.
K-Photo Lab
Image credit: EveC via Google Maps
No photobooth museum would be complete without the iconic Korean-style photo strips we’ve all come to love.
At the K-Photo Lab , you can squeeze up to 6 people into a spacious booth, complete with a wide-angle camera and a bench so everyone gets their moment in the spotlight.
Image credit: Ng Jun Xian via Google Maps
Expect the familiar countdown timer that’ll have you frantically switching poses and trying not to burst into laughter before the camera flashes.
You can choose from several formats, including Mall 4-Cut , XL Strip , Museum Strip , Halloween Strip , and Tablet Booth , alongside different Booth Effects .
Image credit: @chalkak.collective via Instagram
Once you’ve selected your favourite shots, your photo strips are printed on the spot, with 2 copies provided as standard.
It’s an ideal stop for friend groups looking to update their photo collections without leaving anyone awkwardly cropped out of the frame.
Self Portrait Atelier
Image credit: Chalkak Collective
Ever wanted a professional-looking photoshoot without having a photographer watching your every move? The Self Portrait Atelier lets you take matters into your own hands, quite literally.
This minimalist studio features a seamless white backdrop , professional softbox lighting , and a camera connected to a wired remote shutter.
Instead of racing against a countdown, you get to decide exactly when to take each shot, giving you more freedom to experiment with different poses and expressions.
Image adapted from: Chalkak Collective
…
summary: Your camera roll is about to get a serious upgrade.
title: Asia’s First Photobooth Museum Opens In SG With Unlimited Photos, DIY Keychains & Unique Photostrip Designs

body:
Long-distance hiking trails in S G
Training for your next marathon or gearing up for an overseas hiking adventure? You don’t have to travel far to put your stamina to the test. There are plenty of long-distance hiking trails in SG that take you through lush forests, scenic coastlines, and winding nature paths, all while giving your legs a proper workout.
From the 36km Coast-to-Coast Trail to the greenery-filled Rail Corridor, these routes are great for building endurance and getting used to different terrains. So, lace up your hiking shoes and pack your water bottle – we’ve rounded up some long-distance trails, sorted by region, to help you prepare for that Mount Kinabalu hike.
Central
1. MacRitchie Nature Trail, Sime Track & Chempaerai Trail Loop
12.7km of a rainforest hike
Image credit: Tommy Lee via AllTrails
If you prefer being surrounded by greenery instead of skyscrapers, the MacRitchie Nature Trail, Sime Track, and Chempaerai Trail Loop might be right up your alley. Located within MacRitchie Reservoir Park , this 12.7km route takes you through one of Singapore’s oldest rainforest areas.
Image credit: Paul V via AllTrails
You’ll encounter a combination of wooden boardwalks overlooking the reservoir and earthy trails that wind through dense vegetation. Towering trees, ferns, and forest canopies provide plenty of greenery to admire as you make your way through the reserve.
Keep your eyes peeled for wildlife too. Long-tailed macaques, turtles, monkeys, squirrels, monitor lizards, and colourful kingfishers are among the creatures you might spot along the way. If you’re lucky, you might even catch a glimpse of the greater racket-tailed drongo, a bird known for its distinctive tail feathers.
Image adapted from: Austin Jennings, Edouard Clouet des Pesruches & Kayatoast User via AllTrails
Although the trails are generally well-maintained, the uneven forest paths and Singapore’s infamous humidity can make the journey more challenging, so come prepared. It’s also a good option for hikers looking to improve their endurance while getting accustomed to natural terrain.
How to get there: Take the MRT to Caldecott MRT Station and walk approximately 15-20 minutes towards MacRitchie Reservoir Park via Lornie Road . Alternatively, take bus 157 . You can also access the trails near the Singapore Island Country Club entrance .
Check out the MacRitchie Nature Trail, Sime Track, and Chempaerai Trail Loop .
2. MacRitchie to Bukit Panjang
12.4km hike through forest trails & nature parks
For another nature-filled adventure, try the MacRitchie to Bukit Panjang trail . Spanning 12.4km , this route starts at MacRitchie Reservoir before taking you through forested paths, park connectors, and quieter stretches of Singapore’s central greenery.
Image adapted from: Kevin CT See via Facebook , Trip.com
The journey begins among dense secondary rainforest before connecting to the Central Catchment Park Connector network . Along the way, you’ll pass landmarks such as Terentang Hut before making your way towards the Bukit Timah area.
Zhenghua Nature Park .
Image credit: NParks
Eventually, the trail leads towards Zhenghua Nature Park , a peaceful green space that’s also a popular spot for birdwatching. It’s a nice change of scenery after navigating the more demanding forest sections earlier in the hike.
With a combination of dirt tracks, paved pathways, and longer walking stretches, this route offers a decent workout for those preparing for overseas hikes. Plus, you’ll get to explore several green spaces in a single outing.
How to get there: Alight at Caldecott MRT Station , take Exit A , and walk approximately 10-15 minutes towards MacRitchie Reservoir Park . Alternatively, take buses 52 , 74 , 130 , 132 , 157 , 165 , 166 , 167 , 852 , or 855 to a nearby bus stop along Thomson Road or Lornie Road .
Check out the MacRitchie to Bukit Panjang Trail .
3. Coast-to-Coast Trail (Central)
36km route across Singapore
Image credit: Park Connector Network
If a regular weekend stroll no longer cuts it, challenge yourself to the Coast-to-Coast Trail (Central) . Stretching an impressive 36km , this cross-island route connects Jurong Lake Gardens in the west to Coney Island Park in the northeast.
Image credit: Jurong Lake Gardens
The trail takes you through a variety of landscapes, from bustling residential estates to peaceful parks and nature reserves. Some highlights include Bukit Batok Nature Park , Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park , Sengkang Floating Wetland , and Punggol Waterway Park .
Image adapted from: NParks & Tripadvisor
One of the best things about this route is that you won’t be staring at the same scenery for hours. Expect a mix of forested trails, park connectors, waterfront paths, and urban stretches, with several checkpoints where you can stop for a breather.
…
summary: Get those steps in before your next big hiking adventure.
title: 13 Long-Distance Hiking Trails In Singapore To Build Stamina For Your Next Overseas Adventure

Career sites & Telegram channels for jobs in Singapore
Job hunting can feel like a full-time job in itself, especially when you’re looking for unique jobs in Singapore that let you break free from the usual 9-to-6 grind. Scrolling through endless listings, tailoring resumes, and waiting for replies that may never come just makes the whole process feel sian .
Thankfully, there are more ways to job hunt than refreshing LinkedIn every few hours. From career portals with handy application features to Telegram channels sharing job openings, here are some places to look for your next gig.
Best job hunting platforms in Singapore
These career websites are great if you prefer a more structured job search, with filters to narrow down listings by job type, industry, and experience level.
1. CreativesAtWork
Best for freelance writers, designers, videographers & other creatives
Image credit: CreativesAtWork
If you’re a creative looking for freelance opportunities, CreativesAtWork is worth checking out. Rather than functioning like a traditional job portal, it operates more as a creative media network that connects freelance professionals with relevant projects and clients.
It covers a wide range of disciplines, including video production, photography, graphic design, animation, writing, and creative strategy. Its affiliated community, Freelancer Nation , also provides opportunities for networking and project matching.
This makes it a good platform for creatives who are keen to build experience and grow their portfolios. Just take note that it might not be the best platform if you’re looking for a conventional, searchable list of job vacancies.
2. Snatchjobs
Part-time & temporary jobs
Image credit: SnatchJobs
For those searching for flexible work, Snatchjobs is one of the more practical platforms to browse. It lists part-time, full-time, contract, and internship opportunities in Singapore, with categories ranging from F&B and retail to admin, logistics, and event staffing.
One useful feature is that many listings display hourly or monthly pay upfront, making it easier to compare opportunities at a glance. The platform also has Snatchmatch , which sends you alerts for jobs that match your preferences.
Snatchjobs says employers are verified through their Singapore UEN before posting. But as always, we recommend doing your due diligence to confirm the role details and company legitimacy before applying.
3. Staffie
For flexible F&B shifts
Image credit: Staffie
If you’d rather pick up flexible shifts instead of committing to a fixed schedule, Staffie is an option. The platform focuses on food and beverage work, allowing users to browse shifts at restaurants, cafes, and other establishments.
You can choose jobs based on your availability, so it’s suitable for students and freelancers who require more flexible working hours. Staffie also lets users browse nearby opportunities, book shifts, track earnings, and manage their schedules.
4. NodeFlair
For tech & IT jobs
Screenshot from: NodeFlair
NodeFlair is one of the more specialised options available for job seekers in the tech space. The Singapore-founded platform focuses on technology-related roles such as software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, and product management.
One of the platform’s biggest strengths is its filters, which allow users to narrow roles by job title, seniority, company, salary, and tech stack. It also includes salary insights and company reviews.
However, since many of its listings are aggregated from external sources, it’s a good idea to confirm that the role you are looking into is still active on the employer’s official website.
5. e27 Jobs
Opportunities in startups
Screenshot from: e27 Jobs
Part of the wider e27 ecosystem, e27 Jobs focuses on startup and tech-related companies across Singapore and the region.
Roles listed on its platform span areas such as software engineering, business development, marketing, and operations. It’s a useful place to search if you’re interested in smaller, fast-moving teams or emerging industries.
But the platform tends to have a smaller pool of listings than broader career portals, so it works best as a supplementary site rather than your only job-search platform.
6. Cultjobs
Best for creative, marketing & media roles
Screenshot from: Cultjobs
Another alternative job-hunting platform is Cultjobs , which caters specifically to Singapore’s creative, media, and marketing industries. This platform includes careers in design, copywriting, social media, content, branding, and communications.
Its focus on the creative industry makes it a refreshing alternative to general job portals, especially for those who don’t want to scroll through pages of unrelated listings. Openings range from internships and junior roles to more experienced positions, and can include permanent, freelance, and contract opportunities.
…
summary: Includes tips for spotting job scams so you stay safe while job hunting.
title: 15 Lesser-Known Career Sites & Telegram Channels For Job Seekers Hunting For A Gig In SG

House-brined overnight before being slow-roasted till golden brown for succulence.

Fortune Centre food guide
Fortune Centre is known to be a food haven for many vegetarians, but they also have several non-vegetarian gems worth checking out. From customisable artisanal pasta to affordable Korean food, this list will take you through the best food places at Fortune Centre .
1. Sakedokoro Eizaburo
This one’s for Japanese food fans: Sakedokoro Eizaburo has XL don and sashimi at affordable prices that won’t break the bank. One of the most popular items is the Mega Chicken Karaage Don ($13.90++) , featuring a pile of fried chicken chunks atop a bed of rice. If you’re there for seafood, consider the Unagi Don ($15.90++) or Fujiyama Kaisen Don ($16.90++) instead; the latter comes with uni, crab meat, ikura, diced salmon and seabass sashimi, tamagoyaki, nori, and a dollop of wasabi.
Read our Sakedokoro Eizaburo review .
Unit number: #03-16
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 12pm to 2pm, 5:30pm to 10:30pm, Sat 5:30pm to 10:30pm
Tel: 9117 5094
Website
Sakedokoro Eizaburo is not halal-certified.
We Tried XL Japanese Don At This New Izakaya In Fortune Centre
2. Yuen Kee Dumpling
When Yuen Kee Dumpling first opened at Fortune Centre, there was a snaking long queue every day, where diners had to wait an hour just to try the China-famous dumplings. We too had to wait just to get the Shrimp and Vegetables Pork Dumpling with the Viral Mixed Sauce with Chilli Oil La Mian , a hefty portion that only cost us $11.80+ . The dumplings were not overly doughy, and packed with just the right amount of pork, sweet shrimp, chives, and black fungus.
Read our Yuen Kee Dumpling review .
Unit number: #01-10
Opening hours: Daily 9am to 8:30pm
Tel: 8931 9588
Website
Yuen Kee Dumpling is not halal-certified.
Is Yuen Kee Dumpling Actually Worth Braving The Long Queues?
3. New Station Rice Bar
When you don’t know what to eat, don’t think twice and just head to New Station Rice Bar straight. Most of the items are priced at $8.50 here, including the crowd-favourite Salted Egg Chicken Rice with Fried Egg and our personal favourite Eggplants lying on a bed of Minced Meat with Rice . You can add on a comforting bowl of Black and White Garlic Chicken Soup ($10) or a hearty plate of Handmade Radish Cake Omelette ($12) .
Read our New Station Rice Bar feature .
Unit number: #03-04
Opening hours: Mon-Sat 11am to 8:30pm
Website
New Station Rice Bar is not halal-certified.
Far East Plaza’s Popular New Station Snack Bar Opens Outlet In Fortune Centre
4. Bao Er Cafe
Bao Er Cafe is one of the only spots at Fortune Centre that opens early, which makes for a great breakfast spot . An ideal morning starts with warm, comforting Kaya Butter Toast Set ($6.20) , which comes with two soft boiled eggs and a cup of hot kopi. Teh goes for $1.90 if you’re more of a tea person. If you’re dining in during lunch or dinner, opt for the Prawn Noodle Soup ($7.50) or Yang Zhou Fried Rice ($6.50) instead—they are equally popular choices among the regulars.
Unit number: #02-06
Opening hours: Daily 8am to 8pm
Tel: 8686 9777
Bao Er Cafe is not halal-certified.
5. Onigiri GON
Image credit: Onigiri GON via Google Maps
Another Japanese spot here is Onigiri GON , run by a Fukuoka native. Despite its limited dining space, the onigiri eatery still draws long queues even months after opening. Each onigiri is handmade fresh on-site, with 20 flavours to choose from. Prices range from $4.90 to $6.90 , with fillings such as Ume , Mentaiko Mayo , and Spicy Salmon . For a more wholesome meal, opt for the Onigiri Set Meal ($13.90) , comprising your choice of two onigiri, a bowl of miso soup, plus a side of pickles. Diners can also DIY their own onigiri with additional ingredients for a small top-up, starting from $1.50 .
Read our Onigiri GON feature .
Unit number: #01-18
Opening hours: Tue-Sat 11:30am to 4pm
Website
Onigiri GON is not halal-certified.
There’s A New Japanese-Run Onigiri Shop At Fortune Centre
6. Wawa Lala Bee Hoon
There used to be a time Singaporeans went head over heels for lala. If you’re a fan, head to Wawa Lala Bee Hoon for a comforting bowl of Authentic Clam Noodles with Chinese Wine ($9.50) , which comes with either rice noodle or glass noodle. If you’d like it without alcohol, get the Refreshing Clam Soup Noodles ($8.90) instead! There are dry options too, with the likes of Fresh Cockles in Wawa Special Sauce ($13.50) and Fresh Clams in Homemade Garlic Butter Sauce ($8.90) .
Read our Wawa Lala Bee Hoon review .
Unit number: #01-11/12
Opening hours: Daily 11:30am to 9:30pm
Website
Wawa Lala Bee Hoon is not halal-certified.
7. A9 Noodle Dumpling
…

Singapore’s social clubs are more than just places to meet people; many, such as The American Club, have a long history and rich heritage. Then, there are newer spaces such as The Nanson, which offer a modern wellness-centred experience apart from networking opportunities.
If you’re looking to become the social butterfly you’ve always wanted to be, here are the best social clubs in Singapore . Whether you enjoy attending social events, playing sports, or simply meeting new people, there’s a club to suit your interests on this list.
How I chose these best social clubs
These are the 3 main criteria I used to decide which social clubs to recommend:
• Variety : The list includes traditional social and sporting clubs as well as modern private members’ clubs.
• Wide range of interests : From sports to dining to wine, these clubs offer different experiences.
• Community : These clubs boast a strong community, where you can bond with others over shared interests, organised activities and member gatherings.
This isn’t a ranked best-to-worst list, but a collection of the best social clubs overall, in no particular order. Do note that since these are private clubs, you should check their current membership terms and policies; some may require referrals. It is also best to enquire with them directly about membership fees and applications.
